rules.title: AWS Bucket Deleted
rules.description:
Detects the deletion of S3 buckets in AWS CloudTrail logs.
Monitoring the deletion of S3 buckets is critical for security and data integrity, as it may indicate potential data loss or unauthorized access attempts.
rules.author: Ivan Saakov, Nasreddine Bencherchali

rules.title: AWS ConsoleLogin Failed Authentication
rules.description: Detects failed AWS console login attempts due to authentication failures. Monitoring these events is crucial for identifying potential brute-force attacks or unauthorized access attempts to AWS accounts.
rules.author: Ivan Saakov, Nasreddine Bencherchali

rules.title: AWS Successful Console Login Without MFA
rules.description:
Detects successful AWS console logins that were performed without Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA).
This alert can be used to identify potential unauthorized access attempts, as logging in without MFA can indicate compromised credentials or misconfigured security settings.
rules.author: Thuya@Hacktilizer, Ivan Saakov

rules.title: AWS CloudTrail Important Change
rules.description: Detects disabling, deleting and updating of a Trail
rules.author: vitaliy0x1

rules.title: AWS GuardDuty Detector Deleted Or Updated
rules.description:
Detects successful deletion or disabling of an AWS GuardDuty detector, possibly by an attacker trying to avoid detection of its malicious activities.
Upon deletion, GuardDuty stops monitoring the environment and all existing findings are lost.
Verify with the user identity that this activity is legi
rules.author: suktech24

rules.title: Malicious Usage Of IMDS Credentials Outside Of AWS Infrastructure
rules.description:
Detects when an instance identity has taken an action that isn't inside SSM.
This can indicate that a compromised EC2 instance is being used as a pivot point.
rules.author: jamesc-grafana

rules.title: New Network ACL Entry Added
rules.description: Detects that network ACL entries have been added to a route table which could indicate that new attack vectors have been opened up in the AWS account.
rules.author: jamesc-grafana

rules.title: New Network Route Added
rules.description: Detects the addition of a new network route to a route table in AWS.
rules.author: jamesc-grafana

rules.title: PUA - AWS TruffleHog Execution
rules.description:
Detects the execution of TruffleHog, a popular open-source tool used for scanning repositories for secrets and sensitive information, within an AWS environment.
It has been reported to be used by threat actors for credential harvesting. All detections should be investigated to determine if the usage
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: AWS EnableRegion Command Monitoring
rules.description:
Detects the use of the EnableRegion command in AWS CloudTrail logs.
While AWS has 30+ regions, some of them are enabled by default, others must be explicitly enabled in each account separately.
There may be situations where security monitoring does not cover some new AWS regions.
Monitoring the Enab
rules.author: Ivan Saakov, Sergey Zelenskiy

rules.title: Ingress/Egress Security Group Modification
rules.description:
Detects when an account makes changes to the ingress or egress rules of a security group.
This can indicate that an attacker is attempting to open up new attack vectors in the account, that they are trying to exfiltrate data over the network, or that they are trying to allow machines in that VPC/Sub
rules.author: jamesc-grafana

rules.title: LoadBalancer Security Group Modification
rules.description:
Detects changes to the security groups associated with an Elastic Load Balancer (ELB) or Application Load Balancer (ALB).
This can indicate that a misconfiguration allowing more traffic into the system than required, or could indicate that an attacker is attempting to enable new connections into a V
rules.author: jamesc-grafana

rules.title: RDS Database Security Group Modification
rules.description:
Detects changes to the security group entries for RDS databases.
This can indicate that a misconfiguration has occurred which potentially exposes the database to the public internet, a wider audience within the VPC or that removal of valid rules has occurred which could impact the availability of th
rules.author: jamesc-grafana

rules.title: Potential Malicious Usage of CloudTrail System Manager
rules.description: Detect when System Manager successfully executes commands against an instance.
rules.author: jamesc-grafana

rules.title: AWS VPC Flow Logs Deleted
rules.description:
Detects the deletion of one or more VPC Flow Logs in AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) through the DeleteFlowLogs API call.
Adversaries may delete flow logs to evade detection or remove evidence of network activity, hindering forensic investigations and visibility into malicious operations.
rules.author: Ivan Saakov

rules.title: AWS Config Disabling Channel/Recorder
rules.description: Detects AWS Config Service disabling
rules.author: vitaliy0x1

rules.title: AWS Console GetSigninToken Potential Abuse
rules.description:
Detects potentially suspicious events involving "GetSigninToken".
An adversary using the "aws_consoler" tool can leverage this console API to create temporary federated credential that help obfuscate which AWS credential is compromised (the original access key) and enables the adversary to pivot fro
rules.author: Chester Le Bron (@123Le_Bron)

rules.title: SES Identity Has Been Deleted
rules.description: Detects an instance of an SES identity being deleted via the "DeleteIdentity" event. This may be an indicator of an adversary removing the account that carried out suspicious or malicious activities
rules.author: Janantha Marasinghe

rules.title: AWS SAML Provider Deletion Activity
rules.description:
Detects the deletion of an AWS SAML provider, potentially indicating malicious intent to disrupt administrative or security team access.
An attacker can remove the SAML provider for the information security team or a team of system administrators, to make it difficult for them to work and investigat
rules.author: Ivan Saakov

rules.title: AWS S3 Bucket Versioning Disable
rules.description: Detects when S3 bucket versioning is disabled. Threat actors use this technique during AWS ransomware incidents prior to deleting S3 objects.
rules.author: Sean Johnstone | Unit 42

rules.title: AWS EC2 Disable EBS Encryption
rules.description:
Identifies disabling of default Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) encryption in the current region.
Disabling default encryption does not change the encryption status of your existing volumes.
rules.author: Sittikorn S

rules.title: AWS Key Pair Import Activity
rules.description: Detects the import of SSH key pairs into AWS EC2, which may indicate an attacker attempting to gain unauthorized access to instances. This activity could lead to initial access, persistence, or privilege escalation, potentially compromising sensitive data and operations.
rules.author: Ivan Saakov

rules.title: AWS EC2 Startup Shell Script Change
rules.description: Detects changes to the EC2 instance startup script. The shell script will be executed as root/SYSTEM every time the specific instances are booted up.
rules.author: faloker

rules.title: AWS EC2 VM Export Failure
rules.description: An attempt to export an AWS EC2 instance has been detected. A VM Export might indicate an attempt to extract information from an instance.
rules.author: Diogo Braz

rules.title: AWS ECS Task Definition That Queries The Credential Endpoint
rules.description:
Detects when an Elastic Container Service (ECS) Task Definition includes a command to query the credential endpoint.
This can indicate a potential adversary adding a backdoor to establish persistence or escalate privileges.
rules.author: Darin Smith

rules.title: AWS EFS Fileshare Modified or Deleted
rules.description:
Detects when a EFS Fileshare is modified or deleted.
You can't delete a file system that is in use.
If the file system has any mount targets, the adversary must first delete them, so deletion of a mount will occur before deletion of a fileshare.
rules.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

rules.title: AWS EFS Fileshare Mount Modified or Deleted
rules.description: Detects when a EFS Fileshare Mount is modified or deleted. An adversary breaking any file system using the mount target that is being deleted, which might disrupt instances or applications using those mounts.
rules.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

rules.title: AWS EKS Cluster Created or Deleted
rules.description: Identifies when an EKS cluster is created or deleted.
rules.author: Austin Songer

rules.title: AWS ElastiCache Security Group Created
rules.description: Detects when an ElastiCache security group has been created.
rules.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

rules.title: AWS ElastiCache Security Group Modified or Deleted
rules.description: Identifies when an ElastiCache security group has been modified or deleted.
rules.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

rules.title: Potential Bucket Enumeration on AWS
rules.description: Looks for potential enumeration of AWS buckets via ListBuckets.
rules.author: Christopher Peacock @securepeacock, SCYTHE @scythe_io

rules.title: AWS GuardDuty Important Change
rules.description: Detects updates of the GuardDuty list of trusted IPs, perhaps to disable security alerts against malicious IPs.
rules.author: faloker

rules.title: AWS IAM Backdoor Users Keys
rules.description:
Detects AWS API key creation for a user by another user.
Backdoored users can be used to obtain persistence in the AWS environment.
Also with this alert, you can detect a flow of AWS keys in your org.
rules.author: faloker

rules.title: AWS IAM S3Browser LoginProfile Creation
rules.description: Detects S3 Browser utility performing reconnaissance looking for existing IAM Users without a LoginProfile defined then (when found) creating a LoginProfile.
rules.author: daniel.bohannon@permiso.io (@danielhbohannon)

rules.title: AWS IAM S3Browser Templated S3 Bucket Policy Creation
rules.description: Detects S3 browser utility creating Inline IAM policy containing default S3 bucket name placeholder value of "<YOUR-BUCKET-NAME>".
rules.author: daniel.bohannon@permiso.io (@danielhbohannon)

rules.title: AWS IAM S3Browser User or AccessKey Creation
rules.description: Detects S3 Browser utility creating IAM User or AccessKey.
rules.author: daniel.bohannon@permiso.io (@danielhbohannon)

rules.title: AWS KMS Imported Key Material Usage
rules.description: Detects the import or deletion of key material in AWS KMS, which can be used as part of ransomware attacks. This activity is uncommon and provides a high certainty signal.
rules.author: toopricey

rules.title: New AWS Lambda Function URL Configuration Created
rules.description:
Detects when a user creates a Lambda function URL configuration, which could be used to expose the function to the internet and potentially allow unauthorized access to the function's IAM role for AWS API calls.
This could give an adversary access to the privileges associated with the Lambda service
rules.author: Ivan Saakov

rules.title: AWS New Lambda Layer Attached
rules.description:
Detects when a user attached a Lambda layer to an existing Lambda function.
A malicious Lambda layer could execute arbitrary code in the context of the function's IAM role.
This would give an adversary access to resources that the function has access to.
rules.author: Austin Songer

rules.title: AWS Glue Development Endpoint Activity
rules.description: Detects possible suspicious glue development endpoint activity.
rules.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

rules.title: AWS RDS Master Password Change
rules.description: Detects the change of database master password. It may be a part of data exfiltration.
rules.author: faloker

rules.title: Modification or Deletion of an AWS RDS Cluster
rules.description: Detects modifications to an RDS cluster or its deletion, which may indicate potential data exfiltration attempts, unauthorized access, or exposure of sensitive information.
rules.author: Ivan Saakov

rules.title: Restore Public AWS RDS Instance
rules.description: Detects the recovery of a new public database instance from a snapshot. It may be a part of data exfiltration.
rules.author: faloker

rules.title: AWS Root Credentials
rules.description: Detects AWS root account usage
rules.author: vitaliy0x1

rules.title: AWS Route 53 Domain Transfer Lock Disabled
rules.description: Detects when a transfer lock was removed from a Route 53 domain. It is recommended to refrain from performing this action unless intending to transfer the domain to a different registrar.
rules.author: Elastic, Austin Songer @austinsonger

rules.title: AWS Route 53 Domain Transferred to Another Account
rules.description: Detects when a request has been made to transfer a Route 53 domain to another AWS account.
rules.author: Elastic, Austin Songer @austinsonger

rules.title: AWS S3 Data Management Tampering
rules.description: Detects when a user tampers with S3 data management in Amazon Web Services.
rules.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

rules.title: AWS SecurityHub Findings Evasion
rules.description: Detects the modification of the findings on SecurityHub.
rules.author: Sittikorn S

rules.title: AWS Snapshot Backup Exfiltration
rules.description: Detects the modification of an EC2 snapshot's permissions to enable access from another account
rules.author: Darin Smith

rules.title: AWS Identity Center Identity Provider Change
rules.description:
Detects a change in the AWS Identity Center (FKA AWS SSO) identity provider.
A change in identity provider allows an attacker to establish persistent access or escalate privileges via user impersonation.
rules.author: Michael McIntyre @wtfender

rules.title: AWS STS AssumeRole Misuse
rules.description: Identifies the suspicious use of AssumeRole. Attackers could move laterally and escalate privileges.
rules.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

rules.title: AWS STS GetCallerIdentity Enumeration Via TruffleHog
rules.description:
Detects the use of TruffleHog for AWS credential validation by identifying GetCallerIdentity API calls where the userAgent indicates TruffleHog.
Threat actors leverage TruffleHog to enumerate and validate exposed AWS keys.
Successful exploitation allows threat actors to confirm the validity of compr
rules.author: Adan Alvarez @adanalvarez

rules.title: AWS STS GetSessionToken Misuse
rules.description: Identifies the suspicious use of GetSessionToken. Tokens could be created and used by attackers to move laterally and escalate privileges.
rules.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

rules.title: AWS Suspicious SAML Activity
rules.description: Identifies when suspicious SAML activity has occurred in AWS. An adversary could gain backdoor access via SAML.
rules.author: Austin Songer

rules.title: AWS User Login Profile Was Modified
rules.description:
Detects activity when someone is changing passwords on behalf of other users.
An attacker with the "iam:UpdateLoginProfile" permission on other users can change the password used to login to the AWS console on any user that already has a login profile setup.
rules.author: toffeebr33k

rules.title: Azure Active Directory Hybrid Health AD FS New Server
rules.description:
This detection uses azureactivity logs (Administrative category) to identify the creation or update of a server instance in an Azure AD Hybrid health AD FS service.
A threat actor can create a new AD Health ADFS service and create a fake server instance to spoof AD FS signing logs. There is no need
rules.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research), MSTIC

rules.title: Azure Active Directory Hybrid Health AD FS Service Delete
rules.description:
This detection uses azureactivity logs (Administrative category) to identify the deletion of an Azure AD Hybrid health AD FS service instance in a tenant.
A threat actor can create a new AD Health ADFS service and create a fake server to spoof AD FS signing logs.
The health AD FS service can then be
rules.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research), MSTIC

Identifies when an admission controller is executed in Azure Kubernetes.
A Kubernetes Admission controller intercepts, and possibly modifies, requests to the Kubernetes API server.
The behavior of this admission controller is determined by an admission webhook (MutatingAdmissionWebhook or Validating
rules.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

Identifies when a Azure Kubernetes CronJob runs in Azure Cloud. Kubernetes Job is a controller that creates one or more pods and ensures that a specified number of them successfully terminate.
Kubernetes Job can be used to run containers that perform finite tasks for batch jobs. Kubernetes CronJob i
rules.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

rules.description: Detects when Events are deleted in Azure Kubernetes. An adversary may delete events in Azure Kubernetes in an attempt to evade detection.
rules.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

rules.description: Identifies when a service principal was removed in Azure.
rules.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

rules.title: Azure Subscription Permission Elevation Via ActivityLogs
rules.description:
Detects when a user has been elevated to manage all Azure Subscriptions.
This change should be investigated immediately if it isn't planned.
This setting could allow an attacker access to Azure subscriptions in your environment.
rules.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

rules.title: Azure Suppression Rule Created
rules.description: Identifies when a suppression rule is created in Azure. Adversary's could attempt this to evade detection.
rules.author: Austin Songer

rules.title: Azure Virtual Network Modified or Deleted
rules.description: Identifies when a Virtual Network is modified or deleted in Azure.
rules.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

rules.title: Azure VPN Connection Modified or Deleted
rules.description: Identifies when a VPN connection is modified or deleted.
rules.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

rules.title: New CA Policy by Non-approved Actor
rules.description: Monitor and alert on conditional access changes.

rules.description: Detects when an account was created and deleted in a short period of time.
rules.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', MikeDuddington, '@dudders1', Tim Shelton

rules.description: Monitor and alert for Bitlocker key retrieval.

rules.author: Bailey Bercik '@baileybercik', Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow'

rules.title: Application URI Configuration Changes
rules.description:
Detects when a configuration change is made to an applications URI.
URIs for domain names that no longer exist (dangling URIs), not using HTTPS, wildcards at the end of the domain, URIs that are no unique to that app, or URIs that point to domains you do not control should be investigated.
rules.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Bailey Bercik '@baileybercik'

rules.description:
Detects when a user has been elevated to manage all Azure Subscriptions.
This change should be investigated immediately if it isn't planned.
This setting could allow an attacker access to Azure subscriptions in your environment.
rules.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

rules.title: Temporary Access Pass Added To An Account
rules.description: Detects when a temporary access pass (TAP) is added to an account. TAPs added to priv accounts should be investigated
rules.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Yochana Henderson, '@Yochana-H'

rules.title: User Risk and MFA Registration Policy Updated
rules.description:
Detects changes and updates to the user risk and MFA registration policy.
Attackers can modified the policies to Bypass MFA, weaken security thresholds, facilitate further attacks, maintain persistence.
rules.author: Harjot Singh (@cyb3rjy0t)

rules.title: Multi Factor Authentication Disabled For User Account
rules.description:
Detects changes to the "StrongAuthenticationRequirement" value, where the state is set to "0" or "Disabled".
Threat actors were seen disabling multi factor authentication for users in order to maintain or achieve access to the account. Also see in SIM Swap attacks.
rules.author: Harjot Singh (@cyb3rjy0t)

rules.title: Password Reset By User Account
rules.description: Detect when a user has reset their password in Azure AD
rules.author: YochanaHenderson, '@Yochana-H'

rules.title: Anomalous Token
rules.description: Indicates that there are abnormal characteristics in the token such as an unusual token lifetime or a token that is played from an unfamiliar location.
rules.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow'

rules.title: Anomalous User Activity
rules.description: Indicates that there are anomalous patterns of behavior like suspicious changes to the directory.
rules.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

rules.title: Activity From Anonymous IP Address
rules.description: Identifies that users were active from an IP address that has been identified as an anonymous proxy IP address.
rules.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

rules.title: Anonymous IP Address
rules.description: Indicates sign-ins from an anonymous IP address, for example, using an anonymous browser or VPN.
rules.author: Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

rules.title: Atypical Travel
rules.description: Identifies two sign-ins originating from geographically distant locations, where at least one of the locations may also be atypical for the user, given past behavior.
rules.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

rules.title: Impossible Travel
rules.description: Identifies user activities originating from geographically distant locations within a time period shorter than the time it takes to travel from the first location to the second.
rules.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

rules.title: Suspicious Inbox Forwarding Identity Protection
rules.description: Indicates suspicious rules such as an inbox rule that forwards a copy of all emails to an external address
rules.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

rules.title: Suspicious Inbox Manipulation Rules
rules.description: Detects suspicious rules that delete or move messages or folders are set on a user's inbox.
rules.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

rules.title: Azure AD Account Credential Leaked
rules.description: Indicates that the user's valid credentials have been leaked.
rules.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

rules.title: Malicious IP Address Sign-In Failure Rate
rules.description: Indicates sign-in from a malicious IP address based on high failure rates.
rules.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

rules.title: Malicious IP Address Sign-In Suspicious
rules.description: Indicates sign-in from a malicious IP address known to be malicious at time of sign-in.
rules.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

rules.title: Sign-In From Malware Infected IP
rules.description: Indicates sign-ins from IP addresses infected with malware that is known to actively communicate with a bot server.
rules.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

rules.title: New Country
rules.description: Detects sign-ins from new countries. The detection considers past activity locations to determine new and infrequent locations.
rules.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

rules.title: Password Spray Activity
rules.description: Indicates that a password spray attack has been successfully performed.
rules.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

rules.title: Primary Refresh Token Access Attempt
rules.description: Indicates access attempt to the PRT resource which can be used to move laterally into an organization or perform credential theft
rules.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

rules.title: Suspicious Browser Activity
rules.description: Indicates anomalous behavior based on suspicious sign-in activity across multiple tenants from different countries in the same browser
rules.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

rules.title: Azure AD Threat Intelligence
rules.description: Indicates user activity that is unusual for the user or consistent with known attack patterns.
rules.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

rules.title: SAML Token Issuer Anomaly
rules.description: Indicates the SAML token issuer for the associated SAML token is potentially compromised. The claims included in the token are unusual or match known attacker patterns
rules.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

rules.title: Unfamiliar Sign-In Properties
rules.description: Detects sign-in with properties that are unfamiliar to the user. The detection considers past sign-in history to look for anomalous sign-ins.
rules.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

rules.title: Stale Accounts In A Privileged Role
rules.description: Identifies when an account hasn't signed in during the past n number of days.
rules.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

rules.title: Invalid PIM License
rules.description: Identifies when an organization doesn't have the proper license for PIM and is out of compliance.
rules.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

rules.title: Roles Assigned Outside PIM
rules.description: Identifies when a privilege role assignment has taken place outside of PIM and may indicate an attack.
rules.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

rules.title: Roles Activated Too Frequently
rules.description: Identifies when the same privilege role has multiple activations by the same user.
rules.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

rules.title: Roles Are Not Being Used
rules.description: Identifies when a user has been assigned a privilege role and are not using that role.
rules.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

rules.title: Roles Activation Doesn't Require MFA
rules.description: Identifies when a privilege role can be activated without performing mfa.
rules.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

rules.title: Too Many Global Admins
rules.description: Identifies an event where there are there are too many accounts assigned the Global Administrator role.
rules.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

rules.title: Account Lockout
rules.description: Identifies user account which has been locked because the user tried to sign in too many times with an incorrect user ID or password.
rules.author: AlertIQ

rules.title: Successful Authentications From Countries You Do Not Operate Out Of
rules.description: Detect successful authentications from countries you do not operate out of.
rules.author: MikeDuddington, '@dudders1'

rules.title: Increased Failed Authentications Of Any Type
rules.description: Detects when sign-ins increased by 10% or greater.
rules.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', MikeDuddington, '@dudders1'

rules.title: Measurable Increase Of Successful Authentications
rules.description: Detects when successful sign-ins increased by 10% or greater.
rules.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', MikeDuddington, '@dudders1', Tim Shelton

rules.title: Authentications To Important Apps Using Single Factor Authentication

rules.author: MikeDuddington, '@dudders1'

rules.title: Device Registration or Join Without MFA

rules.title: Failed Authentications From Countries You Do Not Operate Out Of
rules.description: Detect failed authentications from countries you do not operate out of.
rules.author: MikeDuddington, '@dudders1'

rules.title: Azure AD Only Single Factor Authentication Required
rules.description: Detect when users are authenticating without MFA being required.
rules.author: MikeDuddington, '@dudders1'

rules.author: Harjot Singh, '@cyb3rjy0t'

rules.title: Sign-ins from Non-Compliant Devices
rules.description: Monitor and alert for sign-ins where the device was non-compliant.
rules.author: Michael Epping, '@mepples21'

rules.title: Sign-ins by Unknown Devices
rules.description: Monitor and alert for Sign-ins by unknown devices from non-Trusted locations.
rules.author: Michael Epping, '@mepples21'

rules.title: Potential MFA Bypass Using Legacy Client Authentication
rules.description: Detects successful authentication from potential clients using legacy authentication via user agent strings. This could be a sign of MFA bypass using a password spray attack.
rules.author: Harjot Singh, '@cyb3rjy0t'

rules.title: Application Using Device Code Authentication Flow
rules.description:
Device code flow is an OAuth 2.0 protocol flow specifically for input constrained devices and is not used in all environments.
If this type of flow is seen in the environment and not being used in an input constrained device scenario, further investigation is warranted.
This can be a misconfigured a
rules.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Bailey Bercik '@baileybercik'

rules.title: Applications That Are Using ROPC Authentication Flow
rules.description:
Resource owner password credentials (ROPC) should be avoided if at all possible as this requires the user to expose their current password credentials to the application directly.
The application then uses those credentials to authenticate the user against the identity provider.
rules.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Bailey Bercik '@baileybercik'

rules.title: Account Disabled or Blocked for Sign in Attempts
rules.description: Detects when an account is disabled or blocked for sign in but tried to log in
rules.author: Yochana Henderson, '@Yochana-H'

rules.title: Sign-in Failure Due to Conditional Access Requirements Not Met
rules.description: Define a baseline threshold for failed sign-ins due to Conditional Access failures
rules.author: Yochana Henderson, '@Yochana-H'

rules.title: Use of Legacy Authentication Protocols
rules.description: Alert on when legacy authentication has been used on an account
rules.author: Yochana Henderson, '@Yochana-H'

rules.title: Login to Disabled Account
rules.description: Detect failed attempts to sign in to disabled accounts.
rules.author: AlertIQ

rules.title: Multifactor Authentication Denied
rules.description: User has indicated they haven't instigated the MFA prompt and could indicate an attacker has the password for the account.
rules.author: AlertIQ

rules.title: Multifactor Authentication Interrupted
rules.description: Identifies user login with multifactor authentication failures, which might be an indication an attacker has the password for the account but can't pass the MFA challenge.
rules.author: AlertIQ

rules.title: Azure Unusual Authentication Interruption
rules.description: Detects when there is a interruption in the authentication process.

rules.title: Users Authenticating To Other Azure AD Tenants

Detect access has been blocked by Conditional Access policies.
The access policy does not allow token issuance which might be sights≈ of unauthorizeed login to valid accounts.

Detects when an access policy that is applied to a GCP cloud resource is deleted.
An adversary would be able to remove access policies to gain access to a GCP cloud resource.

Identifies when an admission controller is executed in GCP Kubernetes.

The behavior of this admission controller is determined by an admission webhook (MutatingAdmissionWebhook or ValidatingAd
rules.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

rules.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

Detects when an access level is changed for a Google workspace application.
An access level is part of BeyondCorp Enterprise which is Google Workspace's way of enforcing Zero Trust model.
An adversary would be able to remove access levels to gain easier access to Google workspace resources.

Detects instances where an email, identified as malicious or suspicious by the Microsoft Defender for Office 365 (formerly ATP) engine, was delivered to a user's Inbox or Junk folder.

This is especially relevant for users who use another account to manage resources, since these accounts are often not t

rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: PUA - System Informer Driver Load
rules.description: Detects driver load of the System Informer tool
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Driver Load From A Temporary Directory
rules.description: Detects a driver load from a temporary directory
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Vulnerable Driver Load By Name
rules.description: Detects the load of known vulnerable drivers via the file name of the drivers.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Vulnerable HackSys Extreme Vulnerable Driver Load
rules.description: Detects the load of HackSys Extreme Vulnerable Driver which is an intentionally vulnerable Windows driver developed for security enthusiasts to learn and polish their exploitation skills at Kernel level and often abused by threat actors
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Vulnerable WinRing0 Driver Load
rules.description: Detects the load of a signed WinRing0 driver often used by threat actors, crypto miners (XMRIG) or malware for privilege escalation
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: WinDivert Driver Load
rules.description: Detects the load of the Windiver driver, a powerful user-mode capture/sniffing/modification/blocking/re-injection package for Windows
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Credential Manager Access By Uncommon Applications
rules.description:
Detects suspicious processes based on name and location that access the windows credential manager and vault.
Which can be a sign of credential stealing. Example case would be usage of mimikatz "dpapi::cred" function
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Access To Windows Credential History File By Uncommon Applications
rules.description:
Detects file access requests to the Windows Credential History File by an uncommon application.
This can be a sign of credential stealing. Example case would be usage of mimikatz "dpapi::credhist" function
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Access To Crypto Currency Wallets By Uncommon Applications
rules.description:
Detects file access requests to crypto currency files by uncommon processes.
Could indicate potential attempt of crypto currency wallet stealing.
rules.author: X__Junior (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Access To Windows DPAPI Master Keys By Uncommon Applications
rules.description:
Detects file access requests to the the Windows Data Protection API Master keys by an uncommon application.
This can be a sign of credential stealing. Example case would be usage of mimikatz "dpapi::masterkey" function
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Access To Potentially Sensitive Sysvol Files By Uncommon Applications
rules.description: Detects file access requests to potentially sensitive files hosted on the Windows Sysvol share.
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Suspicious File Access to Browser Credential Storage
rules.description:
Detects file access to browser credential storage paths by non-browser processes, which may indicate credential access attempts.
Adversaries may attempt to access browser credential storage to extract sensitive information such as usernames and passwords or cookies.
This behavior is often commonly o
rules.author: frack113, X__Junior (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems), Parth-FourCore

rules.title: Microsoft Teams Sensitive File Access By Uncommon Applications
rules.description: Detects file access attempts to sensitive Microsoft teams files (leveldb, cookies) by an uncommon process.
rules.author: @SerkinValery

rules.title: Unusual File Modification by dns.exe
rules.description: Detects an unexpected file being modified by dns.exe which my indicate activity related to remote code execution or other forms of exploitation as seen in CVE-2020-1350 (SigRed)
rules.author: Tim Rauch (Nextron Systems), Elastic (idea)

rules.title: Backup Files Deleted
rules.description: Detects deletion of files with extensions often used for backup files. Adversaries may delete or remove built-in operating system data and turn off services designed to aid in the recovery of a corrupted system to prevent recovery.
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: EventLog EVTX File Deleted
rules.description: Detects the deletion of the event log files which may indicate an attempt to destroy forensic evidence
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Exchange PowerShell Cmdlet History Deleted
rules.description: Detects the deletion of the Exchange PowerShell cmdlet History logs which may indicate an attempt to destroy forensic evidence
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: IIS WebServer Access Logs Deleted
rules.description: Detects the deletion of IIS WebServer access logs which may indicate an attempt to destroy forensic evidence
rules.author: Tim Rauch (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Process Deletion of Its Own Executable
rules.description: Detects the deletion of a process's executable by itself. This is usually not possible without workarounds and may be used by malware to hide its traces.
rules.author: Max Altgelt (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: PowerShell Console History Logs Deleted
rules.description: Detects the deletion of the PowerShell console History logs which may indicate an attempt to destroy forensic evidence
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Prefetch File Deleted
rules.description: Detects the deletion of a prefetch file which may indicate an attempt to destroy forensic evidence
rules.author: Cedric MAURUGEON

rules.title: TeamViewer Log File Deleted
rules.description: Detects the deletion of the TeamViewer log files which may indicate an attempt to destroy forensic evidence
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Tomcat WebServer Logs Deleted
rules.description: Detects the deletion of tomcat WebServer logs which may indicate an attempt to destroy forensic evidence
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: File Deleted Via Sysinternals SDelete
rules.description: Detects the deletion of files by the Sysinternals SDelete utility. It looks for the common name pattern used to rename files.
rules.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)

rules.title: Unusual File Deletion by Dns.exe
rules.description: Detects an unexpected file being deleted by dns.exe which my indicate activity related to remote code execution or other forms of exploitation as seen in CVE-2020-1350 (SigRed)
rules.author: Tim Rauch (Nextron Systems), Elastic (idea)

rules.title: ADS Zone.Identifier Deleted By Uncommon Application
rules.description: Detects the deletion of the "Zone.Identifier" ADS by an uncommon process. Attackers can leverage this in order to bypass security restrictions that make use of the ADS such as Microsoft Office apps.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: ADSI-Cache File Creation By Uncommon Tool
rules.description: Detects the creation of an "Active Directory Schema Cache File" (.sch) file by an uncommon tool.
rules.author: xknow @xknow_infosec, Tim Shelton

rules.title: Advanced IP Scanner - File Event
rules.description: Detects the use of Advanced IP Scanner. Seems to be a popular tool for ransomware groups.
rules.author: @ROxPinTeddy

rules.title: Anydesk Temporary Artefact
rules.description:
An adversary may use legitimate desktop support and remote access software, such as Team Viewer, Go2Assist, LogMein, AmmyyAdmin, etc, to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks.
These services are commonly used as legitimate technical support software,
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Suspicious Binary Writes Via AnyDesk
rules.description:
Detects AnyDesk writing binary files to disk other than "gcapi.dll".
According to RedCanary research it is highly abnormal for AnyDesk to write executable files to disk besides gcapi.dll,
which is a legitimate DLL that is part of the Google Chrome web browser used to interact with the Google Cloud A
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious File Created by ArcSOC.exe
rules.description:
Detects instances where the ArcGIS Server process ArcSOC.exe, which hosts REST services running on an ArcGIS
server, creates a file with suspicious file type, indicating that it may be an executable, script file,
or otherwise unusual.
rules.author: Micah Babinski

rules.title: Assembly DLL Creation Via AspNetCompiler
rules.description: Detects the creation of new DLL assembly files by "aspnet_compiler.exe", which could be a sign of "aspnet_compiler" abuse to proxy execution through a build provider.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: BloodHound Collection Files
rules.description: Detects default file names outputted by the BloodHound collection tool SharpHound
rules.author: C.J. May

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious File Creation by OpenEDR's ITSMService
rules.description:
Detects the creation of potentially suspicious files by OpenEDR's ITSMService process.
The ITSMService is responsible for remote management operations and can create files on the system through the Process Explorer or file management features.
While legitimate for IT operations, creation of executab
rules.author: @kostastsale

rules.title: EVTX Created In Uncommon Location
rules.description:
Detects the creation of new files with the ".evtx" extension in non-common or non-standard location.
This could indicate tampering with default EVTX locations in order to evade security controls or simply exfiltration of event log to search for sensitive information within.
Note that backup software
rules.author: D3F7A5105

rules.title: Creation Of Non-Existent System DLL
rules.description:
Detects creation of specific system DLL files that are  usually not present on the system (or at least not in system directories) but may be loaded by legitimate processes.
Phantom DLL hijacking involves placing malicious DLLs with names of non-existent system binaries in locations where legitimate
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), fornotes

rules.title: Suspicious Deno File Written from Remote Source
rules.description:
Detects Deno writing a file from a direct HTTP(s) call and writing to the appdata folder or bringing it's own malicious DLL.
This behavior may indicate an attempt to execute remotely hosted, potentially malicious files through deno.
rules.author: Josh Nickels, Michael Taggart

rules.title: New Custom Shim Database Created
rules.description:
Adversaries may establish persistence and/or elevate privileges by executing malicious content triggered by application shims.
The Microsoft Windows Application Compatibility Infrastructure/Framework (Application Shim) was created to allow for backward compatibility of software as the operating syst
rules.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Screensaver Binary File Creation
rules.description:
Adversaries may establish persistence by executing malicious content triggered by user inactivity.
Screensavers are programs that execute after a configurable time of user inactivity and consist of Portable Executable (PE) files with a .scr file extension
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Files With System DLL Name In Unsuspected Locations
rules.description:
Detects the creation of a file with the ".dll" extension that has the name of a System DLL in uncommon or unsuspected locations. (Outisde of "System32", "SysWOW64", etc.).
It is highly recommended to perform an initial baseline before using this rule in production.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Files With System Process Name In Unsuspected Locations
rules.description:
Detects the creation of an executable with a system process name in folders other than the system ones (System32, SysWOW64, etc.).
It is highly recommended to perform an initial baseline before using this rule in production.
rules.author: Sander Wiebing, Tim Shelton, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Creation Exe for Service with Unquoted Path
rules.description:
Adversaries may execute their own malicious payloads by hijacking vulnerable file path references.
Adversaries can take advantage of paths that lack surrounding quotations by placing an executable in a higher level directory within the path, so that Windows will choose the adversary's executable to
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Cred Dump Tools Dropped Files
rules.description: Files with well-known filenames (parts of credential dump software or files produced by them) creation
rules.author: Teymur Kheirkhabarov, oscd.community

rules.title: WScript or CScript Dropper - File
rules.description: Detects a file ending in jse, vbe, js, vba, vbs, wsf, wsh written by cscript.exe or wscript.exe
rules.author: Tim Shelton

rules.title: CSExec Service File Creation
rules.description: Detects default CSExec service filename which indicates CSExec service installation and execution
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Dynamic CSharp Compile Artefact
rules.description:
When C# is compiled dynamically, a .cmdline file will be created as a part of the process.
Certain processes are not typically observed compiling C# code, but can do so without touching disk.
This can be used to unpack a payload for execution
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Potential DCOM InternetExplorer.Application DLL Hijack
rules.description: Detects potential DLL hijack of "iertutil.dll" found in the DCOM InternetExplorer.Application Class over the network
rules.author: Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g, Open Threat Research (OTR), wagga

rules.title: Desktop.INI Created by Uncommon Process
rules.description: Detects unusual processes accessing desktop.ini, which can be leveraged to alter how Explorer displays a folder's content (i.e. renaming files) without changing them on disk.
rules.author: Maxime Thiebaut (@0xThiebaut), Tim Shelton (HAWK.IO)

rules.title: DLL Search Order Hijackig Via Additional Space in Path
rules.description:
Detects when an attacker create a similar folder structure to windows system folders such as (Windows, Program Files...)
but with a space in order to trick DLL load search order and perform a "DLL Search Order Hijacking" attack
rules.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious DMP/HDMP File Creation
rules.description: Detects the creation of a file with the ".dmp"/".hdmp" extension by a shell or scripting application such as "cmd", "powershell", etc. Often created by software during a crash. Memory dumps can sometimes contain sensitive information such as credentials. It's best to determine the source of the cras
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential Persistence Attempt Via ErrorHandler.Cmd
rules.description:
Detects creation of a file named "ErrorHandler.cmd" in the "C:\WINDOWS\Setup\Scripts\" directory which could be used as a method of persistence
The content of C:\WINDOWS\Setup\Scripts\ErrorHandler.cmd is read whenever some tools under C:\WINDOWS\System32\oobe\ (e.g. Setup.exe) fail to run for any re
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious ASPX File Drop by Exchange
rules.description: Detects suspicious file type dropped by an Exchange component in IIS into a suspicious folder
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), MSTI (query, idea)

rules.title: Suspicious File Drop by Exchange
rules.description: Detects suspicious file type dropped by an Exchange component in IIS
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: GoToAssist Temporary Installation Artefact
rules.description:
An adversary may use legitimate desktop support and remote access software, such as Team Viewer, Go2Assist, LogMein, AmmyyAdmin, etc, to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks.
These services are commonly used as legitimate technical support software,
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Uncommon File Created by Notepad++ Updater Gup.EXE
rules.description:
Detects when the Notepad++ updater (gup.exe) creates files in suspicious or uncommon locations.
This could indicate potential exploitation of the updater component to deliver unwanted malware or unwarranted files.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: HackTool - CrackMapExec File Indicators
rules.description: Detects file creation events with filename patterns used by CrackMapExec.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: HackTool - Dumpert Process Dumper Default File
rules.description: Detects the creation of the default dump file used by Outflank Dumpert tool. A process dumper, which dumps the lsass process memory
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: HackTool - Typical HiveNightmare SAM File Export
rules.description: Detects files written by the different tools that exploit HiveNightmare
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: HackTool - Inveigh Execution Artefacts
rules.description: Detects the presence and execution of Inveigh via dropped artefacts
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: HackTool - RemoteKrbRelay SMB Relay Secrets Dump Module Indicators
rules.description: Detects the creation of file with specific names used by RemoteKrbRelay SMB Relay attack module.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: HackTool - Mimikatz Kirbi File Creation
rules.description: Detects the creation of files created by mimikatz such as ".kirbi", "mimilsa.log", etc.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), David ANDRE

rules.title: HackTool - NetExec File Indicators
rules.description:
Detects file creation events indicating NetExec (nxc.exe) execution on the local machine.
NetExec is a PyInstaller-bundled binary that extracts its embedded data files to a "_MEI<random>" directory
under the Temp folder upon execution. Files dropped under the "\nxc\" sub-directory of that
extraction
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: HackTool - NPPSpy Hacktool Usage
rules.description: Detects the use of NPPSpy hacktool that stores cleartext passwords of users that logged in to a local file
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: HackTool - Powerup Write Hijack DLL
rules.description:
Powerup tool's Write Hijack DLL exploits DLL hijacking for privilege escalation.
In it's default mode, it builds a self deleting .bat file which executes malicious command.
The detection rule relies on creation of the malicious bat file (debug.bat by default).
rules.author: Subhash Popuri (@pbssubhash)

rules.title: HackTool - QuarksPwDump Dump File
rules.description: Detects a dump file written by QuarksPwDump password dumper
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: HackTool - Potential Remote Credential Dumping Activity Via CrackMapExec Or Impacket-Secretsdump
rules.description: Detects default filenames output from the execution of CrackMapExec and Impacket-secretsdump against an endpoint.
rules.author: SecurityAura

rules.title: HackTool - SafetyKatz Dump Indicator
rules.description: Detects default lsass dump filename generated by SafetyKatz.
rules.author: Markus Neis

rules.title: HackTool - Impacket File Indicators
rules.description: Detects file creation events with filename patterns used by Impacket.
rules.author: The DFIR Report, IrishDeath

rules.title: Potential Initial Access via DLL Search Order Hijacking
rules.description: Detects attempts to create a DLL file to a known desktop application dependencies folder such as Slack, Teams or OneDrive and by an unusual process. This may indicate an attempt to load a malicious module via DLL search order hijacking.
rules.author: Tim Rauch (rule), Elastic (idea)

rules.title: Installation of TeamViewer Desktop
rules.description: TeamViewer_Desktop.exe is create during install
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Malicious DLL File Dropped in the Teams or OneDrive Folder
rules.description:
Detects creation of a malicious DLL file in the location where the OneDrive or Team applications
Upon execution of the Teams or OneDrive application, the dropped malicious DLL file ("iphlpapi.dll") is sideloaded
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: ISO File Created Within Temp Folders
rules.description: Detects the creation of a ISO file in the Outlook temp folder or in the Appdata temp folder. Typical of Qakbot TTP from end-July 2022.
rules.author: @sam0x90

rules.title: ISO or Image Mount Indicator in Recent Files
rules.description:
Detects the creation of recent element file that points to an .ISO, .IMG, .VHD or .VHDX file as often used in phishing attacks.
This can be a false positive on server systems but on workstations users should rarely mount .iso or .img files.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: GatherNetworkInfo.VBS Reconnaissance Script Output
rules.description: Detects creation of files which are the results of executing the built-in reconnaissance script "C:\Windows\System32\gatherNetworkInfo.vbs".
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: LSASS Process Memory Dump Files
rules.description: Detects creation of files with names used by different memory dumping tools to create a memory dump of the LSASS process memory, which contains user credentials.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: LSASS Process Dump Artefact In CrashDumps Folder
rules.description: Detects the presence of an LSASS dump file in the "CrashDumps" folder. This could be a sign of LSASS credential dumping. Techniques such as the LSASS Shtinkering have been seen abusing the Windows Error Reporting to dump said process.
rules.author: @pbssubhash

rules.title: WerFault LSASS Process Memory Dump
rules.description: Detects WerFault creating a dump file with a name that indicates that the dump file could be an LSASS process memory, which contains user credentials
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Adwind RAT / JRAT File Artifact
rules.description: Detects javaw.exe in AppData folder as used by Adwind / JRAT
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Tom Ueltschi, Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community

rules.title: Octopus Scanner Malware
rules.description: Detects Octopus Scanner Malware.
rules.author: NVISO

rules.title: File Creation In Suspicious Directory By Msdt.EXE
rules.description: Detects msdt.exe creating files in suspicious directories which could be a sign of exploitation of either Follina or Dogwalk vulnerabilities
rules.author: Vadim Varganov, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Uncommon File Creation By Mysql Daemon Process
rules.description:
Detects the creation of files with scripting or executable extensions by Mysql daemon.
Which could be an indicator of "User Defined Functions" abuse to download malware.
rules.author: Joseph Kamau

rules.title: Suspicious DotNET CLR Usage Log Artifact
rules.description: Detects the creation of Usage Log files by the CLR (clr.dll). These files are named after the executing process once the assembly is finished executing for the first time in the (user) session context.
rules.author: frack113, omkar72, oscd.community, Wojciech Lesicki

rules.title: Suspicious File Creation In Uncommon AppData Folder
rules.description: Detects the creation of suspicious files and folders inside the user's AppData folder but not inside any of the common and well known directories (Local, Romaing, LocalLow). This method could be used as a method to bypass detection who exclude the AppData folder in fear of FPs
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: SCR File Write Event
rules.description: Detects the creation of screensaver files (.scr) outside of system folders. Attackers may execute an application as an ".SCR" file using "rundll32.exe desk.cpl,InstallScreenSaver" for example.
rules.author: Christopher Peacock @securepeacock, SCYTHE @scythe_io

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via Notepad++ Plugins
rules.description: Detects creation of new ".dll" files inside the plugins directory of a notepad++ installation by a process other than "gup.exe". Which could indicates possible persistence
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: NTDS.DIT Created
rules.description: Detects creation of a file named "ntds.dit" (Active Directory Database)
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: NTDS.DIT Creation By Uncommon Parent Process
rules.description: Detects creation of a file named "ntds.dit" (Active Directory Database) by an uncommon parent process or directory
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: NTDS.DIT Creation By Uncommon Process
rules.description: Detects creation of a file named "ntds.dit" (Active Directory Database) by an uncommon process or a process located in a suspicious directory
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: NTDS Exfiltration Filename Patterns
rules.description: Detects creation of files with specific name patterns seen used in various tools that export the NTDS.DIT for exfiltration.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via Microsoft Office Add-In
rules.description: Detects potential persistence activity via startup add-ins that load when Microsoft Office starts (.wll/.xll are simply .dll fit for Word or Excel).
rules.author: NVISO

rules.title: Office Macro File Creation
rules.description: Detects the creation of a new office macro files on the systems
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Office Macro File Download
rules.description:
Detects the creation of a new office macro files on the system via an application (browser, mail client).
This can help identify potential malicious activity, such as the download of macro-enabled documents that could be used for exploitation.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Office Macro File Creation From Suspicious Process
rules.description: Detects the creation of a office macro file from a a suspicious process
rules.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: OneNote Attachment File Dropped In Suspicious Location
rules.description: Detects creation of files with the ".one"/".onepkg" extension in suspicious or uncommon locations. This could be a sign of attackers abusing OneNote attachments
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious File Created Via OneNote Application
rules.description: Detects suspicious files created via the OneNote application. This could indicate a potential malicious ".one"/".onepkg" file was executed as seen being used in malware activity in the wild
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: New Outlook Macro Created
rules.description: Detects the creation of a macro file for Outlook.
rules.author: @ScoubiMtl

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via Outlook Form
rules.description: Detects the creation of a new Outlook form which can contain malicious code
rules.author: Tobias Michalski (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious File Created in Outlook Temporary Directory
rules.description:
Detects the creation of files with suspicious file extensions in the temporary directory that Outlook uses when opening attachments.
This can be used to detect spear-phishing campaigns that use suspicious files as attachments, which may contain malicious code.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Outlook Macro Created
rules.description: Detects the creation of a macro file for Outlook.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Publisher Attachment File Dropped In Suspicious Location
rules.description: Detects creation of files with the ".pub" extension in suspicious or uncommon locations. This could be a sign of attackers abusing Publisher documents
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via Microsoft Office Startup Folder
rules.description: Detects creation of Microsoft Office files inside of one of the default startup folders in order to achieve persistence.
rules.author: Max Altgelt (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: File With Uncommon Extension Created By An Office Application
rules.description: Detects the creation of files with an executable or script extension by an Office application.
rules.author: Vadim Khrykov (ThreatIntel), Cyb3rEng (Rule), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Uncommon File Created In Office Startup Folder
rules.description: Detects the creation of a file with an uncommon extension in an Office application startup folder
rules.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: PCRE.NET Package Temp Files
rules.description: Detects processes creating temp files related to PCRE.NET package
rules.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)

rules.title: Suspicious File Created In PerfLogs
rules.description: Detects suspicious file based on their extension being created in "C:\PerfLogs\". Note that this directory mostly contains ".etl" files
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential Binary Or Script Dropper Via PowerShell
rules.description: Detects PowerShell creating a binary executable or a script file.
rules.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: PowerShell Script Dropped Via PowerShell.EXE
rules.description: Detects PowerShell creating a PowerShell file (.ps1). While often times this behavior is benign, sometimes it can be a sign of a dropper script trying to achieve persistence.
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Malicious PowerShell Scripts - FileCreation
rules.description: Detects the creation of known offensive powershell scripts used for exploitation
rules.author: Markus Neis, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Mustafa Kaan Demir, Georg Lauenstein

rules.title: PowerShell Module File Created
rules.description: Detects the creation of a new PowerShell module ".psm1", ".psd1", ".dll", ".ps1", etc.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential Suspicious PowerShell Module File Created
rules.description: Detects the creation of a new PowerShell module in the first folder of the module directory structure "\WindowsPowerShell\Modules\malware\malware.psm1". This is somewhat an uncommon practice as legitimate modules often includes a version folder.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: PowerShell Module File Created By Non-PowerShell Process

Detects DLLs loading from a spoofed Windows directory path with an extra space (e.g "C:\Windows \System32") which can bypass Windows trusted path verification.

rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
