Detects execution of the builtin "del"/"erase" commands in order to delete files.
Adversaries may delete files left behind by the actions of their intrusion activity.
Malware, tools, or other non-native files dropped or created on a system by an adversary may leave traces to indicate to what was don
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Greedy File Deletion Using Del
rules.description: Detects execution of the "del" builtin command to remove files using greedy/wildcard expression. This is often used by malware to delete content of folders that perhaps contains the initial malware infection or to delete evidence.
rules.author: frack113 , X__Junior (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: File And SubFolder Enumeration Via Dir Command
rules.description: Detects usage of the "dir" command part of Windows CMD with the "/S" command line flag in order to enumerate files in a specified directory and all subdirectories.
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Potential Dosfuscation Activity
rules.description: Detects possible payload obfuscation via the commandline
rules.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Command Line Execution with Suspicious URL and AppData Strings
rules.description: Detects a suspicious command line execution that includes an URL and AppData string in the command line parameters as used by several droppers (js/vbs > powershell)
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community

rules.title: Cmd Launched with Hidden Start Flags to Suspicious Targets
rules.description:
Detects cmd.exe executing commands with the "start" utility using "/b" (no window) or "/min" (minimized) flags.
To reduce false positives from standard background tasks, detection is restricted to scenarios where the target is a known script extension or located in suspicious temporary/public direct
rules.author: Vladan Sekulic, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential Privilege Escalation Using Symlink Between Osk and Cmd
rules.description: Detects the creation of a symbolic link between "cmd.exe" and the accessibility on-screen keyboard binary (osk.exe) using "mklink". This technique provides an elevated command prompt to the user from the login screen without the need to log in.
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: VolumeShadowCopy Symlink Creation Via Mklink
rules.description: Shadow Copies storage symbolic link creation using operating systems utilities
rules.author: Teymur Kheirkhabarov, oscd.community

rules.title: Suspicious File Execution From Internet Hosted WebDav Share
rules.description: Detects the execution of the "net use" command to mount a WebDAV server and then immediately execute some content in it. As seen being used in malicious LNK files
rules.author: pH-T (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Cmd.EXE Missing Space Characters Execution Anomaly
rules.description:
Detects Windows command lines that miss a space before or after the /c flag when running a command using the cmd.exe.
This could be a sign of obfuscation of a fat finger problem (typo by the developer).
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: NtdllPipe Like Activity Execution
rules.description: Detects command that type the content of ntdll.dll to a different file or a pipe in order to evade AV / EDR detection. As seen being used in the POC NtdllPipe
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential CommandLine Path Traversal Via Cmd.EXE
rules.description: Detects potential path traversal attempt via cmd.exe. Could indicate possible command/argument confusion/hijacking
rules.author: xknow @xknow_infosec, Tim Shelton

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Ping/Copy Command Combination
rules.description: Detects uncommon and potentially suspicious one-liner command containing both "ping" and "copy" at the same time, which is usually used by malware.
rules.author: X__Junior (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Ping/Del Command Combination
rules.description: Detects a method often used by ransomware. Which combines the "ping" to wait a couple of seconds and then "del" to delete the file in question. Its used to hide the file responsible for the initial infection for example
rules.author: Ilya Krestinichev

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious CMD Shell Output Redirect
rules.description:
Detects inline Windows shell commands redirecting output via the ">" symbol to a suspicious location.
This technique is sometimes used by malicious actors in order to redirect the output of reconnaissance commands such as "hostname" and "dir" to files for future exfiltration.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Directory Removal Via Rmdir
rules.description:
Detects execution of the builtin "rmdir" command in order to delete directories.
Adversaries may delete files left behind by the actions of their intrusion activity.
Malware, tools, or other non-native files dropped or created on a system by an adversary may leave traces to indicate to what was done
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Copy From VolumeShadowCopy Via Cmd.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of the builtin "copy" command that targets a shadow copy (sometimes used to copy registry hives that are in use)
rules.author: Max Altgelt (Nextron Systems), Tobias Michalski (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Read Contents From Stdin Via Cmd.EXE
rules.description: Detect the use of "<" to read and potentially execute a file via cmd.exe
rules.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Persistence Via Sticky Key Backdoor
rules.description:
By replacing the sticky keys executable with the local admins CMD executable, an attacker is able to access a privileged windows console session without authenticating to the system.
When the sticky keys are "activated" the privilleged shell is launched.
rules.author: Sreeman

rules.title: Sticky Key Like Backdoor Execution
rules.description: Detects the usage and installation of a backdoor that uses an option to register a malicious debugger for built-in tools that are accessible in the login screen
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), @twjackomo, Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community

rules.title: Potential Download/Upload Activity Using Type Command
rules.description: Detects usage of the "type" command to download/upload data from WebDAV server
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Unusual Parent Process For Cmd.EXE
rules.description: Detects suspicious parent process for cmd.exe
rules.author: Tim Rauch, Elastic (idea)

rules.title: CMSTP Execution Process Creation
rules.description: Detects various indicators of Microsoft Connection Manager Profile Installer execution
rules.author: Nik Seetharaman

rules.title: OpenEDR Spawning Command Shell
rules.description:
Detects the OpenEDR ssh-shellhost.exe spawning a command shell (cmd.exe) or PowerShell with PTY (pseudo-terminal) capabilities.
This may indicate remote command execution through OpenEDR's remote management features, which could be legitimate administrative activity or potential abuse of the remote
rules.author: @kostastsale

rules.title: Arbitrary File Download Via ConfigSecurityPolicy.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the execution of "ConfigSecurityPolicy.EXE", a binary part of Windows Defender used to manage settings in Windows Defender.
Users can configure different pilot collections for each of the co-management workloads.
It can be abused by attackers in order to upload or download files.
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Powershell Executed From Headless ConHost Process
rules.description:
Detects the use of powershell commands from headless ConHost window.
The "--headless" flag hides the windows from the user upon execution.
rules.author: Matt Anderson (Huntress)

rules.title: Suspicious High IntegrityLevel Conhost Legacy Option
rules.description: ForceV1 asks for information directly from the kernel space. Conhost connects to the console application. High IntegrityLevel means the process is running with elevated privileges, such as an Administrator context.
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Conhost.exe CommandLine Path Traversal
rules.description: detects the usage of path traversal in conhost.exe indicating possible command/argument confusion/hijacking
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Uncommon Child Process Of Conhost.EXE
rules.description: Detects uncommon "conhost" child processes. This could be a sign of "conhost" usage as a LOLBIN or potential process injection activity.
rules.author: omkar72

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Child Processes Spawned by ConHost
rules.description: Detects suspicious child processes related to Windows Shell utilities spawned by `conhost.exe`, which could indicate malicious activity using trusted system components.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Conhost Spawned By Uncommon Parent Process
rules.description: Detects when the Console Window Host (conhost.exe) process is spawned by an uncommon parent process, which could be indicative of potential code injection activity.
rules.author: Tim Rauch, Elastic (idea)

rules.title: Control Panel Items
rules.description: Detects the malicious use of a control panel item
rules.author: Kyaw Min Thein, Furkan Caliskan (@caliskanfurkan_)

rules.title: CreateDump Process Dump
rules.description: Detects uses of the createdump.exe LOLOBIN utility to dump process memory
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: New DMSA Service Account Created in Specific OUs
rules.description:
Detects the creation of a dMSASvc account using the New-ADServiceAccount cmdlet in certain OUs.
The fact that the Cmdlet is used to create a dMSASvc account in a specific OU is highly suspicious.
It is a pattern trying to exploit the BadSuccessor privilege escalation vulnerability in Windows Server
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Windows Credential Guard Registry Tampering Via CommandLine
rules.description:
Detects attempts to add, modify, or delete Windows Credential Guard related registry keys or values via command line tools such as Reg.exe or PowerShell.
Credential Guard uses virtualization-based security to isolate secrets so that only privileged system software can access them.
Adversaries may di
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Dynamic .NET Compilation Via Csc.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of "csc.exe" to compile .NET code. Attackers often leverage this to compile code on the fly and use it in other stages.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), X__Junior (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Csc.EXE Execution Form Potentially Suspicious Parent
rules.description: Detects a potentially suspicious parent of "csc.exe", which could be a sign of payload delivery.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), X__Junior (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Csi.exe Usage
rules.description: Csi.exe is a signed binary from Microsoft that comes with Visual Studio and provides C# interactive capabilities. It can be used to run C# code from a file passed as a parameter in command line. Early version of this utility provided with Microsoft “Roslyn” Community Technology Preview was named 'rc
rules.author: Konstantin Grishchenko, oscd.community

rules.title: Suspicious Use of CSharp Interactive Console
rules.description: Detects the execution of CSharp interactive console by PowerShell
rules.author: Michael R. (@nahamike01)

rules.title: Active Directory Structure Export Via Csvde.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of "csvde.exe" in order to export organizational Active Directory structure.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential Cookies Session Hijacking
rules.description: Detects execution of "curl.exe" with the "-c" flag in order to save cookie data.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Curl Web Request With Potential Custom User-Agent
rules.description: Detects execution of "curl.exe" with a potential custom "User-Agent". Attackers can leverage this to download or exfiltrate data via "curl" to a domain that only accept specific "User-Agent" strings
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: File Download From IP URL Via Curl.EXE
rules.description: Detects file downloads directly from IP address URL using curl.exe
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious File Download From IP Via Curl.EXE
rules.description: Detects potentially suspicious file downloads directly from IP addresses using curl.exe
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious File Download From File Sharing Domain Via Curl.EXE
rules.description: Detects potentially suspicious file download from file sharing domains using curl.exe
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Insecure Transfer Via Curl.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of "curl.exe" with the "--insecure" flag.
rules.author: X__Junior (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Insecure Proxy/DOH Transfer Via Curl.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of "curl.exe" with the "insecure" flag over proxy or DOH.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Local File Read Using Curl.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of "curl.exe" with the "file://" protocol handler in order to read local files.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Curl.EXE Download
rules.description: Detects a suspicious curl process start on Windows and outputs the requested document to a local file
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious CustomShellHost Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of CustomShellHost.exe where the child isn't located in 'C:\Windows\explorer.exe'. CustomShellHost is a known LOLBin that can be abused by attackers for defense evasion techniques.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: ManageEngine Endpoint Central Dctask64.EXE Potential Abuse
rules.description:
Detects the execution of "dctask64.exe", a signed binary by ZOHO Corporation part of ManageEngine Endpoint Central.
This binary can be abused for DLL injection, arbitrary command and process execution.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Uncommon Child Process Of Defaultpack.EXE
rules.description: Detects uncommon child processes of "DefaultPack.EXE" binary as a proxy to launch other programs
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: PowerShell Defender Threat Severity Default Action Set to 'Allow' or 'NoAction'
rules.description:
Detects the use of PowerShell to execute the 'Set-MpPreference' cmdlet to configure Windows Defender's threat severity default action to 'Allow' (value '6') or 'NoAction' (value '9').
This is a highly suspicious configuration change that effectively disables Defender's ability to automatically mitig
rules.author: Matt Anderson (Huntress)

rules.title: Windows Defender Context Menu Removed
rules.description:
Detects the use of reg.exe or PowerShell to delete the Windows Defender context menu handler registry keys.
This action removes the "Scan with Microsoft Defender" option from the right-click menu for files, directories, and drives.
Attackers may use this technique to hinder manual, on-demand scans a
rules.author: Matt Anderson (Huntress)

rules.title: Remote File Download Via Desktopimgdownldr Utility
rules.description: Detects the desktopimgdownldr utility being used to download a remote file. An adversary may use desktopimgdownldr to download arbitrary files as an alternative to certutil.
rules.author: Tim Rauch, Elastic (idea)

rules.title: Suspicious Desktopimgdownldr Command
rules.description: Detects a suspicious Microsoft desktopimgdownldr execution with parameters used to download files from the Internet
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Devcon Execution Disabling VMware VMCI Device
rules.description:
Detects execution of devcon.exe with commands that disable the VMware Virtual Machine Communication Interface (VMCI) device.
This can be legitimate during VMware Tools troubleshooting or driver conflicts, but may also indicate malware attempting to hijack communication with the hardware via the VMCI
rules.author: Matt Anderson, Dray Agha, Anna Pham (Huntress)

rules.title: Potential DLL Sideloading Via DeviceEnroller.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the use of the PhoneDeepLink parameter to potentially sideload a DLL file that does not exist. This non-existent DLL file is named "ShellChromeAPI.dll".
Adversaries can drop their own renamed DLL and execute it via DeviceEnroller.exe using this parameter
rules.author: @gott_cyber

rules.title: DeviceCredentialDeployment Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of DeviceCredentialDeployment to hide a process from view.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Arbitrary MSI Download Via Devinit.EXE
rules.description: Detects a certain command line flag combination used by "devinit.exe", which can be abused as a LOLBIN to download arbitrary MSI packages on a Windows system
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Child Process Of ClickOnce Application
rules.description: Detects potentially suspicious child processes of a ClickOnce deployment application
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: DirLister Execution
rules.description: Detect the usage of "DirLister.exe" a utility for quickly listing folder or drive contents. It was seen used by BlackCat ransomware to create a list of accessible directories and files.
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: System Information Discovery via Registry Queries
rules.description: Detects attempts to query system information directly from the Windows Registry.
rules.author: lazarg

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Child Process Of DiskShadow.EXE
rules.description: Detects potentially suspicious child processes of "Diskshadow.exe". This could be an attempt to bypass parent/child relationship detection or application whitelisting rules.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Diskshadow Script Mode - Uncommon Script Extension Execution
rules.description:
Detects execution of "Diskshadow.exe" in script mode to execute an script with a potentially uncommon extension.
Initial baselining of the allowed extension list is required.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Diskshadow Script Mode - Execution From Potential Suspicious Location
rules.description: Detects execution of "Diskshadow.exe" in script mode using the "/s" flag where the script is located in a potentially suspicious location.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: PowerShell Web Access Feature Enabled Via DISM
rules.description: Detects the use of DISM to enable the PowerShell Web Access feature, which could be used for remote access and potential abuse
rules.author: Michael Haag

rules.title: Dism Remove Online Package
rules.description: Deployment Image Servicing and Management tool. DISM is used to enumerate, install, uninstall, configure, and update features and packages in Windows images
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Dllhost.EXE Execution Anomaly
rules.description: Detects a "dllhost" process spawning with no commandline arguments which is very rare to happen and could indicate process injection activity or malware mimicking similar system processes.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: DLL Sideloading by VMware Xfer Utility
rules.description: Detects execution of VMware Xfer utility (VMwareXferlogs.exe) from the non-default directory which may be an attempt to sideload arbitrary DLL
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential Discovery Activity Via Dnscmd.EXE
rules.description: Detects an attempt to leverage dnscmd.exe to enumerate the DNS zones of a domain. DNS zones used to host the DNS records for a particular domain.
rules.author: @gott_cyber

rules.title: New DNS ServerLevelPluginDll Installed Via Dnscmd.EXE
rules.description: Detects the installation of a DNS plugin DLL via ServerLevelPluginDll parameter in registry, which can be used to execute code in context of the DNS server (restart required)
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: DNS Exfiltration and Tunneling Tools Execution
rules.description: Well-known DNS Exfiltration tools execution
rules.author: Daniil Yugoslavskiy, oscd.community

rules.title: Unusual Child Process of dns.exe
rules.description: Detects an unexpected process spawning from dns.exe which may indicate activity related to remote code execution or other forms of exploitation as seen in CVE-2020-1350 (SigRed)
rules.author: Tim Rauch, Elastic (idea)

rules.title: Potential Application Whitelisting Bypass via Dnx.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the execution of Dnx.EXE. The Dnx utility allows for the execution of C# code.
Attackers might abuse this in order to bypass application whitelisting.
rules.author: Beyu Denis, oscd.community

rules.title: Process Memory Dump Via Dotnet-Dump
rules.description: Detects the execution of "dotnet-dump" with the "collect" flag. The execution could indicate potential process dumping of critical processes such as LSASS.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Arbitrary DLL or Csproj Code Execution Via Dotnet.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of arbitrary DLLs or unsigned code via a ".csproj" files via Dotnet.EXE.
rules.author: Beyu Denis, oscd.community

rules.title: Binary Proxy Execution Via Dotnet-Trace.EXE
rules.description: Detects commandline arguments for executing a child process via dotnet-trace.exe
rules.author: Jimmy Bayne (@bohops)

rules.title: Potential Recon Activity Using DriverQuery.EXE
rules.description: Detect usage of the "driverquery" utility to perform reconnaissance on installed drivers
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: DriverQuery.EXE Execution
rules.description: Detect usage of the "driverquery" utility. Which can be used to perform reconnaissance on installed drivers
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potentially Over Permissive Permissions Granted Using Dsacls.EXE
rules.description: Detects usage of Dsacls to grant over permissive permissions
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential Password Spraying Attempt Using Dsacls.EXE
rules.description: Detects possible password spraying attempts using Dsacls
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Domain Trust Discovery Via Dsquery
rules.description: Detects execution of "dsquery.exe" for domain trust discovery
rules.author: E.M. Anhaus, Tony Lambert, oscd.community, omkar72

rules.title: Suspicious Kernel Dump Using Dtrace
rules.description: Detects suspicious way to dump the kernel on Windows systems using dtrace.exe, which is available on Windows systems since Windows 10 19H1
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential Windows Defender AV Bypass Via Dump64.EXE Rename
rules.description:
Detects when a user is potentially trying to bypass the Windows Defender AV by renaming a tool to dump64.exe and placing it in the Visual Studio folder.
Currently the rule is covering only usage of procdump but other utilities can be added in order to increase coverage.
rules.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: DumpMinitool Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of "DumpMinitool.exe" a tool that allows the dump of process memory via the use of the "MiniDumpWriteDump"
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious DumpMinitool Execution
rules.description: Detects suspicious ways to use the "DumpMinitool.exe" binary
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: New Capture Session Launched Via DXCap.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of "DXCap.EXE" with the "-c" flag, which allows a user to launch any arbitrary binary or windows package through DXCap itself. This can be abused to potentially bypass application whitelisting.
rules.author: Beyu Denis, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Esentutl Gather Credentials
rules.description: Conti recommendation to its affiliates to use esentutl to access NTDS dumped file. Trickbot also uses this utilities to get MSEdge info via its module pwgrab.
rules.author: sam0x90

rules.title: Copying Sensitive Files with Credential Data
rules.description: Files with well-known filenames (sensitive files with credential data) copying
rules.author: Teymur Kheirkhabarov, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, oscd.community

rules.title: Esentutl Steals Browser Information
rules.description: One way Qbot steals sensitive information is by extracting browser data from Internet Explorer and Microsoft Edge by using the built-in utility esentutl.exe
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Event Viewer Child Process
rules.description: Detects uncommon or suspicious child processes of "eventvwr.exe" which might indicate a UAC bypass attempt
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Security Event Logging Disabled via MiniNt Registry Key - Process
rules.description:
Detects attempts to disable security event logging by adding the `MiniNt` registry key.
This key is used to disable the Windows Event Log service, which collects and stores event logs from the operating system and applications.
Adversaries may want to disable this service to prevent logging of secur
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Cabinet File Expansion
rules.description: Detects the expansion or decompression of cabinet files from potentially suspicious or uncommon locations, e.g. seen in Iranian MeteorExpress related attacks
rules.author: Bhabesh Raj, X__Junior (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Explorer Process Tree Break
rules.description:
Detects a command line process that uses explorer.exe to launch arbitrary commands or binaries,
which is similar to cmd.exe /c, only it breaks the process tree and makes its parent a new instance of explorer spawning from "svchost"
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), @gott_cyber

rules.title: File Explorer Folder Opened Using Explorer Folder Shortcut Via Shell
rules.description: Detects the initial execution of "cmd.exe" which spawns "explorer.exe" with the appropriate command line arguments for opening the "My Computer" folder.
rules.author: @Kostastsale

rules.title: Explorer NOUACCHECK Flag
rules.description: Detects suspicious starts of explorer.exe that use the /NOUACCHECK flag that allows to run all sub processes of that newly started explorer.exe without any UAC checks
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Remote File Download Via Findstr.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of "findstr" with specific flags and a remote share path. This specific set of CLI flags would allow "findstr" to download the content of the file located on the remote share as described in the LOLBAS entry.
rules.author: Furkan CALISKAN, @caliskanfurkan_, @oscd_initiative, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Findstr GPP Passwords
rules.description: Look for the encrypted cpassword value within Group Policy Preference files on the Domain Controller. This value can be decrypted with gpp-decrypt.
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Findstr Launching .lnk File
rules.description: Detects usage of findstr to identify and execute a lnk file as seen within the HHS redirect attack
rules.author: Trent Liffick

rules.title: LSASS Process Reconnaissance Via Findstr.EXE
rules.description: Detects findstring commands that include the keyword lsass, which indicates recon actviity for the LSASS process PID
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Permission Misconfiguration Reconnaissance Via Findstr.EXE
rules.description:
Detects usage of findstr with the "EVERYONE" or "BUILTIN" keywords.
This was seen being used in combination with "icacls" and other utilities to spot misconfigured files or folders permissions.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Recon Command Output Piped To Findstr.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the execution of a potential recon command where the results are piped to "findstr". This is meant to trigger on inline calls of "cmd.exe" via the "/c" or "/k" for example.
Attackers often time use this technique to extract specific information they require in their reconnaissance phase.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), frack113

rules.title: Security Tools Keyword Lookup Via Findstr.EXE
rules.description:
Detects execution of "findstr" to search for common names of security tools. Attackers often pipe the results of recon commands such as "tasklist" or "whoami" to "findstr" in order to filter out the results.
This detection focuses on the keywords that the attacker might use as a filter.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), frack113

rules.title: Insensitive Subfolder Search Via Findstr.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of findstr with the "s" and "i" flags for a "subfolder" and "insensitive" search respectively. Attackers sometimes leverage this built-in utility to search the system for interesting files or filter through results of commands.
rules.author: Furkan CALISKAN, @caliskanfurkan_, @oscd_initiative, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Sysmon Discovery Via Default Driver Altitude Using Findstr.EXE
rules.description: Detects usage of "findstr" with the argument "385201". Which could indicate potential discovery of an installed Sysinternals Sysmon service using the default driver altitude (even if the name is changed).
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Finger.EXE Execution
rules.description:
Detects execution of the "finger.exe" utility.
Finger.EXE or "TCPIP Finger Command" is an old utility that is still present on modern Windows installation. It Displays information about users on a specified remote computer (typically a UNIX computer) that is running the finger service or daemon.
Due
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), omkar72, oscd.community

rules.title: Filter Driver Unloaded Via Fltmc.EXE
rules.description: Detect filter driver unloading activity via fltmc.exe

rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

If not legitimately used in the enterprise environment, its presence may indicat

While it is a legitimate tool, intended for use in CI pipelines and security assessments,
It was observed in the Shai-Hulud malware campai

Threat actors can abuse this technique as a phishing vector to capture authentication credentials or other sensitive data.

rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Where Execution
rules.description:
Adversaries may enumerate browser bookmarks to learn more about compromised hosts.
Browser bookmarks may reveal personal information about users (ex: banking sites, interests, social media, etc.) as well as details about
internal network resources such as servers, tools/dashboards, or other related
rules.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Enumerate All Information With Whoami.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of "whoami.exe" with the "/all" flag
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Whoami.EXE Execution From Privileged Process
rules.description: Detects the execution of "whoami.exe" by privileged accounts that are often abused by threat actors
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Teymur Kheirkhabarov

rules.title: Group Membership Reconnaissance Via Whoami.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of whoami.exe with the /group command line flag to show group membership for the current user, account type, security identifiers (SID), and attributes.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Whoami.EXE Execution With Output Option
rules.description: Detects the execution of "whoami.exe" with the "/FO" flag to choose CSV as output format or with redirection options to export the results to a file for later use.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Whoami.EXE Execution Anomaly
rules.description: Detects the execution of whoami.exe with suspicious parent processes.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Security Privileges Enumeration Via Whoami.EXE
rules.description: Detects a whoami.exe executed with the /priv command line flag instructing the tool to show all current user privileges. This is often used after a privilege escalation attempt.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious WindowsTerminal Child Processes
rules.description: Detects suspicious children spawned via the Windows Terminal application which could be a sign of persistence via WindowsTerminal (see references section)
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Add New Download Source To Winget
rules.description: Detects usage of winget to add new additional download sources
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Add Insecure Download Source To Winget
rules.description:
Detects usage of winget to add a new insecure (http) download source.
Winget will not allow the addition of insecure sources, hence this could indicate potential suspicious activity (or typos)
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Add Potential Suspicious New Download Source To Winget
rules.description: Detects usage of winget to add new potentially suspicious download sources
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Install New Package Via Winget Local Manifest
rules.description:
Detects usage of winget to install applications via manifest file. Adversaries can abuse winget to download payloads remotely and execute them.
The manifest option enables you to install an application by passing in a YAML file directly to the client.
Winget can be used to download and install exe,
rules.author: Sreeman, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), frack113

rules.title: Winrar Compressing Dump Files
rules.description: Detects execution of WinRAR in order to compress a file with a ".dmp"/".dump" extension, which could be a step in a process of dump file exfiltration.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Child Process Of WinRAR.EXE
rules.description: Detects potentially suspicious child processes of WinRAR.exe.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: WinRAR Execution in Non-Standard Folder
rules.description: Detects a suspicious WinRAR execution in a folder which is not the default installation folder
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Tigzy

rules.title: AWL Bypass with Winrm.vbs and Malicious WsmPty.xsl/WsmTxt.xsl
rules.description: Detects execution of attacker-controlled WsmPty.xsl or WsmTxt.xsl via winrm.vbs and copied cscript.exe (can be renamed)
rules.author: Julia Fomina, oscd.community

rules.title: Remote Code Execute via Winrm.vbs
rules.description: Detects an attempt to execute code or create service on remote host via winrm.vbs.
rules.author: Julia Fomina, oscd.community

rules.title: Remote PowerShell Session Host Process (WinRM)
rules.description: Detects remote PowerShell sections by monitoring for wsmprovhost (WinRM host process) as a parent or child process (sign of an active PowerShell remote session).
rules.author: Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g

rules.title: Suspicious Processes Spawned by WinRM
rules.description: Detects suspicious processes including shells spawnd from WinRM host process
rules.author: Andreas Hunkeler (@Karneades), Markus Neis

rules.title: Potential Lateral Movement via Windows Remote Shell
rules.description: Detects a child process spawned by 'winrshost.exe', which suggests remote command execution through Windows Remote Shell (WinRs) and may indicate potential lateral movement activity.
rules.author: Liran Ravich

rules.title: Winrs Local Command Execution
rules.description:
Detects the execution of Winrs.exe where it is used to execute commands locally.
Commands executed this way are launched under Winrshost.exe and can represent proxy execution used for defense evasion or lateral movement.
rules.author: Liran Ravich, Nasreddine Bencherchali

rules.title: Compress Data and Lock With Password for Exfiltration With WINZIP
rules.description: An adversary may compress or encrypt data that is collected prior to exfiltration using 3rd party utilities
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Wlrmdr.EXE Uncommon Argument Or Child Process
rules.description:
Detects the execution of "Wlrmdr.exe" with the "-u" command line flag which allows anything passed to it to be an argument of the ShellExecute API, which would allow an attacker to execute arbitrary binaries.
This detection also focuses on any uncommon child processes spawned from "Wlrmdr.exe" as a
rules.author: frack113, manasmbellani

rules.title: New ActiveScriptEventConsumer Created Via Wmic.EXE
rules.description: Detects WMIC executions in which an event consumer gets created. This could be used to establish persistence
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential Windows Defender Tampering Via Wmic.EXE
rules.description: Detects potential tampering with Windows Defender settings such as adding exclusion using wmic
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: New Process Created Via Wmic.EXE
rules.description: Detects new process creation using WMIC via the "process call create" flag
rules.author: Michael Haag, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), juju4, oscd.community

rules.title: Computer System Reconnaissance Via Wmic.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of wmic utility with the "computersystem" flag in order to obtain information about the machine such as the domain, username, model, etc.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Hardware Model Reconnaissance Via Wmic.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of WMIC with the "csproduct" which is used to obtain information such as hardware models and vendor information
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Local Groups Reconnaissance Via Wmic.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the execution of "wmic" with the "group" flag.
Adversaries may attempt to find local system groups and permission settings.
The knowledge of local system permission groups can help adversaries determine which groups exist and which users belong to a particular group.
Adversaries may use this
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Windows Hotfix Updates Reconnaissance Via Wmic.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of wmic with the "qfe" flag in order to obtain information about installed hotfix updates on the system. This is often used by pentester and attacker enumeration scripts
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Process Reconnaissance Via Wmic.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of "wmic" with the "process" flag, which adversary might use to list processes running on the compromised host or list installed software hotfixes and patches.
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Potential Product Reconnaissance Via Wmic.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of WMIC in order to get a list of firewall and antivirus products
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali

rules.title: Potential Product Class Reconnaissance Via Wmic.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the execution of WMIC in order to get a list of firewall, antivirus and antispywware products.
Adversaries often enumerate security products installed on a system to identify security controls and potential ways to evade detection or disable protection mechanisms.
This information helps them
rules.author: Michael Haag, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), juju4, oscd.community, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Service Reconnaissance Via Wmic.EXE
rules.description:
An adversary might use WMI to check if a certain remote service is running on a remote device.
When the test completes, a service information will be displayed on the screen if it exists.
A common feedback message is that "No instance(s) Available" if the service queried is not running.
A common err
rules.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Uncommon System Information Discovery Via Wmic.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the use of the WMI command-line (WMIC) utility to identify and display various system information,
including OS, CPU, GPU, and disk drive names; memory capacity; display resolution; and baseboard, BIOS,
and GPU driver products/versions.
Some of these commands were used by Aurora Stealer in l
rules.author: TropChaud

rules.title: Potential Unquoted Service Path Reconnaissance Via Wmic.EXE
rules.description: Detects known WMI recon method to look for unquoted service paths using wmic. Often used by pentester and attacker enumeration scripts
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: System Disk And Volume Reconnaissance Via Wmic.EXE
rules.description:
An adversary might use WMI to discover information about the system, such as the volume name, size,
free space, and other disk information. This can be done using the 'wmic' command-line utility and has been
observed being used by threat actors such as Volt Typhoon.
rules.author: Stephen Lincoln '@slincoln-aiq' (AttackIQ)

rules.title: WMIC Remote Command Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of WMIC to query information on a remote system
rules.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Service Started/Stopped Via Wmic.EXE
rules.description: Detects usage of wmic to start or stop a service
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Service Startup Type Change Via Wmic.EXE
rules.description: Detects changes to service startup type to 'disabled' or 'manual' using the WMIC command-line utility.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential Remote SquiblyTwo Technique Execution
rules.description:
Detects potential execution of the SquiblyTwo technique that leverages Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI)
to execute malicious code remotely. This technique bypasses application whitelisting by using wmic.exe to process
malicious XSL (eXtensible Stylesheet Language) scripts that can contain em
rules.author: Markus Neis, Florian Roth, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Registry Manipulation via WMI Stdregprov
rules.description:
Detects the usage of wmic.exe to manipulate Windows registry via the WMI StdRegProv class.
This behaviour could be potentially suspicious because it uses an alternative method to modify registry keys instead of legitimate registry tools like reg.exe or regedit.exe.
Attackers specifically choose this
rules.author: Daniel Koifman (KoifSec)

rules.title: Suspicious WMIC Execution Via Office Process
rules.description: Office application called wmic to proxye execution through a LOLBIN process. This is often used to break suspicious parent-child chain (Office app spawns LOLBin).
rules.author: Vadim Khrykov, Cyb3rEng

rules.title: Suspicious Process Created Via Wmic.EXE
rules.description: Detects WMIC executing "process call create" with suspicious calls to processes such as "rundll32", "regsrv32", etc.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Application Terminated Via Wmic.EXE
rules.description: Detects calls to the "terminate" function via wmic in order to kill an application
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Application Removed Via Wmic.EXE
rules.description: Detects the removal or uninstallation of an application via "Wmic.EXE".
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Potential Tampering With Security Products Via WMIC
rules.description: Detects uninstallation or termination of security products using the WMIC utility
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: XSL Script Execution Via WMIC.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the execution of WMIC with the "format" flag to potentially load local XSL files.
Adversaries abuse this functionality to execute arbitrary files while potentially bypassing application whitelisting defenses.
Extensible Stylesheet Language (XSL) files are commonly used to describe the proces
rules.author: Timur Zinniatullin, oscd.community, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel

rules.author: Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g

rules.author: Vadim Khrykov (ThreatIntel), Cyb3rEng, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.description: Detects a WMI backdoor in Exchange Transport Agents via WMI event filters
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.description: Detects the use of wmic.exe to modify user account settings and explicitly disable password expiration.

rules.author: Margaritis Dimitrios (idea), Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems),

rules.title: Cscript/Wscript Potentially Suspicious Child Process
rules.description:
Detects potentially suspicious child processes of Wscript/Cscript. These include processes such as rundll32 with uncommon exports or PowerShell spawning rundll32 or regsvr32.
Malware such as Pikabot and Qakbot were seen using similar techniques as well as many others.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Alejandro Houspanossian ('@lekz86')

rules.title: Cscript/Wscript Uncommon Script Extension Execution
rules.description: Detects Wscript/Cscript executing a file with an uncommon (i.e. non-script) extension
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: WSL Child Process Anomaly
rules.description: Detects uncommon or suspicious child processes spawning from a WSL process. This could indicate an attempt to evade parent/child relationship detections or persistence attempts via cron using WSL
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Installation of WSL Kali-Linux
rules.description:
Detects installation of Kali Linux distribution through Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL).
Attackers may use Kali Linux WSL to leverage its penetration testing tools and capabilities for malicious purposes.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: WSL Kali-Linux Usage
rules.description: Detects the use of Kali Linux through Windows Subsystem for Linux
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Windows Binary Executed From WSL
rules.description:
Detects the execution of Windows binaries from within a WSL instance.
This could be used to masquerade parent-child relationships
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Proxy Execution Via Wuauclt.EXE
rules.description: Detects the use of the Windows Update Client binary (wuauclt.exe) for proxy execution.
rules.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research), Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Sreeman, FPT.EagleEye Team

rules.title: Suspicious Windows Update Agent Empty Cmdline
rules.description: Detects suspicious Windows Update Agent activity in which a wuauclt.exe process command line doesn't contain any command line flags
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Cab File Extraction Via Wusa.EXE From Potentially Suspicious Paths
rules.description: Detects the execution of the "wusa.exe" (Windows Update Standalone Installer) utility to extract ".cab" files using the "/extract" argument from potentially suspicious paths.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Wusa.EXE Executed By Parent Process Located In Suspicious Location
rules.description:
Detects execution of the "wusa.exe" (Windows Update Standalone Installer) utility by a parent process that is located in a suspicious location.
Attackers could instantiate an instance of "wusa.exe" in order to bypass User Account Control (UAC). They can duplicate the access token from "wusa.exe" to
rules.author: X__Junior (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Xwizard.EXE Execution From Non-Default Location
rules.description:
Detects the execution of Xwizard tool from a non-default directory.
When executed from a non-default directory, this utility can be abused in order to side load a custom version of "xwizards.dll".
rules.author: Christian Burkard (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: COM Object Execution via Xwizard.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the execution of Xwizard tool with the "RunWizard" flag and a GUID like argument.
This utility can be abused in order to run custom COM object created in the registry.
rules.author: Ensar Şamil, @sblmsrsn, @oscd_initiative, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential Process Hollowing Activity

rules.author: Christopher Peacock '@securepeacock', SCYTHE '@scythe_io', Sittikorn S

rules.title: Potential Defense Evasion Via Raw Disk Access By Uncommon Tools
rules.description: Detects raw disk access using uncommon tools or tools that are located in suspicious locations (heavy filtering is required), which could indicate possible defense evasion attempts
rules.author: Teymur Kheirkhabarov, oscd.community

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via Disk Cleanup Handler - Registry
rules.description:
Detects when an attacker modifies values of the Disk Cleanup Handler in the registry to achieve persistence.
The disk cleanup manager is part of the operating system. It displays the dialog box […]
The user has the option of enabling or disabling individual handlers by selecting or clearing their ch
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.description: Detects deletion of registry key that adds 'Scan with Defender' option in context menu. Attackers may use this to make it harder for users to scan files that are suspicious.
rules.author: Matt Anderson (Huntress)

rules.title: Windows Credential Guard Related Registry Value Deleted - Registry
rules.description:
Detects attempts to disable Windows Credential Guard by deleting registry values. Credential Guard uses virtualization-based security to isolate secrets so that only privileged system software can access them.
Adversaries may disable Credential Guard to gain access to sensitive credentials stored in
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Windows Recall Feature Enabled - DisableAIDataAnalysis Value Deleted
rules.description:
Detects the enabling of the Windows Recall feature via registry manipulation. Windows Recall can be enabled by deleting the existing "DisableAIDataAnalysis" registry value.
Adversaries may enable Windows Recall as part of post-exploitation discovery and collection activities.
This rule assumes that
rules.author: Sajid Nawaz Khan

rules.title: Folder Removed From Exploit Guard ProtectedFolders List - Registry
rules.description: Detects the removal of folders from the "ProtectedFolders" list of of exploit guard. This could indicate an attacker trying to launch an encryption process or trying to manipulate data inside of the protected folder
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Terminal Server Client Connection History Cleared - Registry
rules.description: Detects the deletion of registry keys containing the MSTSC connection history
rules.author: Christian Burkard (Nextron Systems)

rules.description: Detects the deletion of AMSI provider registry key entries in HKLM\Software\Microsoft\AMSI. This technique could be used by an attacker in order to disable AMSI inspection.
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Removal of Potential COM Hijacking Registry Keys
rules.description:
Detects any deletion of entries in ".*\shell\open\command" registry keys.
These registry keys might have been used for COM hijacking activities by a threat actor or an attacker and the deletion could indicate steps to remove its tracks.
rules.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)

rules.title: RunMRU Registry Key Deletion - Registry
rules.description:
Detects attempts to delete the RunMRU registry key, which stores the history of commands executed via the run dialog.

Adversaries may delete this key to cover their tr
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Removal Of Index Value to Hide Schedule Task - Registry
rules.description: Detects when the "index" value of a scheduled task is removed or deleted from the registry. Which effectively hides it from any tooling such as "schtasks /query"
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Removal Of SD Value to Hide Schedule Task - Registry
rules.description: Remove SD (Security Descriptor) value in \Schedule\TaskCache\Tree registry hive to hide schedule task. This technique is used by Tarrask malware
rules.author: Sittikorn S

rules.title: Creation of a Local Hidden User Account by Registry
rules.description: Sysmon registry detection of a local hidden user account.
rules.author: Christian Burkard (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: UAC Bypass Via Wsreset
rules.description: Unfixed method for UAC bypass from Windows 10. WSReset.exe file associated with the Windows Store. It will run a binary file contained in a low-privilege registry.
rules.author: oscd.community, Dmitry Uchakin

rules.title: CMSTP Execution Registry Event
rules.description: Detects various indicators of Microsoft Connection Manager Profile Installer execution
rules.author: Nik Seetharaman

rules.title: Windows Defender Threat Severity Default Action Modified
rules.description:
Detects modifications or creations of Windows Defender's default threat action settings based on severity to 'allow' or take 'no action'.
This is a highly suspicious configuration change that effectively disables Defender's ability to automatically mitigate threats of a certain severity level,
allow
rules.author: Matt Anderson (Huntress)

rules.title: Disable Security Events Logging Adding Reg Key MiniNt
rules.description: Detects the addition of a key 'MiniNt' to the registry. Upon a reboot, Windows Event Log service will stop writing events.
rules.author: Ilyas Ochkov, oscd.community

rules.title: Wdigest CredGuard Registry Modification
rules.description:
Detects potential malicious modification of the property value of IsCredGuardEnabled from
HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\WDigest to disable Cred Guard on a system.
This is usually used with UseLogonCredential to manipulate the caching credentials.
rules.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)

rules.title: Esentutl Volume Shadow Copy Service Keys
rules.description: Detects the volume shadow copy service initialization and processing via esentutl. Registry keys such as HKLM\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\VSS\\Diag\\VolSnap\\Volume are captured.
rules.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)

rules.title: Windows Credential Editor Registry
rules.description: Detects the use of Windows Credential Editor (WCE)
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: HybridConnectionManager Service Installation - Registry
rules.description: Detects the installation of the Azure Hybrid Connection Manager service to allow remote code execution from Azure function.
rules.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)

rules.title: Potential Qakbot Registry Activity
rules.description: Detects a registry key used by IceID in a campaign that distributes malicious OneNote files
rules.author: Hieu Tran

rules.title: Registry Entries For Azorult Malware
rules.description: Detects the presence of a registry key created during Azorult execution
rules.author: Trent Liffick

rules.title: Path To Screensaver Binary Modified
rules.description: Detects value modification of registry key containing path to binary used as screensaver.
rules.author: Bartlomiej Czyz @bczyz1, oscd.community

rules.title: Narrator's Feedback-Hub Persistence
rules.description: Detects abusing Windows 10 Narrator's Feedback-Hub

rules.title: NetNTLM Downgrade Attack - Registry
rules.description: Detects NetNTLM downgrade attack
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), wagga, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Splunk STRT)

rules.description:
Dynamic-link libraries (DLLs) that are specified in the AppCertDLLs value in the Registry key can be abused to obtain persistence and privilege escalation
by causing a malicious DLL to be loaded and run in the context of separate processes on the computer.
rules.author: Ilyas Ochkov, oscd.community

rules.description: DLLs that are specified in the AppInit_DLLs value in the Registry key HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Windows are loaded by user32.dll into every process that loads user32.dll
rules.author: Ilyas Ochkov, oscd.community, Tim Shelton

rules.author: Antonlovesdnb, Trent Liffick (@tliffick)

rules.title: Registry Persistence Mechanisms in Recycle Bin
rules.description: Detects persistence registry keys for Recycle Bin
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: New PortProxy Registry Entry Added

rules.title: RedMimicry Winnti Playbook Registry Manipulation

rules.title: WINEKEY Registry Modification

rules.author: omkar72

rules.description: Detects the shell open key manipulation (exefile and ms-settings) used for persistence and the pattern of UAC Bypass using fodhelper.exe, computerdefaults.exe, slui.exe via registry keys (e.g. UACMe 33 or 62)
rules.author: Christian Burkard (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential Credential Dumping Via LSASS SilentProcessExit Technique
rules.description: Detects changes to the Registry in which a monitor program gets registered to dump the memory of the lsass.exe process
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Security Support Provider (SSP) Added to LSA Configuration
rules.description: Detects the addition of a SSP to the registry. Upon a reboot or API call, SSP DLLs gain access to encrypted and plaintext passwords stored in Windows.
