T1685.title: Sysmon Driver Unloaded Via Fltmc.EXE
T1685.description: Detects possible Sysmon filter driver unloaded via fltmc.exe
T1685.author: Kirill Kiryanov, oscd.community

T1685.title: HackTool - EDRSilencer Execution
T1685.description: Detects the execution of EDRSilencer, a tool that leverages Windows Filtering Platform (WFP) to block Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) agents from reporting security events to the server based on PE metadata information.
T1685.author: @gott_cyber

T1685.title: Hacktool - EDR-Freeze Execution
T1685.description:
Detects execution of EDR-Freeze, a tool that exploits the MiniDumpWriteDump function and WerFaultSecure.exe to suspend EDR and Antivirus processes on Windows.
EDR-Freeze leverages a race-condition attack to put security processes into a dormant state by suspending WerFaultSecure at the moment it fre
T1685.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: HackTool - PowerTool Execution
T1685.description: Detects the execution of the tool PowerTool which has the ability to kill a process, delete its process file, unload drivers, and delete the driver files
T1685.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: HackTool - Stracciatella Execution
T1685.description: Detects Stracciatella which executes a Powershell runspace from within C# (aka SharpPick technique) with AMSI, ETW and Script Block Logging disabled based on PE metadata characteristics.
T1685.author: pH-T (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Hypervisor-protected Code Integrity (HVCI) Related Registry Tampering Via CommandLine
T1685.description:
Detects the tampering of Hypervisor-protected Code Integrity (HVCI) related registry values via command line tool reg.exe.
HVCI uses virtualization-based security to protect code integrity by ensuring that only trusted code can run in kernel mode.
Adversaries may tamper with HVCI to load malicious o
T1685.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Suspicious Windows Trace ETW Session Tamper Via Logman.EXE
T1685.description: Detects the execution of "logman" utility in order to disable or delete Windows trace sessions
T1685.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Windows Defender Definition Files Removed
T1685.description: Adversaries may disable security tools to avoid possible detection of their tools and activities by removing Windows Defender Definition Files
T1685.author: frack113

T1685.title: Potential AMSI Bypass Via .NET Reflection
T1685.description: Detects Request to "amsiInitFailed" that can be used to disable AMSI Scanning
T1685.author: Markus Neis, @Kostastsale

T1685.title: Potential AMSI Bypass Using NULL Bits
T1685.description: Detects usage of special strings/null bits in order to potentially bypass AMSI functionalities
T1685.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Powershell Base64 Encoded MpPreference Cmdlet
T1685.description: Detects base64 encoded "MpPreference" PowerShell cmdlet code that tries to modifies or tamper with Windows Defender AV
T1685.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Powershell Defender Disable Scan Feature
T1685.description: Detects requests to disable Microsoft Defender features using PowerShell commands
T1685.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Powershell Defender Exclusion
T1685.description: Detects requests to exclude files, folders or processes from Antivirus scanning using PowerShell cmdlets
T1685.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Disable Windows Defender AV Security Monitoring
T1685.description: Detects attackers attempting to disable Windows Defender using Powershell
T1685.author: ok @securonix invrep-de, oscd.community, frack113

T1685.title: Windows Firewall Disabled via PowerShell
T1685.description: Detects attempts to disable the Windows Firewall using PowerShell
T1685.author: Tim Rauch, Elastic (idea)

T1685.title: Disabled IE Security Features
T1685.description: Detects command lines that indicate unwanted modifications to registry keys that disable important Internet Explorer security features
T1685.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Obfuscated PowerShell OneLiner Execution
T1685.description: Detects the execution of a specific OneLiner to download and execute powershell modules in memory.
T1685.author: @Kostastsale, TheDFIRReport

T1685.title: Tamper Windows Defender Remove-MpPreference
T1685.description: Detects attempts to remove Windows Defender configurations using the 'MpPreference' cmdlet
T1685.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Service StartupType Change Via PowerShell Set-Service
T1685.description: Detects the use of the PowerShell "Set-Service" cmdlet to change the startup type of a service to "disabled" or "manual"
T1685.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Suspicious Uninstall of Windows Defender Feature via PowerShell
T1685.description: Detects the use of PowerShell with Uninstall-WindowsFeature or Remove-WindowsFeature cmdlets to disable or remove the Windows Defender GUI feature, a common technique used by adversaries to evade defenses.
T1685.author: yxinmiracle

T1685.title: PUA - CleanWipe Execution
T1685.description: Detects the use of CleanWipe a tool usually used to delete Symantec antivirus.
T1685.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Python Function Execution Security Warning Disabled In Excel
T1685.description:
Detects changes to the registry value "PythonFunctionWarnings" that would prevent any warnings or alerts from showing when Python functions are about to be executed.
Threat actors could run malicious code through the new Microsoft Excel feature that allows Python to run within the spreadsheet.
T1685.author: @Kostastsale

T1685.title: Add SafeBoot Keys Via Reg Utility
T1685.description: Detects execution of "reg.exe" commands with the "add" or "copy" flags on safe boot registry keys. Often used by attacker to allow the ransomware to work in safe mode as some security products do not
T1685.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Suspicious Windows Defender Folder Exclusion Added Via Reg.EXE
T1685.description: Detects the usage of "reg.exe" to add Defender folder exclusions. Qbot has been seen using this technique to add exclusions for folders within AppData and ProgramData.
T1685.author: frack113

T1685.title: SafeBoot Registry Key Deleted Via Reg.EXE
T1685.description: Detects execution of "reg.exe" commands with the "delete" flag on safe boot registry keys. Often used by attacker to prevent safeboot execution of security products
T1685.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Tim Shelton

T1685.title: Service Registry Key Deleted Via Reg.EXE
T1685.description: Detects execution of "reg.exe" commands with the "delete" flag on services registry key. Often used by attacker to remove AV software services
T1685.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Disabling Windows Defender WMI Autologger Session via Reg.exe
T1685.description:
Detects the use of reg.exe to disable the Event Tracing for Windows (ETW) Autologger session for Windows Defender API and Audit events.
By setting the 'Start' value to '0' for the 'DefenderApiLogger' or 'DefenderAuditLogger' session, an attacker can prevent these critical security events
from being
T1685.author: Matt Anderson (Huntress)

T1685.title: Security Service Disabled Via Reg.EXE
T1685.description: Detects execution of "reg.exe" to disable security services such as Windows Defender.
T1685.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), John Lambert (idea), elhoim

T1685.title: Reg Add Suspicious Paths
T1685.description: Detects when an adversary uses the reg.exe utility to add or modify new keys or subkeys
T1685.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Disabled Volume Snapshots
T1685.description: Detects commands that temporarily turn off Volume Snapshots
T1685.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Suspicious Windows Defender Registry Key Tampering Via Reg.EXE
T1685.description: Detects the usage of "reg.exe" to tamper with different Windows Defender registry keys in order to disable some important features related to protection and detection
T1685.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Write Protect For Storage Disabled
T1685.description:
Detects applications trying to modify the registry in order to disable any write-protect property for storage devices.
This could be a precursor to a ransomware attack and has been an observed technique used by cypherpunk group.
T1685.author: Sreeman

T1685.title: Service StartupType Change Via Sc.EXE
T1685.description: Detect the use of "sc.exe" to change the startup type of a service to "disabled" or "demand"
T1685.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Potential Suspicious Activity Using SeCEdit
T1685.description: Detects potential suspicious behaviour using secedit.exe. Such as exporting or modifying the security policy
T1685.author: Janantha Marasinghe

T1685.title: Raccine Uninstall
T1685.description: Detects commands that indicate a Raccine removal from an end system. Raccine is a free ransomware protection tool.
T1685.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: ETW Logging Tamper In .NET Processes Via CommandLine
T1685.description:
Detects changes to environment variables related to ETW logging via the CommandLine.
This could indicate potential adversaries stopping ETW providers recording loaded .NET assemblies.
T1685.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)

T1685.title: ETW Trace Evasion Activity
T1685.description: Detects command line activity that tries to clear or disable any ETW trace log which could be a sign of logging evasion.
T1685.author: @neu5ron, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community

T1685.title: Suspicious Windows Service Tampering
T1685.description: Detects the usage of binaries such as 'net', 'sc' or 'powershell' in order to stop, pause, disable or delete critical or important Windows services such as AV, Backup, etc. As seen being used in some ransomware scripts
T1685.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), frack113 , X__Junior (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Sysinternals PsSuspend Suspicious Execution
T1685.description: Detects suspicious execution of Sysinternals PsSuspend, where the utility is used to suspend critical processes such as AV or EDR to bypass defenses
T1685.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Sysmon Configuration Update
T1685.description: Detects updates to Sysmon's configuration. Attackers might update or replace the Sysmon configuration with a bare bone one to avoid monitoring without shutting down the service completely
T1685.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Uninstall Sysinternals Sysmon
T1685.description: Detects the removal of Sysmon, which could be a potential attempt at defense evasion
T1685.author: frack113

T1685.title: Taskkill Symantec Endpoint Protection
T1685.description:
Detects one of the possible scenarios for disabling Symantec Endpoint Protection.
Symantec Endpoint Protection antivirus software services incorrectly implement the protected service mechanism.
As a result, the NT AUTHORITY/SYSTEM user can execute the taskkill /im command several times ccSvcHst.exe
T1685.author: Ilya Krestinichev, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Uninstall Crowdstrike Falcon Sensor
T1685.description: Adversaries may disable security tools to avoid possible detection of their tools and activities by uninstalling Crowdstrike Falcon
T1685.author: frack113

T1685.title: Vulnerable Driver Blocklist Registry Tampering Via CommandLine
T1685.description:
Detects tampering of the Vulnerable Driver Blocklist registry via command line tools such as PowerShell or REG.EXE.
The Vulnerable Driver Blocklist is a security feature that helps prevent the loading of known vulnerable drivers.
Disabling this feature may indicate an attempt to bypass security cont
T1685.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: PPL Tampering Via WerFaultSecure
T1685.description:
Detects potential abuse of WerFaultSecure.exe to dump Protected Process Light (PPL) processes like LSASS or to freeze security solutions (EDR/antivirus).
This technique is used by tools such as EDR-Freeze and WSASS to bypass PPL protections and access sensitive information or disable security softwa
T1685.author: Jason (https://github.com/0xbcf)

T1685.title: Potential Windows Defender Tampering Via Wmic.EXE
T1685.description: Detects potential tampering with Windows Defender settings such as adding exclusion using wmic
T1685.author: frack113

T1685.title: Service Startup Type Change Via Wmic.EXE
T1685.description: Detects changes to service startup type to 'disabled' or 'manual' using the WMIC command-line utility.
T1685.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Potential Tampering With Security Products Via WMIC
T1685.description: Detects uninstallation or termination of security products using the WMIC utility
T1685.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Windows Credential Guard Related Registry Value Deleted - Registry
T1685.description:
Detects attempts to disable Windows Credential Guard by deleting registry values. Credential Guard uses virtualization-based security to isolate secrets so that only privileged system software can access them.
Adversaries may disable Credential Guard to gain access to sensitive credentials stored in
T1685.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Folder Removed From Exploit Guard ProtectedFolders List - Registry
T1685.description: Detects the removal of folders from the "ProtectedFolders" list of of exploit guard. This could indicate an attacker trying to launch an encryption process or trying to manipulate data inside of the protected folder
T1685.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Removal Of AMSI Provider Registry Keys
T1685.description: Detects the deletion of AMSI provider registry key entries in HKLM\Software\Microsoft\AMSI. This technique could be used by an attacker in order to disable AMSI inspection.
T1685.author: frack113

T1685.title: Removal Of Index Value to Hide Schedule Task - Registry
T1685.description: Detects when the "index" value of a scheduled task is removed or deleted from the registry. Which effectively hides it from any tooling such as "schtasks /query"
T1685.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Removal Of SD Value to Hide Schedule Task - Registry
T1685.description: Remove SD (Security Descriptor) value in \Schedule\TaskCache\Tree registry hive to hide schedule task. This technique is used by Tarrask malware
T1685.author: Sittikorn S

T1685.title: Windows Defender Threat Severity Default Action Modified
T1685.description:
Detects modifications or creations of Windows Defender's default threat action settings based on severity to 'allow' or take 'no action'.
This is a highly suspicious configuration change that effectively disables Defender's ability to automatically mitigate threats of a certain severity level,
allow
T1685.author: Matt Anderson (Huntress)

T1685.title: NetNTLM Downgrade Attack - Registry
T1685.description: Detects NetNTLM downgrade attack
T1685.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), wagga, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Splunk STRT)

T1685.title: Enable Remote Connection Between Anonymous Computer - AllowAnonymousCallback
T1685.description: Detects enabling of the "AllowAnonymousCallback" registry value, which allows a remote connection between computers that do not have a trust relationship.
T1685.author: X__Junior (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Potential AMSI COM Server Hijacking
T1685.description: Detects changes to the AMSI come server registry key in order disable AMSI scanning functionalities. When AMSI attempts to starts its COM component, it will query its registered CLSID and return a non-existent COM server. This causes a load failure and prevents any scanning methods from being access
T1685.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: AMSI Disabled via Registry Modification
T1685.description:
Detects attempts to disable AMSI (Anti-Malware Scan Interface) by modifying the AmsiEnable registry value.
Anti-Malware Scan Interface (AMSI) is a security feature in Windows that allows applications and services to integrate with anti-malware products for enhanced protection against malicious conte
T1685.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Sysmon Driver Altitude Change
T1685.description:
Detects changes in Sysmon driver altitude value.
If the Sysmon driver is configured to load at an altitude of another registered service, it will fail to load at boot.
T1685.author: B.Talebi

T1685.title: Windows Credential Guard Disabled - Registry
T1685.description:
Detects attempts to disable Windows Credential Guard by setting registry values to 0. Credential Guard uses virtualization-based security to isolate secrets so that only privileged system software can access them.
Adversaries may disable Credential Guard to gain access to sensitive credentials store
T1685.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Windows Defender Exclusions Added - Registry
T1685.description: Detects the Setting of Windows Defender Exclusions
T1685.author: Christian Burkard (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Antivirus Filter Driver Disallowed On Dev Drive - Registry
T1685.description: Detects activity that indicates a user disabling the ability for Antivirus mini filter to inspect a "Dev Drive".
T1685.author: @kostastsale, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Windows Hypervisor Enforced Code Integrity Disabled
T1685.description: Detects changes to the HypervisorEnforcedCodeIntegrity registry key and the "Enabled" value being set to 0 in order to disable the Hypervisor Enforced Code Integrity feature. This allows an attacker to load unsigned and untrusted code to be run in the kernel
T1685.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Anish Bogati

T1685.title: Hypervisor Enforced Paging Translation Disabled
T1685.description: Detects changes to the "DisableHypervisorEnforcedPagingTranslation" registry value. Where the it is set to "1" in order to disable the Hypervisor Enforced Paging Translation feature.
T1685.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Disable Exploit Guard Network Protection on Windows Defender
T1685.description: Detects disabling Windows Defender Exploit Guard Network Protection
T1685.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

T1685.title: Disabled Windows Defender Eventlog
T1685.description: Detects the disabling of the Windows Defender eventlog as seen in relation to Lockbit 3.0 infections
T1685.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Disable PUA Protection on Windows Defender
T1685.description: Detects disabling Windows Defender PUA protection
T1685.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

T1685.title: Disable Tamper Protection on Windows Defender
T1685.description: Detects disabling Windows Defender Tamper Protection
T1685.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

T1685.title: Disable Privacy Settings Experience in Registry
T1685.description: Detects registry modifications that disable Privacy Settings Experience
T1685.author: frack113

T1685.title: Windows Defender Service Disabled - Registry
T1685.description: Detects when an attacker or tool disables the  Windows Defender service (WinDefend) via the registry
T1685.author: Ján Trenčanský, frack113, AlertIQ, Nasreddine Bencherchali

T1685.title: ETW Logging Disabled In .NET Processes - Sysmon Registry
T1685.description: Potential adversaries stopping ETW providers recording loaded .NET assemblies.
T1685.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)

T1685.title: Scripted Diagnostics Turn Off Check Enabled - Registry
T1685.description: Detects enabling TurnOffCheck which can be used to bypass defense of MSDT Follina vulnerability
T1685.author: Christopher Peacock @securepeacock, SCYTHE @scythe_io

T1685.title: Suspicious Application Allowed Through Exploit Guard
T1685.description: Detects applications being added to the "allowed applications" list of exploit guard in order to bypass controlled folder settings
T1685.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Hide Schedule Task Via Index Value Tamper
T1685.description:
Detects when the "index" value of a scheduled task is modified from the registry
Which effectively hides it from any tooling such as "schtasks /query" (Read the referenced link for more information about the effects of this technique)
T1685.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1685.description:
Detects usage of Windows Input Method Editor (IME) keyboard layout feature, which allows an attacker to load a DLL into the process after sending the WM_INPUTLANGCHANGEREQUEST message.
Before doing this, the client needs to register the DLL in a special registry key that is assumed to implement this

T1685.title: Suspicious Path In Keyboard Layout IME File Registry Value
T1685.description:
Detects usage of Windows Input Method Editor (IME) keyboard layout feature, which allows an attacker to load a DLL into the process after sending the WM_INPUTLANGCHANGEREQUEST message.
Before doing this, the client needs to register the DLL in a special registry key that is assumed to implement this
T1685.author: X__Junior (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Microsoft Office Protected View Disabled
T1685.description: Detects changes to Microsoft Office protected view registry keys with which the attacker disables this feature.
T1685.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Python Function Execution Security Warning Disabled In Excel - Registry
T1685.description:
Detects changes to the registry value "PythonFunctionWarnings" that would prevent any warnings or alerts from showing when Python functions are about to be executed.
Threat actors could run malicious code through the new Microsoft Excel feature that allows Python to run within the spreadsheet.
T1685.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), @Kostastsale

T1685.title: ETW Logging Disabled For rpcrt4.dll
T1685.description: Detects changes to the "ExtErrorInformation" key in order to disable ETW logging for rpcrt4.dll
T1685.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: ETW Logging Disabled For SCM
T1685.description: Detects changes to the "TracingDisabled" key in order to disable ETW logging for services.exe (SCM)
T1685.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Tamper With Sophos AV Registry Keys
T1685.description: Detects tamper attempts to sophos av functionality via registry key modification
T1685.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Suspicious Service Installed
T1685.description:
Detects installation of NalDrv or PROCEXP152 services via registry-keys to non-system32 folders.
Both services are used in the tool Ghost-In-The-Logs (https://github.com/bats3c/Ghost-In-The-Logs), which uses KDU (https://github.com/hfiref0x/KDU)
T1685.author: xknow (@xknow_infosec), xorxes (@xor_xes)

T1685.title: WFP Filter Added via Registry
T1685.description: Detects registry modifications that add Windows Filtering Platform (WFP) filters, which may be used to block security tools and EDR agents from reporting events.
T1685.author: Frack113

T1685.title: Windows Vulnerable Driver Blocklist Disabled
T1685.description:
Detects when the Windows Vulnerable Driver Blocklist is set to disabled. This setting is crucial for preventing the loading of known vulnerable drivers,
and its modification may indicate an attempt to bypass security controls. It is often targeted by threat actors to facilitate the installation of m
T1685.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1685.title: Disable Windows Defender Functionalities Via Registry Keys
T1685.description: Detects when attackers or tools disable Windows Defender functionalities via the Windows registry
T1685.author: AlertIQ, Ján Trenčanský, frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel

T1078.title: Malicious Usage Of IMDS Credentials Outside Of AWS Infrastructure
T1078.description:
Detects when an instance identity has taken an action that isn't inside SSM.
This can indicate that a compromised EC2 instance is being used as a pivot point.
T1078.author: jamesc-grafana

T1078.title: AWS Key Pair Import Activity
T1078.description: Detects the import of SSH key pairs into AWS EC2, which may indicate an attacker attempting to gain unauthorized access to instances. This activity could lead to initial access, persistence, or privilege escalation, potentially compromising sensitive data and operations.
T1078.author: Ivan Saakov

T1078.title: AWS Suspicious SAML Activity
T1078.description: Identifies when suspicious SAML activity has occurred in AWS. An adversary could gain backdoor access via SAML.
T1078.author: Austin Songer

T1078.title: User Added to an Administrator's Azure AD Role
T1078.description: User Added to an Administrator's Azure AD Role
T1078.author: Raphaël CALVET, @MetallicHack

T1078.title: Azure Kubernetes Admission Controller
T1078.description:
Identifies when an admission controller is executed in Azure Kubernetes.
A Kubernetes Admission controller intercepts, and possibly modifies, requests to the Kubernetes API server.
The behavior of this admission controller is determined by an admission webhook (MutatingAdmissionWebhook or Validating
T1078.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

T1078.title: Account Created And Deleted Within A Close Time Frame
T1078.description: Detects when an account was created and deleted in a short period of time.
T1078.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', MikeDuddington, '@dudders1', Tim Shelton

T1078.title: Guest Users Invited To Tenant By Non Approved Inviters
T1078.description: Detects guest users being invited to tenant by non-approved inviters
T1078.author: MikeDuddington, '@dudders1'

T1078.title: Azure Domain Federation Settings Modified
T1078.description: Identifies when an user or application modified the federation settings on the domain.
T1078.author: Austin Songer

T1078.title: PIM Alert Setting Changes To Disabled
T1078.description: Detects when PIM alerts are set to disabled.
T1078.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Yochana Henderson, '@Yochana-H'

T1078.title: Azure Subscription Permission Elevation Via AuditLogs
T1078.description:
Detects when a user has been elevated to manage all Azure Subscriptions.
This change should be investigated immediately if it isn't planned.
This setting could allow an attacker access to Azure subscriptions in your environment.
T1078.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

T1078.title: Activity From Anonymous IP Address
T1078.description: Identifies that users were active from an IP address that has been identified as an anonymous proxy IP address.
T1078.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

T1078.title: Atypical Travel
T1078.description: Identifies two sign-ins originating from geographically distant locations, where at least one of the locations may also be atypical for the user, given past behavior.
T1078.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

T1078.title: Impossible Travel
T1078.description: Identifies user activities originating from geographically distant locations within a time period shorter than the time it takes to travel from the first location to the second.
T1078.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

T1078.title: New Country
T1078.description: Detects sign-ins from new countries. The detection considers past activity locations to determine new and infrequent locations.
T1078.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

T1078.title: Suspicious Browser Activity
T1078.description: Indicates anomalous behavior based on suspicious sign-in activity across multiple tenants from different countries in the same browser
T1078.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

T1078.title: Azure AD Threat Intelligence
T1078.description: Indicates user activity that is unusual for the user or consistent with known attack patterns.
T1078.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

T1078.title: Unfamiliar Sign-In Properties
T1078.description: Detects sign-in with properties that are unfamiliar to the user. The detection considers past sign-in history to look for anomalous sign-ins.
T1078.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

T1078.title: Stale Accounts In A Privileged Role
T1078.description: Identifies when an account hasn't signed in during the past n number of days.

T1078.title: Roles Assigned Outside PIM

T1078.title: Roles Activated Too Frequently

T1078.title: Roles Are Not Being Used

T1078.title: Too Many Global Admins
T1078.description: Identifies an event where there are there are too many accounts assigned the Global Administrator role.

T1078.title: Increased Failed Authentications Of Any Type

T1078.title: Measurable Increase Of Successful Authentications

T1078.title: Authentications To Important Apps Using Single Factor Authentication

T1078.title: Application Using Device Code Authentication Flow
T1078.description:
Device code flow is an OAuth 2.0 protocol flow specifically for input constrained devices and is not used in all environments.
If this type of flow is seen in the environment and not being used in an input constrained device scenario, further investigation is warranted.
This can be a misconfigured a
T1078.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Bailey Bercik '@baileybercik'

T1078.title: Applications That Are Using ROPC Authentication Flow
T1078.description:
Resource owner password credentials (ROPC) should be avoided if at all possible as this requires the user to expose their current password credentials to the application directly.
The application then uses those credentials to authenticate the user against the identity provider.
T1078.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Bailey Bercik '@baileybercik'

T1078.title: Azure Unusual Authentication Interruption
T1078.description: Detects when there is a interruption in the authentication process.

T1078.title: Google Cloud Kubernetes Admission Controller

A Kubernetes Admission controller intercepts, and possibly modifies, requests to the Kubernetes API server.
The behavior of this admission controller is determined by an admission webhook (MutatingAdmissionWebhook or ValidatingAd

T1078.title: Google Workspace Government Attack Warning

T1078.title: Logon from a Risky IP Address
T1078.description: Detects when a Microsoft Cloud App Security reported when a user signs into your sanctioned apps from a risky IP address.

T1078.title: Suspicious Remote Logon with Explicit Credentials

T1078.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1078.title: External Remote RDP Logon from Public IP

T1078.title: External Remote SMB Logon from Public IP

T1078.author: NVISO

T1078.title: Suspicious Computer Machine Password by PowerShell
T1078.description:
The Reset-ComputerMachinePassword cmdlet changes the computer account password that the computers use to authenticate to the domain controllers in the domain.
You can use it to reset the password of the local computer.

T1078.title: Password Provided In Command Line Of Net.EXE

T1078.002.title: Malicious Usage Of IMDS Credentials Outside Of AWS Infrastructure

This can indicate that a compromised EC2 instance is being used as a pivot point.

T1078.002.title: Admin User Remote Logon

T1078.002.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1078.002.title: DMSA Link Attributes Modified
T1078.002.description:
Detects modification of dMSA link attributes (msDS-ManagedAccountPrecededByLink) via PowerShell scripts.
This command line pattern could be an indicator an attempt to exploit the BadSuccessor privilege escalation vulnerability in Windows Server 2025.
T1078.002.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1078.002.title: New DMSA Service Account Created in Specific OUs
T1078.002.description:
Detects the creation of a dMSASvc account using the New-ADServiceAccount cmdlet in certain OUs.
The fact that the Cmdlet is used to create a dMSASvc account in a specific OU is highly suspicious.
It is a pattern trying to exploit the BadSuccessor privilege escalation vulnerability in Windows Server
T1078.002.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1686.001.description: Detects that network ACL entries have been added to a route table which could indicate that new attack vectors have been opened up in the AWS account.

T1686.001.title: New Network Route Added

T1686.001.title: Azure Network Firewall Policy Modified or Deleted

Detects access to Signal Desktop's sensitive data files: db.sqlite and config.json.

Detects file access requests to crypto currency files by uncommon processes.

T1003.description:
Detects loading of dbgcore.dll or dbghelp.dll from uncommon locations such as user directories.
These DLLs contain the MiniDumpWriteDump function, which can be abused for credential dumping purposes or in some cases for evading EDR/AV detection by suspending processes.

T1003.description: Detects use of aspnet_regiis to decrypt Microsoft IIS connection strings. An attacker with Microsoft IIS web server access via a webshell or alike can decrypt and dump any hardcoded connection strings, such as the MSSQL service account password using aspnet_regiis command.

T1003.description:

T1003.description:
Detects the enumeration and query of interesting and in some cases sensitive services on the system via "sc.exe".
Attackers often try to enumerate the services currently running on a system in order to find different attack vectors.

T1070.title: IIS WebServer Access Logs Deleted

T1070.title: PowerShell Console History Logs Deleted

T1070.title: Tomcat WebServer Logs Deleted
T1070.description: Detects the deletion of tomcat WebServer logs which may indicate an attempt to destroy forensic evidence

T1070.title: DLL Load By System Process From Suspicious Locations
T1070.description: Detects when a system process (i.e. located in system32, syswow64, etc.) loads a DLL from a suspicious location or a location with permissive permissions such as "C:\Users\Public"
T1070.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1070.title: Clearing Windows Console History
T1070.description: Identifies when a user attempts to clear console history. An adversary may clear the command history of a compromised account to conceal the actions undertaken during an intrusion.
T1070.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

T1070.title: Disable of ETW Trace - Powershell
T1070.description: Detects usage of powershell cmdlets to disable or remove ETW trace sessions
T1070.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1070.title: Potential Ransomware or Unauthorized MBR Tampering Via Bcdedit.EXE
T1070.description: Detects potential malicious and unauthorized usage of bcdedit.exe
T1070.author: @neu5ron

T1070.title: Filter Driver Unloaded Via Fltmc.EXE
T1070.description: Detect filter driver unloading activity via fltmc.exe
T1070.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1070.title: Sysmon Driver Unloaded Via Fltmc.EXE
T1070.description: Detects possible Sysmon filter driver unloaded via fltmc.exe
T1070.author: Kirill Kiryanov, oscd.community

T1070.title: Fsutil Suspicious Invocation
T1070.description:
Detects suspicious parameters of fsutil (deleting USN journal, configuring it with small size, etc).
Might be used by ransomwares during the attack (seen by NotPetya and others).
T1070.author: Ecco, E.M. Anhaus, oscd.community

T1070.title: IIS WebServer Log Deletion via CommandLine Utilities
T1070.description:
Detects attempts to delete Internet Information Services (IIS) log files via command line utilities, which is a common defense evasion technique used by attackers to cover their tracks.
Threat actors often abuse vulnerabilities in web applications hosted on IIS servers to gain initial access and lat
T1070.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1070.title: ETW Trace Evasion Activity
T1070.description: Detects command line activity that tries to clear or disable any ETW trace log which could be a sign of logging evasion.
T1070.author: @neu5ron, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community

T1070.title: Shadow Copies Deletion Using Operating Systems Utilities
T1070.description: Shadow Copies deletion using operating systems utilities

T1070.title: Terminal Server Client Connection History Cleared - Registry
T1070.description: Detects the deletion of registry keys containing the MSTSC connection history
T1070.author: Christian Burkard (Nextron Systems)

T1531.title: AWS SAML Provider Deletion Activity
T1531.description:
Detects the deletion of an AWS SAML provider, potentially indicating malicious intent to disrupt administrative or security team access.
An attacker can remove the SAML provider for the information security team or a team of system administrators, to make it difficult for them to work and investigat
T1531.author: Ivan Saakov

T1531.title: AWS ElastiCache Security Group Modified or Deleted
T1531.description: Identifies when an ElastiCache security group has been modified or deleted.
T1531.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

T1531.title: Azure Kubernetes Service Account Modified or Deleted
T1531.description: Identifies when a service account is modified or deleted.

T1531.title: Google Cloud Service Account Disabled or Deleted
T1531.description: Identifies when a service account is disabled or deleted in Google Cloud.

T1531.title: User Logoff Event
T1531.description: Detects a user log-off activity. Could be used for example to correlate information during forensic investigations
T1531.author: frack113

T1531.title: Remove Account From Domain Admin Group
T1531.description:
Adversaries may interrupt availability of system and network resources by inhibiting access to accounts utilized by legitimate users.
Accounts may be deleted, locked, or manipulated (ex: changed credentials) to remove access to accounts.
T1531.author: frack113

T1490.title: AWS S3 Bucket Versioning Disable
T1490.description: Detects when S3 bucket versioning is disabled. Threat actors use this technique during AWS ransomware incidents prior to deleting S3 objects.

T1490.title: Cisco Modify Configuration
T1490.description: Modifications to a config that will serve an adversary's impacts or persistence
T1490.author: Austin Clark

T1490.title: Backup Files Deleted
T1490.description: Detects deletion of files with extensions often used for backup files. Adversaries may delete or remove built-in operating system data and turn off services designed to aid in the recovery of a corrupted system to prevent recovery.
T1490.author: frack113

T1490.title: Suspicious Volume Shadow Copy Vssapi.dll Load
T1490.description: Detects the image load of VSS DLL by uncommon executables
T1490.author: frack113

T1490.title: Potentially Suspicious Volume Shadow Copy Vsstrace.dll Load
T1490.description: Detects the image load of VSS DLL by uncommon executables
T1490.author: frack113

T1490.title: Suspicious Volume Shadow Copy VSS_PS.dll Load
T1490.description:
Detects the image load of vss_ps.dll by uncommon executables. This DLL is used by the Volume Shadow Copy Service (VSS) to manage shadow copies of files and volumes.
It is often abused by attackers to delete or manipulate shadow copies, which can hinder forensic investigations and data recovery effor
T1490.author: Markus Neis, @markus_neis

T1490.title: Delete Volume Shadow Copies Via WMI With PowerShell
T1490.description: Shadow Copies deletion using operating systems utilities via PowerShell
T1490.author: frack113

T1490.title: Deletion of Volume Shadow Copies via WMI with PowerShell - PS Script
T1490.description: Detects deletion of Windows Volume Shadow Copies with PowerShell code and Get-WMIObject. This technique is used by numerous ransomware families such as Sodinokibi/REvil
T1490.author: Tim Rauch, frack113

T1490.title: Boot Configuration Tampering Via Bcdedit.EXE
T1490.description: Detects the use of the bcdedit command to tamper with the boot configuration data. This technique is often times used by malware or attackers as a destructive way before launching ransomware.
T1490.author: E.M. Anhaus (originally from Atomic Blue Detections, Endgame), oscd.community

T1490.title: Copy From VolumeShadowCopy Via Cmd.EXE
T1490.description: Detects the execution of the builtin "copy" command that targets a shadow copy (sometimes used to copy registry hives that are in use)
T1490.author: Max Altgelt (Nextron Systems), Tobias Michalski (Nextron Systems)

T1490.title: Deletion of Volume Shadow Copies via WMI with PowerShell
T1490.description: Detects deletion of Windows Volume Shadow Copies with PowerShell code and Get-WMIObject. This technique is used by numerous ransomware families such as Sodinokibi/REvil
T1490.author: Tim Rauch, Elastic (idea)

T1490.title: Windows Recovery Environment Disabled Via Reagentc
T1490.description:
Detects attempts to disable windows recovery environment using Reagentc.
ReAgentc.exe is a command-line tool in Windows used to manage the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE).
It allows users to enable, disable, and configure WinRE, which is used for troubleshooting and repairing common boot issues
T1490.author: Daniel Koifman (KoifSec), Michael Vilshin

T1490.title: System Restore Registry Modification via CommandLine
T1490.description: Detects system restore registry modification via command line, which can be used by adversaries to disable system restore on the computer.
T1490.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1490.title: Sensitive File Access Via Volume Shadow Copy Backup
T1490.description: Detects a command that accesses the VolumeShadowCopy in order to extract sensitive files such as the Security or SAM registry hives or the AD database (ntds.dit)

T1490.title: All Backups Deleted Via Wbadmin.EXE
T1490.description:
Detects the deletion of all backups or system state backups via "wbadmin.exe".
This technique is used by numerous ransomware families and actors.
This may only be successful on server platforms that have Windows Backup enabled.
T1490.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1490.title: Windows Backup Deleted Via Wbadmin.EXE
T1490.description:
Detects the deletion of backups or system state backups via "wbadmin.exe".
This technique is used by numerous ransomware families and actors.
This may only be successful on server platforms that have Windows Backup enabled.
T1490.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1490.title: File Recovery From Backup Via Wbadmin.EXE

Attackers can restore sensitive files such as NTDS.DIT or Registry Hives from backups in order to potentially extract credentials.

T1486.title: Suspicious Appended Extension
T1486.description: Detects file renames where the target filename uses an uncommon double extension. Could indicate potential ransomware activity renaming files and adding a custom extension to the encrypted files, such as ".jpg.crypted", ".docx.locky", etc.

T1059.001.description: Detects suspicious PowerShell invocation with a parameter substring
T1059.001.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Daniel Bohannon (idea), Roberto Rodriguez (Fix)

T1059.001.title: Suspicious PowerShell Parent Process

T1059.001.author: Teymur Kheirkhabarov, Harish Segar

T1059.001.title: PowerShell Script Run in AppData

T1059.001.title: Net WebClient Casing Anomalies

T1059.001.title: Suspicious XOR Encoded PowerShell Command
T1059.001.description: Detects presence of a potentially xor encoded powershell command
T1059.001.author: Sami Ruohonen, Harish Segar, Tim Shelton, Teymur Kheirkhabarov, Vasiliy Burov, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali

T1059.001.title: Suspicious Schtasks Execution AppData Folder
T1059.001.description: Detects the creation of a schtask that executes a file from C:\Users\<USER>\AppData\Local
T1059.001.author: pH-T (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1059.001.title: Potential Persistence Via Powershell Search Order Hijacking - Task
T1059.001.description: Detects suspicious powershell execution via a schedule task where the command ends with an suspicious flags to hide the powershell instance instead of executeing scripts or commands. This could be a sign of persistence via PowerShell "Get-Variable" technique as seen being used in Colibri Loader

T1059.001.title: Scheduled Task Executing Payload from Registry
T1059.001.description: Detects the creation of a schtasks that potentially executes a payload stored in the Windows Registry using PowerShell.
T1059.001.author: X__Junior (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1059.001.title: Scheduled Task Executing Encoded Payload from Registry
T1059.001.description: Detects the creation of a schtask that potentially executes a base64 encoded payload stored in the Windows Registry using PowerShell.
T1059.001.author: pH-T (Nextron Systems), @Kostastsale, TheDFIRReport, X__Junior (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Syste

T1059.001.title: Potential Data Exfiltration Activity Via CommandLine Tools
T1059.001.description: Detects the use of various CLI utilities exfiltrating data via web requests
T1059.001.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1059.001.title: Hidden Powershell in Link File Pattern
T1059.001.description: Detects events that appear when a user click on a link file with a powershell command in it
T1059.001.author: frack113

T1059.001.title: Windows Shell/Scripting Processes Spawning Suspicious Programs
T1059.001.description: Detects suspicious child processes of a Windows shell and scripting processes such as wscript, rundll32, powershell, mshta...etc.
T1059.001.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Tim Shelton

T1059.001.title: Usage Of Web Request Commands And Cmdlets
T1059.001.description: Detects the use of various web request commands with commandline tools and Windows PowerShell cmdlets (including aliases) via CommandLine
T1059.001.author: James Pemberton / @4A616D6573, Endgame, JHasenbusch, oscd.community, Austin Songer @austinsonger

T1059.001.title: Potentially Suspicious WebDAV LNK Execution
T1059.001.description: Detects possible execution via LNK file accessed on a WebDAV server.
T1059.001.author: Micah Babinski

T1059.001.title: Remote PowerShell Session Host Process (WinRM)
T1059.001.description: Detects remote PowerShell sections by monitoring for wsmprovhost (WinRM host process) as a parent or child process (sign of an active PowerShell remote session).
T1059.001.author: Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g

T1059.001.title: Potential WMI Lateral Movement WmiPrvSE Spawned PowerShell
T1059.001.description: Detects Powershell as a child of the WmiPrvSE process. Which could be a sign of lateral movement via WMI.
T1059.001.author: Markus Neis @Karneades

T1059.001.title: Potentially Suspicious Command Executed Via Run Dialog Box - Registry
T1059.001.description:
Detects execution of commands via the run dialog box on Windows by checking values of the "RunMRU" registry key.
This technique was seen being abused by threat actors to deceive users into pasting and executing malicious commands, often disguised as CAPTCHA verification steps.
T1059.001.author: Ahmed Farouk, Nasreddine Bencherchali

T1059.003.title: AWS EC2 Startup Shell Script Change
T1059.003.description: Detects changes to the EC2 instance startup script. The shell script will be executed as root/SYSTEM every time the specific instances are booted up.
T1059.003.author: faloker

T1059.003.title: Remote Access Tool - ScreenConnect Command Execution
T1059.003.description: Detects command execution via ScreenConnect RMM
T1059.003.author: Ali Alwashali

T1059.003.title: Remote Access Tool - ScreenConnect File Transfer
T1059.003.description: Detects file being transferred via ScreenConnect RMM
T1059.003.author: Ali Alwashali

T1059.003.title: AppLocker Prevented Application or Script from Running
T1059.003.description: Detects when AppLocker prevents the execution of an Application, DLL, Script, MSI, or Packaged-App from running.
T1059.003.author: Pushkarev Dmitry

T1059.003.title: DNS Query by Finger Utility
T1059.003.description:
Detects DNS queries made by the finger utility, which can be abused by threat actors to retrieve remote commands for execution on Windows devices.
In one ClickFix malware campaign, adversaries leveraged the finger protocol to fetch commands from a remote server.
Since the finger utility is not commo
T1059.003.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1059.003.title: Remote Access Tool - ScreenConnect Temporary File
T1059.003.description:
Detects the creation of files in a specific location by ScreenConnect RMM.
ScreenConnect has feature to remotely execute binaries on a target machine. These binaries will be dropped to ":\Users\<username>\Documents\ConnectWiseControl\Temp\" before execution.
T1059.003.author: Ali Alwashali

T1059.003.title: Network Connection Initiated via Finger.EXE
T1059.003.description:
Detects network connections via finger.exe, which can be abused by threat actors to retrieve remote commands for execution on Windows devices.
In one ClickFix malware campaign, adversaries leveraged the finger protocol to fetch commands from a remote server.
Since the finger utility is not commonly
T1059.003.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1059.003.title: Powershell Execute Batch Script
T1059.003.description:
Adversaries may abuse the Windows command shell for execution.
The Windows command shell ([cmd](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0106)) is the primary command prompt on Windows systems.
The Windows command prompt can be used to control almost any aspect of a system, with various permission levels
T1059.003.author: frack113

T1059.003.title: Command Line Execution with Suspicious URL and AppData Strings
T1059.003.description: Detects a suspicious command line execution that includes an URL and AppData string in the command line parameters as used by several droppers (js/vbs > powershell)
T1059.003.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community

T1059.003.title: Potential CommandLine Path Traversal Via Cmd.EXE
T1059.003.description: Detects potential path traversal attempt via cmd.exe. Could indicate possible command/argument confusion/hijacking
T1059.003.author: xknow @xknow_infosec, Tim Shelton

T1059.003.title: Read Contents From Stdin Via Cmd.EXE
T1059.003.description: Detect the use of "<" to read and potentially execute a file via cmd.exe
T1059.003.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1059.003.title: OpenEDR Spawning Command Shell
T1059.003.description:
Detects the OpenEDR ssh-shellhost.exe spawning a command shell (cmd.exe) or PowerShell with PTY (pseudo-terminal) capabilities.
This may indicate remote command execution through OpenEDR's remote management features, which could be legitimate administrative activity or potential abuse of the remote
T1059.003.author: @kostastsale

T1059.003.title: Powershell Executed From Headless ConHost Process
T1059.003.description:
Detects the use of powershell commands from headless ConHost window.
The "--headless" flag hides the windows from the user upon execution.
T1059.003.author: Matt Anderson (Huntress)

T1059.003.title: Conhost.exe CommandLine Path Traversal
T1059.003.description: detects the usage of path traversal in conhost.exe indicating possible command/argument confusion/hijacking
T1059.003.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1059.003.title: HTML Help HH.EXE Suspicious Child Process
T1059.003.description: Detects a suspicious child process of a Microsoft HTML Help (HH.exe)
T1059.003.author: Maxim Pavlunin, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1059.003.title: Suspicious HH.EXE Execution
T1059.003.description: Detects a suspicious execution of a Microsoft HTML Help (HH.exe)
T1059.003.author: Maxim Pavlunin

T1059.003.title: Operator Bloopers Cobalt Strike Commands
T1059.003.description: Detects use of Cobalt Strike commands accidentally entered in the CMD shell
T1059.003.author: _pete_0, TheDFIRReport

T1059.003.title: Operator Bloopers Cobalt Strike Modules
T1059.003.description: Detects Cobalt Strike module/commands accidentally entered in CMD shell
T1059.003.author: _pete_0, TheDFIRReport

T1059.003.title: HackTool - CrackMapExec Execution
T1059.003.description: This rule detect common flag combinations used by CrackMapExec in order to detect its use even if the binary has been replaced.
T1059.003.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1059.003.title: HackTool - CrackMapExec Execution Patterns
T1059.003.description: Detects various execution patterns of the CrackMapExec pentesting framework
T1059.003.author: Thomas Patzke

T1059.003.title: HackTool - Jlaive In-Memory Assembly Execution
T1059.003.description: Detects the use of Jlaive to execute assemblies in a copied PowerShell
T1059.003.author: Jose Luis Sanchez Martinez (@Joseliyo_Jstnk)

T1059.003.title: HackTool - Koadic Execution
T1059.003.description: Detects command line parameters used by Koadic hack tool
T1059.003.author: wagga, Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community

T1059.003.title: HackTool - RedMimicry Winnti Playbook Execution
T1059.003.description: Detects actions caused by the RedMimicry Winnti playbook a automated breach emulations utility
T1059.003.author: Alexander Rausch

T1059.003.title: Suspicious HWP Sub Processes
T1059.003.description: Detects suspicious Hangul Word Processor (Hanword) sub processes that could indicate an exploitation
T1059.003.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1059.003.title: PUA - AdvancedRun Execution
T1059.003.description: Detects the execution of AdvancedRun utility
T1059.003.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1059.003.title: Remote Access Tool - ScreenConnect Remote Command Execution
T1059.003.description: Detects the execution of a system command via the ScreenConnect RMM service.
T1059.003.author: Ali Alwashali

T1059.003.title: Suspicious Usage of For Loop with Recursive Directory Search in CMD
T1059.003.description:
Detects suspicious usage of the cmd.exe 'for /f' loop combined with the 'tokens=' parameter and a recursive directory listing.
This pattern may indicate an attempt to discover and execute system binaries dynamically, for example powershell, a technique sometimes used by attackers to evade detection.
T1059.003.author: Joseliyo Sanchez, @Joseliyo_Jstnk

T1059.004.title: AWS EC2 Startup Shell Script Change
T1059.004.description: Detects changes to the EC2 instance startup script. The shell script will be executed as root/SYSTEM every time the specific instances are booted up.
T1059.004.author: faloker

T1005.title: AWS EC2 VM Export Failure
T1005.description: An attempt to export an AWS EC2 instance has been detected. A VM Export might indicate an attempt to extract information from an instance.
T1005.author: Diogo Braz

T1005.title: Cisco Collect Data
T1005.description: Collect pertinent data from the configuration files
T1005.author: Austin Clark

T1005.title: Crash Dump Created By Operating System
T1005.description: Detects "BugCheck" errors indicating the system rebooted due to a crash, capturing the bugcheck code, dump file path, and report ID.
T1005.author: Jason Mull

T1005.title: ADFS Database Named Pipe Connection By Uncommon Tool
T1005.description:
Detects suspicious local connections via a named pipe to the AD FS configuration database (Windows Internal Database).
Used to access information such as the AD FS configuration settings which contains sensitive information used to sign SAML tokens.
T1005.author: Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g

T1005.title: Esentutl Steals Browser Information
T1005.description: One way Qbot steals sensitive information is by extracting browser data from Internet Explorer and Microsoft Edge by using the built-in utility esentutl.exe
T1005.author: frack113

T1005.title: Veeam Backup Database Suspicious Query
T1005.description: Detects potentially suspicious SQL queries using SQLCmd targeting the Veeam backup databases in order to steal information.
T1005.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1005.title: VeeamBackup Database Credentials Dump Via Sqlcmd.EXE
T1005.description: Detects dump of credentials in VeeamBackup dbo
T1005.author: frack113

T1005.title: SQLite Chromium Profile Data DB Access
T1005.description: Detect usage of the "sqlite" binary to query databases in Chromium-based browsers for potential data stealing.
T1005.author: TropChaud

T1005.title: SQLite Firefox Profile Data DB Access
T1005.description: Detect usage of the "sqlite" binary to query databases in Firefox and other Gecko-based browsers for potential data stealing.
T1005.author: frack113

T1005.title: Script Interpreter Spawning Credential Scanner - Windows
T1005.description:
Detects a script interpreter process (like node.js or bun) spawning a known credential scanning tool (e.g., trufflehog, gitleaks).
This behavior is indicative of an attempt to find and steal secrets, as seen in the "Shai-Hulud: The Second Coming" campaign.
T1005.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1537.title: AWS EC2 VM Export Failure
T1537.description: An attempt to export an AWS EC2 instance has been detected. A VM Export might indicate an attempt to extract information from an instance.
T1537.author: Diogo Braz

T1537.title: AWS S3 Data Management Tampering
T1537.description: Detects when a user tampers with S3 data management in Amazon Web Services.
T1537.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

T1537.title: AWS Snapshot Backup Exfiltration
T1537.description: Detects the modification of an EC2 snapshot's permissions to enable access from another account
T1537.author: Darin Smith

T1537.title: Data Exfiltration to Unsanctioned Apps
T1537.description: Detects when a Microsoft Cloud App Security reported when a user or IP address uses an app that is not sanctioned to perform an activity that resembles an attempt to exfiltrate information from your organization.
T1537.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

T1525.title: AWS ECS Task Definition That Queries The Credential Endpoint
T1525.description:
Detects when an Elastic Container Service (ECS) Task Definition includes a command to query the credential endpoint.
This can indicate a potential adversary adding a backdoor to establish persistence or escalate privileges.
T1525.author: Darin Smith

T1485.title: AWS EFS Fileshare Mount Modified or Deleted
T1485.description: Detects when a EFS Fileshare Mount is modified or deleted. An adversary breaking any file system using the mount target that is being deleted, which might disrupt instances or applications using those mounts.
T1485.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

T1485.title: AWS EKS Cluster Created or Deleted
T1485.description: Identifies when an EKS cluster is created or deleted.
T1485.author: Austin Songer

T1485.title: Azure Container Registry Created or Deleted
T1485.description: Detects when a Container Registry is created or deleted.
T1485.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

T1485.title: Azure Device or Configuration Modified or Deleted
T1485.description: Identifies when a device or device configuration in azure is modified or deleted.
T1485.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

T1485.title: Azure Kubernetes Cluster Created or Deleted
T1485.description: Detects when a Azure Kubernetes Cluster is created or deleted.
T1485.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

T1485.title: Azure Kubernetes Network Policy Change
T1485.description: Identifies when a Azure Kubernetes network policy is modified or deleted.
T1485.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

T1485.title: Azure Kubernetes RoleBinding/ClusterRoleBinding Modified and Deleted
T1485.description: Detects the creation or patching of potential malicious RoleBinding/ClusterRoleBinding.
T1485.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

T1485.title: Azure Kubernetes Sensitive Role Access
T1485.description: Identifies when ClusterRoles/Roles are being modified or deleted.
T1485.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

T1485.title: Azure Kubernetes Secret or Config Object Access
T1485.description: Identifies when a Kubernetes account access a sensitive objects such as configmaps or secrets.
T1485.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

T1485.title: Azure Kubernetes Service Account Modified or Deleted
T1485.description: Identifies when a service account is modified or deleted.
T1485.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

T1485.title: Microsoft 365 - Unusual Volume of File Deletion
T1485.description: Detects when a Microsoft Cloud App Security reported a user has deleted a unusual a large volume of files.
T1485.author: austinsonger

T1485.title: MSSQL Destructive Query
T1485.description: Detects the invocation of MS SQL transactions that are destructive towards table or database data, such as "DROP TABLE" or "DROP DATABASE".
T1485.author: Daniel Degasperi '@d4ns4n_'

T1485.title: Potential Secure Deletion with SDelete
T1485.description: Detects files that have extensions commonly seen while SDelete is used to wipe files.
T1485.author: Thomas Patzke

T1485.title: Deleted Data Overwritten Via Cipher.EXE
T1485.description:
Detects usage of the "cipher" built-in utility in order to overwrite deleted data from disk.
Adversaries may destroy data and files on specific systems or in large numbers on a network to interrupt availability to systems, services, and network resources.
Data destruction is likely to render stored
T1485.author: frack113

T1485.title: Fsutil Suspicious Invocation
T1485.description:
Detects suspicious parameters of fsutil (deleting USN journal, configuring it with small size, etc).
Might be used by ransomwares during the attack (seen by NotPetya and others).
T1485.author: Ecco, E.M. Anhaus, oscd.community

T1485.title: Renamed Sysinternals Sdelete Execution
T1485.description: Detects the use of a renamed SysInternals Sdelete, which is something an administrator shouldn't do (the renaming)
T1485.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1485.title: Potential File Overwrite Via Sysinternals SDelete
T1485.description: Detects the use of SDelete to erase a file not the free space
T1485.author: frack113

T1136.title: AWS ElastiCache Security Group Created
T1136.description: Detects when an ElastiCache security group has been created.
T1136.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

T1136.003.title: AWS ElastiCache Security Group Created
T1136.003.description: Detects when an ElastiCache security group has been created.
T1136.003.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

T1136.003.title: New Federated Domain Added - Exchange
T1136.003.description: Detects the addition of a new Federated Domain.
T1136.003.author: Splunk Threat Research Team (original rule), '@ionsor (rule)'

T1580.title: Potential Bucket Enumeration on AWS
T1580.description: Looks for potential enumeration of AWS buckets via ListBuckets.
T1580.author: Christopher Peacock @securepeacock, SCYTHE @scythe_io

T1619.title: Potential Bucket Enumeration on AWS
T1619.description: Looks for potential enumeration of AWS buckets via ListBuckets.
T1619.author: Christopher Peacock @securepeacock, SCYTHE @scythe_io

T1098.title: AWS IAM Backdoor Users Keys
T1098.description:
Detects AWS API key creation for a user by another user.
Backdoored users can be used to obtain persistence in the AWS environment.
Also with this alert, you can detect a flow of AWS keys in your org.
T1098.author: faloker

T1098.title: AWS Route 53 Domain Transfer Lock Disabled
T1098.description: Detects when a transfer lock was removed from a Route 53 domain. It is recommended to refrain from performing this action unless intending to transfer the domain to a different registrar.
T1098.author: Elastic, Austin Songer @austinsonger

T1098.title: AWS Route 53 Domain Transferred to Another Account
T1098.description: Detects when a request has been made to transfer a Route 53 domain to another AWS account.
T1098.author: Elastic, Austin Songer @austinsonger

T1098.title: AWS User Login Profile Was Modified
T1098.description:
Detects activity when someone is changing passwords on behalf of other users.
An attacker with the "iam:UpdateLoginProfile" permission on other users can change the password used to login to the AWS console on any user that already has a login profile setup.
T1098.author: toffeebr33k

T1098.title: Number Of Resource Creation Or Deployment Activities
T1098.description: Number of VM creations or deployment activities occur in Azure via the azureactivity log.
T1098.author: sawwinnnaung

T1098.title: Change to Authentication Method
T1098.description: Change to authentication method could be an indicator of an attacker adding an auth method to the account so they can have continued access.
T1098.author: AlertIQ

T1098.title: Bulk Deletion Changes To Privileged Account Permissions
T1098.description: Detects when a user is removed from a privileged role. Bulk changes should be investigated.
T1098.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Yochana Henderson, '@Yochana-H'

T1098.title: Anomalous User Activity
T1098.description: Indicates that there are anomalous patterns of behavior like suspicious changes to the directory.
T1098.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

T1098.title: GCP Access Policy Deleted
T1098.description:
Detects when an access policy that is applied to a GCP cloud resource is deleted.
An adversary would be able to remove access policies to gain access to a GCP cloud resource.
T1098.author: Bryan Lim

T1098.title: Google Workspace Granted Domain API Access
T1098.description: Detects when an API access service account is granted domain authority.
T1098.author: Austin Songer

T1098.title: Google Workspace User Granted Admin Privileges
T1098.description: Detects when an Google Workspace user is granted admin privileges.
T1098.author: Austin Songer

T1098.title: Cisco Local Accounts
T1098.description: Find local accounts being created or modified as well as remote authentication configurations
T1098.author: Austin Clark

T1098.title: Powerview Add-DomainObjectAcl DCSync AD Extend Right
T1098.description: Backdooring domain object to grant the rights associated with DCSync to a regular user or machine account using Powerview\Add-DomainObjectAcl DCSync Extended Right cmdlet, will allow to re-obtain the pwd hashes of any user/computer
T1098.author: Samir Bousseaden, Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g, oscd.community, Tim Shelton, Maxence Fossat

T1098.title: Enabled User Right in AD to Control User Objects
T1098.description: Detects scenario where if a user is assigned the SeEnableDelegationPrivilege right in Active Directory it would allow control of other AD user objects.
T1098.author: @neu5ron

T1098.title: Active Directory User Backdoors
T1098.description: Detects scenarios where one can control another users or computers account without having to use their credentials.
T1098.author: @neu5ron

T1098.title: A New Trust Was Created To A Domain
T1098.description: Addition of domains is seldom and should be verified for legitimacy.
T1098.author: Thomas Patzke

T1098.title: Password Change on Directory Service Restore Mode (DSRM) Account
T1098.description:
Detects potential attempts made to set the Directory Services Restore Mode administrator password.
The Directory Service Restore Mode (DSRM) account is a local administrator account on Domain Controllers.
Attackers may change the password in order to obtain persistence.
T1098.author: Thomas Patzke

T1098.title: User Added to Local Administrator Group
T1098.description: Detects the addition of a new member to the local administrator group, which could be legitimate activity or a sign of privilege escalation activity
T1098.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1098.title: A Member Was Added to a Security-Enabled Global Group
T1098.description: Detects activity when a member is added to a security-enabled global group
T1098.author: Alexandr Yampolskyi, SOC Prime

T1098.title: A Member Was Removed From a Security-Enabled Global Group
T1098.description: Detects activity when a member is removed from a security-enabled global group
T1098.author: Alexandr Yampolskyi, SOC Prime

T1098.title: A Security-Enabled Global Group Was Deleted
T1098.description: Detects activity when a security-enabled global group is deleted
T1098.author: Alexandr Yampolskyi, SOC Prime

T1098.title: DMSA Service Account Created in Specific OUs - PowerShell
T1098.description:
Detects the creation of a dMSA service account using the New-ADServiceAccount cmdlet in certain OUs.
The fact that the cmdlet is used to create a dMSASvc account in a specific OU is highly suspicious.
It is a pattern trying to exploit the BadSuccessor privilege escalation vulnerability in Windows Se
T1098.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1098.title: Powershell LocalAccount Manipulation
T1098.description:
Adversaries may manipulate accounts to maintain access to victim systems.
Account manipulation may consist of any action that preserves adversary access to a compromised account, such as modifying credentials or permission groups
T1098.author: frack113

T1098.title: DMSA Link Attributes Modified
T1098.description:
Detects modification of dMSA link attributes (msDS-ManagedAccountPrecededByLink) via PowerShell scripts.
This command line pattern could be an indicator an attempt to exploit the BadSuccessor privilege escalation vulnerability in Windows Server 2025.
T1098.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1098.title: New DMSA Service Account Created in Specific OUs
T1098.description:
Detects the creation of a dMSASvc account using the New-ADServiceAccount cmdlet in certain OUs.
The fact that the Cmdlet is used to create a dMSASvc account in a specific OU is highly suspicious.
It is a pattern trying to exploit the BadSuccessor privilege escalation vulnerability in Windows Server
T1098.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1098.title: User Added to Local Administrators Group
T1098.description: Detects addition of users to the local administrator group via "Net" or "Add-LocalGroupMember".
T1098.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1098.title: User Added To Highly Privileged Group
T1098.description: Detects addition of users to highly privileged groups via "Net" or "Add-LocalGroupMember".
T1098.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1098.title: Password Set to Never Expire via WMI
T1098.description: Detects the use of wmic.exe to modify user account settings and explicitly disable password expiration.
T1098.author: Daniel Koifman (KoifSec)

T1059.009.title: AWS IAM S3Browser LoginProfile Creation
T1059.009.description: Detects S3 Browser utility performing reconnaissance looking for existing IAM Users without a LoginProfile defined then (when found) creating a LoginProfile.
