T1059.description: Detects Clfs.sys being loaded by a process running from a potentially suspicious location. Clfs.sys is loaded as part of many CVEs exploits that targets Common Log File.
T1059.author: X__Junior

T1059.title: PCRE.NET Package Image Load
T1059.description: Detects processes loading modules related to PCRE.NET package
T1059.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)

T1059.title: Abusable DLL Potential Sideloading From Suspicious Location
T1059.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading of DLLs that are known to be abused from suspicious locations
T1059.author: X__Junior (Nextron Systems)

T1059.title: Windows Defender Exclusions Added - PowerShell
T1059.description: Detects modifications to the Windows Defender configuration settings using PowerShell to add exclusions
T1059.author: Tim Rauch, Elastic (idea)

T1059.title: Suspicious ArcSOC.exe Child Process
T1059.description:
Detects script interpreters, command-line tools, and similar suspicious child processes of ArcSOC.exe.
ArcSOC.exe is the process name which hosts ArcGIS Server REST services. If an attacker compromises an ArcGIS
Server system and uploads a malicious Server Object Extension (SOE), they can send craft
T1059.author: Micah Babinski

T1059.title: Potential Dosfuscation Activity
T1059.description: Detects possible payload obfuscation via the commandline
T1059.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1059.title: Unusual Parent Process For Cmd.EXE
T1059.description: Detects suspicious parent process for cmd.exe
T1059.author: Tim Rauch, Elastic (idea)

T1059.title: Conhost Spawned By Uncommon Parent Process
T1059.description: Detects when the Console Window Host (conhost.exe) process is spawned by an uncommon parent process, which could be indicative of potential code injection activity.
T1059.author: Tim Rauch, Elastic (idea)

T1059.title: Forfiles Command Execution
T1059.description:
Detects the execution of "forfiles" with the "/c" flag.
While this is an expected behavior of the tool, it can be abused in order to proxy execution through it with any binary.
Can be used to bypass application whitelisting.
T1059.author: Tim Rauch, Elastic, E.M. Anhaus (originally from Atomic Blue Detections, Endgame), oscd.community

T1059.title: Use of FSharp Interpreters
T1059.description:
Detects the execution of FSharp Interpreters "FsiAnyCpu.exe" and "FSi.exe"
Both can be used for AWL bypass and to execute F# code via scripts or inline.
T1059.author: Christopher Peacock @SecurePeacock, SCYTHE @scythe_io

T1059.title: Potentially Suspicious NTFS Symlink Behavior Modification
T1059.description: Detects the modification of NTFS symbolic link behavior using fsutil, which could be used to enable remote to local or remote to remote symlinks for potential attacks.
T1059.author: frack113, The DFIR Report

T1059.title: Potential Arbitrary Command Execution Via FTP.EXE
T1059.description: Detects execution of "ftp.exe" script with the "-s" or "/s" flag and any child processes ran by "ftp.exe".
T1059.author: Victor Sergeev, oscd.community

T1059.title: Potential CobaltStrike Process Patterns
T1059.description: Detects potential process patterns related to Cobalt Strike beacon activity
T1059.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1059.title: HackTool - Sliver C2 Implant Activity Pattern
T1059.description: Detects process activity patterns as seen being used by Sliver C2 framework implants
T1059.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1059.title: HackTool - Stracciatella Execution
T1059.description: Detects Stracciatella which executes a Powershell runspace from within C# (aka SharpPick technique) with AMSI, ETW and Script Block Logging disabled based on PE metadata characteristics.
T1059.author: pH-T (Nextron Systems)

T1059.title: Use of OpenConsole
T1059.description: Detects usage of OpenConsole binary as a LOLBIN to launch other binaries to bypass application Whitelisting
T1059.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1059.title: Use of Pcalua For Execution
T1059.description: Detects execition of commands and binaries from the context of The program compatibility assistant (Pcalua.exe). This can be used as a LOLBIN in order to bypass application whitelisting.
T1059.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), E.M. Anhaus (originally from Atomic Blue Detections, Endgame), oscd.community

T1059.title: Suspicious Runscripthelper.exe
T1059.description: Detects execution of powershell scripts via Runscripthelper.exe
T1059.author: Victor Sergeev, oscd.community

T1059.title: Wscript Shell Run In CommandLine
T1059.description: Detects the presence of the keywords "Wscript", "Shell" and "Run" in the command, which could indicate a suspicious activity
T1059.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1059.title: Outlook EnableUnsafeClientMailRules Setting Enabled
T1059.description: Detects an attacker trying to enable the outlook security setting "EnableUnsafeClientMailRules" which allows outlook to run applications or execute macros
T1059.author: Markus Neis, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1059.title: Suspicious Remote Child Process From Outlook
T1059.description: Detects a suspicious child process spawning from Outlook where the image is located in a remote location (SMB/WebDav shares).
T1059.author: Markus Neis, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1059.title: Perl Inline Command Execution
T1059.description: Detects execution of perl using the "-e"/"-E" flags. This is could be used as a way to launch a reverse shell or execute live perl code.
T1059.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1059.title: Php Inline Command Execution
T1059.description: Detects execution of php using the "-r" flag. This is could be used as a way to launch a reverse shell or execute live php code.
T1059.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1059.title: PowerShell Download and Execution Cradles
T1059.description: Detects PowerShell download and execution cradles.
T1059.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1059.title: Run PowerShell Script from Redirected Input Stream
T1059.description: Detects PowerShell script execution via input stream redirect
T1059.author: Moriarty Meng (idea), Anton Kutepov (rule), oscd.community

T1059.title: PUA - Wsudo Suspicious Execution
T1059.description: Detects usage of wsudo (Windows Sudo Utility). Which is a tool that let the user execute programs with different permissions (System, Trusted Installer, Administrator...etc)
T1059.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1059.title: Python Inline Command Execution
T1059.description: Detects execution of python using the "-c" flag. This is could be used as a way to launch a reverse shell or execute live python code.
T1059.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1059.title: Python Spawning Pretty TTY on Windows
T1059.description: Detects python spawning a pretty tty
T1059.author: Nextron Systems

T1059.title: Suspicious Greedy Compression Using Rar.EXE
T1059.description: Detects RAR usage that creates an archive from a suspicious folder, either a system folder or one of the folders often used by attackers for staging purposes
T1059.author: X__Junior (Nextron Systems), Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1059.title: Suspicious RASdial Activity
T1059.description: Detects suspicious process related to rasdial.exe
T1059.author: juju4

T1059.title: Renamed CURL.EXE Execution
T1059.description: Detects the execution of a renamed "CURL.exe" binary based on the PE metadata fields
T1059.author: X__Junior (Nextron Systems)

T1059.title: Renamed FTP.EXE Execution
T1059.description: Detects the execution of a renamed "ftp.exe" binary based on the PE metadata fields
T1059.author: Victor Sergeev, oscd.community

T1059.title: Renamed NirCmd.EXE Execution
T1059.description: Detects the execution of a renamed "NirCmd.exe" binary based on the PE metadata fields.
T1059.author: X__Junior (Nextron Systems)

T1059.title: Renamed PingCastle Binary Execution
T1059.description: Detects the execution of a renamed "PingCastle" binary based on the PE metadata fields.
T1059.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), X__Junior (Nextron Systems)

T1059.title: Ruby Inline Command Execution
T1059.description: Detects execution of ruby using the "-e" flag. This is could be used as a way to launch a reverse shell or execute live ruby code.
T1059.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1059.title: Elevated System Shell Spawned From Uncommon Parent Location
T1059.description: Detects when a shell program such as the Windows command prompt or PowerShell is launched with system privileges from a uncommon parent location.
T1059.author: frack113, Tim Shelton (update fp)

T1059.title: Potentially Suspicious Execution From Parent Process In Public Folder
T1059.description: Detects a potentially suspicious execution of a parent process located in the "\Users\Public" folder executing a child process containing references to shell or scripting binaries and commandlines.
T1059.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1059.title: Writing Of Malicious Files To The Fonts Folder
T1059.description: Monitors for the hiding possible malicious files in the C:\Windows\Fonts\ location. This folder doesn't require admin privillege to be written and executed from.
T1059.author: Sreeman

T1059.title: Suspicious Scan Loop Network
T1059.description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of other systems by IP address, hostname, or other logical identifier on a network that may be used for Lateral Movement from the current system
T1059.author: frack113

T1059.title: Suspicious Program Names
T1059.description: Detects suspicious patterns in program names or folders that are often found in malicious samples or hacktools
T1059.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1059.title: Script Interpreter Execution From Suspicious Folder
T1059.description:
Detects suspicious script execution from suspicious directories or folders accessible by environment variables that may indicate malware activity.
Script interpreters (cscript, wscript, mshta, powershell) executing from folders like Temp, Public, or user profile directories may suggest attempts to e
T1059.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1059.title: Sysprep on AppData Folder
T1059.description: Detects suspicious sysprep process start with AppData folder as target (as used by Trojan Syndicasec in Thrip report by Symantec)
T1059.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1059.title: Potential Persistence Via VMwareToolBoxCmd.EXE VM State Change Script
T1059.description: Detects execution of the "VMwareToolBoxCmd.exe" with the "script" and "set" flag to setup a specific script to run for a specific VM state
T1059.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1059.title: Suspicious Persistence Via VMwareToolBoxCmd.EXE VM State Change Script
T1059.description: Detects execution of the "VMwareToolBoxCmd.exe" with the "script" and "set" flag to setup a specific script that's located in a potentially suspicious location to run for a specific VM state
T1059.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1059.title: VMToolsd Suspicious Child Process
T1059.description: Detects suspicious child process creations of VMware Tools process which may indicate persistence setup
T1059.author: bohops, Bhabesh Raj

T1059.title: Add New Download Source To Winget
T1059.description: Detects usage of winget to add new additional download sources
T1059.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1059.title: Add Insecure Download Source To Winget
T1059.description:
Detects usage of winget to add a new insecure (http) download source.
Winget will not allow the addition of insecure sources, hence this could indicate potential suspicious activity (or typos)
T1059.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1059.title: Add Potential Suspicious New Download Source To Winget
T1059.description: Detects usage of winget to add new potentially suspicious download sources
T1059.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1059.title: Install New Package Via Winget Local Manifest
T1059.description:
Detects usage of winget to install applications via manifest file. Adversaries can abuse winget to download payloads remotely and execute them.
The manifest option enables you to install an application by passing in a YAML file directly to the client.
Winget can be used to download and install exe,
T1059.author: Sreeman, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), frack113

T1059.title: Installation of WSL Kali-Linux
T1059.description:
Detects installation of Kali Linux distribution through Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL).
Attackers may use Kali Linux WSL to leverage its penetration testing tools and capabilities for malicious purposes.
T1059.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1484.title: Changes to Device Registration Policy
T1484.description: Monitor and alert for changes to the device registration policy.
T1484.author: Michael Epping, '@mepples21'

T1098.001.title: Added Credentials to Existing Application
T1098.001.description: Detects when a new credential is added to an existing application. Any additional credentials added outside of expected processes could be a malicious actor using those credentials.
T1098.001.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Bailey Bercik '@baileybercik'

T1528.title: Delegated Permissions Granted For All Users
T1528.description: Detects when highly privileged delegated permissions are granted on behalf of all users
T1528.author: Bailey Bercik '@baileybercik', Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow'

T1528.title: End User Consent
T1528.description: Detects when an end user consents to an application
T1528.author: Bailey Bercik '@baileybercik', Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow'

T1528.title: End User Consent Blocked
T1528.description: Detects when end user consent is blocked due to risk-based consent.
T1528.author: Bailey Bercik '@baileybercik', Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow'

T1528.title: App Granted Microsoft Permissions
T1528.description: Detects when an application is granted delegated or app role permissions for Microsoft Graph, Exchange, Sharepoint, or Azure AD
T1528.author: Bailey Bercik '@baileybercik', Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow'

T1528.title: Application URI Configuration Changes
T1528.description:
Detects when a configuration change is made to an applications URI.
URIs for domain names that no longer exist (dangling URIs), not using HTTPS, wildcards at the end of the domain, URIs that are no unique to that app, or URIs that point to domains you do not control should be investigated.
T1528.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Bailey Bercik '@baileybercik'

T1528.title: Anomalous Token
T1528.description: Indicates that there are abnormal characteristics in the token such as an unusual token lifetime or a token that is played from an unfamiliar location.
T1528.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow'

T1528.title: Anonymous IP Address
T1528.description: Indicates sign-ins from an anonymous IP address, for example, using an anonymous browser or VPN.
T1528.author: Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

T1528.title: Primary Refresh Token Access Attempt
T1528.description: Indicates access attempt to the PRT resource which can be used to move laterally into an organization or perform credential theft
T1528.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

T1528.title: Suspicious Teams Application Related ObjectAcess Event
T1528.description: Detects an access to authentication tokens and accounts of Microsoft Teams desktop application.
T1528.author: @SerkinValery

T1528.title: Microsoft Teams Sensitive File Access By Uncommon Applications
T1528.description: Detects file access attempts to sensitive Microsoft teams files (leveldb, cookies) by an uncommon process.
T1528.author: @SerkinValery

T1528.title: HackTool - Koh Default Named Pipe
T1528.description: Detects creation of default named pipes used by the Koh tool
T1528.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1528.title: Renamed BrowserCore.EXE Execution
T1528.description: Detects process creation with a renamed BrowserCore.exe (used to extract Azure tokens)
T1528.author: Max Altgelt (Nextron Systems)

T1528.title: Potentially Suspicious JWT Token Search Via CLI
T1528.description:
Detects potentially suspicious search for JWT tokens via CLI by looking for the string "eyJ0eX" or "eyJhbG".
JWT tokens are often used for access-tokens across various applications and services like Microsoft 365, Azure, AWS, Google Cloud, and others.
Threat actors may search for these tokens to ste
T1528.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), kagebunsher

T1528.title: Potentially Suspicious Command Targeting Teams Sensitive Files
T1528.description:
Detects a commandline containing references to the Microsoft Teams database or cookies files from a process other than Teams.
The database might contain authentication tokens and other sensitive information about the logged in accounts.
T1528.author: @SerkinValery

T1098.005.title: Windows LAPS Credential Dump From Entra ID
T1098.005.description: Detects when an account dumps the LAPS password from Entra ID.
T1098.005.author: andrewdanis

T1114.003.title: Suspicious Inbox Forwarding Identity Protection
T1114.003.description: Indicates suspicious rules such as an inbox rule that forwards a copy of all emails to an external address
T1114.003.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

T1114.003.title: Google Workspace Out Of Domain Email Forwarding
T1114.003.description: Detects automatic email forwarding to external domains in Google Workspace, which may indicate data leakage or misuse.
T1114.003.author: Tom kluter

T1140.title: Suspicious Inbox Manipulation Rules
T1140.description: Detects suspicious rules that delete or move messages or folders are set on a user's inbox.
T1140.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

T1140.title: PowerShell Decompress Commands
T1140.description: A General detection for specific decompress commands in PowerShell logs. This could be an adversary decompressing files.
T1140.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)

T1140.title: MSHTA Execution with Suspicious File Extensions
T1140.description:
Detects execution of mshta.exe with file types that looks like they do not typically represent HTA (HTML Application) content,
such as .png, .jpg, .zip, .pdf, and others, which are often polyglots. MSHTA is a legitimate Windows utility for executing HTML Applications
containing VBScript or JScript.
T1140.author: Diego Perez (@darkquassar), Markus Neis, Swisscom (Improve Rule), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1140.title: Ping Hex IP
T1140.description: Detects a ping command that uses a hex encoded IP address
T1140.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1140.title: PowerShell Base64 Encoded FromBase64String Cmdlet
T1140.description: Detects usage of a base64 encoded "FromBase64String" cmdlet in a process command line
T1140.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1140.title: Base64 Encoded PowerShell Command Detected
T1140.description: Detects usage of the "FromBase64String" function in the commandline which is used to decode a base64 encoded string
T1140.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1140.title: Suspicious XOR Encoded PowerShell Command
T1140.description: Detects presence of a potentially xor encoded powershell command
T1140.author: Sami Ruohonen, Harish Segar, Tim Shelton, Teymur Kheirkhabarov, Vasiliy Burov, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali

T1140.title: Potential Commandline Obfuscation Using Escape Characters
T1140.description: Detects potential commandline obfuscation using known escape characters
T1140.author: juju4

T1140.title: DNS-over-HTTPS Enabled by Registry
T1140.description:
Detects when a user enables DNS-over-HTTPS.
This can be used to hide internet activity or be used to hide the process of exfiltrating data.
With this enabled organization will lose visibility into data such as query type, response and originating IP that are used to determine bad actors.
T1140.author: Austin Songer

T1589.title: Azure AD Account Credential Leaked
T1589.description: Indicates that the user's valid credentials have been leaked.
T1589.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

T1090.title: Malicious IP Address Sign-In Failure Rate
T1090.description: Indicates sign-in from a malicious IP address based on high failure rates.
T1090.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

T1090.title: Malicious IP Address Sign-In Suspicious
T1090.description: Indicates sign-in from a malicious IP address known to be malicious at time of sign-in.
T1090.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

T1090.title: Sign-In From Malware Infected IP
T1090.description: Indicates sign-ins from IP addresses infected with malware that is known to actively communicate with a bot server.
T1090.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

T1090.title: Ngrok Usage with Remote Desktop Service
T1090.description: Detects cases in which ngrok, a reverse proxy tool, forwards events to the local RDP port, which could be a sign of malicious behaviour
T1090.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1090.title: Communication To LocaltoNet Tunneling Service Initiated
T1090.description:
Detects an executable initiating a network connection to "LocaltoNet" tunneling sub-domains.
LocaltoNet is a reverse proxy that enables localhost services to be exposed to the Internet.
Attackers have been seen to use this service for command-and-control activities to bypass MFA and perimeter contro
T1090.author: Andreas Braathen (mnemonic.io)

T1090.title: Communication To Ngrok Tunneling Service Initiated
T1090.description:
Detects an executable initiating a network connection to "ngrok" tunneling domains.
Attackers were seen using this "ngrok" in order to store their second stage payloads and malware.
While communication with such domains can be legitimate, often times is a sign of either data exfiltration by maliciou
T1090.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1090.title: Suspicious TCP Tunnel Via PowerShell Script
T1090.description: Detects powershell scripts that creates sockets/listeners which could be indicative of tunneling activity
T1090.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1090.title: Cloudflared Tunnel Connections Cleanup
T1090.description: Detects execution of the "cloudflared" tool with the tunnel "cleanup" flag in order to cleanup tunnel connections.
T1090.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1090.title: Cloudflared Tunnel Execution
T1090.description: Detects execution of the "cloudflared" tool to connect back to a tunnel. This was seen used by threat actors to maintain persistence and remote access to compromised networks.
T1090.author: Janantha Marasinghe, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1090.title: HackTool - Htran/NATBypass Execution
T1090.description: Detects executable names or flags used by Htran or Htran-like tools (e.g. NATBypass)
T1090.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1090.title: New Port Forwarding Rule Added Via Netsh.EXE
T1090.description: Detects the execution of netsh commands that configure a new port forwarding (PortProxy) rule
T1090.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), omkar72, oscd.community, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel

T1090.title: RDP Port Forwarding Rule Added Via Netsh.EXE
T1090.description: Detects the execution of netsh to configure a port forwarding of port 3389 (RDP) rule
T1090.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), oscd.community

T1090.title: PUA - Fast Reverse Proxy (FRP) Execution
T1090.description: Detects the use of Fast Reverse Proxy. frp is a fast reverse proxy to help you expose a local server behind a NAT or firewall to the Internet.
T1090.author: frack113, Florian Roth

T1090.title: PUA- IOX Tunneling Tool Execution
T1090.description: Detects the use of IOX - a tool for port forwarding and intranet proxy purposes
T1090.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1090.title: PUA - NPS Tunneling Tool Execution
T1090.description: Detects the use of NPS, a port forwarding and intranet penetration proxy server
T1090.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1090.title: Potentially Suspicious Usage Of Qemu
T1090.description:
Detects potentially suspicious execution of the Qemu utility in a Windows environment.
Threat actors have leveraged this utility and this technique for achieving network access as reported by Kaspersky.
T1090.author: Muhammad Faisal (@faisalusuf), Hunter Juhan (@threatHNTR)

T1090.title: New PortProxy Registry Entry Added
T1090.description: Detects the modification of the PortProxy registry key which is used for port forwarding.
T1090.author: Andreas Hunkeler (@Karneades)

T1606.title: SAML Token Issuer Anomaly
T1606.description: Indicates the SAML token issuer for the associated SAML token is potentially compromised. The claims included in the token are unusual or match known attacker patterns
T1606.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

T1526.title: Discovery Using AzureHound
T1526.description: Detects AzureHound (A BloodHound data collector for Microsoft Azure) activity via the default User-Agent that is used during its operation after successful authentication.
T1526.author: Janantha Marasinghe

T1526.title: PUA - Seatbelt Execution
T1526.description: Detects the execution of the PUA/Recon tool Seatbelt via PE information of command line parameters
T1526.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1556.006.title: Azure AD Only Single Factor Authentication Required
T1556.006.description: Detect when users are authenticating without MFA being required.
T1556.006.author: MikeDuddington, '@dudders1'

T1556.006.title: Disabling Multi Factor Authentication
T1556.006.description: Detects disabling of Multi Factor Authentication.
T1556.006.author: Splunk Threat Research Team (original rule), Harjot Singh @cyb3rjy0t (sigma rule)

T1621.title: Multifactor Authentication Denied
T1621.description: User has indicated they haven't instigated the MFA prompt and could indicate an attacker has the password for the account.
T1621.author: AlertIQ

T1621.title: Multifactor Authentication Interrupted
T1621.description: Identifies user login with multifactor authentication failures, which might be an indication an attacker has the password for the account but can't pass the MFA challenge.
T1621.author: AlertIQ

T1074.title: Google Full Network Traffic Packet Capture
T1074.description: Identifies potential full network packet capture in gcp. This feature can potentially be abused to read sensitive data from unencrypted internal traffic.
T1074.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

T1074.title: Cisco Stage Data
T1074.description: Various protocols maybe used to put data on the device for exfil or infil
T1074.author: Austin Clark

T1484.002.title: New Federated Domain Added
T1484.002.description: Detects the addition of a new Federated Domain.
T1484.002.author: Splunk Threat Research Team (original rule), Harjot Singh @cyb3rjy0t (sigma rule)

T1566.001.title: Suspicious Email Delivered In Microsoft 365
T1566.001.description:
Detects instances where an email, identified as malicious or suspicious by the Microsoft Defender for Office 365 (formerly ATP) engine, was delivered to a user's Inbox or Junk folder.
It might indicate that a potential threat, such as a spearphishing attachment or links, has bypassed initial blockin
T1566.001.author: Marco Pedrinazzi (@pedrinazziM) (InTheCyber)

T1566.001.title: ISO Image Mounted
T1566.001.description: Detects the mount of an ISO image on an endpoint
T1566.001.author: Syed Hasan (@syedhasan009)

T1566.001.title: Password Protected ZIP File Opened (Email Attachment)
T1566.001.description: Detects the extraction of password protected ZIP archives. See the filename variable for more details on which file has been opened.
T1566.001.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1566.001.title: Potential Initial Access via DLL Search Order Hijacking
T1566.001.description: Detects attempts to create a DLL file to a known desktop application dependencies folder such as Slack, Teams or OneDrive and by an unusual process. This may indicate an attempt to load a malicious module via DLL search order hijacking.
T1566.001.author: Tim Rauch (rule), Elastic (idea)

T1566.001.title: ISO File Created Within Temp Folders
T1566.001.description: Detects the creation of a ISO file in the Outlook temp folder or in the Appdata temp folder. Typical of Qakbot TTP from end-July 2022.
T1566.001.author: @sam0x90

T1566.001.title: ISO or Image Mount Indicator in Recent Files
T1566.001.description:
Detects the creation of recent element file that points to an .ISO, .IMG, .VHD or .VHDX file as often used in phishing attacks.
This can be a false positive on server systems but on workstations users should rarely mount .iso or .img files.
T1566.001.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1566.001.title: Office Macro File Creation
T1566.001.description: Detects the creation of a new office macro files on the systems
T1566.001.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1566.001.title: Office Macro File Download
T1566.001.description:
Detects the creation of a new office macro files on the system via an application (browser, mail client).
This can help identify potential malicious activity, such as the download of macro-enabled documents that could be used for exploitation.
T1566.001.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1566.001.title: Office Macro File Creation From Suspicious Process
T1566.001.description: Detects the creation of a office macro file from a a suspicious process
T1566.001.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1566.001.title: Suspicious File Created in Outlook Temporary Directory
T1566.001.description:
Detects the creation of files with suspicious file extensions in the temporary directory that Outlook uses when opening attachments.
This can be used to detect spear-phishing campaigns that use suspicious files as attachments, which may contain malicious code.
T1566.001.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1566.001.title: HTML Help HH.EXE Suspicious Child Process
T1566.001.description: Detects a suspicious child process of a Microsoft HTML Help (HH.exe)
T1566.001.author: Maxim Pavlunin, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1566.001.title: Suspicious HH.EXE Execution
T1566.001.description: Detects a suspicious execution of a Microsoft HTML Help (HH.exe)
T1566.001.author: Maxim Pavlunin

T1566.001.title: Suspicious HWP Sub Processes
T1566.001.description: Detects suspicious Hangul Word Processor (Hanword) sub processes that could indicate an exploitation
T1566.001.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1566.001.title: Suspicious Microsoft OneNote Child Process
T1566.001.description: Detects suspicious child processes of the Microsoft OneNote application. This may indicate an attempt to execute malicious embedded objects from a .one file.
T1566.001.author: Tim Rauch (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Elastic (idea)

T1566.001.title: Suspicious Execution From Outlook Temporary Folder
T1566.001.description: Detects a suspicious program execution in Outlook temp folder
T1566.001.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1566.001.title: Arbitrary Shell Command Execution Via Settingcontent-Ms
T1566.001.description: The .SettingContent-ms file type was introduced in Windows 10 and allows a user to create "shortcuts" to various Windows 10 setting pages. These files are simply XML and contain paths to various Windows 10 settings binaries.
T1566.001.author: Sreeman

T1566.001.title: Suspicious Double Extension File Execution
T1566.001.description: Detects suspicious use of an .exe extension after a non-executable file extension like .pdf.exe, a set of spaces or underlines to cloak the executable file in spear phishing campaigns
T1566.001.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), @blu3_team (idea), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1566.001.title: Windows Registry Trust Record Modification
T1566.001.description: Alerts on trust record modification within the registry, indicating usage of macros
T1566.001.author: Antonlovesdnb, Trent Liffick (@tliffick)

T1573.title: Activity from Suspicious IP Addresses
T1573.description:
Detects when a Microsoft Cloud App Security reported users were active from an IP address identified as risky by Microsoft Threat Intelligence.
These IP addresses are involved in malicious activities, such as Botnet C&C, and may indicate compromised account.
T1573.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

T1573.title: Activity from Anonymous IP Addresses
T1573.description: Detects when a Microsoft Cloud App Security reported when users were active from an IP address that has been identified as an anonymous proxy IP address.
T1573.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

T1573.title: Activity from Infrequent Country
T1573.description: Detects when a Microsoft Cloud App Security reported when an activity occurs from a location that wasn't recently or never visited by any user in the organization.
T1573.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

T1573.title: Suspicious SSL Connection
T1573.description: Adversaries may employ a known encryption algorithm to conceal command and control traffic rather than relying on any inherent protections provided by a communication protocol.

T1114.title: PST Export Alert Using New-ComplianceSearchAction
T1114.description: Alert when a user has performed an export to a search using 'New-ComplianceSearchAction' with the '-Export' flag. This detection will detect PST export even if the 'eDiscovery search or exported' alert is disabled in the O365.This rule will apply to ExchangePowerShell usage and from the cloud.

T1114.title: Hacktool Ruler

T1114.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1114.title: Exchange PowerShell Snap-Ins Usage

T1199.title: Microsoft 365 - User Restricted from Sending Email

T1199.author: austinsonger

T1070.003.title: Cisco Clear Logs

T1070.003.title: Clear PowerShell History - PowerShell
T1070.003.description: Detects keywords that could indicate clearing PowerShell history
T1070.003.author: Ilyas Ochkov, Jonhnathan Ribeiro, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, oscd.community

T1070.003.title: Disable Powershell Command History

T1070.003.author: Ali Alwashali

T1070.003.title: Suspicious IO.FileStream
T1070.003.description: Open a handle on the drive volume via the \\.\ DOS device path specifier and perform direct access read of the first few bytes of the volume.
T1070.003.author: frack113

T1070.003.title: RunMRU Registry Key Deletion
T1070.003.description:
Detects deletion of the RunMRU registry key, which stores the history of commands executed via the Run dialog.
In the clickfix techniques, the phishing lures instruct users to open a run dialog through (Win + R) and execute malicious commands.
Adversaries may delete this key to cover their tracks af
T1070.003.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1070.003.title: RunMRU Registry Key Deletion - Registry
T1070.003.description:
Detects attempts to delete the RunMRU registry key, which stores the history of commands executed via the run dialog.
In the clickfix techniques, the phishing lures instruct users to open a run dialog through (Win + R) and execute malicious commands.
Adversaries may delete this key to cover their tr
T1070.003.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

Check if the user that executed the commands is suspicious (e.g. service accounts, LOCAL_SYSTEM)

T1087.001.title: Suspicious Reconnaissance Activity Using Get-LocalGroupMember Cmdlet
T1087.001.description: Detects suspicious reconnaissance command line activity on Windows systems using the PowerShell Get-LocalGroupMember Cmdlet
T1087.001.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1087.001.title: Malicious PowerShell Commandlets - ProcessCreation

Adversaries may install a root certificate on a compromised system to avoid warnings when connecting to adversary controlled web servers.

Detects execution of "certutil" with the "addstore" flag in order to install a new certificate on the system.
Adversaries may install a root certificate on a compromised system to avoid warnings when connecting to adversary controlled web servers.

T1553.004.title: Root Certificate Installed From Susp Locations

T1552.004.title: PowerShell Get-Process LSASS
T1552.004.description: Detects a "Get-Process" cmdlet and it's aliases on lsass process, which is in almost all cases a sign of malicious activity

T1552.004.title: Private Keys Reconnaissance Via CommandLine Tools

T1003.003.title: Sensitive File Dump Via Print.EXE
T1003.003.description: Detects the abuse of the Print.exe utility for credential harvesting which involves using Print.Exe to copy sensitive files such as ntds.dit, SAM, SECURITY, or SYSTEM from the Windows directory in order to extract credentials, locally or remotely.

T1003.003.title: Sensitive File Dump Via Wbadmin.EXE

T1003.003.title: Sensitive File Recovery From Backup Via Wbadmin.EXE

T1003.001.description: Detects remote thread creation by PowerShell processes into "lsass.exe"
T1003.001.author: oscd.community, Natalia Shornikova

T1003.001.title: Password Dumper Remote Thread in LSASS
T1003.001.description:
Detects password dumper activity by monitoring remote thread creation EventID 8 in combination with the lsass.exe process as TargetImage.
The process in field Process is the malicious program. A single execution can lead to hundreds of events.

T1003.001.description: Detects the creation of the default dump file used by Outflank Dumpert tool. A process dumper, which dumps the lsass process memory

T1003.001.title: HackTool - SafetyKatz Dump Indicator
T1003.001.description: Detects default lsass dump filename generated by SafetyKatz.

T1003.001.title: HackTool - Impacket File Indicators
T1003.001.description: Detects file creation events with filename patterns used by Impacket.

T1003.001.title: LSASS Process Memory Dump Files
T1003.001.description: Detects creation of files with names used by different memory dumping tools to create a memory dump of the LSASS process memory, which contains user credentials.
T1003.001.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1003.001.title: LSASS Process Dump Artefact In CrashDumps Folder
T1003.001.description: Detects the presence of an LSASS dump file in the "CrashDumps" folder. This could be a sign of LSASS credential dumping. Techniques such as the LSASS Shtinkering have been seen abusing the Windows Error Reporting to dump said process.
T1003.001.author: @pbssubhash

T1003.001.title: WerFault LSASS Process Memory Dump
T1003.001.description: Detects WerFault creating a dump file with a name that indicates that the dump file could be an LSASS process memory, which contains user credentials
T1003.001.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1003.001.title: LSASS Process Memory Dump Creation Via Taskmgr.EXE
T1003.001.description: Detects the creation of an "lsass.dmp" file by the taskmgr process. This indicates a manual dumping of the LSASS.exe process memory using Windows Task Manager.
T1003.001.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel

T1003.001.title: Suspicious Renamed Comsvcs DLL Loaded By Rundll32
T1003.001.description: Detects rundll32 loading a renamed comsvcs.dll to dump process memory
T1003.001.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1003.001.title: Suspicious Unsigned Dbghelp/Dbgcore DLL Loaded
T1003.001.description:
Detects the load of dbghelp/dbgcore DLL (used to make memory dumps) by suspicious processes.
Tools like ProcessHacker and some attacker tradecract use MiniDumpWriteDump API found in dbghelp.dll or dbgcore.dll.
As an example, SilentTrynity C2 Framework has a module that leverages this API to dump the
T1003.001.author: Perez Diego (@darkquassar), oscd.community, Ecco

T1003.001.title: Time Travel Debugging Utility Usage - Image
T1003.001.description: Detects usage of Time Travel Debugging Utility. Adversaries can execute malicious processes and dump processes, such as lsass.exe, via tttracer.exe.
T1003.001.author: Ensar Şamil, @sblmsrsn, @oscd_initiative

T1003.001.title: Unsigned Image Loaded Into LSASS Process
T1003.001.description: Loading unsigned image (DLL, EXE) into LSASS process
T1003.001.author: Teymur Kheirkhabarov, oscd.community

T1003.001.title: HackTool - Credential Dumping Tools Named Pipe Created
T1003.001.description: Detects well-known credential dumping tools execution via specific named pipe creation
T1003.001.author: Teymur Kheirkhabarov, oscd.community

T1003.001.title: PowerShell Get-Process LSASS in ScriptBlock
T1003.001.description: Detects a Get-Process command on lsass process, which is in almost all cases a sign of malicious activity

T1003.001.title: HackTool - Generic Process Access
T1003.001.description: Detects process access requests from hacktool processes based on their default image name
T1003.001.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel

T1003.001.title: HackTool - HandleKatz Duplicating LSASS Handle
T1003.001.description: Detects HandleKatz opening LSASS to duplicate its handle to later dump the memory without opening any new handles
T1003.001.author: Bhabesh Raj (rule), @thefLinkk

T1003.001.title: Lsass Memory Dump via Comsvcs DLL
T1003.001.description: Detects adversaries leveraging the MiniDump export function from comsvcs.dll via rundll32 to perform a memory dump from lsass.
T1003.001.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)

T1003.001.title: LSASS Memory Access by Tool With Dump Keyword In Name
T1003.001.description: Detects LSASS process access requests from a source process with the "dump" keyword in its image name.
T1003.001.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1003.001.title: Potential Credential Dumping Activity Via LSASS
T1003.001.description:
Detects process access requests to the LSASS process with specific call trace calls and access masks.
This behaviour is expressed by many credential dumping tools such as Mimikatz, NanoDump, Invoke-Mimikatz, Procdump and even the Taskmgr dumping feature.
T1003.001.author: Samir Bousseaden, Michael Haag

T1003.001.title: Credential Dumping Activity By Python Based Tool
T1003.001.description: Detects LSASS process access for potential credential dumping by a Python-like tool such as LaZagne or Pypykatz.
T1003.001.author: Bhabesh Raj, Jonhnathan Ribeiro

T1003.001.title: Remote LSASS Process Access Through Windows Remote Management
T1003.001.description: Detects remote access to the LSASS process via WinRM. This could be a sign of credential dumping from tools like mimikatz.
T1003.001.author: Patryk Prauze - ING Tech

T1003.001.title: Suspicious LSASS Access Via MalSecLogon
T1003.001.description: Detects suspicious access to LSASS handle via a call trace to "seclogon.dll" with a suspicious access right.
T1003.001.author: Samir Bousseaden (original elastic rule), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1003.001.title: Potentially Suspicious GrantedAccess Flags On LSASS
T1003.001.description: Detects process access requests to LSASS process with potentially suspicious access flags
T1003.001.author: Florian Roth, Roberto Rodriguez, Dimitrios Slamaris, Mark Russinovich, Thomas Patzke, Teymur Kheirkhabarov, Sherif Eldee

T1003.001.title: Credential Dumping Attempt Via WerFault
T1003.001.description: Detects process LSASS memory dump using Mimikatz, NanoDump, Invoke-Mimikatz, Procdump or Taskmgr based on the CallTrace pointing to ntdll.dll, dbghelp.dll or dbgcore.dll for win10, server2016 and up.
T1003.001.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1003.001.title: LSASS Access From Potentially White-Listed Processes
T1003.001.description: Detects a possible process memory dump that uses a white-listed filename like TrolleyExpress.exe as a way to dump the LSASS process memory without Microsoft Defender interference
T1003.001.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1003.001.title: Suspicious Process Access to LSASS with Dbgcore/Dbghelp DLLs
T1003.001.description:
Detects suspicious process access to LSASS.exe from processes located in uncommon locations with dbgcore.dll or dbghelp.dll in the call trace.
These DLLs contain functions like MiniDumpWriteDump that can be abused for credential dumping purposes. While modern tools like Mimikatz have moved to using
T1003.001.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1003.001.title: Potential Adplus.EXE Abuse
T1003.001.description: Detects execution of "AdPlus.exe", a binary that is part of the Windows SDK that can be used as a LOLBIN in order to dump process memory and execute arbitrary commands.
T1003.001.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1003.001.title: Process Access via TrolleyExpress Exclusion
T1003.001.description: Detects a possible process memory dump that uses the white-listed Citrix TrolleyExpress.exe filename as a way to dump the lsass process memory
T1003.001.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1003.001.title: CreateDump Process Dump
T1003.001.description: Detects uses of the createdump.exe LOLOBIN utility to dump process memory
T1003.001.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1003.001.title: Potential Windows Defender AV Bypass Via Dump64.EXE Rename
T1003.001.description:
Detects when a user is potentially trying to bypass the Windows Defender AV by renaming a tool to dump64.exe and placing it in the Visual Studio folder.
Currently the rule is covering only usage of procdump but other utilities can be added in order to increase coverage.
T1003.001.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1003.001.title: DumpMinitool Execution
T1003.001.description: Detects the use of "DumpMinitool.exe" a tool that allows the dump of process memory via the use of the "MiniDumpWriteDump"
T1003.001.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1003.001.title: Suspicious DumpMinitool Execution
T1003.001.description: Detects suspicious ways to use the "DumpMinitool.exe" binary
T1003.001.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1003.001.title: HackTool - CrackMapExec Process Patterns
T1003.001.description: Detects suspicious process patterns found in logs when CrackMapExec is used
T1003.001.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1003.001.title: HackTool - CreateMiniDump Execution
T1003.001.description: Detects the use of CreateMiniDump hack tool used to dump the LSASS process memory for credential extraction on the attacker's machine
T1003.001.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1003.001.title: HackTool - Doppelanger LSASS Dumper Execution
T1003.001.description: Detects the execution of the Doppelanger hacktool which is used to dump LSASS memory via process cloning while evading common detection methods
T1003.001.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1003.001.title: HackTool - Dumpert Process Dumper Execution
T1003.001.description: Detects the use of Dumpert process dumper, which dumps the lsass.exe process memory
T1003.001.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1003.001.title: HackTool - HandleKatz LSASS Dumper Execution
T1003.001.description: Detects the use of HandleKatz, a tool that demonstrates the usage of cloned handles to Lsass in order to create an obfuscated memory dump of the same
T1003.001.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1003.001.title: HackTool - Inveigh Execution
T1003.001.description: Detects the use of Inveigh a cross-platform .NET IPv4/IPv6 machine-in-the-middle tool
T1003.001.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1003.001.title: HackTool - Mimikatz Execution
T1003.001.description: Detection well-known mimikatz command line arguments
T1003.001.author: Teymur Kheirkhabarov, oscd.community, David ANDRE (additional keywords), Tim Shelton

T1003.001.title: HackTool - SafetyKatz Execution
T1003.001.description: Detects the execution of the hacktool SafetyKatz via PE information and default Image name
T1003.001.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1003.001.title: HackTool - Windows Credential Editor (WCE) Execution
T1003.001.description:
Detects the use of Windows Credential Editor (WCE), a popular post-exploitation tool used to extract plaintext passwords, hash, PIN code and Kerberos tickets from memory.
It is often used by threat actors for credential dumping and lateral movement within compromised networks.
T1003.001.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1003.001.title: HackTool - WSASS Execution
T1003.001.description:
Detects execution of WSASS, a tool used to dump LSASS memory on Windows systems by leveraging WER's
(Windows Error Reporting) WerFaultSecure.EXE to bypass PPL (Protected Process Light) protections.
T1003.001.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1003.001.title: HackTool - XORDump Execution
T1003.001.description: Detects suspicious use of XORDump process memory dumping utility
T1003.001.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1003.001.title: Dumping Process via Sqldumper.exe
T1003.001.description: Detects process dump via legitimate sqldumper.exe binary

T1003.001.title: Time Travel Debugging Utility Usage
T1003.001.description: Detects usage of Time Travel Debugging Utility. Adversaries can execute malicious processes and dump processes, such as lsass.exe, via tttracer.exe.
T1003.001.author: Ensar Şamil, @sblmsrsn, @oscd_initiative

T1003.001.description: Detects a suspicious LSASS process process clone that could be a sign of credential dumping activity
T1003.001.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Samir Bousseaden

T1003.001.title: PUA - Memory Dump Mount Via MemProcFS
T1003.001.description:
Detects execution of MemProcFS a memory forensics tool with the '-device' parameter.
MemProcFS mounts physical memory as a virtual file system, allowing direct access to process memory and system structures.
Threat actors were seen abusing this utility to mount memory dumps and then extract sensitiv
T1003.001.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1003.001.title: Process Memory Dump via RdrLeakDiag.EXE
T1003.001.description: Detects the use of the Microsoft Windows Resource Leak Diagnostic tool "rdrleakdiag.exe" to dump process memory
T1003.001.author: Cedric MAURUGEON, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1003.001.title: Renamed CreateDump Utility Execution
T1003.001.description: Detects uses of a renamed legitimate createdump.exe LOLOBIN utility to dump process memory
T1003.001.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1003.001.description: Detects a process memory dump via "comsvcs.dll" using rundll32, covering multiple different techniques (ordinal, minidump function, etc.)

T1003.001.title: Procdump Execution
T1003.001.description: Detects usage of the SysInternals Procdump utility

T1003.001.description: Detects uses of the SysInternals ProcDump utility in which ProcDump or its output get renamed, or a dump file is moved or copied to a different name

T1003.001.description:
Detects potential credential harvesting attempts through LSASS memory dumps using ProcDump.
This rule identifies suspicious command-line patterns that combine memory dump flags (-ma, -mm, -mp) with LSASS-related process markers.
LSASS (Local Security Authority Subsystem Service) contains sensitive a

T1003.001.description:
Detects potential abuse of WerFaultSecure.exe to dump Protected Process Light (PPL) processes like LSASS or to freeze security solutions (EDR/antivirus).

T1003.001.title: Potential Credential Dumping Via WER
T1003.001.description: Detects potential credential dumping via Windows Error Reporting LSASS Shtinkering technique which uses the Windows Error Reporting to dump lsass
T1003.001.author: @pbssubhash , Nasreddine Bencherchali

T1003.001.title: Windows Credential Editor Registry
T1003.001.description: Detects the use of Windows Credential Editor (WCE)
T1003.001.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1003.001.title: Potential Credential Dumping Via LSASS SilentProcessExit Technique
T1003.001.description: Detects changes to the Registry in which a monitor program gets registered to dump the memory of the lsass.exe process

T1003.001.description: Detects the setting of the "DumpType" registry value to "2" which stands for a "Full Dump". Technique such as LSASS Shtinkering requires this value to be "2" in order to dump LSASS.

T1558.003.title: Kerberos Network Traffic RC4 Ticket Encryption
T1558.003.description: Detects kerberos TGS request using RC4 encryption which may be indicative of kerberoasting

T1558.003.description:

T1558.003.title: HackTool - Rubeus Execution

T1558.003.title: Suspicious Kerberos Ticket Request via CLI
T1558.003.description:

perform offline password cracking attacks commonly known as
T1558.003.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1558.003.title: Potential SPN Enumeration Via Setspn.EXE

T1003.006.title: Suspicious Get-ADReplAccount
T1003.006.description:
The DSInternals PowerShell Module exposes several internal features of Active Directory and Azure Active Directory.
These include FIDO2 and NGC key auditing, offline ntds.dit file manipulation, password auditing, DC recovery from IFM backups and password hash calculation.
T1003.006.author: frack113

T1003.006.title: HackTool - Mimikatz Execution
T1003.006.description: Detection well-known mimikatz command line arguments
T1003.006.author: Teymur Kheirkhabarov, oscd.community, David ANDRE (additional keywords), Tim Shelton

Detects an office application (Word, Excel, PowerPoint)  that initiate a network connection to a non-private IP addresses.
This rule aims to detect traffic similar to one seen exploited in CVE-2021-42292.
This rule will require an initial baseline and tuning that is specific to your organization.

T1068.description:
Detects creation of the Process Explorer drivers by processes other than Process Explorer (procexp) itself.
Hack tools or malware may use the Process Explorer driver to elevate privileges, drops it to disk for a few moments, runs a service using that driver and removes it afterwards.

T1068.description:
Detects the execution of SharpSuccessor, a tool used to exploit the BadSuccessor attack for privilege escalation in WinServer 2025 Active Directory environments.
Successful usage of this tool can let the attackers gain the domain admin privileges by exploiting the BadSuccessor vulnerability.

T1210.description:
Detects the execution of SharpWSUS or WSUSpendu, utilities that allow for lateral movement through WSUS.
Windows Server Update Services (WSUS) is a critical component of Windows systems and is frequently configured in a way that allows an attacker to circumvent internal networking limitations.
T1210.author: @Kostastsale, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1210.title: Suspicious SysAidServer Child
T1210.description: Detects suspicious child processes of SysAidServer (as seen in MERCURY threat actor intrusions)

T1072.description: Csi.exe is a signed binary from Microsoft that comes with Visual Studio and provides C# interactive capabilities. T1218.title: Self Extraction Directive File Created In Potentially Suspicious Location
T1218.description:
Detects the creation of Self Extraction Directive files (.sed) in a potentially suspicious location.
These files are used by the "iexpress.exe" utility in order to create self extracting packages.
Attackers were seen abusing this utility and creating PE files with embedded ".sed" entries.

T1218.title: Created Files by Microsoft Sync Center

T1218.description: Detects programs on a Windows system that should not write an archive to disk
T1218.author: frack113, Florian Roth

T1218.title: Legitimate Application Dropped Executable
T1218.description: Detects programs on a Windows system that should not write executables to disk
T1218.author: frack113, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Legitimate Application Writing Files In Uncommon Location
T1218.description:
Detects legitimate applications writing any type of file to uncommon or suspicious locations that are not typical for application data storage or execution.
Adversaries may leverage legitimate applications (Living off the Land Binaries - LOLBins) to drop or download malicious files to uncommon locat
T1218.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Legitimate Application Dropped Script
T1218.description: Detects programs on a Windows system that should not write scripts to disk
T1218.author: frack113, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Potentially Suspicious Self Extraction Directive File Created
T1218.description:
Detects the creation of a binary file with the ".sed" extension. The ".sed" extension stand for Self Extraction Directive files.
These files are used by the "iexpress.exe" utility in order to create self extracting packages.
Attackers were seen abusing this utility and creating PE files with embedde

T1218.title: Potential DLL Sideloading Using Coregen.exe
T1218.description: Detect usage of the "coregen.exe" (Microsoft CoreCLR Native Image Generator) binary to sideload arbitrary DLLs.

T1218.description:

This technique abuses COM Classes configured as INTERACTIVE USER to spawn processes

T1218.title: Network Connection Initiated By AddinUtil.EXE
T1218.description:
Detects a network connection initiated by the Add-In deployment cache updating utility "AddInutil.exe".
This could indicate a potential command and control communication as this tool doesn't usually initiate network activity.

T1218.title: Microsoft Sync Center Suspicious Network Connections
T1218.description: Detects suspicious connections from Microsoft Sync Center to non-private IPs.

T1218.title: Potentially Suspicious Wuauclt Network Connection
T1218.description:
Detects the use of the Windows Update Client binary (wuauclt.exe) to proxy execute code and making network connections.
One could easily make the DLL spawn a new process and inject to it to proxy the network connection and bypass this rule.
T1218.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)

T1218.title: Potential RemoteFXvGPUDisablement.EXE Abuse
T1218.description: Detects PowerShell module creation where the module Contents are set to "function Get-VMRemoteFXPhysicalVideoAdapter". This could be a sign of potential abuse of  the "RemoteFXvGPUDisablement.exe" binary which is known to be vulnerable to module load-order hijacking.

T1218.title: Potential RemoteFXvGPUDisablement.EXE Abuse - PowerShell Module
T1218.description: Detects PowerShell module creation where the module Contents are set to "function Get-VMRemoteFXPhysicalVideoAdapter". This could be a sign of potential abuse of the "RemoteFXvGPUDisablement.exe" binary which is known to be vulnerable to module load-order hijacking.

T1218.title: SyncAppvPublishingServer Bypass Powershell Restriction - PS Module

T1218.title: Potential RemoteFXvGPUDisablement.EXE Abuse - PowerShell ScriptBlock
T1218.description: Detects PowerShell module creation where the module Contents are set to "function Get-VMRemoteFXPhysicalVideoAdapter". This could be a sign of potential abuse of the "RemoteFXvGPUDisablement.exe" binary which is known to be vulnerable to module load-order hijacking.

T1218.description: Detects execution of the Add-In deployment cache updating utility (AddInutil.exe) with suspicious Addinroot or Pipelineroot paths. An adversary may execute AddinUtil.exe with uncommon Addinroot/Pipelineroot paths that point to the adversaries Addins.Store payload.

T1218.description: Detects uncommon child processes of the Add-In deployment cache updating utility (AddInutil.exe) which could be a sign of potential abuse of the binary to proxy execution via a custom Addins.Store payload.
T1218.author: Michael McKinley (@McKinleyMike), Tony Latteri (@TheLatteri)

T1218.title: Uncommon AddinUtil.EXE CommandLine Execution
T1218.description: Detects execution of the Add-In deployment cache updating utility (AddInutil.exe) with uncommon Addinroot or Pipelineroot paths. An adversary may execute AddinUtil.exe with uncommon Addinroot/Pipelineroot paths that point to the adversaries Addins.Store payload.

T1218.title: AddinUtil.EXE Execution From Uncommon Directory
T1218.description: Detects execution of the Add-In deployment cache updating utility (AddInutil.exe) from a non-standard directory.

T1218.title: AgentExecutor PowerShell Execution
T1218.description: Detects execution of the AgentExecutor.exe binary. Which can be abused as a LOLBIN to execute powershell scripts with the ExecutionPolicy "Bypass" or any binary named "powershell.exe" located in the path provided by 6th positional argument
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), memory-shards

T1218.title: Suspicious AgentExecutor PowerShell Execution
T1218.description: Detects execution of the AgentExecutor.exe binary. Which can be abused as a LOLBIN to execute powershell scripts with the ExecutionPolicy "Bypass" or any binary named "powershell.exe" located in the path provided by 6th positional argument
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), memory-shards

Detects uncommon child processes of Appvlp.EXE
Appvlp or the Application Virtualization Utility is included with Microsoft Office. Attackers are able to abuse "AppVLP" to execute shell commands.
Normally, this binary is used for Application Virtualization, but it can also be abused to circumvent the
T1218.author: Sreeman

T1218.title: Uncommon  Assistive Technology Applications Execution Via AtBroker.EXE
T1218.description: Detects the start of a non built-in assistive technology applications via "Atbroker.EXE".
T1218.author: Mateusz Wydra, oscd.community

T1218.title: Suspicious BitLocker Access Agent Update Utility Execution
T1218.description:
Detects the execution of the BitLocker Access Agent Update Utility (baaupdate.exe) which is not a common parent process for other processes.
Suspicious child processes spawned by baaupdate.exe could indicate an attempt at lateral movement via BitLocker DCOM & COM Hijacking.
T1218.author: andrewdanis, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Suspicious Child Process Of BgInfo.EXE
T1218.description: Detects suspicious child processes of "BgInfo.exe" which could be a sign of potential abuse of the binary to proxy execution via external VBScript
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Uncommon Child Process Of BgInfo.EXE
T1218.description: Detects uncommon child processes of "BgInfo.exe" which could be a sign of potential abuse of the binary to proxy execution via external VBScript
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Beyu Denis, oscd.community

T1218.title: BitLockerTogo.EXE Execution
T1218.description:
Detects the execution of "BitLockerToGo.EXE".
BitLocker To Go is BitLocker Drive Encryption on removable data drives. This feature includes the encryption of, USB flash drives, SD cards, External hard disk drives, Other drives that are formatted by using the NTFS, FAT16, FAT32, or exFAT file system.
T1218.author: Josh Nickels, mttaggart

T1218.title: Potential Binary Proxy Execution Via Cdb.EXE
T1218.description: Detects usage of "cdb.exe" to launch arbitrary processes or commands from a debugger script file

T1218.title: DLL Loaded via CertOC.EXE

T1218.title: Suspicious DLL Loaded via CertOC.EXE
