T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Potential NTLM Coercion Via Certutil.EXE
T1218.description: Detects possible NTLM coercion via certutil using the 'syncwithWU' flag
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Potential Arbitrary File Download Via Cmdl32.EXE
T1218.description:
Detects execution of Cmdl32 with the "/vpn" and "/lan" flags.
Attackers can abuse this utility in order to download arbitrary files via a configuration file.
Inspect the location and the content of the file passed as an argument in order to determine if it is suspicious.
T1218.author: frack113

T1218.title: Curl Download And Execute Combination
T1218.description: Adversaries can use curl to download payloads remotely and execute them. Curl is included by default in Windows 10 build 17063 and later.
T1218.author: Sreeman, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Potentially Suspicious CMD Shell Output Redirect
T1218.description:
Detects inline Windows shell commands redirecting output via the ">" symbol to a suspicious location.
This technique is sometimes used by malicious actors in order to redirect the output of reconnaissance commands such as "hostname" and "dir" to files for future exfiltration.
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Potentially Suspicious Child Processes Spawned by ConHost
T1218.description: Detects suspicious child processes related to Windows Shell utilities spawned by `conhost.exe`, which could indicate malicious activity using trusted system components.
T1218.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Suspicious Csi.exe Usage
T1218.description: Csi.exe is a signed binary from Microsoft that comes with Visual Studio and provides C# interactive capabilities. It can be used to run C# code from a file passed as a parameter in command line. Early version of this utility provided with Microsoft “Roslyn” Community Technology Preview was named 'rc
T1218.author: Konstantin Grishchenko, oscd.community

T1218.title: Uncommon Child Process Of Defaultpack.EXE
T1218.description: Detects uncommon child processes of "DefaultPack.EXE" binary as a proxy to launch other programs
T1218.author: frack113

T1218.title: DeviceCredentialDeployment Execution
T1218.description: Detects the execution of DeviceCredentialDeployment to hide a process from view.
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Arbitrary MSI Download Via Devinit.EXE
T1218.description: Detects a certain command line flag combination used by "devinit.exe", which can be abused as a LOLBIN to download arbitrary MSI packages on a Windows system
T1218.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Potentially Suspicious Child Process Of DiskShadow.EXE
T1218.description: Detects potentially suspicious child processes of "Diskshadow.exe". This could be an attempt to bypass parent/child relationship detection or application whitelisting rules.
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Diskshadow Script Mode - Uncommon Script Extension Execution
T1218.description:
Detects execution of "Diskshadow.exe" in script mode to execute an script with a potentially uncommon extension.
Initial baselining of the allowed extension list is required.
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Diskshadow Script Mode - Execution From Potential Suspicious Location
T1218.description: Detects execution of "Diskshadow.exe" in script mode using the "/s" flag where the script is located in a potentially suspicious location.
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Potential Application Whitelisting Bypass via Dnx.EXE
T1218.description:
Detects the execution of Dnx.EXE. The Dnx utility allows for the execution of C# code.
Attackers might abuse this in order to bypass application whitelisting.
T1218.author: Beyu Denis, oscd.community

T1218.title: Process Memory Dump Via Dotnet-Dump
T1218.description: Detects the execution of "dotnet-dump" with the "collect" flag. The execution could indicate potential process dumping of critical processes such as LSASS.
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Arbitrary DLL or Csproj Code Execution Via Dotnet.EXE
T1218.description: Detects execution of arbitrary DLLs or unsigned code via a ".csproj" files via Dotnet.EXE.
T1218.author: Beyu Denis, oscd.community

T1218.title: Binary Proxy Execution Via Dotnet-Trace.EXE
T1218.description: Detects commandline arguments for executing a child process via dotnet-trace.exe
T1218.author: Jimmy Bayne (@bohops)

T1218.title: Potentially Over Permissive Permissions Granted Using Dsacls.EXE
T1218.description: Detects usage of Dsacls to grant over permissive permissions
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Potential Password Spraying Attempt Using Dsacls.EXE
T1218.description: Detects possible password spraying attempts using Dsacls
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: New Capture Session Launched Via DXCap.EXE
T1218.description: Detects the execution of "DXCap.EXE" with the "-c" flag, which allows a user to launch any arbitrary binary or windows package through DXCap itself. This can be abused to potentially bypass application whitelisting.
T1218.author: Beyu Denis, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Potentially Suspicious Cabinet File Expansion
T1218.description: Detects the expansion or decompression of cabinet files from potentially suspicious or uncommon locations, e.g. seen in Iranian MeteorExpress related attacks
T1218.author: Bhabesh Raj, X__Junior (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Remote File Download Via Findstr.EXE
T1218.description: Detects execution of "findstr" with specific flags and a remote share path. This specific set of CLI flags would allow "findstr" to download the content of the file located on the remote share as described in the LOLBAS entry.
T1218.author: Furkan CALISKAN, @caliskanfurkan_, @oscd_initiative, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Insensitive Subfolder Search Via Findstr.EXE
T1218.description: Detects execution of findstr with the "s" and "i" flags for a "subfolder" and "insensitive" search respectively. Attackers sometimes leverage this built-in utility to search the system for interesting files or filter through results of commands.
T1218.author: Furkan CALISKAN, @caliskanfurkan_, @oscd_initiative, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: HTML Help HH.EXE Suspicious Child Process
T1218.description: Detects a suspicious child process of a Microsoft HTML Help (HH.exe)
T1218.author: Maxim Pavlunin, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Suspicious HH.EXE Execution
T1218.description: Detects a suspicious execution of a Microsoft HTML Help (HH.exe)
T1218.author: Maxim Pavlunin

T1218.title: Suspicious ZipExec Execution
T1218.description: ZipExec is a Proof-of-Concept (POC) tool to wrap binary-based tools into a password-protected zip file.
T1218.author: frack113

T1218.title: Self Extracting Package Creation Via Iexpress.EXE From Potentially Suspicious Location
T1218.description:
Detects the use of iexpress.exe to create binaries via Self Extraction Directive (SED) files located in potentially suspicious locations.
This behavior has been observed in-the-wild by different threat actors.
T1218.author: Joseliyo Sanchez, @Joseliyo_Jstnk, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Arbitrary File Download Via IMEWDBLD.EXE
T1218.description: Detects usage of "IMEWDBLD.exe" to download arbitrary files
T1218.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel

T1218.title: InfDefaultInstall.exe .inf Execution
T1218.description: Executes SCT script using scrobj.dll from a command in entered into a specially prepared INF file.
T1218.author: frack113

T1218.title: File Download Via InstallUtil.EXE
T1218.description: Detects use of .NET InstallUtil.exe in order to download arbitrary files. The files will be written to "%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\INetCache\IE\"
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Import LDAP Data Interchange Format File Via Ldifde.EXE
T1218.description: Detects the execution of "Ldifde.exe" with the import flag "-i". The can be abused to include HTTP-based arguments which will allow the arbitrary download of files from a remote server.
T1218.author: @gott_cyber

T1218.title: Uncommon Link.EXE Parent Process
T1218.description:
Detects an uncommon parent process of "LINK.EXE".
Link.EXE in Microsoft incremental linker. Its a utility usually bundled with Visual Studio installation.
Multiple utilities often found in the same folder (editbin.exe, dumpbin.exe, lib.exe, etc) have a hardcode call to the "LINK.EXE" binary without
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Devtoolslauncher.exe Executes Specified Binary
T1218.description: The Devtoolslauncher.exe executes other binary
T1218.author: Beyu Denis, oscd.community (rule), @_felamos (idea)

T1218.title: Gpscript Execution
T1218.description: Detects the execution of the LOLBIN gpscript, which executes logon or startup scripts configured in Group Policy
T1218.author: frack113

T1218.title: Ie4uinit Lolbin Use From Invalid Path
T1218.description: Detect use of ie4uinit.exe to execute commands from a specially prepared ie4uinit.inf file from a directory other than the usual directories
T1218.author: frack113

T1218.title: MpiExec Lolbin
T1218.description: Detects a certain command line flag combination used by mpiexec.exe LOLBIN from HPC pack that can be used to execute any other binary
T1218.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Execute Files with Msdeploy.exe
T1218.description: Detects file execution using the msdeploy.exe lolbin
T1218.author: Beyu Denis, oscd.community

T1218.title: OpenWith.exe Executes Specified Binary
T1218.description: The OpenWith.exe executes other binary
T1218.author: Beyu Denis, oscd.community (rule), @harr0ey (idea)

T1218.title: Indirect Command Execution By Program Compatibility Wizard
T1218.description: Detect indirect command execution via Program Compatibility Assistant pcwrun.exe
T1218.author: A. Sungurov , oscd.community

T1218.title: Execute Pcwrun.EXE To Leverage Follina
T1218.description: Detects indirect command execution via Program Compatibility Assistant "pcwrun.exe" leveraging the follina (CVE-2022-30190) vulnerability
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: DLL Execution via Rasautou.exe
T1218.description: Detects using Rasautou.exe for loading arbitrary .DLL specified in -d option and executes the export specified in -p.
T1218.author: Julia Fomina, oscd.community

T1218.title: REGISTER_APP.VBS Proxy Execution
T1218.description: Detects the use of a Microsoft signed script 'REGISTER_APP.VBS' to register a VSS/VDS Provider as a COM+ application.
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Lolbin Runexehelper Use As Proxy
T1218.description: Detect usage of the "runexehelper.exe" binary as a proxy to launch other programs
T1218.author: frack113

T1218.title: Use of Scriptrunner.exe
T1218.description: The "ScriptRunner.exe" binary can be abused to proxy execution through it and bypass possible whitelisting
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Use Of The SFTP.EXE Binary As A LOLBIN
T1218.description: Detects the usage of the "sftp.exe" binary as a LOLBIN by abusing the "-D" flag
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: SyncAppvPublishingServer Execute Arbitrary PowerShell Code
T1218.description: Executes arbitrary PowerShell code using SyncAppvPublishingServer.exe.
T1218.author: frack113

T1218.title: SyncAppvPublishingServer VBS Execute Arbitrary PowerShell Code
T1218.description: Executes arbitrary PowerShell code using SyncAppvPublishingServer.vbs
T1218.author: frack113

T1218.title: Time Travel Debugging Utility Usage
T1218.description: Detects usage of Time Travel Debugging Utility. Adversaries can execute malicious processes and dump processes, such as lsass.exe, via tttracer.exe.
T1218.author: Ensar Şamil, @sblmsrsn, @oscd_initiative

T1218.title: Lolbin Unregmp2.exe Use As Proxy
T1218.description: Detect usage of the "unregmp2.exe" binary as a proxy to launch a custom version of "wmpnscfg.exe"
T1218.author: frack113

T1218.title: Use of VisualUiaVerifyNative.exe
T1218.description: VisualUiaVerifyNative.exe is a Windows SDK that can be used for AWL bypass and is listed in Microsoft's recommended block rules.
T1218.author: Christopher Peacock @SecurePeacock, SCYTHE @scythe_io

T1218.title: Potential Register_App.Vbs LOLScript Abuse
T1218.description: Detects potential abuse of the "register_app.vbs" script that is part of the Windows SDK. The script offers the capability to register new VSS/VDS Provider as a COM+ application. Attackers can use this to install malicious DLLs for persistence and execution.
T1218.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

T1218.title: Potential Suspicious Mofcomp Execution
T1218.description:
Detects execution of the "mofcomp" utility as a child of a suspicious shell or script running utility or by having a suspicious path in the commandline.
The "mofcomp" utility parses a file containing MOF statements and adds the classes and class instances defined in the file to the WMI repository.
A
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: File Download Via Windows Defender MpCmpRun.EXE
T1218.description: Detects the use of Windows Defender MpCmdRun.EXE to download files
T1218.author: Matthew Matchen

T1218.title: MSDT Execution Via Answer File
T1218.description: Detects execution of "msdt.exe" using an answer file which is simulating the legitimate way of calling msdt via "pcwrun.exe" (For example from the compatibility tab).
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Suspicious MSDT Parent Process
T1218.description: Detects msdt.exe executed by a suspicious parent as seen in CVE-2022-30190 / Follina exploitation
T1218.author: Nextron Systems

T1218.title: Arbitrary File Download Via MSEDGE_PROXY.EXE
T1218.description: Detects usage of "msedge_proxy.exe" to download arbitrary files
T1218.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel

T1218.title: Windows MSIX Package Support Framework AI_STUBS Execution
T1218.description:
Detects execution of Advanced Installer MSIX Package Support Framework (PSF) components, specifically AI_STUBS executables with original filename 'popupwrapper.exe'.
This activity may indicate malicious MSIX packages build with Advanced Installer leveraging the Package Support Framework to bypass ap
T1218.author: Michael Haag, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Arbitrary File Download Via MSOHTMED.EXE
T1218.description: Detects usage of "MSOHTMED" to download arbitrary files
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Arbitrary File Download Via MSPUB.EXE
T1218.description: Detects usage of "MSPUB" (Microsoft Publisher) to download arbitrary files
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Potential Mpclient.DLL Sideloading Via OfflineScannerShell.EXE Execution
T1218.description:
Detects execution of Windows Defender "OfflineScannerShell.exe" from its non standard directory.
The "OfflineScannerShell.exe" binary is vulnerable to DLL side loading and will load any DLL named "mpclient.dll" from the current working directory.
T1218.author: frack113

T1218.title: PowerShell MSI Install via WindowsInstaller COM From Remote Location
T1218.description:
Detects the execution of PowerShell commands that attempt to install MSI packages via the
Windows Installer COM object (`WindowsInstaller.Installer`) hosted remotely.
This could be indication of malicious software deployment or lateral movement attempts using Windows Installer functionality.
And the
T1218.author: Meroujan Antonyan (vx3r)

T1218.title: RemoteFXvGPUDisablement Abuse Via AtomicTestHarnesses
T1218.description: Detects calls to the AtomicTestHarnesses "Invoke-ATHRemoteFXvGPUDisablementCommand" which is designed to abuse the "RemoteFXvGPUDisablement.exe" binary to run custom PowerShell code via module load-order hijacking.
T1218.author: frack113

T1218.title: Arbitrary File Download Via PresentationHost.EXE
T1218.description: Detects usage of "PresentationHost" which is a utility that runs ".xbap" (Browser Applications) files to download arbitrary files
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: XBAP Execution From Uncommon Locations Via PresentationHost.EXE
T1218.description: Detects the execution of ".xbap" (Browser Applications) files via PresentationHost.EXE from an uncommon location. These files can be abused to run malicious ".xbap" files any bypass AWL
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Visual Studio NodejsTools PressAnyKey Arbitrary Binary Execution
T1218.description: Detects child processes of Microsoft.NodejsTools.PressAnyKey.exe that can be used to execute any other binary
T1218.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Sensitive File Dump Via Print.EXE
T1218.description: Detects the abuse of the Print.exe utility for credential harvesting which involves using Print.Exe to copy sensitive files such as ntds.dit, SAM, SECURITY, or SYSTEM from the Windows directory in order to extract credentials, locally or remotely.
T1218.author: Ayush Anand (Securityinbits)

T1218.title: Abusing Print Executable
T1218.description: Attackers can use print.exe for remote file copy
T1218.author: Furkan CALISKAN, @caliskanfurkan_, @oscd_initiative

T1218.title: File Download Using ProtocolHandler.exe
T1218.description: Detects usage of "ProtocolHandler" to download files. Downloaded files will be located in the cache folder (for example - %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\INetCache\IE)
T1218.author: frack113

T1218.title: Potential Provlaunch.EXE Binary Proxy Execution Abuse
T1218.description: Detects child processes of "provlaunch.exe" which might indicate potential abuse to proxy execution.
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel

T1218.title: Suspicious Provlaunch.EXE Child Process
T1218.description: Detects suspicious child processes of "provlaunch.exe" which might indicate potential abuse to proxy execution.
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Potential Provisioning Registry Key Abuse For Binary Proxy Execution
T1218.description: Detects potential abuse of the provisioning registry key for indirect command execution through "Provlaunch.exe".
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel

T1218.title: Renamed ZOHO Dctask64 Execution
T1218.description:
Detects a renamed "dctask64.exe" execution, a signed binary by ZOHO Corporation part of ManageEngine Endpoint Central.
This binary can be abused for DLL injection, arbitrary command and process execution.
T1218.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Renamed MegaSync Execution
T1218.description: Detects the execution of a renamed MegaSync.exe as seen used by ransomware families like Nefilim, Sodinokibi, Pysa, and Conti.
T1218.author: Sittikorn S

T1218.title: Visual Studio NodejsTools PressAnyKey Renamed Execution
T1218.description: Detects renamed execution of "Microsoft.NodejsTools.PressAnyKey.exe", which can be abused as a LOLBIN to execute arbitrary binaries
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Scheduled Task Creation with Curl and PowerShell Execution Combo
T1218.description:
Detects the creation of a scheduled task using schtasks.exe, potentially in combination with curl for downloading payloads and PowerShell for executing them.
This facilitates executing malicious payloads or connecting with C&C server persistently without dropping the malware sample on the host.
T1218.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Sdiagnhost Calling Suspicious Child Process
T1218.description: Detects sdiagnhost.exe calling a suspicious child process (e.g. used in exploits for Follina / CVE-2022-30190)
T1218.author: Nextron Systems, @Kostastsale

T1218.title: Uncommon Child Process Of Setres.EXE
T1218.description:
Detects uncommon child process of Setres.EXE.
Setres.EXE is a Windows server only process and tool that can be used to set the screen resolution.
It can potentially be abused in order to launch any arbitrary file with a name containing the word "choice" from the current execution path.
T1218.author: @gott_cyber, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Suspicious Speech Runtime Binary Child Process
T1218.description:
Detects suspicious Speech Runtime Binary Execution by monitoring its child processes.
Child processes spawned by SpeechRuntime.exe could indicate an attempt for lateral movement via COM & DCOM hijacking.
T1218.author: andrewdanis

T1218.title: Arbitrary File Download Via Squirrel.EXE
T1218.description: Detects the usage of the "Squirrel.exe" to download arbitrary files. This binary is part of multiple Electron based software installations (Slack, Teams, Discord, etc.)
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Karneades / Markus Neis, Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community

T1218.title: Process Proxy Execution Via Squirrel.EXE
T1218.description: Detects the usage of the "Squirrel.exe" binary to execute arbitrary processes. This binary is part of multiple Electron based software installations (Slack, Teams, Discord, etc.)
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Karneades / Markus Neis, Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community

T1218.title: Program Executed Using Proxy/Local Command Via SSH.EXE
T1218.description: Detect usage of the "ssh.exe" binary as a proxy to launch other programs.
T1218.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali

T1218.title: Execution via stordiag.exe
T1218.description: Detects the use of stordiag.exe to execute schtasks.exe systeminfo.exe and fltmc.exe
T1218.author: Austin Songer (@austinsonger)

T1218.title: Potential File Download Via MS-AppInstaller Protocol Handler
T1218.description:
Detects usage of the "ms-appinstaller" protocol handler via command line to potentially download arbitrary files via AppInstaller.EXE
The downloaded files are temporarly stored in ":\Users\%username%\AppData\Local\Packages\Microsoft.DesktopAppInstaller_8wekyb3d8bbwe\AC\INetCache\<RANDOM-8-CHAR-DIREC
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel

T1218.title: Windows Shell/Scripting Processes Spawning Suspicious Programs
T1218.description: Detects suspicious child processes of a Windows shell and scripting processes such as wscript, rundll32, powershell, mshta...etc.
T1218.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Tim Shelton

T1218.title: Malicious Windows Script Components File Execution by TAEF Detection
T1218.description:
Windows Test Authoring and Execution Framework (TAEF) framework allows you to run automation by executing tests files written on different languages (C, C#, Microsoft COM Scripting interfaces
Adversaries may execute malicious code (such as WSC file with VBScript, dll and so on) directly by running t
T1218.author: Agro (@agro_sev) oscd.community

T1218.title: Malicious PE Execution by Microsoft Visual Studio Debugger
T1218.description:
There is an option for a MS VS Just-In-Time Debugger "vsjitdebugger.exe" to launch specified executable and attach a debugger.
This option may be used adversaries to execute malicious code by signed verified binary.
The debugger is installed alongside with Microsoft Visual Studio package.
T1218.author: Agro (@agro_sev), Ensar Şamil (@sblmsrsn), oscd.community

T1218.title: Execution via WorkFolders.exe
T1218.description: Detects using WorkFolders.exe to execute an arbitrary control.exe
T1218.author: Maxime Thiebaut (@0xThiebaut)

T1218.title: Potential Binary Impersonating Sysinternals Tools
T1218.description:
Detects binaries that use the same name as legitimate sysinternals tools to evade detection.
This rule looks for the execution of binaries that are named similarly to Sysinternals tools.
Adversary may rename their malicious tools as legitimate Sysinternals tools to evade detection.
T1218.author: frack113, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Verclsid.exe Runs COM Object
T1218.description: Detects when verclsid.exe is used to run COM object via GUID
T1218.author: Victor Sergeev, oscd.community

T1218.title: Potentially Suspicious Child Process Of VsCode
T1218.description: Detects uncommon or suspicious child processes spawning from a VsCode "code.exe" process. This could indicate an attempt of persistence via VsCode tasks or terminal profiles.
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Potential Binary Proxy Execution Via VSDiagnostics.EXE
T1218.description: Detects execution of "VSDiagnostics.exe" with the "start" command in order to launch and proxy arbitrary binaries.
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Suspicious Vsls-Agent Command With AgentExtensionPath Load
T1218.description: Detects Microsoft Visual Studio vsls-agent.exe lolbin execution with a suspicious library load using the --agentExtensionPath parameter
T1218.author: bohops

T1218.title: Winrs Local Command Execution
T1218.description:
Detects the execution of Winrs.exe where it is used to execute commands locally.
Commands executed this way are launched under Winrshost.exe and can represent proxy execution used for defense evasion or lateral movement.
T1218.author: Liran Ravich, Nasreddine Bencherchali

T1218.title: Wlrmdr.EXE Uncommon Argument Or Child Process
T1218.description:
Detects the execution of "Wlrmdr.exe" with the "-u" command line flag which allows anything passed to it to be an argument of the ShellExecute API, which would allow an attacker to execute arbitrary binaries.
This detection also focuses on any uncommon child processes spawned from "Wlrmdr.exe" as a
T1218.author: frack113, manasmbellani

T1218.title: WSL Child Process Anomaly
T1218.description: Detects uncommon or suspicious child processes spawning from a WSL process. This could indicate an attempt to evade parent/child relationship detections or persistence attempts via cron using WSL
T1218.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Proxy Execution Via Wuauclt.EXE
T1218.description: Detects the use of the Windows Update Client binary (wuauclt.exe) for proxy execution.
T1218.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research), Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Sreeman, FPT.EagleEye Team

T1218.title: COM Object Execution via Xwizard.EXE
T1218.description:
Detects the execution of Xwizard tool with the "RunWizard" flag and a GUID like argument.
This utility can be abused in order to run custom COM object created in the registry.
T1218.author: Ensar Şamil, @sblmsrsn, @oscd_initiative, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.title: Atbroker Registry Change
T1218.description: Detects creation/modification of Assistive Technology applications and persistence with usage of 'at'
T1218.author: Mateusz Wydra, oscd.community

T1218.title: Potential Provisioning Registry Key Abuse For Binary Proxy Execution - REG
T1218.description: Detects potential abuse of the provisioning registry key for indirect command execution through "Provlaunch.exe".
T1218.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel

T1218.title: Execution DLL of Choice Using WAB.EXE
T1218.description: This rule detects that the path to the DLL written in the registry is different from the default one. Launched WAB.exe tries to load the DLL from Registry.
T1218.author: oscd.community, Natalia Shornikova

T1218.007.title: MSI Installation From Web
T1218.007.description: Detects installation of a remote msi file from web.
T1218.007.author: Stamatis Chatzimangou

T1218.007.title: PowerShell WMI Win32_Product Install MSI
T1218.007.description: Detects the execution of an MSI file using PowerShell and the WMI Win32_Product class
T1218.007.author: frack113

T1218.007.title: DllUnregisterServer Function Call Via Msiexec.EXE
T1218.007.description: Detects MsiExec loading a DLL and calling its DllUnregisterServer function
T1218.007.author: frack113

T1218.007.title: Suspicious MsiExec Embedding Parent
T1218.007.description: Adversaries may abuse msiexec.exe to proxy the execution of malicious payloads

T1685.005.description: One of the Windows Eventlogs has been cleared. e.g. caused by "wevtutil cl" command execution

T1685.005.title: Important Windows Eventlog Cleared
T1685.005.description: Detects the clearing of one of the Windows Core Eventlogs. e.g. caused by "wevtutil cl" command execution
T1685.005.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Tim Shelton, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1685.005.title: Suspicious Eventlog Clear
T1685.005.description: Detects usage of known powershell cmdlets such as "Clear-EventLog" to clear the Windows event logs
T1685.005.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1685.005.title: Suspicious Windows Trace ETW Session Tamper Via Logman.EXE

T1685.005.title: Suspicious Eventlog Clearing or Configuration Change Activity
T1685.005.description:
Detects the clearing or configuration tampering of EventLog using utilities such as "wevtutil", "powershell" and "wmic".
This technique were seen used by threat actors and ransomware strains in order to evade defenses.
T1685.005.author: Ecco, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, oscd.community, D3F7A5105, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1123.title: Processes Accessing the Microphone and Webcam
T1123.description: Potential adversaries accessing the microphone and webcam in an endpoint.
T1123.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)

T1123.title: Audio Capture via PowerShell
T1123.description: Detects audio capture via PowerShell Cmdlet.

T1123.title: Audio Capture via SoundRecorder
T1123.description: Detect attacker collecting audio via SoundRecorder application.
T1123.author: E.M. Anhaus (originally from Atomic Blue Detections, Endgame), oscd.community

T1123.title: Suspicious Camera and Microphone Access
T1123.description: Detects Processes accessing the camera and microphone from suspicious folder
T1123.author: Den Iuzvyk

T1543.003.description: Detects known malicious service installs that appear in cases in which a Cobalt Strike beacon elevates privileges or lateral movement

T1543.003.title: Remote Access Tool Services Have Been Installed - Security

T1543.003.description: Detects known malicious service installs that appear in cases in which a Cobalt Strike beacon elevates privileges or lateral movement
T1543.003.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Wojciech Lesicki

T1543.003.title: Moriya Rootkit - System
T1543.003.description: Detects the use of Moriya rootkit as described in the securelist's Operation TunnelSnake report
T1543.003.author: Bhabesh Raj

T1543.003.title: New PDQDeploy Service - Server Side
T1543.003.description:
Detects a PDQDeploy service installation which indicates that PDQDeploy was installed on the machines.
PDQDeploy can be abused by attackers to remotely install packages or execute commands on target machines
T1543.003.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1543.003.title: New PDQDeploy Service - Client Side
T1543.003.description:
Detects PDQDeploy service installation on the target system.
When a package is deployed via PDQDeploy it installs a remote service on the target machine with the name "PDQDeployRunner-X" where "X" is an integer starting from 1
T1543.003.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1543.003.title: ProcessHacker Privilege Elevation
T1543.003.description: Detects a ProcessHacker tool that elevated privileges to a very high level
T1543.003.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1543.003.title: Remote Access Tool Services Have Been Installed - System
T1543.003.description: Detects service installation of different remote access tools software. These software are often abused by threat actors to perform
T1543.003.author: Connor Martin, Nasreddine Bencherchali

T1543.003.title: Sliver C2 Default Service Installation
T1543.003.description: Detects known malicious service installation that appear in cases in which a Sliver implants execute the PsExec commands
T1543.003.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1543.003.title: Suspicious Service Installation
T1543.003.description: Detects suspicious service installation commands
T1543.003.author: pH-T (Nextron Systems), Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1543.003.title: Uncommon Service Installation Image Path
T1543.003.description: Detects uncommon service installation commands by looking at suspicious or uncommon image path values containing references to encoded powershell commands, temporary paths, etc.
T1543.003.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1543.003.title: Service Installation in Suspicious Folder
T1543.003.description: Detects service installation in suspicious folder appdata
T1543.003.author: pH-T (Nextron Systems)

T1543.003.title: Service Installation with Suspicious Folder Pattern
T1543.003.description: Detects service installation with suspicious folder patterns
T1543.003.author: pH-T (Nextron Systems)

T1543.003.title: Suspicious Service Installation Script
T1543.003.description: Detects suspicious service installation scripts
T1543.003.author: pH-T (Nextron Systems)

T1543.003.title: Malicious Driver Load
T1543.003.description: Detects loading of known malicious drivers via their hash.
T1543.003.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1543.003.title: Malicious Driver Load By Name
T1543.003.description: Detects loading of known malicious drivers via the file name of the drivers.
T1543.003.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1543.003.title: Driver Load From A Temporary Directory
T1543.003.description: Detects a driver load from a temporary directory
T1543.003.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1543.003.title: Vulnerable Driver Load By Name
T1543.003.description: Detects the load of known vulnerable drivers via the file name of the drivers.
T1543.003.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1543.003.title: Vulnerable HackSys Extreme Vulnerable Driver Load
T1543.003.description: Detects the load of HackSys Extreme Vulnerable Driver which is an intentionally vulnerable Windows driver developed for security enthusiasts to learn and polish their exploitation skills at Kernel level and often abused by threat actors
T1543.003.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1543.003.title: Vulnerable WinRing0 Driver Load
T1543.003.description: Detects the load of a signed WinRing0 driver often used by threat actors, crypto miners (XMRIG) or malware for privilege escalation
T1543.003.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1543.003.title: PSEXEC Remote Execution File Artefact
T1543.003.description: Detects creation of the PSEXEC key file. Which is created anytime a PsExec command is executed. It gets written to the file system and will be recorded in the USN Journal on the target system
T1543.003.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1543.003.title: Devcon Execution Disabling VMware VMCI Device
T1543.003.description:
Detects execution of devcon.exe with commands that disable the VMware Virtual Machine Communication Interface (VMCI) device.
This can be legitimate during VMware Tools troubleshooting or driver conflicts, but may also indicate malware attempting to hijack communication with the hardware via the VMCI
T1543.003.author: Matt Anderson, Dray Agha, Anna Pham (Huntress)

T1543.003.title: New Service Creation Using PowerShell
T1543.003.description: Detects the creation of a new service using powershell.
T1543.003.author: Timur Zinniatullin, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, oscd.community

T1543.003.title: Suspicious Service DACL Modification Via Set-Service Cmdlet
T1543.003.description: Detects suspicious DACL modifications via the "Set-Service" cmdlet using the "SecurityDescriptorSddl" flag (Only available with PowerShell 7) that can be used to hide services or make them unstopable
T1543.003.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1543.003.title: PUA - Kernel Driver Utility (KDU) Execution
T1543.003.description:
Detects execution of the Kernel Driver Utility (KDU) tool.
KDU can be used to bypass driver signature enforcement and load unsigned or malicious drivers into the Windows kernel.
Potentially allowing for privilege escalation, persistence, or evasion of security controls.
T1543.003.author: Matt Anderson, Dray Agha, Anna Pham (Huntress)

T1543.003.title: New Service Creation Using Sc.EXE
T1543.003.description: Detects the creation of a new service using the "sc.exe" utility.
T1543.003.author: Timur Zinniatullin, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, oscd.community

T1543.003.title: New Kernel Driver Via SC.EXE
T1543.003.description: Detects creation of a new service (kernel driver) with the type "kernel"
T1543.003.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1543.003.title: Allow Service Access Using Security Descriptor Tampering Via Sc.EXE
T1543.003.description: Detects suspicious DACL modifications to allow access to a service from a suspicious trustee. This can be used to override access restrictions set by previous ACLs.
T1543.003.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1543.003.title: Deny Service Access Using Security Descriptor Tampering Via Sc.EXE
T1543.003.description: Detects suspicious DACL modifications to deny access to a service that affects critical trustees. This can be used to hide services or make them unstoppable.
T1543.003.author: Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community

T1543.003.title: Suspicious Service Path Modification
T1543.003.description: Detects service path modification via the "sc" binary to a suspicious command or path
T1543.003.author: Victor Sergeev, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1543.003.title: Potential Persistence Attempt Via Existing Service Tampering
T1543.003.description: Detects the modification of an existing service in order to execute an arbitrary payload when the service is started or killed as a potential method for persistence.
T1543.003.author: Sreeman

T1543.003.title: Suspicious New Service Creation
T1543.003.description: Detects creation of a new service via "sc" command or the powershell "new-service" cmdlet with suspicious binary paths
T1543.003.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1543.003.title: Sysinternals PsService Execution
T1543.003.description: Detects usage of Sysinternals PsService which can be abused for service reconnaissance and tampering
T1543.003.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1543.003.title: Sysinternals PsSuspend Execution
T1543.003.description: Detects usage of Sysinternals PsSuspend which can be abused to suspend critical processes
T1543.003.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1543.003.title: Potential CobaltStrike Service Installations - Registry
T1543.003.description: Detects known malicious service installs that appear in cases in which a Cobalt Strike beacon elevates privileges or lateral movement.
T1543.003.author: Wojciech Lesicki

T1543.003.title: ServiceDll Hijack
T1543.003.description:
Detects changes to the "ServiceDLL" value related to a service in the registry.
This is often used as a method of persistence.
T1543.003.author: frack113

T1027.001.title: Failed Code Integrity Checks
T1027.001.description: Detects code integrity failures such as missing page hashes or corrupted drivers due unauthorized modification. This could be a sign of tampered binaries.
T1027.001.author: Thomas Patzke

T1021.003.title: DCOM InternetExplorer.Application Iertutil DLL Hijack - Security
T1021.003.description: Detects a threat actor creating a file named `iertutil.dll` in the `C:\Program Files\Internet Explorer\` directory over the network for a DCOM InternetExplorer DLL Hijack scenario.
T1021.003.author: Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g, Open Threat Research (OTR)

T1021.003.title: Potential DCOM InternetExplorer.Application DLL Hijack
T1021.003.description: Detects potential DLL hijack of "iertutil.dll" found in the DCOM InternetExplorer.Application Class over the network
T1021.003.author: Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g, Open Threat Research (OTR), wagga

T1021.003.title: Potential DCOM InternetExplorer.Application DLL Hijack - Image Load
T1021.003.description: Detects potential DLL hijack of "iertutil.dll" found in the DCOM InternetExplorer.Application Class
T1021.003.author: Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g, Open Threat Research (OTR), wagga

T1021.003.title: BaaUpdate.exe Suspicious DLL Load
T1021.003.description:
Detects BitLocker Access Agent Update Utility (baaupdate.exe) loading DLLs from suspicious locations that are publicly writable which could indicate an attempt to lateral movement via BitLocker DCOM & COM Hijacking.
This technique abuses COM Classes configured as INTERACTIVE USER to spawn processes
T1021.003.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1021.003.title: Suspicious WSMAN Provider Image Loads
T1021.003.description: Detects signs of potential use of the WSMAN provider from uncommon processes locally and remote execution.
T1021.003.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)

T1021.003.title: Suspicious Non PowerShell WSMAN COM Provider
T1021.003.description: Detects suspicious use of the WSMAN provider without PowerShell.exe as the host application.
T1021.003.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)

T1021.003.title: Suspicious BitLocker Access Agent Update Utility Execution
T1021.003.description:
Detects the execution of the BitLocker Access Agent Update Utility (baaupdate.exe) which is not a common parent process for other processes.
Suspicious child processes spawned by baaupdate.exe could indicate an attempt at lateral movement via BitLocker DCOM & COM Hijacking.
T1021.003.author: andrewdanis, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1021.003.title: HackTool - Potential Impacket Lateral Movement Activity
T1021.003.author: Ecco, oscd.community, Jonhnathan Ribeiro, Tim Rauch

T1021.003.title: MMC20 Lateral Movement
T1021.003.description: Detects MMC20.Application Lateral Movement; specifically looks for the spawning of the parent MMC.exe with a command line of "-Embedding" as a child of svchost.exe
T1021.003.author: @2xxeformyshirt (Security Risk Advisors) - rule; Teymur Kheirkhabarov (idea)

T1021.003.title: MMC Spawning Windows Shell
T1021.003.description: Detects a Windows command line executable started from MMC
T1021.003.author: Karneades, Swisscom CSIRT

T1021.003.title: Potential Excel.EXE DCOM Lateral Movement Via ActivateMicrosoftApp
T1021.003.description: Detects suspicious child processes of Excel which could be an indicator of lateral movement leveraging the "ActivateMicrosoftApp" Excel DCOM object.
T1021.003.author: Aaron Stratton

T1021.003.title: Suspicious Speech Runtime Binary Child Process
T1021.003.description:
Detects suspicious Speech Runtime Binary Execution by monitoring its child processes.
Child processes spawned by SpeechRuntime.exe could indicate an attempt for lateral movement via COM & DCOM hijacking.
T1021.003.author: andrewdanis

T1484.001.title: Windows Default Domain GPO Modification
T1484.001.description:
Detects modifications to Default Domain or Default Domain Controllers Group Policy Objects (GPOs).
Adversaries may modify these default GPOs to deploy malicious configurations across the domain.
T1484.001.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1484.001.title: Group Policy Abuse for Privilege Addition
T1484.001.description: Detects the first occurrence of a modification to Group Policy Object Attributes to add privileges to user accounts or use them to add users as local admins.
T1484.001.author: Elastic, Josh Nickels, Marius Rothenbücher

T1484.001.title: Startup/Logon Script Added to Group Policy Object
T1484.001.description: Detects the modification of Group Policy Objects (GPO) to add a startup/logon script to users or computer objects.
T1484.001.author: Elastic, Josh Nickels, Marius Rothenbücher

T1484.001.title: Modify Group Policy Settings - ScriptBlockLogging
T1484.001.description: Detect malicious GPO modifications can be used to implement many other malicious behaviors.
T1484.001.author: frack113

T1484.001.title: Windows Default Domain GPO Modification via GPME
T1484.001.description:
Detects the use of the Group Policy Management Editor (GPME) to modify Default Domain or Default Domain Controllers Group Policy Objects (GPOs).
Adversaries may leverage GPME to make stealthy changes in these default GPOs to deploy malicious GPOs configurations across the domain without raising susp
T1484.001.author: TropChaud

T1484.001.title: Modify Group Policy Settings
T1484.001.description: Detect malicious GPO modifications can be used to implement many other malicious behaviors.
T1484.001.author: frack113

T1112.title: ETW Logging Disabled In .NET Processes - Registry

T1112.description: Detects NetNTLM downgrade attack

T1112.title: Sysmon Channel Reference Deletion
T1112.description: Potential threat actor tampering with Sysmon manifest and eventually disabling it
T1112.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)

T1112.title: Registry Modification Attempt Via VBScript - PowerShell
T1112.description:
Detects attempts to modify the registry using VBScript's CreateObject("Wscript.shell") and RegWrite methods embedded within PowerShell scripts or commands.
Threat actors commonly embed VBScript code within PowerShell to perform registry modifications, attempting to evade detection that monitors for
T1112.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1112.title: New DNS ServerLevelPluginDll Installed Via Dnscmd.EXE
T1112.description: Detects the installation of a DNS plugin DLL via ServerLevelPluginDll parameter in registry, which can be used to execute code in context of the DNS server (restart required)
T1112.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1112.title: Security Event Logging Disabled via MiniNt Registry Key - Process
T1112.description:
Detects attempts to disable security event logging by adding the `MiniNt` registry key.
This key is used to disable the Windows Event Log service, which collects and stores event logs from the operating system and applications.
Adversaries may want to disable this service to prevent logging of secur
T1112.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1112.title: Imports Registry Key From a File
T1112.description: Detects the import of the specified file to the registry with regedit.exe.
T1112.author: Oddvar Moe, Sander Wiebing, oscd.community

T1112.title: Imports Registry Key From an ADS
T1112.description: Detects the import of a alternate datastream to the registry with regedit.exe.
T1112.author: Oddvar Moe, Sander Wiebing, oscd.community

T1112.title: Suspicious Registry Modification From ADS Via Regini.EXE
T1112.description: Detects the import of an alternate data stream with regini.exe, regini.exe can be used to modify registry keys.
T1112.author: Eli Salem, Sander Wiebing, oscd.community

T1112.title: Registry Modification Via Regini.EXE
T1112.description: Detects the execution of regini.exe which can be used to modify registry keys, the changes are imported from one or more text files.
T1112.author: Eli Salem, Sander Wiebing, oscd.community

T1112.title: Potentially Suspicious Desktop Background Change Using Reg.EXE
T1112.description:
Detects the execution of "reg.exe" to alter registry keys that would replace the user's desktop background.
This is a common technique used by malware to change the desktop background to a ransom note or other image.
T1112.author: Stephen Lincoln @slincoln-aiq (AttackIQ)

T1112.title: Potential Suspicious Registry File Imported Via Reg.EXE
T1112.description: Detects the import of '.reg' files from suspicious paths using the 'reg.exe' utility
T1112.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali

T1112.title: RestrictedAdminMode Registry Value Tampering - ProcCreation
T1112.description:
Detects changes to the "DisableRestrictedAdmin" registry value in order to disable or enable RestrictedAdmin mode.
RestrictedAdmin mode prevents the transmission of reusable credentials to the remote system to which you connect using Remote Desktop.
This prevents your credentials from being harveste
T1112.author: frack113

T1112.title: Enable LM Hash Storage - ProcCreation
T1112.description:
Detects changes to the "NoLMHash" registry value in order to allow Windows to store LM Hashes.
By setting this registry value to "0" (DWORD), Windows will be allowed to store a LAN manager hash of your password in Active Directory and local SAM databases.
T1112.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1112.title: Potential Tampering With RDP Related Registry Keys Via Reg.EXE
T1112.description: Detects the execution of "reg.exe" for enabling/disabling the RDP service on the host by tampering with the 'CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server' values
T1112.author: pH-T (Nextron Systems), @Kostastsale, TheDFIRReport

T1112.title: Reg Add Suspicious Paths
T1112.description: Detects when an adversary uses the reg.exe utility to add or modify new keys or subkeys
T1112.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1112.title: ShimCache Flush
T1112.description: Detects actions that clear the local ShimCache and remove forensic evidence
T1112.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1112.title: Run Once Task Execution as Configured in Registry
T1112.description: This rule detects the execution of Run Once task as configured in the registry
T1112.author: Avneet Singh @v3t0_, oscd.community, Christopher Peacock @SecurePeacock (updated)

T1112.title: Non-privileged Usage of Reg or Powershell
T1112.description: Search for usage of reg or Powershell by non-privileged users to modify service configuration in registry
T1112.author: Teymur Kheirkhabarov (idea), Ryan Plas (rule), oscd.community

T1112.title: Registry Modification of MS-settings Protocol Handler
T1112.description:
Detects registry modifications to the 'ms-settings' protocol handler, which is frequently targeted for UAC bypass or persistence.
Attackers can modify this registry to execute malicious code with elevated privileges by hijacking the command execution path.
T1112.author: frack113, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1112.title: User Shell Folders Registry Modification via CommandLine
T1112.description:
Detects modifications to User Shell Folders registry values via reg.exe or PowerShell, which could indicate persistence attempts.
Attackers may modify User Shell Folders registry values to point to malicious executables or scripts that will be executed during startup.
This technique is often used to
T1112.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1112.title: Registry Modification Attempt Via VBScript
T1112.description:
Detects attempts to modify the registry using VBScript's CreateObject("Wscript.shell") and RegWrite methods via common LOLBINs.
It could be an attempt to modify the registry for persistence without using straightforward methods like regedit.exe, reg.exe, or PowerShell.
Threat Actors may use this tec
T1112.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1112.title: Suspicious VBoxDrvInst.exe Parameters
T1112.description:
Detect VBoxDrvInst.exe run with parameters allowing processing INF file.
This allows to create values in the registry and install drivers.
For example one could use this technique to obtain persistence via modifying one of Run or RunOnce registry keys
T1112.author: Konstantin Grishchenko, oscd.community

T1112.title: Registry Manipulation via WMI Stdregprov
T1112.description:
Detects the usage of wmic.exe to manipulate Windows registry via the WMI StdRegProv class.
This behaviour could be potentially suspicious because it uses an alternative method to modify registry keys instead of legitimate registry tools like reg.exe or regedit.exe.
Attackers specifically choose this
T1112.author: Daniel Koifman (KoifSec)

T1112.title: Terminal Server Client Connection History Cleared - Registry
T1112.description: Detects the deletion of registry keys containing the MSTSC connection history
T1112.author: Christian Burkard (Nextron Systems)

T1112.title: Removal of Potential COM Hijacking Registry Keys
T1112.description:
Detects any deletion of entries in ".*\shell\open\command" registry keys.
These registry keys might have been used for COM hijacking activities by a threat actor or an attacker and the deletion could indicate steps to remove its tracks.
T1112.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)

T1112.title: Disable Security Events Logging Adding Reg Key MiniNt
T1112.description: Detects the addition of a key 'MiniNt' to the registry. Upon a reboot, Windows Event Log service will stop writing events.
T1112.author: Ilyas Ochkov, oscd.community

T1112.title: Wdigest CredGuard Registry Modification
T1112.description:
Detects potential malicious modification of the property value of IsCredGuardEnabled from
HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\WDigest to disable Cred Guard on a system.
This is usually used with UseLogonCredential to manipulate the caching credentials.
T1112.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)

T1112.title: Potential Qakbot Registry Activity
T1112.description: Detects a registry key used by IceID in a campaign that distributes malicious OneNote files
T1112.author: Hieu Tran

T1112.title: Registry Entries For Azorult Malware
T1112.description: Detects the presence of a registry key created during Azorult execution
T1112.author: Trent Liffick

T1112.title: NetNTLM Downgrade Attack - Registry
T1112.description: Detects NetNTLM downgrade attack
T1112.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), wagga, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Splunk STRT)

T1112.title: RedMimicry Winnti Playbook Registry Manipulation
T1112.description: Detects actions caused by the RedMimicry Winnti playbook
T1112.author: Alexander Rausch

T1112.title: Run Once Task Configuration in Registry
T1112.description: Rule to detect the configuration of Run Once registry key. Configured payload can be run by runonce.exe /AlternateShellStartup
T1112.author: Avneet Singh @v3t0_, oscd.community

T1112.title: Registry Tampering by Potentially Suspicious Processes
T1112.description:
Detects suspicious registry modifications made by suspicious processes such as script engine processes such as WScript, or CScript etc.
These processes are rarely used for legitimate registry modifications, and their activity may indicate an attempt to modify the registry
without using standard tool
T1112.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1112.title: Allow RDP Remote Assistance Feature
T1112.description: Detect enable rdp feature to allow specific user to rdp connect on the targeted machine
T1112.author: frack113

T1112.title: New BgInfo.EXE Custom DB Path Registry Configuration
T1112.description: Detects setting of a new registry database value related to BgInfo configuration. Attackers can for example set this value to save the results of the commands executed by BgInfo in order to exfiltrate information.
T1112.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1112.title: New BgInfo.EXE Custom VBScript Registry Configuration
T1112.description: Detects setting of a new registry value related to BgInfo configuration, which can be abused to execute custom VBScript via "BgInfo.exe"
T1112.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1112.title: New BgInfo.EXE Custom WMI Query Registry Configuration
T1112.description: Detects setting of a new registry value related to BgInfo configuration, which can be abused to execute custom WMI query via "BgInfo.exe"
T1112.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1112.title: ClickOnce Trust Prompt Tampering
T1112.description: Detects changes to the ClickOnce trust prompt registry key in order to enable an installation from different locations such as the Internet.
T1112.author: @SerkinValery, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1112.title: CrashControl CrashDump Disabled
T1112.description: Detects disabling the CrashDump per registry (as used by HermeticWiper)
T1112.author: Tobias Michalski (Nextron Systems)

T1112.title: Security Event Logging Disabled via MiniNt Registry Key - Registry Set
T1112.description:
Detects the addition of the 'MiniNt' key to the registry. Upon a reboot, Windows Event Log service will stop writing events.
Windows Event Log is a service that collects and stores event logs from the operating system and applications. It is an important component of Windows security and auditing.
A
T1112.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1112.title: Service Binary in Suspicious Folder
T1112.description: Detect the creation of a service with a service binary located in a suspicious directory
T1112.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), frack113

T1112.title: Potentially Suspicious Desktop Background Change Via Registry
T1112.description:
Detects registry value settings that would replace the user's desktop background.
This is a common technique used by malware to change the desktop background to a ransom note or other image.
T1112.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Stephen Lincoln @slincoln-aiq (AttackIQ)

T1112.title: DHCP Callout DLL Installation
T1112.description: Detects the installation of a Callout DLL via CalloutDlls and CalloutEnabled parameter in Registry, which can be used to execute code in context of the DHCP server (restart required)
T1112.author: Dimitrios Slamaris

T1112.title: Disable Internal Tools or Feature in Registry
T1112.description: Detects registry modifications that change features of internal Windows tools (malware like Agent Tesla uses this technique)
T1112.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), CrimpSec

T1112.title: Disable Windows Security Center Notifications
T1112.description: Detect set UseActionCenterExperience to 0 to disable the Windows security center notification
T1112.author: frack113

T1112.title: Windows Event Log Access Tampering Via Registry
T1112.description: Detects changes to the Windows EventLog channel permission values. It focuses on changes to the Security Descriptor Definition Language (SDDL) string, as modifications to these values can restrict access to specific users or groups, potentially aiding in defense evasion by controlling who can view o
T1112.author: X__Junior

T1112.title: Add DisallowRun Execution to Registry
T1112.description: Detect set DisallowRun to 1 to prevent user running specific computer program
T1112.author: frack113

T1112.title: DNS-over-HTTPS Enabled by Registry
T1112.description:
Detects when a user enables DNS-over-HTTPS.
This can be used to hide internet activity or be used to hide the process of exfiltrating data.
With this enabled organization will lose visibility into data such as query type, response and originating IP that are used to determine bad actors.
T1112.author: Austin Songer

T1112.title: New DNS ServerLevelPluginDll Installed
T1112.description: Detects the installation of a DNS plugin DLL via ServerLevelPluginDll parameter in registry, which can be used to execute code in context of the DNS server (restart required)
T1112.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1112.title: ETW Logging Disabled In .NET Processes - Sysmon Registry
T1112.description: Potential adversaries stopping ETW providers recording loaded .NET assemblies.
T1112.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)

T1112.title: Change User Account Associated with the FAX Service
T1112.description: Detect change of the user account associated with the FAX service to avoid the escalation problem.
T1112.author: frack113

T1112.title: Change the Fax Dll
T1112.description: Detect possible persistence using Fax DLL load when service restart
T1112.author: frack113

T1112.title: Registry Hide Function from User
T1112.description: Detects registry modifications that hide internal tools or functions from the user (malware like Agent Tesla, Hermetic Wiper uses this technique)
T1112.author: frack113

T1112.title: RestrictedAdminMode Registry Value Tampering
T1112.description:
Detects changes to the "DisableRestrictedAdmin" registry value in order to disable or enable RestrictedAdmin mode.
RestrictedAdmin mode prevents the transmission of reusable credentials to the remote system to which you connect using Remote Desktop.
This prevents your credentials from being harveste
T1112.author: frack113

T1112.title: NET NGenAssemblyUsageLog Registry Key Tamper
T1112.description:
Detects changes to the NGenAssemblyUsageLog registry key.
.NET Usage Log output location can be controlled by setting the NGenAssemblyUsageLog CLR configuration knob in the Registry or by configuring an environment variable (as described in the next section).
By simplify specifying an arbitrary valu
T1112.author: frack113

T1112.title: Trust Access Disable For VBApplications
T1112.description: Detects registry changes to Microsoft Office "AccessVBOM" to a value of "1" which disables trust access for VBA on the victim machine and lets attackers execute malicious macros without any Microsoft Office warnings.
T1112.author: Trent Liffick (@tliffick), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1112.title: Outlook EnableUnsafeClientMailRules Setting Enabled - Registry
T1112.description: Detects an attacker trying to enable the outlook security setting "EnableUnsafeClientMailRules" which allows outlook to run applications or execute macros
T1112.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1112.title: Uncommon Microsoft Office Trusted Location Added
T1112.description: Detects changes to registry keys related to "Trusted Location" of Microsoft Office where the path is set to something uncommon. Attackers might add additional trusted locations to avoid macro security restrictions.
T1112.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1112.title: Macro Enabled In A Potentially Suspicious Document
T1112.description: Detects registry changes to Office trust records where the path is located in a potentially suspicious location
T1112.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1112.title: Office Macros Warning Disabled
T1112.description: Detects registry changes to Microsoft Office "VBAWarning" to a value of "1" which enables the execution of all macros, whether signed or unsigned.
T1112.author: Trent Liffick (@tliffick), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1112.title: Potential Persistence Via Custom Protocol Handler
T1112.description: Detects potential persistence activity via the registering of a new custom protocole handlers. While legitimate applications register protocole handlers often times during installation. And attacker can abuse this by setting a custom handler to be used as a persistence mechanism.
T1112.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1112.title: Potential Persistence Via Event Viewer Events.asp
T1112.description: Detects potential registry persistence technique using the Event Viewer "Events.asp" technique
T1112.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1112.title: Modification of IE Registry Settings
T1112.description: Detects modification of the registry settings used for Internet Explorer and other Windows components that use these settings. An attacker can abuse this registry key to add a domain to the trusted sites Zone or insert JavaScript for persistence
T1112.author: frack113

T1112.title: Potential Persistence Via Outlook Home Page
T1112.description:
Detects potential persistence activity via outlook home page.
An attacker can set a home page to achieve code execution and persistence by editing the WebView registry keys.
T1112.author: Tobias Michalski (Nextron Systems), David Bertho (@dbertho) & Eirik Sveen (@0xSV1), Storebrand

T1112.title: Potential Persistence Via Outlook Today Page
T1112.description:
Detects potential persistence activity via outlook today page.
An attacker can set a custom page to execute arbitrary code and link to it via the registry values "URL" and "UserDefinedUrl".
T1112.author: Tobias Michalski (Nextron Systems), David Bertho (@dbertho) & Eirik Sveen (@0xSV1), Storebrand

T1112.title: Registry Modification for OCI DLL Redirection
T1112.description:
Detects registry modifications related to 'OracleOciLib' and 'OracleOciLibPath' under 'MSDTC' settings.
Threat actors may modify these registry keys to redirect the loading of 'oci.dll' to a malicious DLL, facilitating phantom DLL hijacking via the MSDTC service.
T1112.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1112.title: PowerShell Logging Disabled Via Registry Key Tampering
T1112.description: Detects changes to the registry for the currently logged-in user. In order to disable PowerShell module logging, script block logging or transcription and script execution logging
T1112.author: frack113

T1112.title: ETW Logging Disabled For rpcrt4.dll
T1112.description: Detects changes to the "ExtErrorInformation" key in order to disable ETW logging for rpcrt4.dll
T1112.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1112.title: ETW Logging Disabled For SCM
T1112.description: Detects changes to the "TracingDisabled" key in order to disable ETW logging for services.exe (SCM)
T1112.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1112.title: Registry Explorer Policy Modification
T1112.description: Detects registry modifications that disable internal tools or functions in explorer (malware like Agent Tesla uses this technique)
T1112.author: frack113

T1112.title: Activate Suppression of Windows Security Center Notifications
T1112.description: Detect set Notification_Suppress to 1 to disable the Windows security center notification
T1112.author: frack113

T1112.title: Enable LM Hash Storage
T1112.description:
Detects changes to the "NoLMHash" registry value in order to allow Windows to store LM Hashes.
By setting this registry value to "0" (DWORD), Windows will be allowed to store a LAN manager hash of your password in Active Directory and local SAM databases.
T1112.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1112.title: RDP Sensitive Settings Changed to Zero
T1112.description:
Detects tampering of RDP Terminal Service/Server sensitive settings.
Such as allowing unauthorized users access to a system via the 'fAllowUnsolicited' or enabling RDP via 'fDenyTSConnections', etc.
T1112.author: Samir Bousseaden, David ANDRE, Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g, Nasreddine Bencherchali

T1112.title: RDP Sensitive Settings Changed
T1112.description:
Detects tampering of RDP Terminal Service/Server sensitive settings.
Such as allowing unauthorized users access to a system via the 'fAllowUnsolicited' or enabling RDP via 'fDenyTSConnections', etc.

Below is a list of registry keys/values that are monitored by this rule:

- Shadow: Used to enable R
T1112.author: Samir Bousseaden, David ANDRE, Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g, Nasreddine Bencherchali

T1112.title: Wdigest Enable UseLogonCredential
T1112.description: Detects potential malicious modification of the property value of UseLogonCredential from HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\WDigest to enable clear-text credentials
T1112.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)

T1112.title: Winlogon AllowMultipleTSSessions Enable
T1112.description:
Detects when the 'AllowMultipleTSSessions' value is enabled.
Which allows for multiple Remote Desktop connection sessions to be opened at once.
This is often used by attacker as a way to connect to an RDP session without disconnecting the other users
T1112.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1091.title: External Disk Drive Or USB Storage Device Was Recognized By The System
T1091.description: Detects external disk drives or plugged-in USB devices.
T1091.author: Keith Wright

T1053.005.title: Persistence and Execution at Scale via GPO Scheduled Task
T1053.005.description: Detect lateral movement using GPO scheduled task, usually used to deploy ransomware at scale
T1053.005.author: Samir Bousseaden

T1053.005.title: Suspicious Scheduled Task Creation
T1053.005.description: Detects suspicious scheduled task creation events. Based on attributes such as paths, commands line flags, etc.
T1053.005.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1053.005.title: Important Scheduled Task Deleted/Disabled
T1053.005.description: Detects when adversaries stop services or processes by deleting or disabling their respective scheduled tasks in order to conduct data destructive activities
T1053.005.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1053.005.title: Suspicious Scheduled Task Update
T1053.005.description: Detects update to a scheduled task event that contain suspicious keywords.
T1053.005.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1053.005.title: Scheduled Task Executed From A Suspicious Location
T1053.005.description: Detects the execution of Scheduled Tasks where the Program being run is located in a suspicious location or it's an unusale program to be run from a Scheduled Task
T1053.005.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1053.005.title: Scheduled Task Executed Uncommon LOLBIN
T1053.005.description: Detects the execution of Scheduled Tasks where the program being run is located in a suspicious location or where it is an unusual program to be run from a Scheduled Task
T1053.005.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1053.005.title: Powershell Create Scheduled Task
T1053.005.description: Adversaries may abuse the Windows Task Scheduler to perform task scheduling for initial or recurring execution of malicious code
T1053.005.author: frack113

T1053.005.title: HackTool - Default PowerSploit/Empire Scheduled Task Creation
T1053.005.description: Detects the creation of a schtask via PowerSploit or Empire Default Configuration.
T1053.005.author: Markus Neis, @Karneades

T1053.005.title: Renamed Schtasks Execution
T1053.005.description:
Detects the execution of renamed schtasks.exe binary, which is a legitimate Windows utility used for scheduling tasks.
One of the very common persistence techniques is schedule malicious tasks using schtasks.exe.
Since, it is heavily abused, it is also heavily monitored by security products. To evad
T1053.005.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1053.005.title: Suspicious Schtasks Execution AppData Folder
T1053.005.description: Detects the creation of a schtask that executes a file from C:\Users\<USER>\AppData\Local
T1053.005.author: pH-T (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1053.005.title: Suspicious Modification Of Scheduled Tasks
T1053.005.description:
Detects when an attacker tries to modify an already existing scheduled tasks to run from a suspicious location
Attackers can create a simple looking task in order to avoid detection on creation as it's often the most focused on
Instead they modify the task after creation to include their malicious p
T1053.005.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1053.005.title: Scheduled Task Creation Via Schtasks.EXE
T1053.005.description: Detects the creation of scheduled tasks by user accounts via the "schtasks" utility.
T1053.005.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1053.005.title: Suspicious Scheduled Task Creation Involving Temp Folder
T1053.005.description: Detects the creation of scheduled tasks that involves a temporary folder and runs only once
T1053.005.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1053.005.title: Scheduled Task Creation with Curl and PowerShell Execution Combo
T1053.005.description:
Detects the creation of a scheduled task using schtasks.exe, potentially in combination with curl for downloading payloads and PowerShell for executing them.
This facilitates executing malicious payloads or connecting with C&C server persistently without dropping the malware sample on the host.
T1053.005.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1053.005.title: Schedule Task Creation From Env Variable Or Potentially Suspicious Path Via Schtasks.EXE
T1053.005.description: Detects Schtask creations that point to a suspicious folder or an environment variable often used by malware
T1053.005.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1053.005.title: Schtasks From Suspicious Folders
T1053.005.description: Detects scheduled task creations that have suspicious action command and folder combinations
T1053.005.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1053.005.title: Suspicious Scheduled Task Name As GUID
T1053.005.description: Detects creation of a scheduled task with a GUID like name
T1053.005.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1053.005.title: Uncommon One Time Only Scheduled Task At 00:00
T1053.005.description: Detects scheduled task creation events that include suspicious actions, and is run once at 00:00
T1053.005.author: pH-T (Nextron Systems)

T1053.005.title: Potential SSH Tunnel Persistence Install Using A Scheduled Task
T1053.005.description: Detects the creation of new scheduled tasks via commandline, using Schtasks.exe. This rule detects tasks creating that call OpenSSH, which may indicate the creation of reverse SSH tunnel to the attacker's server.
T1053.005.author: Rory Duncan

T1053.005.title: Potential Persistence Via Microsoft Compatibility Appraiser
T1053.005.description:
Detects manual execution of the "Microsoft Compatibility Appraiser" task via schtasks.
In order to trigger persistence stored in the "\AppCompatFlags\TelemetryController" registry key.
T1053.005.author: Sreeman

T1053.005.title: Potential Persistence Via Powershell Search Order Hijacking - Task
T1053.005.description: Detects suspicious powershell execution via a schedule task where the command ends with an suspicious flags to hide the powershell instance instead of executeing scripts or commands. This could be a sign of persistence via PowerShell "Get-Variable" technique as seen being used in Colibri Loader

T1053.005.title: Scheduled Task Executing Payload from Registry

T1053.005.author: X__Junior (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1053.005.title: Scheduled Task Executing Encoded Payload from Registry

T1053.005.title: Suspicious Schtasks Schedule Types
T1053.005.description: Detects scheduled task creations or modification on a suspicious schedule type
T1053.005.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1053.005.title: Suspicious Schtasks Schedule Type With High Privileges
T1053.005.description: Detects scheduled task creations or modification to be run with high privileges on a suspicious schedule type
T1053.005.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1053.005.title: Suspicious Scheduled Task Creation via Masqueraded XML File
T1053.005.description: Detects the creation of a scheduled task using the "-XML" flag with a file without the '.xml' extension. This behavior could be indicative of potential defense evasion attempt during persistence

T1053.005.title: Suspicious Command Patterns In Scheduled Task Creation
T1053.005.description: Detects scheduled task creation using "schtasks" that contain potentially suspicious or uncommon commands
T1053.005.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1053.005.title: Schtasks Creation Or Modification With SYSTEM Privileges
T1053.005.description: Detects the creation or update of a scheduled task to run with "NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM" privileges
T1053.005.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1053.005.title: Scheduled Task Creation Masquerading as System Processes
T1053.005.description: Detects the creation of scheduled tasks that involve system processes, which may indicate malicious actors masquerading as or abusing these processes to execute payloads or maintain persistence.
T1053.005.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1053.005.title: Scheduled TaskCache Change by Uncommon Program
T1053.005.description: Monitor the creation of a new key under 'TaskCache' when a new scheduled task is registered by a process that is not svchost.exe, which is suspicious
T1053.005.author: Syed Hasan (@syedhasan009)

T1053.005.description:
Detects potential persistence behavior using the windows telemetry registry key.
Windows telemetry makes use of the binary CompatTelRunner.exe to run a variety of commands and perform the actual telemetry collections.
This binary was created to be easily extensible, and to that end, it relies on the
T1053.005.author: Lednyov Alexey, oscd.community, Sreeman

T1134.001.title: HackTool - Koh Default Named Pipe

T1134.001.title: HackTool - SharpDPAPI Execution
T1134.001.description:
Detects the execution of the SharpDPAPI tool based on CommandLine flags and PE metadata.
SharpDPAPI is a C# port of some DPAPI functionality from the Mimikatz project.

T1134.001.author: Sai Prashanth Pulisetti @pulisettis, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
