T1055.001.title: Renamed ZOHO Dctask64 Execution
T1055.001.description:
Detects a renamed "dctask64.exe" execution, a signed binary by ZOHO Corporation part of ManageEngine Endpoint Central.
This binary can be abused for DLL injection, arbitrary command and process execution.
T1055.001.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1055.001.title: Renamed Mavinject.EXE Execution
T1055.001.description: Detects the execution of a renamed version of the "Mavinject" process. Which can be abused to perform process injection using the "/INJECTRUNNING" flag
T1055.001.author: frack113, Florian Roth

T1555.005.title: Remote Thread Created In KeePass.EXE
T1555.005.description: Detects remote thread creation in "KeePass.exe" which could indicates potential password dumping activity
T1555.005.author: Timon Hackenjos

T1218.011.title: Remote Thread Creation Via PowerShell In Uncommon Target
T1218.011.description: Detects the creation of a remote thread from a Powershell process in an uncommon target process
T1218.011.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1218.011.title: SCR File Write Event
T1218.011.description: Detects the creation of screensaver files (.scr) outside of system folders. Attackers may execute an application as an ".SCR" file using "rundll32.exe desk.cpl,InstallScreenSaver" for example.
T1218.011.author: Christopher Peacock @securepeacock, SCYTHE @scythe_io

T1218.011.title: Unsigned DLL Loaded by Windows Utility
T1218.011.description:
Detects windows utilities loading an unsigned or untrusted DLL.
Adversaries often abuse those programs to proxy execution of malicious code.
T1218.011.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel

T1218.011.title: Rundll32 Internet Connection
T1218.011.description: Detects a rundll32 that communicates with public IP addresses
T1218.011.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1218.011.title: Outbound Network Connection To Public IP Via Winlogon
T1218.011.description: Detects a "winlogon.exe" process that initiate network communications with public IP addresses
T1218.011.author: Christopher Peacock @securepeacock, SCYTHE @scythe_io

T1218.011.title: Process Access via TrolleyExpress Exclusion
T1218.011.description: Detects a possible process memory dump that uses the white-listed Citrix TrolleyExpress.exe filename as a way to dump the lsass process memory
T1218.011.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1218.011.title: HTML Help HH.EXE Suspicious Child Process
T1218.011.description: Detects a suspicious child process of a Microsoft HTML Help (HH.exe)
T1218.011.author: Maxim Pavlunin, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.011.title: Suspicious HH.EXE Execution
T1218.011.description: Detects a suspicious execution of a Microsoft HTML Help (HH.exe)
T1218.011.author: Maxim Pavlunin

T1218.011.title: HackTool - F-Secure C3 Load by Rundll32
T1218.011.description: F-Secure C3 produces DLLs with a default exported StartNodeRelay function.
T1218.011.author: Alfie Champion (ajpc500)

T1218.011.title: CobaltStrike Load by Rundll32
T1218.011.description: Rundll32 can be use by Cobalt Strike with StartW function to load DLLs from the command line.
T1218.011.author: Wojciech Lesicki

T1218.011.title: HackTool - RedMimicry Winnti Playbook Execution
T1218.011.description: Detects actions caused by the RedMimicry Winnti playbook a automated breach emulations utility
T1218.011.author: Alexander Rausch

T1218.011.title: Code Execution via Pcwutl.dll
T1218.011.description: Detects launch of executable by calling the LaunchApplication function from pcwutl.dll library.
T1218.011.author: Julia Fomina, oscd.community

T1218.011.title: Rundll32 InstallScreenSaver Execution
T1218.011.description: An attacker may execute an application as a SCR File using rundll32.exe desk.cpl,InstallScreenSaver
T1218.011.author: Christopher Peacock @securepeacock, SCYTHE @scythe_io, TactiKoolSec

T1218.011.title: Suspicious Rundll32 Setupapi.dll Activity
T1218.011.description: setupapi.dll library provide InstallHinfSection function for processing INF files. INF file may contain instructions allowing to create values in the registry, modify files and install drivers. This technique could be used to obtain persistence via modifying one of Run or RunOnce registry keys, run
T1218.011.author: Konstantin Grishchenko, oscd.community

T1218.011.title: Shell32 DLL Execution in Suspicious Directory
T1218.011.description: Detects shell32.dll executing a DLL in a suspicious directory
T1218.011.author: Christian Burkard (Nextron Systems)

T1218.011.title: RunDLL32 Spawning Explorer
T1218.011.description: Detects RunDLL32.exe spawning explorer.exe as child, which is very uncommon, often observes Gamarue spawning the explorer.exe process in an unusual way
T1218.011.author: elhoim, CD_ROM_

T1218.011.title: Potentially Suspicious Rundll32 Activity
T1218.011.description: Detects suspicious execution of rundll32, with specific calls to some DLLs with known LOLBIN functionalities
T1218.011.author: juju4, Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.011.title: Suspicious Control Panel DLL Load
T1218.011.description: Detects suspicious Rundll32 execution from control.exe as used by Equation Group and Exploit Kits
T1218.011.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1218.011.title: Suspicious Rundll32 Execution With Image Extension
T1218.011.description: Detects the execution of Rundll32.exe with DLL files masquerading as image files
T1218.011.author: Hieu Tran

T1218.011.title: Suspicious ShellExec_RunDLL Call Via Ordinal
T1218.011.description:
Detects suspicious call to the "ShellExec_RunDLL" exported function of SHELL32.DLL through the ordinal number to launch other commands.
Adversary might only use the ordinal number in order to bypass existing detection that alert on usage of ShellExec_RunDLL on CommandLine.
T1218.011.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel

T1218.011.title: Suspicious Rundll32 Activity Invoking Sys File
T1218.011.description: Detects suspicious process related to rundll32 based on command line that includes a *.sys file as seen being used by UNC2452
T1218.011.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1218.011.title: Potentially Suspicious Rundll32.EXE Execution of UDL File
T1218.011.description:
Detects the execution of rundll32.exe with the oledb32.dll library to open a UDL file.
Threat actors can abuse this technique as a phishing vector to capture authentication credentials or other sensitive data.
T1218.011.author: @kostastsale

T1218.011.title: Rundll32 Execution With Uncommon DLL Extension
T1218.011.description: Detects the execution of rundll32 with a command line that doesn't contain a common extension
T1218.011.author: Tim Shelton, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Yassine Oukessou

T1218.011.title: Rundll32 UNC Path Execution
T1218.011.description: Detects rundll32 execution where the DLL is located on a remote location (share)
T1218.011.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.011.title: Bad Opsec Defaults Sacrificial Processes With Improper Arguments
T1218.011.description:
Detects attackers using tooling with bad opsec defaults.
E.g. spawning a sacrificial process to inject a capability into the process without taking into account how the process is normally run.
One trivial example of this is using rundll32.exe without arguments as a sacrificial process (default in C
T1218.011.author: Oleg Kolesnikov @securonix invrep_de, oscd.community, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Christian Burkard (Nextron Systems

T1218.011.title: Potential PowerShell Execution Via DLL
T1218.011.description:
Detects potential PowerShell execution from a DLL instead of the usual PowerShell process as seen used in PowerShdll.
This detection assumes that PowerShell commands are passed via the CommandLine.
T1218.011.author: Markus Neis, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1218.011.title: ScreenSaver Registry Key Set
T1218.011.description: Detects registry key established after masqueraded .scr file execution using Rundll32 through desk.cpl
T1218.011.author: Jose Luis Sanchez Martinez (@Joseliyo_Jstnk)

T1055.title: Rare Remote Thread Creation By Uncommon Source Image
T1055.description: Detects uncommon processes creating remote threads.
T1055.author: Perez Diego (@darkquassar), oscd.community

T1055.title: Remote Thread Creation By Uncommon Source Image
T1055.description: Detects uncommon processes creating remote threads.
T1055.author: Perez Diego (@darkquassar), oscd.community

T1055.title: Created Files by Microsoft Sync Center
T1055.description: This rule detects suspicious files created by Microsoft Sync Center (mobsync)
T1055.author: elhoim

T1055.title: Potential DLL Sideloading Using Coregen.exe
T1055.description: Detect usage of the "coregen.exe" (Microsoft CoreCLR Native Image Generator) binary to sideload arbitrary DLLs.
T1055.author: frack113

T1055.title: DotNet CLR DLL Loaded By Scripting Applications
T1055.description: Detects .NET CLR DLLs being loaded by scripting applications such as wscript or cscript. This could be an indication of potential suspicious execution.
T1055.author: omkar72, oscd.community

T1055.title: Network Connection Initiated Via Notepad.EXE
T1055.description:
Detects a network connection that is initiated by the "notepad.exe" process.
This might be a sign of process injection from a beacon process or something similar.
Notepad rarely initiates a network communication except when printing documents for example.
T1055.author: EagleEye Team

T1055.title: Microsoft Sync Center Suspicious Network Connections
T1055.description: Detects suspicious connections from Microsoft Sync Center to non-private IPs.
T1055.author: elhoim

T1055.title: CobaltStrike Named Pipe
T1055.description: Detects the creation of a named pipe as used by CobaltStrike
T1055.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Wojciech Lesicki

T1055.title: CobaltStrike Named Pipe Pattern Regex
T1055.description: Detects the creation of a named pipe matching a pattern used by CobaltStrike Malleable C2 profiles
T1055.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1055.title: CobaltStrike Named Pipe Patterns
T1055.description: Detects the creation of a named pipe with a pattern found in CobaltStrike malleable C2 profiles
T1055.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Christian Burkard (Nextron Systems)

T1055.title: HackTool - CoercedPotato Named Pipe Creation
T1055.description: Detects the pattern of a pipe name as used by the hack tool CoercedPotato
T1055.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1055.title: HackTool - EfsPotato Named Pipe Creation
T1055.description: Detects the pattern of a pipe name as used by the hack tool EfsPotato
T1055.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1055.title: Malicious Named Pipe Created
T1055.description: Detects the creation of a named pipe seen used by known APTs or malware.
T1055.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), blueteam0ps, elhoim

T1055.title: PowerShell ShellCode
T1055.description: Detects Base64 encoded Shellcode
T1055.author: David Ledbetter (shellcode), Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1055.title: Dllhost.EXE Execution Anomaly
T1055.description: Detects a "dllhost" process spawning with no commandline arguments which is very rare to happen and could indicate process injection activity or malware mimicking similar system processes.
T1055.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1055.title: HackTool - CoercedPotato Execution
T1055.description: Detects the use of CoercedPotato, a tool for privilege escalation
T1055.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1055.title: HackTool - DInjector PowerShell Cradle Execution
T1055.description: Detects the use of the Dinject PowerShell cradle based on the specific flags
T1055.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1055.title: Potential Process Injection Via Msra.EXE
T1055.description: Detects potential process injection via Microsoft Remote Asssistance (Msra.exe) by looking at suspicious child processes spawned from the aforementioned process. It has been a target used by many threat actors and used for discovery and persistence tactics
T1055.author: Alexander McDonald

T1055.title: Suspicious Rundll32 Invoking Inline VBScript
T1055.description: Detects suspicious process related to rundll32 based on command line that invokes inline VBScript as seen being used by UNC2452
T1055.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1055.title: Process Creation Using Sysnative Folder
T1055.description: Detects process creation events that use the Sysnative folder (common for CobaltStrike spawns)
T1055.author: Max Altgelt (Nextron Systems)

T1055.title: Suspicious Userinit Child Process
T1055.description: Detects a suspicious child process of userinit
T1055.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Samir Bousseaden (idea)

T1055.title: Suspect Svchost Activity
T1055.description: It is extremely abnormal for svchost.exe to spawn without any CLI arguments and is normally observed when a malicious process spawns the process and injects code into the process memory space.
T1055.author: David Burkett, @signalblur

T1055.title: Uncommon Svchost Command Line Parameter
T1055.description:
Detects instances of svchost.exe running with an unusual or uncommon command line parameter by excluding known legitimate or common patterns.
This could point at a file masquerading as svchost, a process injection, or hollowing of a legitimate svchost instance.
T1055.author: Liran Ravich

T1055.title: Suspicious Child Process Of Wermgr.EXE
T1055.description: Detects suspicious Windows Error Reporting manager (wermgr.exe) child process
T1055.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1055.003.title: Remote Thread Creation In Uncommon Target Image
T1055.003.description: Detects uncommon target processes for remote thread creation
T1055.003.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1055.003.title: HackTool - LittleCorporal Generated Maldoc Injection
T1055.003.description: Detects the process injection of a LittleCorporal generated Maldoc.
T1055.003.author: Christian Burkard (Nextron Systems)

T1127.title: Remote Thread Creation Ttdinject.exe Proxy
T1127.description: Detects a remote thread creation of Ttdinject.exe used as proxy
T1127.author: frack113

T1127.title: Suspicious File Created by ArcSOC.exe
T1127.description:
Detects instances where the ArcGIS Server process ArcSOC.exe, which hosts REST services running on an ArcGIS
server, creates a file with suspicious file type, indicating that it may be an executable, script file,
or otherwise unusual.
T1127.author: Micah Babinski

T1127.title: AspNetCompiler Execution
T1127.description: Detects execution of "aspnet_compiler.exe" which can be abused to compile and execute C# code.
T1127.author: frack113

T1127.title: Suspicious Child Process of AspNetCompiler
T1127.description: Detects potentially suspicious child processes of "aspnet_compiler.exe".
T1127.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1127.title: Potentially Suspicious ASP.NET Compilation Via AspNetCompiler
T1127.description: Detects execution of "aspnet_compiler.exe" with potentially suspicious paths for compilation.
T1127.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1127.title: Potential Binary Proxy Execution Via Cdb.EXE
T1127.description: Detects usage of "cdb.exe" to launch arbitrary processes or commands from a debugger script file
T1127.author: Beyu Denis, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1127.title: Suspicious Use of CSharp Interactive Console
T1127.description: Detects the execution of CSharp interactive console by PowerShell
T1127.author: Michael R. (@nahamike01)

T1127.title: C# IL Code Compilation Via Ilasm.EXE
T1127.description: Detects the use of "Ilasm.EXE" in order to compile C# intermediate (IL) code to EXE or DLL.
T1127.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1127.title: JScript Compiler Execution
T1127.description:
Detects the execution of the "jsc.exe" (JScript Compiler).
Attacker might abuse this in order to compile JScript files on the fly and bypassing application whitelisting.
T1127.author: frack113

T1127.title: Kavremover Dropped Binary LOLBIN Usage
T1127.description: Detects the execution of a signed binary dropped by Kaspersky Lab Products Remover (kavremover) which can be abused as a LOLBIN to execute arbitrary commands and binaries.
T1127.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1127.title: Use of Remote.exe
T1127.description: Remote.exe is part of WinDbg in the Windows SDK and can be used for AWL bypass and running remote files.
T1127.author: Christopher Peacock @SecurePeacock, SCYTHE @scythe_io

T1127.title: Use of TTDInject.exe
T1127.description: Detects the executiob of TTDInject.exe, which is used by Windows 10 v1809 and newer to debug time travel (underlying call of tttracer.exe)
T1127.author: frack113

T1127.title: Use of VSIISExeLauncher.exe
T1127.description: The "VSIISExeLauncher.exe" binary part of the Visual Studio/VS Code can be used to execute arbitrary binaries
T1127.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1127.title: Use of Wfc.exe
T1127.description: The Workflow Command-line Compiler can be used for AWL bypass and is listed in Microsoft's recommended block rules.
T1127.author: Christopher Peacock @SecurePeacock, SCYTHE @scythe_io

T1127.title: Potential Mftrace.EXE Abuse
T1127.description: Detects child processes of the "Trace log generation tool for Media Foundation Tools" (Mftrace.exe) which can abused to execute arbitrary binaries.
T1127.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1127.title: Detection of PowerShell Execution via Sqlps.exe
T1127.description:
This rule detects execution of a PowerShell code through the sqlps.exe utility, which is included in the standard set of utilities supplied with the MSSQL Server.
Script blocks are not logged in this case, so this utility helps to bypass protection mechanisms based on the analysis of these logs.
T1127.author: Agro (@agro_sev) oscd.community

T1127.title: SQL Client Tools PowerShell Session Detection
T1127.description:
This rule detects execution of a PowerShell code through the sqltoolsps.exe utility, which is included in the standard set of utilities supplied with the Microsoft SQL Server Management studio.
Script blocks are not logged in this case, so this utility helps to bypass protection mechanisms based on
T1127.author: Agro (@agro_sev) oscd.communitly

T1127.title: Potential Arbitrary Code Execution Via Node.EXE
T1127.description: Detects the execution node.exe which is shipped with multiple software such as VMware, Adobe...etc. In order to execute arbitrary code. For example to establish reverse shell as seen in Log4j attacks...etc
T1127.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1127.title: Node Process Executions
T1127.description: Detects the execution of other scripts using the Node executable packaged with Adobe Creative Cloud
T1127.author: Max Altgelt (Nextron Systems)

T1564.004.title: Hidden Executable In NTFS Alternate Data Stream
T1564.004.description: Detects the creation of an ADS (Alternate Data Stream) that contains an executable by looking at a non-empty Imphash
T1564.004.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), @0xrawsec

T1564.004.title: Suspicious File Download From File Sharing Websites -  File Stream
T1564.004.description: Detects the download of suspicious file type from a well-known file and paste sharing domain
T1564.004.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1564.004.title: Unusual File Download From File Sharing Websites - File Stream
T1564.004.description: Detects the download of suspicious file type from a well-known file and paste sharing domain
T1564.004.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1564.004.title: HackTool Named File Stream Created
T1564.004.description: Detects the creation of a named file stream with the imphash of a well-known hack tool
T1564.004.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1564.004.title: Exports Registry Key To an Alternate Data Stream
T1564.004.description: Exports the target Registry key and hides it in the specified alternate data stream.
T1564.004.author: Oddvar Moe, Sander Wiebing, oscd.community

T1564.004.title: Unusual File Download from Direct IP Address
T1564.004.description: Detects the download of suspicious file type from URLs with IP
T1564.004.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1564.004.title: Potential Hidden Directory Creation Via NTFS INDEX_ALLOCATION Stream
T1564.004.description: Detects the creation of hidden file/folder with the "::$index_allocation" stream. Which can be used as a technique to prevent access to folder and files from tooling such as "explorer.exe" and "powershell.exe"
T1564.004.author: Scoubi (@ScoubiMtl)

T1564.004.title: NTFS Alternate Data Stream
T1564.004.description: Detects writing data into NTFS alternate data streams from powershell. Needs Script Block Logging.
T1564.004.author: Sami Ruohonen

T1564.004.title: Powershell Store File In Alternate Data Stream
T1564.004.description: Storing files in Alternate Data Stream (ADS) similar to Astaroth malware.
T1564.004.author: frack113

T1564.004.title: Remote File Download Via Findstr.EXE
T1564.004.description: Detects execution of "findstr" with specific flags and a remote share path. This specific set of CLI flags would allow "findstr" to download the content of the file located on the remote share as described in the LOLBAS entry.
T1564.004.author: Furkan CALISKAN, @caliskanfurkan_, @oscd_initiative, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1564.004.title: Insensitive Subfolder Search Via Findstr.EXE
T1564.004.description: Detects execution of findstr with the "s" and "i" flags for a "subfolder" and "insensitive" search respectively. Attackers sometimes leverage this built-in utility to search the system for interesting files or filter through results of commands.
T1564.004.author: Furkan CALISKAN, @caliskanfurkan_, @oscd_initiative, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1564.004.title: Suspicious Diantz Alternate Data Stream Execution
T1564.004.description: Compress target file into a cab file stored in the Alternate Data Stream (ADS) of the target file.
T1564.004.author: frack113

T1564.004.title: Suspicious Extrac32 Alternate Data Stream Execution
T1564.004.description: Extract data from cab file and hide it in an alternate data stream
T1564.004.author: frack113

T1564.004.title: PrintBrm ZIP Creation of Extraction
T1564.004.description: Detects the execution of the LOLBIN PrintBrm.exe, which can be used to create or extract ZIP files. PrintBrm.exe should not be run on a normal workstation.
T1564.004.author: frack113

T1564.004.title: Run PowerShell Script from ADS
T1564.004.description: Detects PowerShell script execution from Alternate Data Stream (ADS)
T1564.004.author: Sergey Soldatov, Kaspersky Lab, oscd.community

T1564.004.title: Potential Rundll32 Execution With DLL Stored In ADS
T1564.004.description: Detects execution of rundll32 where the DLL being called is stored in an Alternate Data Stream (ADS).
T1564.004.author: Harjot Singh, '@cyb3rjy0t'

T1564.004.title: Execute From Alternate Data Streams
T1564.004.description: Detects execution from an Alternate Data Stream (ADS). Adversaries may use NTFS file attributes to hide their malicious data in order to evade detection
T1564.004.author: frack113

T1564.004.title: Potential Hidden Directory Creation Via NTFS INDEX_ALLOCATION Stream - CLI
T1564.004.description: Detects command line containing reference to the "::$index_allocation" stream, which can be used as a technique to prevent access to folders or files from tooling such as "explorer.exe" or "powershell.exe"
T1564.004.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Scoubi (@ScoubiMtl)

T1564.004.title: Use Short Name Path in Image
T1564.004.description: Detect use of the Windows 8.3 short name. Which could be used as a method to avoid Image detection
T1564.004.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali

T1564.004.title: Use NTFS Short Name in Command Line
T1564.004.description: Detect use of the Windows 8.3 short name. Which could be used as a method to avoid command-line detection
T1564.004.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1564.004.title: Use NTFS Short Name in Image
T1564.004.description: Detect use of the Windows 8.3 short name. Which could be used as a method to avoid Image based detection
T1564.004.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1572.title: Cloudflared Tunnels Related DNS Requests
T1572.description:
Detects DNS requests to Cloudflared tunnels domains.
Attackers can abuse that feature to establish a reverse shell or persistence on a machine.
T1572.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1572.title: DNS Query To Devtunnels Domain
T1572.description: Detects DNS query requests to Devtunnels domains. Attackers can abuse that feature to establish a reverse shell or persistence on a machine.
T1572.author: citron_ninja

T1572.title: Network Connection Initiated To BTunnels Domains
T1572.description:
Detects network connections to BTunnels domains initiated by a process on the system.
Attackers can abuse that feature to establish a reverse shell or persistence on a machine.
T1572.author: Kamran Saifullah

T1572.title: Network Connection Initiated To Cloudflared Tunnels Domains
T1572.description:
Detects network connections to Cloudflared tunnels domains initiated by a process on the system.
Attackers can abuse that feature to establish a reverse shell or persistence on a machine.
T1572.author: Kamran Saifullah, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1572.title: Network Connection Initiated To DevTunnels Domain
T1572.description: Detects network connections to Devtunnels domains initiated by a process on a system. Attackers can abuse that feature to establish a reverse shell or persistence on a machine.
T1572.author: Kamran Saifullah

T1572.description:
Detects an executable initiating a network connection to "LocaltoNet" tunneling sub-domains.
LocaltoNet is a reverse proxy that enables localhost services to be exposed to the Internet.

T1572.author: Andreas Braathen (mnemonic.io)

T1572.description:
Detects an executable initiating a network connection to "ngrok" domains.
Attackers were seen using this "ngrok" in order to store their second stage payloads and malware.
While communication with such domains can be legitimate, often times is a sign of either data exfiltration by malicious actors o
T1572.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1572.title: Communication To Ngrok Tunneling Service Initiated
T1572.description:
Detects an executable initiating a network connection to "ngrok" tunneling domains.
Attackers were seen using this "ngrok" in order to store their second stage payloads and malware.
While communication with such domains can be legitimate, often times is a sign of either data exfiltration by maliciou
T1572.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1572.title: Network Connection Initiated To Visual Studio Code Tunnels Domain

T1572.title: Suspicious Plink Port Forwarding

T1572.title: Potentially Suspicious Usage Of Qemu

T1195.002.title: Notepad++ Updater DNS Query to Uncommon Domains
T1195.002.description:
Detects when the Notepad++ updater (gup.exe) makes DNS queries to domains that are not part of the known legitimate update infrastructure.
This could indicate potential exploitation of the updater mechanism or suspicious network activity that warrants further investigation.

T1195.002.title: Uncommon File Created by Notepad++ Updater Gup.EXE

Detects when the Notepad++ updater (gup.exe) creates files in suspicious or uncommon locations.
This could indicate potential exploitation of the updater component to deliver unwanted malware or unwarranted files.

T1195.002.title: Suspicious Child Process of Notepad++ Updater - GUP.Exe
T1195.002.description:
Detects suspicious child process creation by the Notepad++ updater process (gup.exe).

T1056.title: DNS Query Request To OneLaunch Update Service
T1056.description:

T1218.010.title: Unsigned DLL Loaded by Windows Utility

T1218.010.title: Network Connection Initiated By Regsvr32.EXE

T1204.004.description: Detects the occurrence of numerous space characters in TypedPaths registry paths, which may indicate execution via phishing lures using file-fix techniques to hide malicious commands.
T1204.004.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

T1608.title: Suspicious Download from Office Domain
T1608.description: Detects suspicious ways to download files from Microsoft domains that are used to store attachments in Emails or OneNote documents

T1608.description: Detects the installation of the Azure Hybrid Connection Manager service to allow remote code execution from Azure function.

T1560.title: Compressed File Extraction Via Tar.EXE
T1560.description:
Detects execution of "tar.exe" in order to extract compressed file.
Adversaries may abuse various utilities in order to decompress data to avoid detection.
T1560.author: AdmU3

T1021.005.title: Suspicious UltraVNC Execution
T1021.005.description: Detects suspicious UltraVNC command line flag combination that indicate a auto reconnect upon execution, e.g. startup (as seen being used by Gamaredon threat group)

T1006.description: Detects raw disk access using uncommon tools or tools that are located in suspicious locations (heavy filtering is required), which could indicate possible defense evasion attempts

T1546.009.description:

T1546.010.description: DLLs that are specified in the AppInit_DLLs value in the Registry key HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Windows are loaded by user32.dll into every process that loads user32.dll
T1546.010.author: Ilyas Ochkov, oscd.community, Tim Shelton

T1137.002.description: Detects the addition of office test registry that allows a user to specify an arbitrary DLL that will be executed every time an Office application is started
T1137.002.author: omkar72

T1547.005.description: Detects the addition of a SSP to the registry. Upon a reboot or API call, SSP DLLs gain access to encrypted and plaintext passwords stored in Windows.

T1547.008.description: Detects a method to load DLL via LSASS process using an undocumented Registry key
T1547.008.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

T1125.title: Suspicious Camera and Microphone Access
T1125.description: Detects Processes accessing the camera and microphone from suspicious folder
T1125.author: Den Iuzvyk

T1559.002.title: Enable Microsoft Dynamic Data Exchange
T1559.002.description: Enable Dynamic Data Exchange protocol (DDE) in all supported editions of Microsoft Word or Excel.
T1559.002.author: frack113

T1546.012.title: Potential Persistence Via App Paths Default Property
T1546.012.description:
Detects changes to the "Default" property for keys located in the \Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\App Paths\ registry. Which might be used as a method of persistence
The entries found under App Paths are used primarily for the following purposes.
First, to map an application's executable
T1546.012.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1546.012.title: Potential Persistence Via GlobalFlags
T1546.012.description: Detects registry persistence technique using the GlobalFlags and SilentProcessExit keys
T1546.012.author: Karneades, Jonhnathan Ribeiro, Florian Roth

T1553.003.title: Persistence Via New SIP Provider
T1553.003.description: Detects when an attacker register a new SIP provider for persistence and defense evasion
T1553.003.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

T1547.003.title: New TimeProviders Registered With Uncommon DLL Name
T1547.003.description:
Detects processes setting a new DLL in DllName in under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\W32Time\TimeProvider.
Adversaries may abuse time providers to execute DLLs when the system boots.
The Windows Time service (W32Time) enables time synchronization across and within domains.
T1547.003.author: frack113

\u001faws.title: AWS Bucket Deleted
\u001faws.description:
Detects the deletion of S3 buckets in AWS CloudTrail logs.
Monitoring the deletion of S3 buckets is critical for security and data integrity, as it may indicate potential data loss or unauthorized access attempts.
\u001faws.author: Ivan Saakov, Nasreddine Bencherchali

\u001faws.title: AWS ConsoleLogin Failed Authentication
\u001faws.description: Detects failed AWS console login attempts due to authentication failures. Monitoring these events is crucial for identifying potential brute-force attacks or unauthorized access attempts to AWS accounts.
\u001faws.author: Ivan Saakov, Nasreddine Bencherchali

\u001faws.title: AWS Successful Console Login Without MFA
\u001faws.description:
Detects successful AWS console logins that were performed without Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA).
This alert can be used to identify potential unauthorized access attempts, as logging in without MFA can indicate compromised credentials or misconfigured security settings.
\u001faws.author: Thuya@Hacktilizer, Ivan Saakov

\u001faws.description: Detects disabling, deleting and updating of a Trail
\u001faws.author: vitaliy0x1

\u001faws.title: AWS GuardDuty Detector Deleted Or Updated
\u001faws.description:
Detects successful deletion or disabling of an AWS GuardDuty detector, possibly by an attacker trying to avoid detection of its malicious activities.
Upon deletion, GuardDuty stops monitoring the environment and all existing findings are lost.
Verify with the user identity that this activity is legi
\u001faws.author: suktech24

\u001faws.title: Malicious Usage Of IMDS Credentials Outside Of AWS Infrastructure
\u001faws.description:
Detects when an instance identity has taken an action that isn't inside SSM.
This can indicate that a compromised EC2 instance is being used as a pivot point.
\u001faws.author: jamesc-grafana

\u001faws.title: New Network ACL Entry Added
\u001faws.description: Detects that network ACL entries have been added to a route table which could indicate that new attack vectors have been opened up in the AWS account.
\u001faws.author: jamesc-grafana

\u001faws.title: New Network Route Added
\u001faws.description: Detects the addition of a new network route to a route table in AWS.
\u001faws.author: jamesc-grafana

\u001faws.title: PUA - AWS TruffleHog Execution
\u001faws.description:
Detects the execution of TruffleHog, a popular open-source tool used for scanning repositories for secrets and sensitive information, within an AWS environment.
It has been reported to be used by threat actors for credential harvesting. All detections should be investigated to determine if the usage
\u001faws.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

\u001faws.title: AWS EnableRegion Command Monitoring
\u001faws.description:
Detects the use of the EnableRegion command in AWS CloudTrail logs.
While AWS has 30+ regions, some of them are enabled by default, others must be explicitly enabled in each account separately.
There may be situations where security monitoring does not cover some new AWS regions.
Monitoring the Enab
\u001faws.author: Ivan Saakov, Sergey Zelenskiy

\u001faws.title: Ingress/Egress Security Group Modification
\u001faws.description:
Detects when an account makes changes to the ingress or egress rules of a security group.

\u001faws.author: jamesc-grafana

\u001faws.title: LoadBalancer Security Group Modification
\u001faws.description:
Detects changes to the security groups associated with an Elastic Load Balancer (ELB) or Application Load Balancer (ALB).
This can indicate that a misconfiguration allowing more traffic into the system than required, or could indicate that an attacker is attempting to enable new connections into a V
\u001faws.author: jamesc-grafana

\u001faws.title: RDS Database Security Group Modification
\u001faws.description:
Detects changes to the security group entries for RDS databases.
This can indicate that a misconfiguration has occurred which potentially exposes the database to the public internet, a wider audience within the VPC or that removal of valid rules has occurred which could impact the availability of th
\u001faws.author: jamesc-grafana

\u001faws.description: Detect when System Manager successfully executes commands against an instance.
\u001faws.author: jamesc-grafana

\u001faws.description:
Detects the deletion of one or more VPC Flow Logs in AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) through the DeleteFlowLogs API call.
Adversaries may delete flow logs to evade detection or remove evidence of network activity, hindering forensic investigations and visibility into malicious operations.

\u001faws.author: vitaliy0x1

\u001faws.description:

\u001faws.author: Chester Le Bron (@123Le_Bron)

\u001faws.title: SES Identity Has Been Deleted
\u001faws.description: Detects an instance of an SES identity being deleted via the "DeleteIdentity" event. This may be an indicator of an adversary removing the account that carried out suspicious or malicious activities
\u001faws.author: Janantha Marasinghe

\u001faws.title: AWS SAML Provider Deletion Activity
\u001faws.description:
Detects the deletion of an AWS SAML provider, potentially indicating malicious intent to disrupt administrative or security team access.
An attacker can remove the SAML provider for the information security team or a team of system administrators, to make it difficult for them to work and investigat
\u001faws.author: Ivan Saakov

\u001faws.title: AWS S3 Bucket Versioning Disable
\u001faws.description: Detects when S3 bucket versioning is disabled. Threat actors use this technique during AWS ransomware incidents prior to deleting S3 objects.
\u001faws.author: Sean Johnstone | Unit 42

\u001faws.title: AWS EC2 Disable EBS Encryption
\u001faws.description:
Identifies disabling of default Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) encryption in the current region.
Disabling default encryption does not change the encryption status of your existing volumes.
\u001faws.author: Sittikorn S

\u001faws.title: AWS Key Pair Import Activity
\u001faws.description: Detects the import of SSH key pairs into AWS EC2, which may indicate an attacker attempting to gain unauthorized access to instances. This activity could lead to initial access, persistence, or privilege escalation, potentially compromising sensitive data and operations.
\u001faws.author: Ivan Saakov

\u001faws.title: AWS EC2 Startup Shell Script Change
\u001faws.description: Detects changes to the EC2 instance startup script. The shell script will be executed as root/SYSTEM every time the specific instances are booted up.
\u001faws.author: faloker

\u001faws.title: AWS EC2 VM Export Failure
\u001faws.description: An attempt to export an AWS EC2 instance has been detected. A VM Export might indicate an attempt to extract information from an instance.
\u001faws.author: Diogo Braz

\u001faws.title: AWS ECS Task Definition That Queries The Credential Endpoint
\u001faws.description:
Detects when an Elastic Container Service (ECS) Task Definition includes a command to query the credential endpoint.
This can indicate a potential adversary adding a backdoor to establish persistence or escalate privileges.
\u001faws.author: Darin Smith

\u001faws.title: AWS EFS Fileshare Modified or Deleted
\u001faws.description:
Detects when a EFS Fileshare is modified or deleted.
You can't delete a file system that is in use.
If the file system has any mount targets, the adversary must first delete them, so deletion of a mount will occur before deletion of a fileshare.
\u001faws.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001faws.title: AWS EFS Fileshare Mount Modified or Deleted
\u001faws.description: Detects when a EFS Fileshare Mount is modified or deleted. An adversary breaking any file system using the mount target that is being deleted, which might disrupt instances or applications using those mounts.

Backdoored users can be used to obtain persistence in the AWS environment.
Also with this alert, you can detect a flow of AWS keys in your org.
\u001faws.author: faloker

\u001faws.title: AWS KMS Imported Key Material Usage
\u001faws.description: Detects the import or deletion of key material in AWS KMS, which can be used as part of ransomware attacks. This activity is uncommon and provides a high certainty signal.
\u001faws.author: toopricey

\u001faws.title: New AWS Lambda Function URL Configuration Created
\u001faws.description:
Detects when a user creates a Lambda function URL configuration, which could be used to expose the function to the internet and potentially allow unauthorized access to the function's IAM role for AWS API calls.
This could give an adversary access to the privileges associated with the Lambda service

\u001faws.title: AWS New Lambda Layer Attached
\u001faws.description:
Detects when a user attached a Lambda layer to an existing Lambda function.
A malicious Lambda layer could execute arbitrary code in the context of the function's IAM role.
This would give an adversary access to resources that the function has access to.
\u001faws.author: Austin Songer

\u001faws.title: AWS Glue Development Endpoint Activity
\u001faws.description: Detects possible suspicious glue development endpoint activity.
\u001faws.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001faws.title: AWS RDS Master Password Change
\u001faws.description: Detects the change of database master password. It may be a part of data exfiltration.
\u001faws.author: faloker

\u001faws.description: Detects modifications to an RDS cluster or its deletion, which may indicate potential data exfiltration attempts, unauthorized access, or exposure of sensitive information.

\u001faws.description: Detects the recovery of a new public database instance from a snapshot. It may be a part of data exfiltration.

\u001faws.description:
Detects the use of TruffleHog for AWS credential validation by identifying GetCallerIdentity API calls where the userAgent indicates TruffleHog.

Successful exploitation allows threat actors to confirm the validity of compr

\u001faws.description: Identifies the suspicious use of GetSessionToken. Tokens could be created and used by attackers to move laterally and escalate privileges.

\u001faws.title: AWS Suspicious SAML Activity

\u001faws.title: AWS User Login Profile Was Modified
\u001faws.description:

An attacker with the "iam:UpdateLoginProfile" permission on other users can change the password used to login to the AWS console on any user that already has a login profile setup.

\u001fazure.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research), MSTIC

\u001fazure.title: Azure Network Security Configuration Modified or Deleted
\u001fazure.description: Identifies when a network security configuration is modified or deleted.
\u001fazure.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001fazure.title: Azure Virtual Network Device Modified or Deleted
\u001fazure.description:
Identifies when a virtual network device is being modified or deleted.
This can be a network interface, network virtual appliance, virtual hub, or virtual router.
\u001fazure.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001fazure.title: Azure New CloudShell Created
\u001fazure.description: Identifies when a new cloudshell is created inside of Azure portal.
\u001fazure.author: Austin Songer

\u001fazure.title: Azure Owner Removed From Application or Service Principal
\u001fazure.description: Identifies when a owner is was removed from a application or service principal in Azure.
\u001fazure.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001fazure.title: Rare Subscription-level Operations In Azure
\u001fazure.description: Identifies IPs from which users grant access to other users on azure resources and alerts when a previously unseen source IP address is used.
\u001fazure.author: sawwinnnaung

\u001fazure.title: Azure Service Principal Created
\u001fazure.description: Identifies when a service principal is created in Azure.
\u001fazure.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001fazure.title: Azure Service Principal Removed
\u001fazure.description: Identifies when a service principal was removed in Azure.
\u001fazure.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001fazure.title: Azure Subscription Permission Elevation Via ActivityLogs
\u001fazure.description:
Detects when a user has been elevated to manage all Azure Subscriptions.
This change should be investigated immediately if it isn't planned.
This setting could allow an attacker access to Azure subscriptions in your environment.
\u001fazure.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001fazure.title: Azure Suppression Rule Created
\u001fazure.description: Identifies when a suppression rule is created in Azure. Adversary's could attempt this to evade detection.
\u001fazure.author: Austin Songer

\u001fazure.title: Azure Virtual Network Modified or Deleted
\u001fazure.description: Identifies when a Virtual Network is modified or deleted in Azure.
\u001fazure.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001fazure.title: Azure VPN Connection Modified or Deleted
\u001fazure.description: Identifies when a VPN connection is modified or deleted.
\u001fazure.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001fazure.title: CA Policy Removed by Non Approved Actor
\u001fazure.description: Monitor and alert on conditional access changes where non approved actor removed CA Policy.
\u001fazure.author: Corissa Koopmans, '@corissalea'

\u001fazure.title: CA Policy Updated by Non Approved Actor
\u001fazure.description: Monitor and alert on conditional access changes. Is Initiated by (actor) approved to make changes? Review Modified Properties and compare "old" vs "new" value.
\u001fazure.author: Corissa Koopmans, '@corissalea'

\u001fazure.title: New CA Policy by Non-approved Actor
\u001fazure.description: Monitor and alert on conditional access changes.
\u001fazure.author: Corissa Koopmans, '@corissalea'

\u001fazure.title: Account Created And Deleted Within A Close Time Frame
\u001fazure.description: Detects when an account was created and deleted in a short period of time.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', MikeDuddington, '@dudders1', Tim Shelton

\u001fazure.title: Bitlocker Key Retrieval
\u001fazure.description: Monitor and alert for Bitlocker key retrieval.
\u001fazure.author: Michael Epping, '@mepples21'

\u001fazure.title: Certificate-Based Authentication Enabled
\u001fazure.description: Detects when certificate based authentication has been enabled in an Azure Active Directory tenant.
\u001fazure.author: Harjot Shah Singh, '@cyb3rjy0t'

\u001fazure.title: Changes to Device Registration Policy
\u001fazure.description: Monitor and alert for changes to the device registration policy.
\u001fazure.author: Michael Epping, '@mepples21'

\u001fazure.title: Guest Users Invited To Tenant By Non Approved Inviters
\u001fazure.description: Detects guest users being invited to tenant by non-approved inviters
\u001fazure.author: MikeDuddington, '@dudders1'

\u001fazure.title: New Root Certificate Authority Added
\u001fazure.description: Detects newly added root certificate authority to an AzureAD tenant to support certificate based authentication.
\u001fazure.author: Harjot Shah Singh, '@cyb3rjy0t'

\u001fazure.title: Users Added to Global or Device Admin Roles
\u001fazure.description: Monitor and alert for users added to device admin roles.
\u001fazure.author: Michael Epping, '@mepples21'

\u001fazure.title: Application AppID Uri Configuration Changes
\u001fazure.description: Detects when a configuration change is made to an applications AppID URI.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Bailey Bercik '@baileybercik'

\u001fazure.title: Added Credentials to Existing Application
\u001fazure.description: Detects when a new credential is added to an existing application. Any additional credentials added outside of expected processes could be a malicious actor using those credentials.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Bailey Bercik '@baileybercik'

\u001fazure.title: Delegated Permissions Granted For All Users
\u001fazure.description: Detects when highly privileged delegated permissions are granted on behalf of all users
\u001fazure.author: Bailey Bercik '@baileybercik', Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow'

\u001fazure.title: End User Consent
\u001fazure.description: Detects when an end user consents to an application
\u001fazure.author: Bailey Bercik '@baileybercik', Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow'

\u001fazure.title: End User Consent Blocked
\u001fazure.description: Detects when end user consent is blocked due to risk-based consent.
\u001fazure.author: Bailey Bercik '@baileybercik', Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow'

\u001fazure.title: Added Owner To Application
\u001fazure.description: Detects when a new owner is added to an application. This gives that account privileges to make modifications and configuration changes to the application.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Bailey Bercik '@baileybercik'

\u001fazure.title: App Granted Microsoft Permissions
\u001fazure.description: Detects when an application is granted delegated or app role permissions for Microsoft Graph, Exchange, Sharepoint, or Azure AD
\u001fazure.author: Bailey Bercik '@baileybercik', Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow'

\u001fazure.title: App Granted Privileged Delegated Or App Permissions
\u001fazure.description: Detects when administrator grants either application permissions (app roles) or highly privileged delegated permissions
\u001fazure.author: Bailey Bercik '@baileybercik', Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow'

\u001fazure.title: App Assigned To Azure RBAC/Microsoft Entra Role
\u001fazure.description: Detects when an app is assigned Azure AD roles, such as global administrator, or Azure RBAC roles, such as subscription owner.
\u001fazure.author: Bailey Bercik '@baileybercik', Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow'

\u001fazure.title: Application URI Configuration Changes
\u001fazure.description:
Detects when a configuration change is made to an applications URI.
URIs for domain names that no longer exist (dangling URIs), not using HTTPS, wildcards at the end of the domain, URIs that are no unique to that app, or URIs that point to domains you do not control should be investigated.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Bailey Bercik '@baileybercik'

\u001fazure.title: Windows LAPS Credential Dump From Entra ID
\u001fazure.description: Detects when an account dumps the LAPS password from Entra ID.
\u001fazure.author: andrewdanis

\u001fazure.title: Change to Authentication Method
\u001fazure.description: Change to authentication method could be an indicator of an attacker adding an auth method to the account so they can have continued access.
\u001fazure.author: AlertIQ

\u001fazure.title: Azure Domain Federation Settings Modified
\u001fazure.description: Identifies when an user or application modified the federation settings on the domain.
\u001fazure.author: Austin Songer

\u001fazure.title: User Added To Group With CA Policy Modification Access
\u001fazure.description: Monitor and alert on group membership additions of groups that have CA policy modification access
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Thomas Detzner '@tdetzner'

\u001fazure.title: User Removed From Group With CA Policy Modification Access
\u001fazure.description: Monitor and alert on group membership removal of groups that have CA policy modification access
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Thomas Detzner '@tdetzner'

\u001fazure.title: Guest User Invited By Non Approved Inviters
\u001fazure.description: Detects when a user that doesn't have permissions to invite a guest user attempts to invite one.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Yochana Henderson, '@Yochana-H'

\u001fazure.title: User State Changed From Guest To Member
\u001fazure.description: Detects the change of user type from "Guest" to "Member" for potential elevation of privilege.
\u001fazure.author: MikeDuddington, '@dudders1'

\u001fazure.title: PIM Approvals And Deny Elevation
\u001fazure.description: Detects when a PIM elevation is approved or denied. Outside of normal operations should be investigated.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Yochana Henderson, '@Yochana-H'

\u001fazure.title: PIM Alert Setting Changes To Disabled
\u001fazure.description: Detects when PIM alerts are set to disabled.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Yochana Henderson, '@Yochana-H'

\u001fazure.title: Changes To PIM Settings
\u001fazure.description: Detects when changes are made to PIM roles
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Yochana Henderson, '@Yochana-H'

\u001fazure.title: User Added To Privilege Role
\u001fazure.description: Detects when a user is added to a privileged role.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Yochana Henderson, '@Yochana-H'

\u001fazure.title: Bulk Deletion Changes To Privileged Account Permissions
\u001fazure.description: Detects when a user is removed from a privileged role. Bulk changes should be investigated.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Yochana Henderson, '@Yochana-H'

\u001fazure.title: Privileged Account Creation
\u001fazure.description: Detects when a new admin is created.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Yochana Henderson, '@Yochana-H', Tim Shelton

\u001fazure.title: Azure Subscription Permission Elevation Via AuditLogs
\u001fazure.description:
Detects when a user has been elevated to manage all Azure Subscriptions.
This change should be investigated immediately if it isn't planned.
This setting could allow an attacker access to Azure subscriptions in your environment.
\u001fazure.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001fazure.title: Temporary Access Pass Added To An Account
\u001fazure.description: Detects when a temporary access pass (TAP) is added to an account. TAPs added to priv accounts should be investigated
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Yochana Henderson, '@Yochana-H'

\u001fazure.title: User Risk and MFA Registration Policy Updated
\u001fazure.description:
Detects changes and updates to the user risk and MFA registration policy.
Attackers can modified the policies to Bypass MFA, weaken security thresholds, facilitate further attacks, maintain persistence.
\u001fazure.author: Harjot Singh (@cyb3rjy0t)

\u001fazure.title: Multi Factor Authentication Disabled For User Account
\u001fazure.description:
Detects changes to the "StrongAuthenticationRequirement" value, where the state is set to "0" or "Disabled".
Threat actors were seen disabling multi factor authentication for users in order to maintain or achieve access to the account. Also see in SIM Swap attacks.
\u001fazure.author: Harjot Singh (@cyb3rjy0t)

\u001fazure.title: Password Reset By User Account
\u001fazure.description: Detect when a user has reset their password in Azure AD
\u001fazure.author: YochanaHenderson, '@Yochana-H'

\u001fazure.title: Anomalous Token
\u001fazure.description: Indicates that there are abnormal characteristics in the token such as an unusual token lifetime or a token that is played from an unfamiliar location.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow'

\u001fazure.title: Anomalous User Activity
\u001fazure.description: Indicates that there are anomalous patterns of behavior like suspicious changes to the directory.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

\u001fazure.title: Activity From Anonymous IP Address
\u001fazure.description: Identifies that users were active from an IP address that has been identified as an anonymous proxy IP address.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

\u001fazure.title: Anonymous IP Address
\u001fazure.description: Indicates sign-ins from an anonymous IP address, for example, using an anonymous browser or VPN.
\u001fazure.author: Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

\u001fazure.title: Atypical Travel
\u001fazure.description: Identifies two sign-ins originating from geographically distant locations, where at least one of the locations may also be atypical for the user, given past behavior.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

\u001fazure.title: Impossible Travel
\u001fazure.description: Identifies user activities originating from geographically distant locations within a time period shorter than the time it takes to travel from the first location to the second.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

\u001fazure.title: Suspicious Inbox Forwarding Identity Protection
\u001fazure.description: Indicates suspicious rules such as an inbox rule that forwards a copy of all emails to an external address
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

\u001fazure.title: Suspicious Inbox Manipulation Rules
\u001fazure.description: Detects suspicious rules that delete or move messages or folders are set on a user's inbox.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

\u001fazure.title: Azure AD Account Credential Leaked
\u001fazure.description: Indicates that the user's valid credentials have been leaked.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

\u001fazure.title: Malicious IP Address Sign-In Failure Rate
\u001fazure.description: Indicates sign-in from a malicious IP address based on high failure rates.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

\u001fazure.title: Malicious IP Address Sign-In Suspicious
\u001fazure.description: Indicates sign-in from a malicious IP address known to be malicious at time of sign-in.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

\u001fazure.title: Sign-In From Malware Infected IP
\u001fazure.description: Indicates sign-ins from IP addresses infected with malware that is known to actively communicate with a bot server.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

\u001fazure.title: New Country
\u001fazure.description: Detects sign-ins from new countries. The detection considers past activity locations to determine new and infrequent locations.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

\u001fazure.title: Password Spray Activity
\u001fazure.description: Indicates that a password spray attack has been successfully performed.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

\u001fazure.title: Primary Refresh Token Access Attempt
\u001fazure.description: Indicates access attempt to the PRT resource which can be used to move laterally into an organization or perform credential theft
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

\u001fazure.title: Suspicious Browser Activity
\u001fazure.description: Indicates anomalous behavior based on suspicious sign-in activity across multiple tenants from different countries in the same browser
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

\u001fazure.title: Azure AD Threat Intelligence
\u001fazure.description: Indicates user activity that is unusual for the user or consistent with known attack patterns.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

\u001fazure.title: SAML Token Issuer Anomaly
\u001fazure.description: Indicates the SAML token issuer for the associated SAML token is potentially compromised. The claims included in the token are unusual or match known attacker patterns
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

\u001fazure.title: Unfamiliar Sign-In Properties
\u001fazure.description: Detects sign-in with properties that are unfamiliar to the user. The detection considers past sign-in history to look for anomalous sign-ins.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

\u001fazure.title: Stale Accounts In A Privileged Role
\u001fazure.description: Identifies when an account hasn't signed in during the past n number of days.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

\u001fazure.title: Invalid PIM License
\u001fazure.description: Identifies when an organization doesn't have the proper license for PIM and is out of compliance.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

\u001fazure.title: Roles Assigned Outside PIM
\u001fazure.description: Identifies when a privilege role assignment has taken place outside of PIM and may indicate an attack.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

\u001fazure.title: Roles Activated Too Frequently
\u001fazure.description: Identifies when the same privilege role has multiple activations by the same user.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

\u001fazure.title: Roles Are Not Being Used
\u001fazure.description: Identifies when a user has been assigned a privilege role and are not using that role.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

\u001fazure.title: Roles Activation Doesn't Require MFA
\u001fazure.description: Identifies when a privilege role can be activated without performing mfa.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

\u001fazure.title: Too Many Global Admins
\u001fazure.description: Identifies an event where there are there are too many accounts assigned the Global Administrator role.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Gloria Lee, '@gleeiamglo'

\u001fazure.title: Account Lockout
\u001fazure.description: Identifies user account which has been locked because the user tried to sign in too many times with an incorrect user ID or password.
\u001fazure.author: AlertIQ

\u001fazure.title: Successful Authentications From Countries You Do Not Operate Out Of
\u001fazure.description: Detect successful authentications from countries you do not operate out of.
\u001fazure.author: MikeDuddington, '@dudders1'

\u001fazure.title: Increased Failed Authentications Of Any Type
\u001fazure.description: Detects when sign-ins increased by 10% or greater.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', MikeDuddington, '@dudders1'

\u001fazure.title: Measurable Increase Of Successful Authentications
\u001fazure.description: Detects when successful sign-ins increased by 10% or greater.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', MikeDuddington, '@dudders1', Tim Shelton

\u001fazure.title: Authentications To Important Apps Using Single Factor Authentication
\u001fazure.description: Detect when authentications to important application(s) only required single-factor authentication
\u001fazure.author: MikeDuddington, '@dudders1'

\u001fazure.title: Discovery Using AzureHound
\u001fazure.description: Detects AzureHound (A BloodHound data collector for Microsoft Azure) activity via the default User-Agent that is used during its operation after successful authentication.
\u001fazure.author: Janantha Marasinghe

\u001fazure.title: Device Registration or Join Without MFA
\u001fazure.description: Monitor and alert for device registration or join events where MFA was not performed.
\u001fazure.author: Michael Epping, '@mepples21'

\u001fazure.title: Failed Authentications From Countries You Do Not Operate Out Of
\u001fazure.description: Detect failed authentications from countries you do not operate out of.
\u001fazure.author: MikeDuddington, '@dudders1'

\u001fazure.title: Azure AD Only Single Factor Authentication Required
\u001fazure.description: Detect when users are authenticating without MFA being required.
\u001fazure.author: MikeDuddington, '@dudders1'

\u001fazure.title: Suspicious SignIns From A Non Registered Device
\u001fazure.description: Detects risky authentication from a non AD registered device without MFA being required.
\u001fazure.author: Harjot Singh, '@cyb3rjy0t'

\u001fazure.title: Sign-ins from Non-Compliant Devices
\u001fazure.description: Monitor and alert for sign-ins where the device was non-compliant.
\u001fazure.author: Michael Epping, '@mepples21'

\u001fazure.title: Sign-ins by Unknown Devices
\u001fazure.description: Monitor and alert for Sign-ins by unknown devices from non-Trusted locations.
\u001fazure.author: Michael Epping, '@mepples21'

\u001fazure.title: Potential MFA Bypass Using Legacy Client Authentication
\u001fazure.description: Detects successful authentication from potential clients using legacy authentication via user agent strings. This could be a sign of MFA bypass using a password spray attack.
\u001fazure.author: Harjot Singh, '@cyb3rjy0t'

\u001fazure.title: Application Using Device Code Authentication Flow
\u001fazure.description:
Device code flow is an OAuth 2.0 protocol flow specifically for input constrained devices and is not used in all environments.
If this type of flow is seen in the environment and not being used in an input constrained device scenario, further investigation is warranted.
This can be a misconfigured a
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Bailey Bercik '@baileybercik'

\u001fazure.title: Applications That Are Using ROPC Authentication Flow
\u001fazure.description:
Resource owner password credentials (ROPC) should be avoided if at all possible as this requires the user to expose their current password credentials to the application directly.
The application then uses those credentials to authenticate the user against the identity provider.
\u001fazure.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Bailey Bercik '@baileybercik'

\u001fazure.title: Account Disabled or Blocked for Sign in Attempts
\u001fazure.description: Detects when an account is disabled or blocked for sign in but tried to log in
\u001fazure.author: Yochana Henderson, '@Yochana-H'

\u001fazure.title: Sign-in Failure Due to Conditional Access Requirements Not Met
\u001fazure.description: Define a baseline threshold for failed sign-ins due to Conditional Access failures
\u001fazure.author: Yochana Henderson, '@Yochana-H'

\u001fazure.title: Use of Legacy Authentication Protocols
\u001fazure.description: Alert on when legacy authentication has been used on an account
\u001fazure.author: Yochana Henderson, '@Yochana-H'

\u001fazure.title: Login to Disabled Account
\u001fazure.description: Detect failed attempts to sign in to disabled accounts.
\u001fazure.author: AlertIQ

\u001fazure.title: Multifactor Authentication Denied
\u001fazure.description: User has indicated they haven't instigated the MFA prompt and could indicate an attacker has the password for the account.
\u001fazure.author: AlertIQ

\u001fazure.title: Multifactor Authentication Interrupted
\u001fazure.description: Identifies user login with multifactor authentication failures, which might be an indication an attacker has the password for the account but can't pass the MFA challenge.
\u001fazure.author: AlertIQ

\u001fazure.title: Azure Unusual Authentication Interruption
\u001fazure.description: Detects when there is a interruption in the authentication process.
\u001fazure.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001fazure.title: Users Authenticating To Other Azure AD Tenants
\u001fazure.description: Detect when users in your Azure AD tenant are authenticating to other Azure AD Tenants.
\u001fazure.author: MikeDuddington, '@dudders1'

\u001fazure.title: User Access Blocked by Azure Conditional Access
\u001fazure.description:
Detect access has been blocked by Conditional Access policies.
The access policy does not allow token issuance which might be sights≈ of unauthorizeed login to valid accounts.
\u001fazure.author: AlertIQ

\u001fgcp.title: GCP Access Policy Deleted
\u001fgcp.description:
Detects when an access policy that is applied to a GCP cloud resource is deleted.
An adversary would be able to remove access policies to gain access to a GCP cloud resource.
\u001fgcp.author: Bryan Lim

\u001fgcp.title: GCP Break-glass Container Workload Deployed
\u001fgcp.description: Detects the deployment of workloads that are deployed by using the break-glass flag to override Binary Authorization controls.
\u001fgcp.author: Bryan Lim

\u001fgcp.title: Google Cloud Storage Buckets Enumeration
\u001fgcp.description: Detects when storage bucket is enumerated in Google Cloud.
\u001fgcp.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001fgcp.title: Google Cloud Storage Buckets Modified or Deleted
\u001fgcp.description: Detects when storage bucket is modified or deleted in Google Cloud.
\u001fgcp.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001fgcp.title: Google Cloud Re-identifies Sensitive Information
\u001fgcp.description: Identifies when sensitive information is re-identified in google Cloud.
\u001fgcp.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001fgcp.title: Google Cloud DNS Zone Modified or Deleted
\u001fgcp.description: Identifies when a DNS Zone is modified or deleted in Google Cloud.
\u001fgcp.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001fgcp.title: Google Cloud Firewall Modified or Deleted
\u001fgcp.description: Detects  when a firewall rule is modified or deleted in Google Cloud Platform (GCP).
\u001fgcp.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001fgcp.title: Google Full Network Traffic Packet Capture
\u001fgcp.description: Identifies potential full network packet capture in gcp. This feature can potentially be abused to read sensitive data from unencrypted internal traffic.
\u001fgcp.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001fgcp.title: Google Cloud Kubernetes Admission Controller
\u001fgcp.description:
Identifies when an admission controller is executed in GCP Kubernetes.
A Kubernetes Admission controller intercepts, and possibly modifies, requests to the Kubernetes API server.
The behavior of this admission controller is determined by an admission webhook (MutatingAdmissionWebhook or ValidatingAd
\u001fgcp.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001fgcp.title: Google Cloud Kubernetes CronJob
\u001fgcp.description:
Identifies when a Google Cloud Kubernetes CronJob runs in Azure Cloud. Kubernetes Job is a controller that creates one or more pods and ensures that a specified number of them successfully terminate.
Kubernetes Job can be used to run containers that perform finite tasks for batch jobs. Kubernetes Cr
\u001fgcp.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001fgcp.title: Google Cloud Kubernetes RoleBinding
\u001fgcp.description: Detects the creation or patching of potential malicious RoleBinding. This includes RoleBindings and ClusterRoleBinding.
\u001fgcp.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001fgcp.title: Google Cloud Kubernetes Secrets Modified or Deleted
\u001fgcp.description: Identifies when the Secrets are Modified or Deleted.
\u001fgcp.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001fgcp.title: Google Cloud Service Account Disabled or Deleted
\u001fgcp.description: Identifies when a service account is disabled or deleted in Google Cloud.
\u001fgcp.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001fgcp.title: Google Cloud Service Account Modified
\u001fgcp.description: Identifies when a service account is modified in Google Cloud.
\u001fgcp.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001fgcp.title: Google Cloud SQL Database Modified or Deleted
\u001fgcp.description: Detect when a Cloud SQL DB has been modified or deleted.
\u001fgcp.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001fgcp.title: Google Cloud VPN Tunnel Modified or Deleted
\u001fgcp.description: Identifies when a VPN Tunnel Modified or Deleted in Google Cloud.
\u001fgcp.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001fgcp.title: Google Workspace Application Access Level Modified
\u001fgcp.description:
Detects when an access level is changed for a Google workspace application.
An access level is part of BeyondCorp Enterprise which is Google Workspace's way of enforcing Zero Trust model.
An adversary would be able to remove access levels to gain easier access to Google workspace resources.
\u001fgcp.author: Bryan Lim

\u001fgcp.title: Google Workspace Application Removed
\u001fgcp.description: Detects when an an application is removed from Google Workspace.
\u001fgcp.author: Austin Songer

\u001fgcp.title: Google Workspace Granted Domain API Access
\u001fgcp.description: Detects when an API access service account is granted domain authority.
\u001fgcp.author: Austin Songer

\u001fgcp.title: Google Workspace MFA Disabled
\u001fgcp.description: Detects when multi-factor authentication (MFA) is disabled.
\u001fgcp.author: Austin Songer

\u001fgcp.title: Google Workspace Role Modified or Deleted
\u001fgcp.description: Detects when an a role is modified or deleted in Google Workspace.
\u001fgcp.author: Austin Songer

\u001fgcp.title: Google Workspace Role Privilege Deleted
\u001fgcp.description: Detects when an a role privilege is deleted in Google Workspace.
\u001fgcp.author: Austin Songer

\u001fgcp.title: Google Workspace User Granted Admin Privileges
\u001fgcp.description: Detects when an Google Workspace user is granted admin privileges.
\u001fgcp.author: Austin Songer

\u001fgcp.title: Google Workspace Government Attack Warning
\u001fgcp.description: Detects a login attempt in Google Workspace flagged as a potential attack by a government-backed threat actor
\u001fgcp.author: Tom Kluter

\u001fgcp.title: Google Workspace Out Of Domain Email Forwarding
\u001fgcp.description: Detects automatic email forwarding to external domains in Google Workspace, which may indicate data leakage or misuse.
\u001fgcp.author: Tom kluter

\u001fgcp.title: Suspicious Login Activity Classified By Google
\u001fgcp.description: Detects Google Workspace login activity that's classified as suspicious by Google.
\u001fgcp.author: Tom Kluter

\u001fm365.title: Azure Login Bypassing Conditional Access Policies
\u001fm365.description: Detects a successful login to the Microsoft Intune Company Portal which could allow bypassing Conditional Access Policies and InTune device trust using a tool like TokenSmith.
\u001fm365.author: Josh Nickels, Marius Rothenbücher

\u001fm365.title: Disabling Multi Factor Authentication
\u001fm365.description: Detects disabling of Multi Factor Authentication.
\u001fm365.author: Splunk Threat Research Team (original rule), Harjot Singh @cyb3rjy0t (sigma rule)

\u001fm365.title: New Federated Domain Added
\u001fm365.description: Detects the addition of a new Federated Domain.
\u001fm365.author: Splunk Threat Research Team (original rule), Harjot Singh @cyb3rjy0t (sigma rule)

\u001fm365.title: Suspicious Email Delivered In Microsoft 365
\u001fm365.description:
Detects instances where an email, identified as malicious or suspicious by the Microsoft Defender for Office 365 (formerly ATP) engine, was delivered to a user's Inbox or Junk folder.
It might indicate that a potential threat, such as a spearphishing attachment or links, has bypassed initial blockin
\u001fm365.author: Marco Pedrinazzi (@pedrinazziM) (InTheCyber)

\u001fm365.title: New Federated Domain Added - Exchange
\u001fm365.description: Detects the addition of a new Federated Domain.
\u001fm365.author: Splunk Threat Research Team (original rule), '@ionsor (rule)'

\u001fm365.title: Activity from Suspicious IP Addresses
\u001fm365.description:
Detects when a Microsoft Cloud App Security reported users were active from an IP address identified as risky by Microsoft Threat Intelligence.
These IP addresses are involved in malicious activities, such as Botnet C&C, and may indicate compromised account.
\u001fm365.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001fm365.title: Activity Performed by Terminated User
\u001fm365.description:
Detects when a Microsoft Cloud App Security reported for users whose account were terminated in Azure AD, but still perform activities in other platforms such as AWS or Salesforce.
This is especially relevant for users who use another account to manage resources, since these accounts are often not t
\u001fm365.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001fm365.title: Activity from Anonymous IP Addresses
\u001fm365.description: Detects when a Microsoft Cloud App Security reported when users were active from an IP address that has been identified as an anonymous proxy IP address.
\u001fm365.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001fm365.title: Activity from Infrequent Country
\u001fm365.description: Detects when a Microsoft Cloud App Security reported when an activity occurs from a location that wasn't recently or never visited by any user in the organization.
\u001fm365.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001fm365.title: Data Exfiltration to Unsanctioned Apps
\u001fm365.description: Detects when a Microsoft Cloud App Security reported when a user or IP address uses an app that is not sanctioned to perform an activity that resembles an attempt to exfiltrate information from your organization.
\u001fm365.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001fm365.title: Microsoft 365 - Impossible Travel Activity
\u001fm365.description: Detects when a Microsoft Cloud App Security reported a risky sign-in attempt due to a login associated with an impossible travel.
\u001fm365.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001fm365.title: Logon from a Risky IP Address
\u001fm365.description: Detects when a Microsoft Cloud App Security reported when a user signs into your sanctioned apps from a risky IP address.
\u001fm365.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001fm365.title: Microsoft 365 - Potential Ransomware Activity
\u001fm365.description: Detects when a Microsoft Cloud App Security reported when a user uploads files to the cloud that might be infected with ransomware.
\u001fm365.author: austinsonger

\u001fm365.title: PST Export Alert Using eDiscovery Alert
\u001fm365.description: Alert on when a user has performed an eDiscovery search or exported a PST file from the search. This PST file usually has sensitive information including email body content
\u001fm365.author: Sorina Ionescu

\u001fm365.title: PST Export Alert Using New-ComplianceSearchAction
\u001fm365.description: Alert when a user has performed an export to a search using 'New-ComplianceSearchAction' with the '-Export' flag. This detection will detect PST export even if the 'eDiscovery search or exported' alert is disabled in the O365.This rule will apply to ExchangePowerShell usage and from the cloud.
\u001fm365.author: Nikita Khalimonenkov

\u001fm365.title: Suspicious Inbox Forwarding
\u001fm365.description: Detects when a Microsoft Cloud App Security reported suspicious email forwarding rules, for example, if a user created an inbox rule that forwards a copy of all emails to an external address.
\u001fm365.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001fm365.title: Suspicious OAuth App File Download Activities
\u001fm365.description: Detects when a Microsoft Cloud App Security reported when an app downloads multiple files from Microsoft SharePoint or Microsoft OneDrive in a manner that is unusual for the user.
\u001fm365.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

\u001fm365.title: Microsoft 365 - Unusual Volume of File Deletion
\u001fm365.description: Detects when a Microsoft Cloud App Security reported a user has deleted a unusual a large volume of files.
\u001fm365.author: austinsonger

\u001fm365.title: Microsoft 365 - User Restricted from Sending Email
\u001fm365.description: Detects when a Security Compliance Center reported a user who exceeded sending limits of the service policies and because of this has been restricted from sending email.
\u001fm365.author: austinsonger

\u001fcisco.title: Cisco Clear Logs
\u001fcisco.description: Clear command history in network OS which is used for defense evasion
\u001fcisco.author: Austin Clark

\u001fcisco.title: Cisco Collect Data
\u001fcisco.description: Collect pertinent data from the configuration files
\u001fcisco.author: Austin Clark
