\u001fcisco.title: Cisco Crypto Commands
\u001fcisco.description: Show when private keys are being exported from the device, or when new certificates are installed
\u001fcisco.author: Austin Clark

\u001fcisco.title: Cisco Disabling Logging
\u001fcisco.description: Turn off logging locally or remote
\u001fcisco.author: Austin Clark

\u001fcisco.title: Cisco Discovery
\u001fcisco.description: Find information about network devices that is not stored in config files
\u001fcisco.author: Austin Clark

\u001fcisco.title: Cisco Denial of Service
\u001fcisco.description: Detect a system being shutdown or put into different boot mode
\u001fcisco.author: Austin Clark

\u001fcisco.title: Cisco Dot1x Disabled
\u001fcisco.description:
Detects the manual disablement of IEEE 802.1X (dot1x) on a Cisco network device interface.
Disabling dot1x bypasses Network Access Control (NAC) mechanisms, potentially allowing unauthorized devices to gain access to the internal network.
This activity is a common technique used by attackers or mali
\u001fcisco.author: Luc Génaux

\u001fcisco.title: Cisco File Deletion
\u001fcisco.description: See what files are being deleted from flash file systems
\u001fcisco.author: Austin Clark

\u001fcisco.title: Cisco Show Commands Input
\u001fcisco.description: See what commands are being input into the device by other people, full credentials can be in the history
\u001fcisco.author: Austin Clark

\u001fcisco.title: Cisco Local Accounts
\u001fcisco.description: Find local accounts being created or modified as well as remote authentication configurations
\u001fcisco.author: Austin Clark

\u001fcisco.title: Cisco Modify Configuration
\u001fcisco.description: Modifications to a config that will serve an adversary's impacts or persistence
\u001fcisco.author: Austin Clark

\u001fcisco.title: Cisco Stage Data
\u001fcisco.description: Various protocols maybe used to put data on the device for exfil or infil
\u001fcisco.author: Austin Clark

\u001fcisco.title: Cisco Sniffing
\u001fcisco.description: Show when a monitor or a span/rspan is setup or modified
\u001fcisco.author: Austin Clark

\u001fcisco.title: Cisco BGP Authentication Failures
\u001fcisco.description: Detects BGP failures which may be indicative of brute force attacks to manipulate routing
\u001fcisco.author: Tim Brown

\u001fcisco.title: Cisco LDP Authentication Failures
\u001fcisco.description: Detects LDP failures which may be indicative of brute force attacks to manipulate MPLS labels
\u001fcisco.author: Tim Brown

dns\u001f.title: DNS Query to External Service Interaction Domains
dns\u001f.description: Detects suspicious DNS queries to external service interaction domains often used for out-of-band interactions after successful RCE
dns\u001f.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Matt Kelly (list of domains)

dns\u001f.title: Cobalt Strike DNS Beaconing
dns\u001f.description: Detects suspicious DNS queries known from Cobalt Strike beacons
dns\u001f.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

dns\u001f.title: Monero Crypto Coin Mining Pool Lookup
dns\u001f.description: Detects suspicious DNS queries to Monero mining pools
dns\u001f.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

dns\u001f.title: Suspicious DNS Query with B64 Encoded String
dns\u001f.description: Detects suspicious DNS queries using base64 encoding
dns\u001f.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

dns\u001f.title: Telegram Bot API Request
dns\u001f.description: Detects suspicious DNS queries to api.telegram.org used by Telegram Bots of any kind
dns\u001f.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

dns\u001f.title: DNS TXT Answer with Possible Execution Strings
dns\u001f.description: Detects strings used in command execution in DNS TXT Answer
dns\u001f.author: Markus Neis

dns\u001f.title: Wannacry Killswitch Domain
dns\u001f.description: Detects wannacry killswitch domain dns queries
dns\u001f.author: Mike Wade

firewall\u001f.title: Cleartext Protocol Usage
firewall\u001f.description:
Ensure that all account usernames and authentication credentials are transmitted across networks using encrypted channels.
Ensure that an encryption is used for all sensitive information in transit. Ensure that an encrypted channels is used for all administrative account access.
firewall\u001f.author: Alexandr Yampolskyi, SOC Prime, Tim Shelton

\u001ffortigate.title: FortiGate - New Administrator Account Created
\u001ffortigate.description: Detects the creation of an administrator account on a Fortinet FortiGate Firewall.
\u001ffortigate.author: Marco Pedrinazzi @pedrinazziM (InTheCyber)

\u001ffortigate.title: FortiGate - Firewall Address Object Added
\u001ffortigate.description: Detects the addition of firewall address objects on a Fortinet FortiGate Firewall.
\u001ffortigate.author: Marco Pedrinazzi @pedrinazziM (InTheCyber)

\u001ffortigate.title: FortiGate - New Firewall Policy Added
\u001ffortigate.description: Detects the addition of a new firewall policy on a Fortinet FortiGate Firewall.
\u001ffortigate.author: Marco Pedrinazzi @pedrinazziM (InTheCyber)

\u001ffortigate.title: FortiGate - New Local User Created
\u001ffortigate.description:
Detects the creation of a new local user on a Fortinet FortiGate Firewall.
The new local user could be used for VPN connections.
\u001ffortigate.author: Marco Pedrinazzi @pedrinazziM (InTheCyber)

\u001ffortigate.title: FortiGate - New VPN SSL Web Portal Added
\u001ffortigate.description:
Detects the addition of a VPN SSL Web Portal on a Fortinet FortiGate Firewall.
This behavior was observed in pair with modification of VPN SSL settings.
\u001ffortigate.author: Marco Pedrinazzi @pedrinazziM (InTheCyber)

\u001ffortigate.title: FortiGate - User Group Modified
\u001ffortigate.description:
Detects the modification of a user group on a Fortinet FortiGate Firewall.
The group could be used to grant VPN access to a network.
\u001ffortigate.author: Marco Pedrinazzi @pedrinazziM (InTheCyber)

\u001ffortigate.title: FortiGate - VPN SSL Settings Modified
\u001ffortigate.description:
Detects the modification of VPN SSL Settings (for example, the modification of authentication rules).
This behavior was observed in pair with the addition of a VPN SSL Web Portal.
\u001ffortigate.author: Marco Pedrinazzi @pedrinazziM (InTheCyber)

\u001fhuawei.title: Huawei BGP Authentication Failures
\u001fhuawei.description: Detects BGP failures which may be indicative of brute force attacks to manipulate routing.
\u001fhuawei.author: Tim Brown

\u001fjuniper.title: Juniper BGP Missing MD5
\u001fjuniper.description: Detects juniper BGP missing MD5 digest. Which may be indicative of brute force attacks to manipulate routing.
\u001fjuniper.author: Tim Brown

\u001fzeek.title: MITRE BZAR Indicators for Execution
\u001fzeek.description: Windows DCE-RPC functions which indicate an execution techniques on the remote system. All credit for the Zeek mapping of the suspicious endpoint/operation field goes to MITRE
\u001fzeek.author: @neu5ron, SOC Prime

\u001fzeek.title: MITRE BZAR Indicators for Persistence
\u001fzeek.description: Windows DCE-RPC functions which indicate a persistence techniques on the remote system. All credit for the Zeek mapping of the suspicious endpoint/operation field goes to MITRE.
\u001fzeek.author: @neu5ron, SOC Prime

\u001fzeek.title: Potential PetitPotam Attack Via EFS RPC Calls
\u001fzeek.description:
Detects usage of the windows RPC library Encrypting File System Remote Protocol (MS-EFSRPC). Variations of this RPC are used within the attack refereed to as PetitPotam.
The usage of this RPC function should be rare if ever used at all.
Thus usage of this function is uncommon enough that any usage o
\u001fzeek.author: @neu5ron, @Antonlovesdnb, Mike Remen

\u001fzeek.title: SMB Spoolss Name Piped Usage
\u001fzeek.description: Detects the use of the spoolss named pipe over SMB. This can be used to trigger the authentication via NTLM of any machine that has the spoolservice enabled.
\u001fzeek.author: OTR (Open Threat Research), @neu5ron

\u001fzeek.title: Default Cobalt Strike Certificate
\u001fzeek.description: Detects the presence of default Cobalt Strike certificate in the HTTPS traffic
\u001fzeek.author: Bhabesh Raj

\u001fzeek.title: Suspicious DNS Query Indicating Kerberos Coercion via DNS Object SPN Spoofing - Network
\u001fzeek.description:
Detects DNS queries containing patterns associated with Kerberos coercion attacks via DNS object spoofing.
The pattern "1UWhRCAAAAA..BAAAA" is a base64-encoded signature that corresponds to a marshaled CREDENTIAL_TARGET_INFORMATION structure.
Attackers can use this technique to coerce authentication
\u001fzeek.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

\u001fzeek.title: DNS Events Related To Mining Pools
\u001fzeek.description: Identifies clients that may be performing DNS lookups associated with common currency mining pools.
\u001fzeek.author: Saw Winn Naung, Azure-Sentinel, @neu5ron

\u001fzeek.title: New Kind of Network (NKN) Detection
\u001fzeek.description: NKN is a networking service using blockchain technology to support a decentralized network of peers. While there are legitimate uses for it, it can also be used as a C2 channel. This rule looks for a DNS request to the ma>
\u001fzeek.author: Michael Portera (@mportatoes)

\u001fzeek.title: Suspicious DNS Z Flag Bit Set
\u001fzeek.description:
The DNS Z flag is bit within the DNS protocol header that is, per the IETF design, meant to be used reserved (unused).
Although recently it has been used in DNSSec, the value being set to anything other than 0 should be rare.
Otherwise if it is set to non 0 and DNSSec is being used, then excluding t
\u001fzeek.author: @neu5ron, SOC Prime Team, Corelight

\u001fzeek.title: DNS TOR Proxies
\u001fzeek.description: Identifies IPs performing DNS lookups associated with common Tor proxies.
\u001fzeek.author: Saw Winn Naung , Azure-Sentinel

\u001fzeek.title: Executable from Webdav
\u001fzeek.description: Detects executable access via webdav6. Can be seen in APT 29 such as from the emulated APT 29 hackathon https://github.com/OTRF/detection-hackathon-apt29/
\u001fzeek.author: SOC Prime, Adam Swan

\u001fzeek.title: HTTP Request to Low Reputation TLD or Suspicious File Extension
\u001fzeek.description: Detects HTTP requests to low reputation TLDs (e.g. .xyz, .top, .ru) or ending in suspicious file extensions (.exe, .dll, .hta), which may indicate malicious activity.
\u001fzeek.author: @signalblur, Corelight

\u001fzeek.title: WebDav Put Request
\u001fzeek.description: A General detection for WebDav user-agent being used to PUT files on a WebDav network share. This could be an indicator of exfiltration.
\u001fzeek.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)

\u001fzeek.title: Publicly Accessible RDP Service
\u001fzeek.description: Detects connections from routable IPs to an RDP listener. Which is indicative of a publicly-accessible RDP service.
\u001fzeek.author: Josh Brower @DefensiveDepth

\u001fzeek.title: Remote Task Creation via ATSVC Named Pipe - Zeek
\u001fzeek.description: Detects remote task creation via at.exe or API interacting with ATSVC namedpipe
\u001fzeek.author: Samir Bousseaden, @neu5rn

\u001fzeek.title: Possible Impacket SecretDump Remote Activity - Zeek
\u001fzeek.description: Detect AD credential dumping using impacket secretdump HKTL. Based on the SIGMA rules/windows/builtin/win_impacket_secretdump.yml
\u001fzeek.author: Samir Bousseaden, @neu5ron

\u001fzeek.title: First Time Seen Remote Named Pipe - Zeek
\u001fzeek.description: This detection excludes known namped pipes accessible remotely and notify on newly observed ones, may help to detect lateral movement and remote exec using named pipes
\u001fzeek.author: Samir Bousseaden, @neu5ron, Tim Shelton

\u001fzeek.title: Suspicious PsExec Execution - Zeek
\u001fzeek.description: detects execution of psexec or paexec with renamed service name, this rule helps to filter out the noise if psexec is used for legit purposes or if attacker uses a different psexec client other than sysinternal one
\u001fzeek.author: Samir Bousseaden, @neu5ron, Tim Shelton

\u001fzeek.title: Suspicious Access to Sensitive File Extensions - Zeek
\u001fzeek.description: Detects known sensitive file extensions via Zeek
\u001fzeek.author: Samir Bousseaden, @neu5ron

\u001fzeek.title: Transferring Files with Credential Data via Network Shares - Zeek
\u001fzeek.description: Transferring files with well-known filenames (sensitive files with credential data) using network shares
\u001fzeek.author: @neu5ron, Teymur Kheirkhabarov, oscd.community

\u001fzeek.title: Kerberos Network Traffic RC4 Ticket Encryption
\u001fzeek.description: Detects kerberos TGS request using RC4 encryption which may be indicative of kerberoasting
\u001fzeek.author: sigma

\u001fwindows.title: Mimikatz Use
\u001fwindows.description: This method detects mimikatz keywords in different Eventlogs (some of them only appear in older Mimikatz version that are however still used by different threat groups)
\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), David ANDRE (additional keywords)

\u001fwindows.title: LSASS Process Crashed - Application
\u001fwindows.description:
Detects Windows error reporting events where the process that crashed is LSASS (Local Security Authority Subsystem Service).
This could be the cause of a provoked crash by techniques such as Lsass-Shtinkering to dump credentials.
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Microsoft Malware Protection Engine Crash
\u001fwindows.description: This rule detects a suspicious crash of the Microsoft Malware Protection Engine
\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Ntdsutil Abuse
\u001fwindows.description: Detects potential abuse of ntdsutil to dump ntds.dit database
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Dump Ntds.dit To Suspicious Location
\u001fwindows.description: Detects potential abuse of ntdsutil to dump ntds.dit database to a suspicious location
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Audit CVE Event
\u001fwindows.description:
Detects events generated by user-mode applications when they call the CveEventWrite API when a known vulnerability is trying to be exploited.
MS started using this log in Jan. 2020 with CVE-2020-0601 (a Windows CryptoAPI vulnerability.
Unfortunately, that is about the only instance of CVEs being wri
\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Zach Mathis

\u001fwindows.title: Backup Catalog Deleted
\u001fwindows.description: Detects backup catalog deletions
\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Tom U. @c_APT_ure (collection)

\u001fwindows.title: Restricted Software Access By SRP
\u001fwindows.description: Detects restricted access to applications by the Software Restriction Policies (SRP) policy
\u001fwindows.author: frack113

\u001fwindows.title: Application Uninstalled
\u001fwindows.description: An application has been removed. Check if it is critical.
\u001fwindows.author: frack113

\u001fwindows.title: MSI Installation From Suspicious Locations
\u001fwindows.description: Detects MSI package installation from suspicious locations
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: MSI Installation From Web
\u001fwindows.description: Detects installation of a remote msi file from web.
\u001fwindows.author: Stamatis Chatzimangou

\u001fwindows.title: Atera Agent Installation
\u001fwindows.description: Detects successful installation of Atera Remote Monitoring & Management (RMM) agent as recently found to be used by Conti operators
\u001fwindows.author: Bhabesh Raj

\u001fwindows.title: MSSQL Add Account To Sysadmin Role
\u001fwindows.description: Detects when an attacker tries to backdoor the MSSQL server by adding a backdoor account to the sysadmin fixed server role
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: MSSQL Destructive Query
\u001fwindows.description: Detects the invocation of MS SQL transactions that are destructive towards table or database data, such as "DROP TABLE" or "DROP DATABASE".
\u001fwindows.author: Daniel Degasperi '@d4ns4n_'

\u001fwindows.title: MSSQL Disable Audit Settings
\u001fwindows.description: Detects when an attacker calls the "ALTER SERVER AUDIT" or "DROP SERVER AUDIT" transaction in order to delete or disable audit logs on the server
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: MSSQL Server Failed Logon
\u001fwindows.description: Detects failed logon attempts from clients to MSSQL server.
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), j4son

\u001fwindows.title: MSSQL Server Failed Logon From External Network
\u001fwindows.description: Detects failed logon attempts from clients with external network IP to an MSSQL server. This can be a sign of a bruteforce attack.
\u001fwindows.author: j4son

\u001fwindows.title: MSSQL SPProcoption Set
\u001fwindows.description: Detects when the a stored procedure is set or cleared for automatic execution in MSSQL. A stored procedure that is set to automatic execution runs every time an instance of SQL Server is started
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: MSSQL XPCmdshell Suspicious Execution
\u001fwindows.description: Detects when the MSSQL "xp_cmdshell" stored procedure is used to execute commands
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: MSSQL XPCmdshell Option Change
\u001fwindows.description: Detects when the MSSQL "xp_cmdshell" stored procedure setting is changed.
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Relevant Anti-Virus Signature Keywords In Application Log
\u001fwindows.description: Detects potentially highly relevant antivirus events in the application log based on known virus signature names and malware keywords.
\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Arnim Rupp

\u001fwindows.title: Remote Access Tool - ScreenConnect Command Execution
\u001fwindows.description: Detects command execution via ScreenConnect RMM
\u001fwindows.author: Ali Alwashali

\u001fwindows.title: Remote Access Tool - ScreenConnect File Transfer
\u001fwindows.description: Detects file being transferred via ScreenConnect RMM
\u001fwindows.author: Ali Alwashali

\u001fwindows.title: Microsoft Malware Protection Engine Crash - WER
\u001fwindows.description: This rule detects a suspicious crash of the Microsoft Malware Protection Engine
\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: AppLocker Prevented Application or Script from Running
\u001fwindows.description: Detects when AppLocker prevents the execution of an Application, DLL, Script, MSI, or Packaged-App from running.
\u001fwindows.author: Pushkarev Dmitry

\u001fwindows.title: Sysinternals Tools AppX Versions Execution
\u001fwindows.description:
Detects execution of Sysinternals tools via an AppX package.
Attackers could install the Sysinternals Suite to get access to tools such as psexec and procdump to avoid detection based on System paths.
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Deployment AppX Package Was Blocked By AppLocker
\u001fwindows.description: Detects an appx package deployment that was blocked by AppLocker policy.
\u001fwindows.author: frack113

\u001fwindows.title: Remote AppX Package Downloaded from File Sharing or CDN Domain
\u001fwindows.description: Detects an appx package that was added to the pipeline of the "to be processed" packages which was downloaded from a file sharing or CDN domain.
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: AppX Package Deployment Failed Due to Signing Requirements
\u001fwindows.description: Detects an appx package deployment / installation with the error code "0x80073cff" which indicates that the package didn't meet the signing requirements.
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: AppX Located in Known Staging Directory Added to Deployment Pipeline
\u001fwindows.description: Detects an appx package that was added to the pipeline of the "to be processed" packages that is located in a known folder often used as a staging directory.
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Potential Malicious AppX Package Installation Attempts
\u001fwindows.description: Detects potential installation or installation attempts of known malicious appx packages
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Deployment Of The AppX Package Was Blocked By The Policy
\u001fwindows.description:
Detects an appx package deployment that was blocked by the local computer policy.
The following events indicate that an AppX package deployment was blocked by a policy:
- Event ID 441: The package deployment operation is blocked by the "Allow deployment operations in special profiles" policy
- Event
\u001fwindows.author: frack113

\u001fwindows.title: AppX Located in Uncommon Directory Added to Deployment Pipeline
\u001fwindows.description: Detects an appx package that was added to the pipeline of the "to be processed" packages that is located in uncommon locations.
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Windows AppX Deployment Full Trust Package Installation
\u001fwindows.description: Detects the installation of MSIX/AppX packages with full trust privileges which run with elevated privileges outside normal AppX container restrictions
\u001fwindows.author: Michael Haag, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Windows AppX Deployment Unsigned Package Installation
\u001fwindows.description: Detects attempts to install unsigned MSIX/AppX packages using the -AllowUnsigned parameter via AppXDeployment-Server events
\u001fwindows.author: Michael Haag, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious Digital Signature Of AppX Package
\u001fwindows.description: Detects execution of AppX packages with known suspicious or malicious signature
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: New BITS Job Created Via Bitsadmin
\u001fwindows.description: Detects the creation of a new bits job by Bitsadmin
\u001fwindows.author: frack113

\u001fwindows.title: New BITS Job Created Via PowerShell
\u001fwindows.description: Detects the creation of a new bits job by PowerShell
\u001fwindows.author: frack113

\u001fwindows.title: BITS Transfer Job Downloading File Potential Suspicious Extension
\u001fwindows.description: Detects new BITS transfer job saving local files with potential suspicious extensions
\u001fwindows.author: frack113

\u001fwindows.title: BITS Transfer Job Download From File Sharing Domains
\u001fwindows.description: Detects BITS transfer job downloading files from a file sharing domain.
\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: BITS Transfer Job Download From Direct IP
\u001fwindows.description: Detects a BITS transfer job downloading file(s) from a direct IP address.
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: BITS Transfer Job With Uncommon Or Suspicious Remote TLD
\u001fwindows.description: Detects a suspicious download using the BITS client from a FQDN that is unusual. Adversaries may abuse BITS jobs to persistently execute or clean up after malicious payloads.
\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: BITS Transfer Job Download To Potential Suspicious Folder
\u001fwindows.description: Detects new BITS transfer job where the LocalName/Saved file is stored in a potentially suspicious location
\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Certificate Private Key Acquired
\u001fwindows.description: Detects when an application acquires a certificate private key
\u001fwindows.author: Zach Mathis

\u001fwindows.title: Certificate Exported From Local Certificate Store
\u001fwindows.description: Detects when an application exports a certificate (and potentially the private key as well) from the local Windows certificate store.
\u001fwindows.author: Zach Mathis

\u001fwindows.title: CodeIntegrity - Unmet Signing Level Requirements By File Under Validation
\u001fwindows.description:
Detects attempted file load events that did not meet the signing level requirements. It often means the file's signature is revoked or a signature with the Lifetime Signing EKU has expired.
This event is best correlated with EID 3089 to determine the error of the validation.
\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: CodeIntegrity - Disallowed File For Protected Processes Has Been Blocked
\u001fwindows.description: Detects block events for files that are disallowed by code integrity for protected processes
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: CodeIntegrity - Blocked Image/Driver Load For Policy Violation
\u001fwindows.description: Detects blocked load events that did not meet the authenticode signing level requirements or violated the code integrity policy.
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: CodeIntegrity - Blocked Driver Load With Revoked Certificate
\u001fwindows.description: Detects blocked load attempts of revoked drivers
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: CodeIntegrity - Revoked Kernel Driver Loaded
\u001fwindows.description: Detects the load of a revoked kernel driver
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: CodeIntegrity - Blocked Image Load With Revoked Certificate
\u001fwindows.description: Detects blocked image load events with revoked certificates by code integrity.
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: CodeIntegrity - Revoked Image Loaded
\u001fwindows.description: Detects image load events with revoked certificates by code integrity.
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: CodeIntegrity - Unsigned Kernel Module Loaded
\u001fwindows.description: Detects the presence of a loaded unsigned kernel module on the system.
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: CodeIntegrity - Unsigned Image Loaded
\u001fwindows.description: Detects loaded unsigned image on the system
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: CodeIntegrity - Unmet WHQL Requirements For Loaded Kernel Module
\u001fwindows.description: Detects loaded kernel modules that did not meet the WHQL signing requirements.
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Loading Diagcab Package From Remote Path
\u001fwindows.description: Detects loading of diagcab packages from a remote path, as seen in DogWalk vulnerability
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: DNS Query for Anonfiles.com Domain - DNS Client
\u001fwindows.description: Detects DNS queries for anonfiles.com, which is an anonymous file upload platform often used for malicious purposes
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious Cobalt Strike DNS Beaconing - DNS Client
\u001fwindows.description: Detects a program that invoked suspicious DNS queries known from Cobalt Strike beacons
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: DNS Query To MEGA Hosting Website - DNS Client
\u001fwindows.description: Detects DNS queries for subdomains related to MEGA sharing website
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: DNS Query To Put.io - DNS Client
\u001fwindows.description: Detects DNS queries for subdomains related to "Put.io" sharing website.
\u001fwindows.author: Omar Khaled (@beacon_exe)

\u001fwindows.title: Query Tor Onion Address - DNS Client
\u001fwindows.description: Detects DNS resolution of an .onion address related to Tor routing networks
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: DNS Query To Ufile.io - DNS Client
\u001fwindows.description: Detects DNS queries to "ufile.io", which was seen abused by malware and threat actors as a method for data exfiltration
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Failed DNS Zone Transfer
\u001fwindows.description: Detects when a DNS zone transfer failed.
\u001fwindows.author: Zach Mathis

\u001fwindows.title: DNS Server Error Failed Loading the ServerLevelPluginDLL
\u001fwindows.description: Detects a DNS server error in which a specified plugin DLL (in registry) could not be loaded
\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: USB Device Plugged
\u001fwindows.description: Detects plugged/unplugged USB devices
\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Uncommon New Firewall Rule Added In Windows Firewall Exception List
\u001fwindows.description: Detects when a rule has been added to the Windows Firewall exception list
\u001fwindows.author: frack113

\u001fwindows.title: New Firewall Rule Added In Windows Firewall Exception List For Potential Suspicious Application
\u001fwindows.description: Detects the addition of a new rule to the Windows Firewall exception list for an application located in a potentially suspicious location.
\u001fwindows.author: frack113

\u001fwindows.title: New Firewall Rule Added In Windows Firewall Exception List Via WmiPrvSE.EXE
\u001fwindows.description:
Detects the addition of a new "Allow" firewall rule by the WMI process (WmiPrvSE.EXE).
This can occur if an attacker leverages PowerShell cmdlets such as "New-NetFirewallRule", or directly uses WMI CIM classes such as "MSFT_NetFirewallRule".
\u001fwindows.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: All Rules Have Been Deleted From The Windows Firewall Configuration
\u001fwindows.description: Detects when a all the rules have been deleted from the Windows Defender Firewall configuration
\u001fwindows.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: A Rule Has Been Deleted From The Windows Firewall Exception List
\u001fwindows.description: Detects when a single rules or all of the rules have been deleted from the Windows Defender Firewall
\u001fwindows.author: frack113

\u001fwindows.title: The Windows Defender Firewall Service Failed To Load Group Policy
\u001fwindows.description: Detects activity when The Windows Defender Firewall service failed to load Group Policy
\u001fwindows.author: frack113

\u001fwindows.title: Windows Defender Firewall Has Been Reset To Its Default Configuration
\u001fwindows.description: Detects activity when Windows Defender Firewall has been reset to its default configuration
\u001fwindows.author: frack113

\u001fwindows.title: Windows Firewall Settings Have Been Changed
\u001fwindows.description: Detects activity when the settings of the Windows firewall have been changed
\u001fwindows.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: ETW Logging/Processing Option Disabled On IIS Server
\u001fwindows.description: Detects changes to of the IIS server configuration in order to disable/remove the ETW logging/processing option.
\u001fwindows.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali

\u001fwindows.title: HTTP Logging Disabled On IIS Server
\u001fwindows.description: Detects changes to of the IIS server configuration in order to disable HTTP logging for successful requests.
\u001fwindows.author: frack113

\u001fwindows.title: New Module Module Added To IIS Server
\u001fwindows.description: Detects the addition of a new module to an IIS server.
\u001fwindows.author: frack113

\u001fwindows.title: Previously Installed IIS Module Was Removed
\u001fwindows.description: Detects the removal of a previously installed IIS module.
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali

\u001fwindows.title: Potential Active Directory Reconnaissance/Enumeration Via LDAP
\u001fwindows.description: Detects potential Active Directory enumeration via LDAP
\u001fwindows.author: Adeem Mawani

\u001fwindows.title: Standard User In High Privileged Group
\u001fwindows.description: Detect standard users login that are part of high privileged groups such as the Administrator group
\u001fwindows.author: frack113

\u001fwindows.title: ProxyLogon MSExchange OabVirtualDirectory
\u001fwindows.description: Detects specific patterns found after a successful ProxyLogon exploitation in relation to a Commandlet invocation of Set-OabVirtualDirectory
\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Certificate Request Export to Exchange Webserver
\u001fwindows.description: Detects a write of an Exchange CSR to an untypical directory or with aspx name suffix which can be used to place a webshell
\u001fwindows.author: Max Altgelt (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Mailbox Export to Exchange Webserver
\u001fwindows.description: Detects a successful export of an Exchange mailbox to untypical directory or with aspx name suffix which can be used to place a webshell or the needed role assignment for it
\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Rich Warren, Christian Burkard (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Remove Exported Mailbox from Exchange Webserver
\u001fwindows.description: Detects removal of an exported Exchange mailbox which could be to cover tracks from ProxyShell exploit
\u001fwindows.author: Christian Burkard (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Exchange Set OabVirtualDirectory ExternalUrl Property
\u001fwindows.description: Rule to detect an adversary setting OabVirtualDirectory External URL property to a script in Exchange Management log
\u001fwindows.author: Jose Rodriguez @Cyb3rPandaH

\u001fwindows.title: MSExchange Transport Agent Installation - Builtin
\u001fwindows.description: Detects the Installation of a Exchange Transport Agent
\u001fwindows.author: Tobias Michalski (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Failed MSExchange Transport Agent Installation
\u001fwindows.description: Detects a failed installation of a Exchange Transport Agent
\u001fwindows.author: Tobias Michalski (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: NTLM Logon
\u001fwindows.description: Detects logons using NTLM, which could be caused by a legacy source or attackers
\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: NTLM Brute Force
\u001fwindows.description: Detects common NTLM brute force device names
\u001fwindows.author: Jerry Shockley '@jsh0x'

\u001fwindows.title: Potential Remote Desktop Connection to Non-Domain Host
\u001fwindows.description: Detects logons using NTLM to hosts that are potentially not part of the domain.
\u001fwindows.author: James Pemberton

\u001fwindows.title: OpenSSH Server Listening On Socket
\u001fwindows.description: Detects scenarios where an attacker enables the OpenSSH server and server starts to listening on SSH socket.
\u001fwindows.author: mdecrevoisier

\u001fwindows.title: Azure AD Health Monitoring Agent Registry Keys Access
\u001fwindows.description:
This detection uses Windows security events to detect suspicious access attempts to the registry key of Azure AD Health monitoring agent.
This detection requires an access control entry (ACE) on the system access control list (SACL) of the following securable object HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Microsoft
\u001fwindows.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research), MSTIC

\u001fwindows.title: Azure AD Health Service Agents Registry Keys Access
\u001fwindows.description:
This detection uses Windows security events to detect suspicious access attempts to the registry key values and sub-keys of Azure AD Health service agents (e.g AD FS).
Information from AD Health service agents can be used to potentially abuse some of the features provided by those services in the cl
\u001fwindows.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research), MSTIC

\u001fwindows.title: Powerview Add-DomainObjectAcl DCSync AD Extend Right
\u001fwindows.description: Backdooring domain object to grant the rights associated with DCSync to a regular user or machine account using Powerview\Add-DomainObjectAcl DCSync Extended Right cmdlet, will allow to re-obtain the pwd hashes of any user/computer
\u001fwindows.author: Samir Bousseaden, Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g, oscd.community, Tim Shelton, Maxence Fossat

\u001fwindows.title: AD Privileged Users or Groups Reconnaissance
\u001fwindows.description: Detect priv users or groups recon based on 4661 eventid and known privileged users or groups SIDs
\u001fwindows.author: Samir Bousseaden

\u001fwindows.title: ADCS Certificate Template Configuration Vulnerability
\u001fwindows.description: Detects certificate creation with template allowing risk permission subject
\u001fwindows.author: Orlinum , BlueDefenZer

\u001fwindows.title: ADCS Certificate Template Configuration Vulnerability with Risky EKU
\u001fwindows.description: Detects certificate creation with template allowing risk permission subject and risky EKU
\u001fwindows.author: Orlinum , BlueDefenZer

\u001fwindows.title: Add or Remove Computer from DC
\u001fwindows.description: Detects the creation or removal of a computer. Can be used to detect attacks such as DCShadow via the creation of a new SPN.
\u001fwindows.author: frack113

\u001fwindows.title: Access To ADMIN$ Network Share
\u001fwindows.description: Detects access to ADMIN$ network share
\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: AD Object WriteDAC Access
\u001fwindows.description: Detects WRITE_DAC access to a domain object
\u001fwindows.author: Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g

\u001fwindows.title: Active Directory Replication from Non Machine Account
\u001fwindows.description: Detects potential abuse of Active Directory Replication Service (ADRS) from a non machine account to request credentials.
\u001fwindows.author: Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g

\u001fwindows.title: Potential AD User Enumeration From Non-Machine Account
\u001fwindows.description: Detects read access to a domain user from a non-machine account
\u001fwindows.author: Maxime Thiebaut (@0xThiebaut)

\u001fwindows.title: Enabled User Right in AD to Control User Objects
\u001fwindows.description: Detects scenario where if a user is assigned the SeEnableDelegationPrivilege right in Active Directory it would allow control of other AD user objects.
\u001fwindows.author: @neu5ron

\u001fwindows.title: Active Directory User Backdoors
\u001fwindows.description: Detects scenarios where one can control another users or computers account without having to use their credentials.
\u001fwindows.author: @neu5ron

\u001fwindows.title: Weak Encryption Enabled and Kerberoast
\u001fwindows.description: Detects scenario where weak encryption is enabled for a user profile which could be used for hash/password cracking.
\u001fwindows.author: @neu5ron

\u001fwindows.title: Hacktool Ruler
\u001fwindows.description: This events that are generated when using the hacktool Ruler by Sensepost
\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Remote Task Creation via ATSVC Named Pipe
\u001fwindows.description: Detects remote task creation via at.exe or API interacting with ATSVC namedpipe
\u001fwindows.author: Samir Bousseaden

\u001fwindows.title: Security Eventlog Cleared
\u001fwindows.description: One of the Windows Eventlogs has been cleared. e.g. caused by "wevtutil cl" command execution
\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Processes Accessing the Microphone and Webcam
\u001fwindows.description: Potential adversaries accessing the microphone and webcam in an endpoint.
\u001fwindows.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)

\u001fwindows.title: CobaltStrike Service Installations - Security
\u001fwindows.description: Detects known malicious service installs that appear in cases in which a Cobalt Strike beacon elevates privileges or lateral movement
\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Wojciech Lesicki

\u001fwindows.title: Failed Code Integrity Checks
\u001fwindows.description: Detects code integrity failures such as missing page hashes or corrupted drivers due unauthorized modification. This could be a sign of tampered binaries.
\u001fwindows.author: Thomas Patzke

\u001fwindows.title: DCERPC SMB Spoolss Named Pipe
\u001fwindows.description: Detects the use of the spoolss named pipe over SMB. This can be used to trigger the authentication via NTLM of any machine that has the spoolservice enabled.
\u001fwindows.author: OTR (Open Threat Research)

\u001fwindows.title: DCOM InternetExplorer.Application Iertutil DLL Hijack - Security
\u001fwindows.description: Detects a threat actor creating a file named `iertutil.dll` in the `C:\Program Files\Internet Explorer\` directory over the network for a DCOM InternetExplorer DLL Hijack scenario.
\u001fwindows.author: Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g, Open Threat Research (OTR)

\u001fwindows.title: Mimikatz DC Sync
\u001fwindows.description: Detects Mimikatz DC sync security events
\u001fwindows.author: Benjamin Delpy, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Scott Dermott, Sorina Ionescu

\u001fwindows.title: Windows Default Domain GPO Modification
\u001fwindows.description:
Detects modifications to Default Domain or Default Domain Controllers Group Policy Objects (GPOs).
Adversaries may modify these default GPOs to deploy malicious configurations across the domain.
\u001fwindows.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Device Installation Blocked
\u001fwindows.description: Detects an installation of a device that is forbidden by the system policy
\u001fwindows.author: frack113

\u001fwindows.title: Windows Event Auditing Disabled
\u001fwindows.description:
Detects scenarios where system auditing (i.e.: Windows event log auditing) is disabled.
This may be used in a scenario where an entity would want to bypass local logging to evade detection when Windows event logging is enabled and reviewed.
Also, it is recommended to turn off "Local Group Policy Obj
\u001fwindows.author: @neu5ron, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Important Windows Event Auditing Disabled
\u001fwindows.description: Detects scenarios where system auditing for important events such as "Process Creation" or "Logon" events is disabled.
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: ETW Logging Disabled In .NET Processes - Registry
\u001fwindows.description: Potential adversaries stopping ETW providers recording loaded .NET assemblies.
\u001fwindows.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)

\u001fwindows.title: DPAPI Domain Backup Key Extraction
\u001fwindows.description: Detects tools extracting LSA secret DPAPI domain backup key from Domain Controllers
\u001fwindows.author: Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g

\u001fwindows.title: DPAPI Domain Master Key Backup Attempt
\u001fwindows.description: Detects anyone attempting a backup for the DPAPI Master Key. This events gets generated at the source and not the Domain Controller.
\u001fwindows.author: Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g

\u001fwindows.title: External Disk Drive Or USB Storage Device Was Recognized By The System
\u001fwindows.description: Detects external disk drives or plugged-in USB devices.
\u001fwindows.author: Keith Wright

\u001fwindows.title: Persistence and Execution at Scale via GPO Scheduled Task
\u001fwindows.description: Detect lateral movement using GPO scheduled task, usually used to deploy ransomware at scale
\u001fwindows.author: Samir Bousseaden

\u001fwindows.title: Hidden Local User Creation
\u001fwindows.description: Detects the creation of a local hidden user account which should not happen for event ID 4720.
\u001fwindows.author: Christian Burkard (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: HackTool - EDRSilencer Execution - Filter Added
\u001fwindows.description: Detects execution of EDRSilencer, a tool that abuses the Windows Filtering Platform (WFP) to block the outbound traffic of running EDR agents based on specific hardcoded filter names.
\u001fwindows.author: Thodoris Polyzos (@SmoothDeploy)

\u001fwindows.title: HackTool - NoFilter Execution
\u001fwindows.description: Detects execution of NoFilter, a tool for abusing the Windows Filtering Platform for privilege escalation via hardcoded policy name indicators
\u001fwindows.author: Stamatis Chatzimangou (st0pp3r)

\u001fwindows.title: HybridConnectionManager Service Installation
\u001fwindows.description: Rule to detect the Hybrid Connection Manager service installation.
\u001fwindows.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)

\u001fwindows.title: Impacket PsExec Execution
\u001fwindows.description: Detects execution of Impacket's psexec.py.
\u001fwindows.author: Bhabesh Raj

\u001fwindows.title: Possible Impacket SecretDump Remote Activity
\u001fwindows.description: Detect AD credential dumping using impacket secretdump HKTL
\u001fwindows.author: Samir Bousseaden, wagga

\u001fwindows.title: Invoke-Obfuscation CLIP+ Launcher - Security
\u001fwindows.description: Detects Obfuscated use of Clip.exe to execute PowerShell
\u001fwindows.author: Jonathan Cheong, oscd.community

\u001fwindows.title: Invoke-Obfuscation Obfuscated IEX Invocation - Security
\u001fwindows.description: Detects all variations of obfuscated powershell IEX invocation code generated by Invoke-Obfuscation framework from the code block linked in the references
\u001fwindows.author: Daniel Bohannon (@Mandiant/@FireEye), oscd.community

\u001fwindows.title: Invoke-Obfuscation STDIN+ Launcher - Security
\u001fwindows.description: Detects Obfuscated use of stdin to execute PowerShell
\u001fwindows.author: Jonathan Cheong, oscd.community

\u001fwindows.title: Invoke-Obfuscation VAR+ Launcher - Security
\u001fwindows.description: Detects Obfuscated use of Environment Variables to execute PowerShell
\u001fwindows.author: Jonathan Cheong, oscd.community

\u001fwindows.title: Invoke-Obfuscation COMPRESS OBFUSCATION - Security
\u001fwindows.description: Detects Obfuscated Powershell via COMPRESS OBFUSCATION
\u001fwindows.author: Timur Zinniatullin, oscd.community

\u001fwindows.title: Invoke-Obfuscation RUNDLL LAUNCHER - Security
\u001fwindows.description: Detects Obfuscated Powershell via RUNDLL LAUNCHER
\u001fwindows.author: Timur Zinniatullin, oscd.community

\u001fwindows.title: Invoke-Obfuscation Via Stdin - Security
\u001fwindows.description: Detects Obfuscated Powershell via Stdin in Scripts
\u001fwindows.author: Nikita Nazarov, oscd.community

\u001fwindows.description: Detects Obfuscated Powershell via use Clip.exe in Scripts

\u001fwindows.title: Invoke-Obfuscation Via Use MSHTA - Security

\u001fwindows.author: Nikita Nazarov, oscd.community

\u001fwindows.title: Invoke-Obfuscation Via Use Rundll32 - Security
\u001fwindows.description: Detects Obfuscated Powershell via use Rundll32 in Scripts
\u001fwindows.author: Nikita Nazarov, oscd.community

\u001fwindows.title: Invoke-Obfuscation VAR++ LAUNCHER OBFUSCATION - Security
\u001fwindows.description: Detects Obfuscated Powershell via VAR++ LAUNCHER
\u001fwindows.author: Timur Zinniatullin, oscd.community

\u001fwindows.title: ISO Image Mounted
\u001fwindows.description: Detects the mount of an ISO image on an endpoint
\u001fwindows.author: Syed Hasan (@syedhasan009)

\u001fwindows.description:
This rule will collect the data needed to start looking into possible kerberoasting activity.
Further analysis or computation within the query is needed focusing on requests from one specific host/IP towards multiple service names within a time period of 5 seconds.
You can then set a threshold for t
\u001fwindows.author: @kostastsale

\u001fwindows.title: Potential AS-REP Roasting via Kerberos TGT Requests
\u001fwindows.description:
Detects suspicious Kerberos TGT requests with pre-authentication disabled (Pre-Authentication Type = 0) and Ticket Encryption Type (0x17) i.e, RC4-HMAC.
This may indicate an AS-REP Roasting attack, where attackers request AS-REP messages for accounts without pre-authentication and attempt to crack t
\u001fwindows.author: ANosir

\u001fwindows.title: Potential Kerberos Coercion by Spoofing SPNs via DNS Manipulation
\u001fwindows.description:
Detects modifications to DNS records in Active Directory where the Distinguished Name (DN) contains a base64-encoded blob
matching the pattern "1UWhRCAAAAA...BAAAA". This pattern corresponds to a marshaled CREDENTIAL_TARGET_INFORMATION structure,
commonly used in Kerberos coercion attacks. Adversari
\u001fwindows.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: First Time Seen Remote Named Pipe
\u001fwindows.description: This detection excludes known namped pipes accessible remotely and notify on newly observed ones, may help to detect lateral movement and remote exec using named pipes
\u001fwindows.author: Samir Bousseaden

\u001fwindows.title: LSASS Access From Non System Account
\u001fwindows.description: Detects potential mimikatz-like tools accessing LSASS from non system account
\u001fwindows.author: Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g

\u001fwindows.title: Credential Dumping Tools Service Execution - Security
\u001fwindows.description: Detects well-known credential dumping tools execution via service execution events
\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Teymur Kheirkhabarov, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, oscd.community

\u001fwindows.title: WCE wceaux.dll Access
\u001fwindows.description: Detects wceaux.dll access while WCE pass-the-hash remote command execution on source host
\u001fwindows.author: Thomas Patzke

\u001fwindows.title: Metasploit SMB Authentication
\u001fwindows.description: Alerts on Metasploit host's authentications on the domain.
\u001fwindows.author: Chakib Gzenayi (@Chak092), Hosni Mribah

\u001fwindows.title: Metasploit Or Impacket Service Installation Via SMB PsExec
\u001fwindows.description: Detects usage of Metasploit SMB PsExec (exploit/windows/smb/psexec) and Impacket psexec.py by triggering on specific service installation
\u001fwindows.author: Bartlomiej Czyz, Relativity

\u001fwindows.title: Meterpreter or Cobalt Strike Getsystem Service Installation - Security
\u001fwindows.description: Detects the use of getsystem Meterpreter/Cobalt Strike command by detecting a specific service installation
\u001fwindows.author: Teymur Kheirkhabarov, Ecco, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: NetNTLM Downgrade Attack
\u001fwindows.description: Detects NetNTLM downgrade attack
\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), wagga

\u001fwindows.title: Windows Network Access Suspicious desktop.ini Action
\u001fwindows.description: Detects unusual processes accessing desktop.ini remotely over network share, which can be leveraged to alter how Explorer displays a folder's content (i.e. renaming files) without changing them on disk.
\u001fwindows.author: Tim Shelton (HAWK.IO)

\u001fwindows.title: New or Renamed User Account with '$' Character
\u001fwindows.description: Detects the creation of a user with the "$" character. This can be used by attackers to hide a user or trick detection systems that lack the parsing mechanisms.
\u001fwindows.author: Ilyas Ochkov, oscd.community

\u001fwindows.title: Denied Access To Remote Desktop
\u001fwindows.description:
This event is generated when an authenticated user who is not allowed to log on remotely attempts to connect to this computer through Remote Desktop.
Often, this event can be generated by attackers when searching for available windows servers in the network.
\u001fwindows.author: Pushkarev Dmitry

\u001fwindows.title: Password Policy Enumerated
\u001fwindows.description: Detects when the password policy is enumerated.
\u001fwindows.author: Zach Mathis

\u001fwindows.title: Windows Pcap Drivers
\u001fwindows.description: Detects Windows Pcap driver installation based on a list of associated .sys files.
\u001fwindows.author: Cian Heasley

\u001fwindows.title: Possible PetitPotam Coerce Authentication Attempt
\u001fwindows.description: Detect PetitPotam coerced authentication activity.
\u001fwindows.author: Mauricio Velazco, Michael Haag

\u001fwindows.title: PetitPotam Suspicious Kerberos TGT Request
\u001fwindows.description:
Detect suspicious Kerberos TGT requests.
Once an attacer obtains a computer certificate by abusing Active Directory Certificate Services in combination with PetitPotam, the next step would be to leverage the certificate for malicious purposes.
One way of doing this is to request a Kerberos Ticket Gr
\u001fwindows.author: Mauricio Velazco, Michael Haag

\u001fwindows.title: Possible DC Shadow Attack
\u001fwindows.description: Detects DCShadow via create new SPN
\u001fwindows.author: Ilyas Ochkov, oscd.community, Chakib Gzenayi (@Chak092), Hosni Mribah

\u001fwindows.title: PowerShell Scripts Installed as Services - Security
\u001fwindows.description: Detects powershell script installed as a Service
\u001fwindows.author: oscd.community, Natalia Shornikova

\u001fwindows.title: Protected Storage Service Access
\u001fwindows.description: Detects access to a protected_storage service over the network. Potential abuse of DPAPI to extract domain backup keys from Domain Controllers
\u001fwindows.author: Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g

\u001fwindows.title: RDP over Reverse SSH Tunnel WFP
\u001fwindows.description: Detects svchost hosting RDP termsvcs communicating with the loopback address
\u001fwindows.author: Samir Bousseaden

\u001fwindows.title: Register new Logon Process by Rubeus
\u001fwindows.description: Detects potential use of Rubeus via registered new trusted logon process
\u001fwindows.author: Roberto Rodriguez (source), Ilyas Ochkov (rule), oscd.community

\u001fwindows.title: Service Registry Key Read Access Request
\u001fwindows.description:
Detects "read access" requests on the services registry key.
Adversaries may execute their own malicious payloads by hijacking the Registry entries used by services.
Adversaries may use flaws in the permissions for Registry keys related to services to redirect from the originally specified executabl
\u001fwindows.author: Center for Threat Informed Defense (CTID) Summiting the Pyramid Team

\u001fwindows.title: Remote PowerShell Sessions Network Connections (WinRM)
\u001fwindows.description: Detects basic PowerShell Remoting (WinRM) by monitoring for network inbound connections to ports 5985 OR 5986
\u001fwindows.author: Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g

\u001fwindows.title: Replay Attack Detected
\u001fwindows.description: Detects possible Kerberos Replay Attack on the domain controllers when "KRB_AP_ERR_REPEAT" Kerberos response is sent to the client
\u001fwindows.author: frack113

\u001fwindows.title: SAM Registry Hive Handle Request
\u001fwindows.description: Detects handles requested to SAM registry hive
\u001fwindows.author: Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g

\u001fwindows.title: SCM Database Handle Failure
\u001fwindows.description: Detects non-system users failing to get a handle of the SCM database.
\u001fwindows.author: Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g

\u001fwindows.title: SCM Database Privileged Operation
\u001fwindows.description: Detects non-system users performing privileged operation os the SCM database
\u001fwindows.author: Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g, Tim Shelton

\u001fwindows.title: Potential Secure Deletion with SDelete
\u001fwindows.description: Detects files that have extensions commonly seen while SDelete is used to wipe files.
\u001fwindows.author: Thomas Patzke

\u001fwindows.title: Service Installed By Unusual Client - Security
\u001fwindows.description: Detects a service installed by a client which has PID 0 or whose parent has PID 0
\u001fwindows.author: Tim Rauch (Nextron Systems), Elastic (idea)

\u001fwindows.title: Remote Access Tool Services Have Been Installed - Security
\u001fwindows.description: Detects service installation of different remote access tools software. These software are often abused by threat actors to perform
\u001fwindows.author: Connor Martin, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: File Access Of Signal Desktop Sensitive Data
\u001fwindows.description:
Detects access to Signal Desktop's sensitive data files: db.sqlite and config.json.
The db.sqlite file in Signal Desktop stores all locally saved messages in an encrypted SQLite database, while the config.json contains the decryption key needed to access that data.
Since the key is stored in plain t
\u001fwindows.author: Andreas Braathen (mnemonic.io)

\u001fwindows.title: SMB Create Remote File Admin Share
\u001fwindows.description: Look for non-system accounts SMB accessing a file with write (0x2) access mask via administrative share (i.e C$).
\u001fwindows.author: Jose Rodriguez (@Cyb3rPandaH), OTR (Open Threat Research)

\u001fwindows.title: A New Trust Was Created To A Domain
\u001fwindows.description: Addition of domains is seldom and should be verified for legitimacy.
\u001fwindows.author: Thomas Patzke

\u001fwindows.title: Addition of SID History to Active Directory Object
\u001fwindows.description: An attacker can use the SID history attribute to gain additional privileges.
\u001fwindows.author: Thomas Patzke, @atc_project (improvements)

\u001fwindows.title: Win Susp Computer Name Containing Samtheadmin
\u001fwindows.description: Detects suspicious computer name samtheadmin-{1..100}$ generated by hacktool
\u001fwindows.author: elhoim

\u001fwindows.title: Password Change on Directory Service Restore Mode (DSRM) Account
\u001fwindows.description:
Detects potential attempts made to set the Directory Services Restore Mode administrator password.
The Directory Service Restore Mode (DSRM) account is a local administrator account on Domain Controllers.
Attackers may change the password in order to obtain persistence.
\u001fwindows.author: Thomas Patzke

\u001fwindows.title: Account Tampering - Suspicious Failed Logon Reasons
\u001fwindows.description: This method uses uncommon error codes on failed logons to determine suspicious activity and tampering with accounts that have been disabled or somehow restricted.
\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Group Policy Abuse for Privilege Addition
\u001fwindows.description: Detects the first occurrence of a modification to Group Policy Object Attributes to add privileges to user accounts or use them to add users as local admins.
\u001fwindows.author: Elastic, Josh Nickels, Marius Rothenbücher

\u001fwindows.title: Startup/Logon Script Added to Group Policy Object
\u001fwindows.description: Detects the modification of Group Policy Objects (GPO) to add a startup/logon script to users or computer objects.
\u001fwindows.author: Elastic, Josh Nickels, Marius Rothenbücher

\u001fwindows.title: Kerberos Manipulation
\u001fwindows.description: Detects failed Kerberos TGT issue operation. This can be a sign of manipulations of TGT messages by an attacker.
\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious LDAP-Attributes Used
\u001fwindows.description: Detects the usage of particular AttributeLDAPDisplayNames, which are known for data exchange via LDAP by the tool LDAPFragger and are additionally not commonly used in companies.
\u001fwindows.author: xknow @xknow_infosec

\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious Windows ANONYMOUS LOGON Local Account Created
\u001fwindows.description: Detects the creation of suspicious accounts similar to ANONYMOUS LOGON, such as using additional spaces. Created as an covering detection for exclusion of Logon Type 3 from ANONYMOUS LOGON accounts.
\u001fwindows.author: James Pemberton / @4A616D6573

\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious Remote Logon with Explicit Credentials
\u001fwindows.description: Detects suspicious processes logging on with explicit credentials
\u001fwindows.author: oscd.community, Teymur Kheirkhabarov @HeirhabarovT, Zach Stanford @svch0st, Tim Shelton

\u001fwindows.title: Password Dumper Activity on LSASS
\u001fwindows.description: Detects process handle on LSASS process with certain access mask and object type SAM_DOMAIN
\u001fwindows.author: sigma

\u001fwindows.title: Potentially Suspicious AccessMask Requested From LSASS
\u001fwindows.description: Detects process handle on LSASS process with certain access mask
\u001fwindows.author: Roberto Rodriguez, Teymur Kheirkhabarov, Dimitrios Slamaris, Mark Russinovich, Aleksey Potapov, oscd.community (update)

\u001fwindows.title: Reconnaissance Activity
\u001fwindows.description: Detects activity as "net user administrator /domain" and "net group domain admins /domain"
\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Jack Croock (method), Jonhnathan Ribeiro (improvements), oscd.community

\u001fwindows.title: Password Protected ZIP File Opened
\u001fwindows.description: Detects the extraction of password protected ZIP archives. See the filename variable for more details on which file has been opened.
\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Password Protected ZIP File Opened (Suspicious Filenames)
\u001fwindows.description: Detects the extraction of password protected ZIP archives with suspicious file names. See the filename variable for more details on which file has been opened.
\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Password Protected ZIP File Opened (Email Attachment)
\u001fwindows.description: Detects the extraction of password protected ZIP archives. See the filename variable for more details on which file has been opened.
\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Uncommon Outbound Kerberos Connection - Security
\u001fwindows.description: Detects uncommon outbound network activity via Kerberos default port indicating possible lateral movement or first stage PrivEsc via delegation.
\u001fwindows.author: Ilyas Ochkov, oscd.community

\u001fwindows.title: Possible Shadow Credentials Added
\u001fwindows.description: Detects possible addition of shadow credentials to an active directory object.
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Elastic (idea)

\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious PsExec Execution
\u001fwindows.description: detects execution of psexec or paexec with renamed service name, this rule helps to filter out the noise if psexec is used for legit purposes or if attacker uses a different psexec client other than sysinternal one
\u001fwindows.author: Samir Bousseaden

\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious Access to Sensitive File Extensions
\u001fwindows.description: Detects known sensitive file extensions accessed on a network share
\u001fwindows.author: Samir Bousseaden

\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious Kerberos RC4 Ticket Encryption
\u001fwindows.description: Detects service ticket requests using RC4 encryption type
\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious Scheduled Task Creation
\u001fwindows.description: Detects suspicious scheduled task creation events. Based on attributes such as paths, commands line flags, etc.
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Important Scheduled Task Deleted/Disabled
\u001fwindows.description: Detects when adversaries stop services or processes by deleting or disabling their respective scheduled tasks in order to conduct data destructive activities
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious Scheduled Task Update
\u001fwindows.description: Detects update to a scheduled task event that contain suspicious keywords.
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Unauthorized System Time Modification
\u001fwindows.description: Detect scenarios where a potentially unauthorized application or user is modifying the system time.
\u001fwindows.author: @neu5ron

\u001fwindows.title: Remote Service Activity via SVCCTL Named Pipe
\u001fwindows.description: Detects remote service activity via remote access to the svcctl named pipe
\u001fwindows.author: Samir Bousseaden

\u001fwindows.title: SysKey Registry Keys Access
\u001fwindows.description: Detects handle requests and access operations to specific registry keys to calculate the SysKey
\u001fwindows.author: Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g

\u001fwindows.title: Sysmon Channel Reference Deletion
\u001fwindows.description: Potential threat actor tampering with Sysmon manifest and eventually disabling it
\u001fwindows.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)

\u001fwindows.title: Tap Driver Installation - Security
\u001fwindows.description: Detects the installation of a well-known TAP driver service. This could be a sign of potential preparation for data exfiltration using tunnelling techniques.
\u001fwindows.author: Daniil Yugoslavskiy, Ian Davis, oscd.community

\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious Teams Application Related ObjectAcess Event
\u001fwindows.description: Detects an access to authentication tokens and accounts of Microsoft Teams desktop application.
\u001fwindows.author: @SerkinValery

\u001fwindows.title: Transferring Files with Credential Data via Network Shares
\u001fwindows.description: Transferring files with well-known filenames (sensitive files with credential data) using network shares
\u001fwindows.author: Teymur Kheirkhabarov, oscd.community

\u001fwindows.title: User Added to Local Administrator Group
\u001fwindows.description: Detects the addition of a new member to the local administrator group, which could be legitimate activity or a sign of privilege escalation activity
\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: User Couldn't Call a Privileged Service 'LsaRegisterLogonProcess'
\u001fwindows.description: The 'LsaRegisterLogonProcess' function verifies that the application making the function call is a logon process by checking that it has the SeTcbPrivilege privilege set. Possible Rubeus tries to get a handle to LSA.
\u001fwindows.author: Roberto Rodriguez (source), Ilyas Ochkov (rule), oscd.community

\u001fwindows.title: Local User Creation
\u001fwindows.description: Detects local user creation on Windows servers, which shouldn't happen in an Active Directory environment. Apply this Sigma Use Case on your Windows server logs and not on your DC logs.
\u001fwindows.author: Patrick Bareiss

\u001fwindows.title: Potential Privileged System Service Operation - SeLoadDriverPrivilege
\u001fwindows.description:
Detects the usage of the 'SeLoadDriverPrivilege' privilege. This privilege is required to load or unload a device driver.
With this privilege, the user can dynamically load and unload device drivers or other code in to kernel mode.
This user right does not apply to Plug and Play device drivers.
If y
\u001fwindows.author: xknow (@xknow_infosec), xorxes (@xor_xes)

\u001fwindows.title: User Logoff Event
\u001fwindows.description: Detects a user log-off activity. Could be used for example to correlate information during forensic investigations
\u001fwindows.author: frack113

\u001fwindows.title: VSSAudit Security Event Source Registration
\u001fwindows.description: Detects the registration of the security event source VSSAudit. It would usually trigger when volume shadow copy operations happen.
\u001fwindows.author: Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g, Open Threat Research (OTR)

\u001fwindows.title: Windows Defender Exclusion List Modified
\u001fwindows.description: Detects modifications to the Windows Defender exclusion registry key. This could indicate a potentially suspicious or even malicious activity by an attacker trying to add a new exclusion in order to bypass security.
\u001fwindows.author: @BarryShooshooga

\u001fwindows.title: Windows Defender Exclusion Registry Key - Write Access Requested
\u001fwindows.description: Detects write access requests to the Windows Defender exclusions registry keys. This could be an indication of an attacker trying to request a handle or access the object to write new exclusions in order to bypass security.
\u001fwindows.author: @BarryShooshooga, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: T1047 Wmiprvse Wbemcomn DLL Hijack
\u001fwindows.description: Detects a threat actor creating a file named `wbemcomn.dll` in the `C:\Windows\System32\wbem\` directory over the network for a WMI DLL Hijack scenario.
\u001fwindows.author: Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g, Open Threat Research (OTR)

\u001fwindows.title: WMI Persistence - Security
\u001fwindows.description: Detects suspicious WMI event filter and command line event consumer based on WMI and Security Logs.
\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Gleb Sukhodolskiy, Timur Zinniatullin oscd.community

\u001fwindows.title: Locked Workstation
\u001fwindows.description: Detects locked workstation session events that occur automatically after a standard period of inactivity.
\u001fwindows.author: Alexandr Yampolskyi, SOC Prime

\u001fwindows.title: Potential Access Token Abuse
\u001fwindows.description: Detects potential token impersonation and theft. Example, when using "DuplicateToken(Ex)" and "ImpersonateLoggedOnUser" with the "LOGON32_LOGON_NEW_CREDENTIALS flag".
\u001fwindows.author: Michaela Adams, Zach Mathis

\u001fwindows.title: Admin User Remote Logon
\u001fwindows.description: Detect remote login by Administrator user (depending on internal pattern).
\u001fwindows.author: juju4

\u001fwindows.title: DiagTrackEoP Default Login Username
\u001fwindows.description: Detects the default "UserName" used by the DiagTrackEoP POC
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: A Member Was Added to a Security-Enabled Global Group
\u001fwindows.description: Detects activity when a member is added to a security-enabled global group
\u001fwindows.author: Alexandr Yampolskyi, SOC Prime

\u001fwindows.title: A Member Was Removed From a Security-Enabled Global Group
\u001fwindows.description: Detects activity when a member is removed from a security-enabled global group
\u001fwindows.author: Alexandr Yampolskyi, SOC Prime

\u001fwindows.title: Successful Overpass the Hash Attempt
\u001fwindows.description: Detects successful logon with logon type 9 (NewCredentials) which matches the Overpass the Hash behavior of e.g Mimikatz's sekurlsa::pth module.
\u001fwindows.author: Roberto Rodriguez (source), Dominik Schaudel (rule)

\u001fwindows.title: Pass the Hash Activity 2
\u001fwindows.description: Detects the attack technique pass the hash which is used to move laterally inside the network
\u001fwindows.author: Dave Kennedy, Jeff Warren (method) / David Vassallo (rule)

\u001fwindows.title: RDP Login from Localhost
\u001fwindows.description: RDP login with localhost source address may be a tunnelled login
\u001fwindows.author: Thomas Patzke

\u001fwindows.title: A Security-Enabled Global Group Was Deleted
\u001fwindows.description: Detects activity when a security-enabled global group is deleted
\u001fwindows.author: Alexandr Yampolskyi, SOC Prime

\u001fwindows.title: External Remote RDP Logon from Public IP
\u001fwindows.description: Detects successful logon from public IP address via RDP. This can indicate a publicly-exposed RDP port.
\u001fwindows.author: Micah Babinski (@micahbabinski), Zach Mathis (@yamatosecurity)

\u001fwindows.title: External Remote SMB Logon from Public IP
\u001fwindows.description: Detects successful logon from public IP address via SMB. This can indicate a publicly-exposed SMB port.
\u001fwindows.author: Micah Babinski (@micahbabinski), Zach Mathis (@yamatosecurity)

\u001fwindows.title: Failed Logon From Public IP
\u001fwindows.description: Detects a failed logon attempt from a public IP. A login from a public IP can indicate a misconfigured firewall or network boundary.
\u001fwindows.author: NVISO

\u001fwindows.title: Outgoing Logon with New Credentials
\u001fwindows.description: Detects logon events that specify new credentials
\u001fwindows.author: Max Altgelt (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Potential Privilege Escalation via Local Kerberos Relay over LDAP
\u001fwindows.description:
Detects a suspicious local successful logon event where the Logon Package is Kerberos, the remote address is set to localhost, and the target user SID is the built-in local Administrator account.
This may indicate an attempt to leverage a Kerberos relay attack variant that can be used to elevate pri
\u001fwindows.author: Elastic, @SBousseaden

\u001fwindows.title: RottenPotato Like Attack Pattern
\u001fwindows.description: Detects logon events that have characteristics of events generated during an attack with RottenPotato and the like
\u001fwindows.author: @SBousseaden, Florian Roth

\u001fwindows.title: Successful Account Login Via WMI
\u001fwindows.description: Detects successful logon attempts performed with WMI
\u001fwindows.author: Thomas Patzke

\u001fwindows.title: Windows Filtering Platform Blocked Connection From EDR Agent Binary
\u001fwindows.description:
Detects a Windows Filtering Platform (WFP) blocked connection event involving common Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) agents.
Adversaries may use WFP filters to prevent Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) agents from reporting security events.
\u001fwindows.author: @gott_cyber

\u001fwindows.title: Microsoft Defender Blocked from Loading Unsigned DLL
\u001fwindows.description: Detects Code Integrity (CI) engine blocking Microsoft Defender's processes (MpCmdRun and NisSrv) from loading unsigned DLLs which may be an attempt to sideload arbitrary DLL
\u001fwindows.author: Bhabesh Raj

\u001fwindows.title: Unsigned Binary Loaded From Suspicious Location
\u001fwindows.description: Detects Code Integrity (CI) engine blocking processes from loading unsigned DLLs residing in suspicious locations
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: HybridConnectionManager Service Running
\u001fwindows.description: Rule to detect the Hybrid Connection Manager service running on an endpoint.
\u001fwindows.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)

\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious Application Installed
\u001fwindows.description: Detects suspicious application installed by looking at the added shortcut to the app resolver cache
\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious Rejected SMB Guest Logon From IP
\u001fwindows.description: Detect Attempt PrintNightmare (CVE-2021-1675) Remote code execution in Windows Spooler Service
\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), KevTheHermit, fuzzyf10w

\u001fwindows.title: Unsigned or Unencrypted SMB Connection to Share Established
\u001fwindows.description:
Detects SMB server connections to shares without signing or encryption enabled.
This could indicate potential lateral movement activity using unsecured SMB shares.
