file_event\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: HackTool - Dumpert Process Dumper Default File
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects the creation of the default dump file used by Outflank Dumpert tool. A process dumper, which dumps the lsass process memory
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: HackTool - Typical HiveNightmare SAM File Export
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects files written by the different tools that exploit HiveNightmare
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: HackTool - Inveigh Execution Artefacts
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects the presence and execution of Inveigh via dropped artefacts
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: HackTool - RemoteKrbRelay SMB Relay Secrets Dump Module Indicators
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects the creation of file with specific names used by RemoteKrbRelay SMB Relay attack module.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: HackTool - Mimikatz Kirbi File Creation
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects the creation of files created by mimikatz such as ".kirbi", "mimilsa.log", etc.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), David ANDRE

file_event\u001fwindows.title: HackTool - NetExec File Indicators
file_event\u001fwindows.description:
Detects file creation events indicating NetExec (nxc.exe) execution on the local machine.
NetExec is a PyInstaller-bundled binary that extracts its embedded data files to a "_MEI<random>" directory
under the Temp folder upon execution. Files dropped under the "\nxc\" sub-directory of that
extraction
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: HackTool - NPPSpy Hacktool Usage
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects the use of NPPSpy hacktool that stores cleartext passwords of users that logged in to a local file
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: HackTool - Powerup Write Hijack DLL
file_event\u001fwindows.description:
Powerup tool's Write Hijack DLL exploits DLL hijacking for privilege escalation.
In it's default mode, it builds a self deleting .bat file which executes malicious command.
The detection rule relies on creation of the malicious bat file (debug.bat by default).
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Subhash Popuri (@pbssubhash)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: HackTool - QuarksPwDump Dump File
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects a dump file written by QuarksPwDump password dumper
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: HackTool - Potential Remote Credential Dumping Activity Via CrackMapExec Or Impacket-Secretsdump
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects default filenames output from the execution of CrackMapExec and Impacket-secretsdump against an endpoint.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: SecurityAura

file_event\u001fwindows.title: HackTool - SafetyKatz Dump Indicator
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects default lsass dump filename generated by SafetyKatz.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Markus Neis

file_event\u001fwindows.title: HackTool - Impacket File Indicators
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects file creation events with filename patterns used by Impacket.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: The DFIR Report, IrishDeath

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Potential Initial Access via DLL Search Order Hijacking
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects attempts to create a DLL file to a known desktop application dependencies folder such as Slack, Teams or OneDrive and by an unusual process. This may indicate an attempt to load a malicious module via DLL search order hijacking.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Tim Rauch (rule), Elastic (idea)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Installation of TeamViewer Desktop
file_event\u001fwindows.description: TeamViewer_Desktop.exe is create during install
file_event\u001fwindows.author: frack113

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Malicious DLL File Dropped in the Teams or OneDrive Folder
file_event\u001fwindows.description:
Detects creation of a malicious DLL file in the location where the OneDrive or Team applications
Upon execution of the Teams or OneDrive application, the dropped malicious DLL file ("iphlpapi.dll") is sideloaded
file_event\u001fwindows.author: frack113

file_event\u001fwindows.title: ISO File Created Within Temp Folders
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects the creation of a ISO file in the Outlook temp folder or in the Appdata temp folder. Typical of Qakbot TTP from end-July 2022.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: @sam0x90

file_event\u001fwindows.title: ISO or Image Mount Indicator in Recent Files
file_event\u001fwindows.description:
Detects the creation of recent element file that points to an .ISO, .IMG, .VHD or .VHDX file as often used in phishing attacks.
This can be a false positive on server systems but on workstations users should rarely mount .iso or .img files.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: GatherNetworkInfo.VBS Reconnaissance Script Output
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects creation of files which are the results of executing the built-in reconnaissance script "C:\Windows\System32\gatherNetworkInfo.vbs".
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: LSASS Process Memory Dump Files
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects creation of files with names used by different memory dumping tools to create a memory dump of the LSASS process memory, which contains user credentials.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: LSASS Process Dump Artefact In CrashDumps Folder
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects the presence of an LSASS dump file in the "CrashDumps" folder. This could be a sign of LSASS credential dumping. Techniques such as the LSASS Shtinkering have been seen abusing the Windows Error Reporting to dump said process.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: @pbssubhash

file_event\u001fwindows.title: WerFault LSASS Process Memory Dump
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects WerFault creating a dump file with a name that indicates that the dump file could be an LSASS process memory, which contains user credentials
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Adwind RAT / JRAT File Artifact
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects javaw.exe in AppData folder as used by Adwind / JRAT
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Tom Ueltschi, Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Octopus Scanner Malware
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects Octopus Scanner Malware.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: NVISO

file_event\u001fwindows.title: File Creation In Suspicious Directory By Msdt.EXE
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects msdt.exe creating files in suspicious directories which could be a sign of exploitation of either Follina or Dogwalk vulnerabilities
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Vadim Varganov, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Uncommon File Creation By Mysql Daemon Process
file_event\u001fwindows.description:
Detects the creation of files with scripting or executable extensions by Mysql daemon.
Which could be an indicator of "User Defined Functions" abuse to download malware.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Joseph Kamau

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious DotNET CLR Usage Log Artifact
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects the creation of Usage Log files by the CLR (clr.dll). These files are named after the executing process once the assembly is finished executing for the first time in the (user) session context.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: frack113, omkar72, oscd.community, Wojciech Lesicki

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious File Creation In Uncommon AppData Folder
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects the creation of suspicious files and folders inside the user's AppData folder but not inside any of the common and well known directories (Local, Romaing, LocalLow). This method could be used as a method to bypass detection who exclude the AppData folder in fear of FPs
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: SCR File Write Event
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects the creation of screensaver files (.scr) outside of system folders. Attackers may execute an application as an ".SCR" file using "rundll32.exe desk.cpl,InstallScreenSaver" for example.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Christopher Peacock @securepeacock, SCYTHE @scythe_io

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Potential Persistence Via Notepad++ Plugins
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects creation of new ".dll" files inside the plugins directory of a notepad++ installation by a process other than "gup.exe". Which could indicates possible persistence
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: NTDS.DIT Created
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects creation of a file named "ntds.dit" (Active Directory Database)
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: NTDS.DIT Creation By Uncommon Parent Process
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects creation of a file named "ntds.dit" (Active Directory Database) by an uncommon parent process or directory
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: NTDS.DIT Creation By Uncommon Process
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects creation of a file named "ntds.dit" (Active Directory Database) by an uncommon process or a process located in a suspicious directory
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: NTDS Exfiltration Filename Patterns
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects creation of files with specific name patterns seen used in various tools that export the NTDS.DIT for exfiltration.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Potential Persistence Via Microsoft Office Add-In
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects potential persistence activity via startup add-ins that load when Microsoft Office starts (.wll/.xll are simply .dll fit for Word or Excel).
file_event\u001fwindows.author: NVISO

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Office Macro File Creation
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects the creation of a new office macro files on the systems
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Office Macro File Download
file_event\u001fwindows.description:
Detects the creation of a new office macro files on the system via an application (browser, mail client).
This can help identify potential malicious activity, such as the download of macro-enabled documents that could be used for exploitation.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Office Macro File Creation From Suspicious Process
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects the creation of a office macro file from a a suspicious process
file_event\u001fwindows.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: OneNote Attachment File Dropped In Suspicious Location
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects creation of files with the ".one"/".onepkg" extension in suspicious or uncommon locations. This could be a sign of attackers abusing OneNote attachments
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious File Created Via OneNote Application
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects suspicious files created via the OneNote application. This could indicate a potential malicious ".one"/".onepkg" file was executed as seen being used in malware activity in the wild
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: New Outlook Macro Created
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects the creation of a macro file for Outlook.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: @ScoubiMtl

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Potential Persistence Via Outlook Form
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects the creation of a new Outlook form which can contain malicious code
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Tobias Michalski (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious File Created in Outlook Temporary Directory
file_event\u001fwindows.description:
Detects the creation of files with suspicious file extensions in the temporary directory that Outlook uses when opening attachments.
This can be used to detect spear-phishing campaigns that use suspicious files as attachments, which may contain malicious code.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious Outlook Macro Created
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects the creation of a macro file for Outlook.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Publisher Attachment File Dropped In Suspicious Location
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects creation of files with the ".pub" extension in suspicious or uncommon locations. This could be a sign of attackers abusing Publisher documents
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Potential Persistence Via Microsoft Office Startup Folder
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects creation of Microsoft Office files inside of one of the default startup folders in order to achieve persistence.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Max Altgelt (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: File With Uncommon Extension Created By An Office Application
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects the creation of files with an executable or script extension by an Office application.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Vadim Khrykov (ThreatIntel), Cyb3rEng (Rule), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Uncommon File Created In Office Startup Folder
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects the creation of a file with an uncommon extension in an Office application startup folder
file_event\u001fwindows.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: PCRE.NET Package Temp Files
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects processes creating temp files related to PCRE.NET package
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious File Created In PerfLogs
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects suspicious file based on their extension being created in "C:\PerfLogs\". Note that this directory mostly contains ".etl" files
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Potential Binary Or Script Dropper Via PowerShell
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects PowerShell creating a binary executable or a script file.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: PowerShell Script Dropped Via PowerShell.EXE
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects PowerShell creating a PowerShell file (.ps1). While often times this behavior is benign, sometimes it can be a sign of a dropper script trying to achieve persistence.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: frack113

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Malicious PowerShell Scripts - FileCreation
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects the creation of known offensive powershell scripts used for exploitation
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Markus Neis, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Mustafa Kaan Demir, Georg Lauenstein

file_event\u001fwindows.title: PowerShell Module File Created
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects the creation of a new PowerShell module ".psm1", ".psd1", ".dll", ".ps1", etc.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Potential Suspicious PowerShell Module File Created
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects the creation of a new PowerShell module in the first folder of the module directory structure "\WindowsPowerShell\Modules\malware\malware.psm1". This is somewhat an uncommon practice as legitimate modules often includes a version folder.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: PowerShell Module File Created By Non-PowerShell Process
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects the creation of a new PowerShell module ".psm1", ".psd1", ".dll", ".ps1", etc. by a non-PowerShell process
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Potential Startup Shortcut Persistence Via PowerShell.EXE
file_event\u001fwindows.description:
Detects PowerShell writing startup shortcuts.
This procedure was highlighted in Red Canary Intel Insights Oct. 2021, "We frequently observe adversaries using PowerShell to write malicious .lnk files into the startup directory to establish persistence.
Accordingly, this detection opportunity is likel
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Christopher Peacock '@securepeacock', SCYTHE

file_event\u001fwindows.title: PSScriptPolicyTest Creation By Uncommon Process
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects the creation of the "PSScriptPolicyTest" PowerShell script by an uncommon process. This file is usually generated by Microsoft Powershell to test against Applocker.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Rclone Config File Creation
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects Rclone config files being created
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Aaron Greetham (@beardofbinary) - NCC Group

file_event\u001fwindows.title: .RDP File Created By Uncommon Application
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects creation of a file with an ".rdp" extension by an application that doesn't commonly create such files.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Potential Winnti Dropper Activity
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects files dropped by Winnti as described in RedMimicry Winnti playbook
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Alexander Rausch

file_event\u001fwindows.title: PDF File Created By RegEdit.EXE
file_event\u001fwindows.description:
Detects the creation of a file with the ".pdf" extension by the "RegEdit.exe" process.
This indicates that a user is trying to print/save a registry key as a PDF in order to potentially extract sensitive information and bypass defenses.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: RemCom Service File Creation
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects default RemCom service filename which indicates RemCom service installation and execution
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: ScreenConnect Temporary Installation Artefact
file_event\u001fwindows.description:
An adversary may use legitimate desktop support and remote access software, such as Team Viewer, Go2Assist, LogMein, AmmyyAdmin, etc, to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks.
These services are commonly used as legitimate technical support software,
file_event\u001fwindows.author: frack113

file_event\u001fwindows.description:
Detects the creation of files in a specific location by ScreenConnect RMM.
ScreenConnect has feature to remotely execute binaries on a target machine. These binaries will be dropped to ":\Users\<username>\Documents\ConnectWiseControl\Temp\" before execution.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Ali Alwashali

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Potential RipZip Attack on Startup Folder
file_event\u001fwindows.description:
Detects a phishing attack which expands a ZIP file containing a malicious shortcut.
If the victim expands the ZIP file via the explorer process, then the explorer process expands the malicious ZIP file and drops a malicious shortcut redirected to a backdoor into the Startup folder.
Additionally, the
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Greg (rule)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Potential SAM Database Dump
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects the creation of files that look like exports of the local SAM (Security Account Manager)
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Self Extraction Directive File Created In Potentially Suspicious Location
file_event\u001fwindows.description:
Detects the creation of Self Extraction Directive files (.sed) in a potentially suspicious location.
These files are used by the "iexpress.exe" utility in order to create self extracting packages.
Attackers were seen abusing this utility and creating PE files with embedded ".sed" entries.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Joseliyo Sanchez, @Joseliyo_Jstnk

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Windows Shell/Scripting Application File Write to Suspicious Folder
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects Windows shells and scripting applications that write files to suspicious folders
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Windows Binaries Write Suspicious Extensions
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects Windows executables that write files with suspicious extensions
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Startup Folder File Write
file_event\u001fwindows.description: A General detection for files being created in the Windows startup directory. This could be an indicator of persistence.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious Creation with Colorcpl
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Once executed, colorcpl.exe will copy the arbitrary file to c:\windows\system32\spool\drivers\color\
file_event\u001fwindows.author: frack113

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Created Files by Microsoft Sync Center
file_event\u001fwindows.description: This rule detects suspicious files created by Microsoft Sync Center (mobsync)
file_event\u001fwindows.author: elhoim

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious Files in Default GPO Folder
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects the creation of copy of suspicious files (EXE/DLL) to the default GPO storage folder
file_event\u001fwindows.author: elhoim

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious Desktopimgdownldr Target File
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects a suspicious Microsoft desktopimgdownldr file creation that stores a file to a suspicious location or contains a file with a suspicious extension
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Creation of a Diagcab
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects the creation of diagcab file, which could be caused by some legitimate installer or is a sign of exploitation (review the filename and its location)
file_event\u001fwindows.author: frack113

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious Double Extension Files
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects dropped files with double extensions, which is often used by malware as a method to abuse the fact that Windows hide default extensions by default.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), frack113

file_event\u001fwindows.title: DPAPI Backup Keys And Certificate Export Activity IOC
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects file names with specific patterns seen generated and used by tools such as Mimikatz and DSInternals related to exported or stolen DPAPI backup keys and certificates.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Nounou Mbeiri, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious MSExchangeMailboxReplication ASPX Write
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects suspicious activity in which the MSExchangeMailboxReplication process writes .asp and .apsx files to disk, which could be a sign of ProxyShell exploitation
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious Executable File Creation
file_event\u001fwindows.description:
Detect creation of suspicious executable file names.
Some strings look for suspicious file extensions, others look for filenames that exploit unquoted service paths.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: frack113

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious File Write to SharePoint Layouts Directory
file_event\u001fwindows.description:
Detects suspicious file writes to SharePoint layouts directory which could indicate webshell activity or post-exploitation.
This behavior has been observed in the exploitation of SharePoint vulnerabilities such as CVE-2025-49704, CVE-2025-49706 or CVE-2025-53770.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious File Write to Webapps Root Directory
file_event\u001fwindows.description:
Detects suspicious file writes to the root directory of web applications, particularly Apache web servers or Tomcat servers.
This may indicate an attempt to deploy malicious files such as web shells or other unauthorized scripts.
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

file_event\u001fwindows.description:
Get-Variable is a valid PowerShell cmdlet
WindowsApps is by default in the path where PowerShell is executed.

file_event\u001fwindows.author: frack113

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Potential Hidden Directory Creation Via NTFS INDEX_ALLOCATION Stream
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects the creation of hidden file/folder with the "::$index_allocation" stream. Which can be used as a technique to prevent access to folder and files from tooling such as "explorer.exe" and "powershell.exe"
file_event\u001fwindows.author: Scoubi (@ScoubiMtl)

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Potential Homoglyph Attack Using Lookalike Characters in Filename
file_event\u001fwindows.description:
Detects the presence of unicode characters which are homoglyphs, or identical in appearance, to ASCII letter characters.

file_event\u001fwindows.author: Micah Babinski, @micahbabinski

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Legitimate Application Dropped Archive
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects programs on a Windows system that should not write an archive to disk
file_event\u001fwindows.author: frack113, Florian Roth

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Legitimate Application Dropped Executable
file_event\u001fwindows.description: Detects programs on a Windows system that should not write executables to disk

file_event\u001fwindows.title: Legitimate Application Writing Files In Uncommon Location
file_event\u001fwindows.description:
Detects legitimate applications writing any type of file to uncommon or suspicious locations that are not typical for application data storage or execution.

process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Sreeman, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: File Deletion Via Del
process_creation\u001fwindows.description:
Detects execution of the builtin "del"/"erase" commands in order to delete files.
Adversaries may delete files left behind by the actions of their intrusion activity.
Malware, tools, or other non-native files dropped or created on a system by an adversary may leave traces to indicate to what was don
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: frack113

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Greedy File Deletion Using Del
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects execution of the "del" builtin command to remove files using greedy/wildcard expression. This is often used by malware to delete content of folders that perhaps contains the initial malware infection or to delete evidence.
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: frack113 , X__Junior (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: File And SubFolder Enumeration Via Dir Command
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects usage of the "dir" command part of Windows CMD with the "/S" command line flag in order to enumerate files in a specified directory and all subdirectories.
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: frack113

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Potential Dosfuscation Activity
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects possible payload obfuscation via the commandline
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Command Line Execution with Suspicious URL and AppData Strings
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects a suspicious command line execution that includes an URL and AppData string in the command line parameters as used by several droppers (js/vbs > powershell)
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Cmd Launched with Hidden Start Flags to Suspicious Targets
process_creation\u001fwindows.description:
Detects cmd.exe executing commands with the "start" utility using "/b" (no window) or "/min" (minimized) flags.
To reduce false positives from standard background tasks, detection is restricted to scenarios where the target is a known script extension or located in suspicious temporary/public direct
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Vladan Sekulic, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Potential Privilege Escalation Using Symlink Between Osk and Cmd
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects the creation of a symbolic link between "cmd.exe" and the accessibility on-screen keyboard binary (osk.exe) using "mklink". This technique provides an elevated command prompt to the user from the login screen without the need to log in.
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: frack113

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: VolumeShadowCopy Symlink Creation Via Mklink
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Shadow Copies storage symbolic link creation using operating systems utilities
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Teymur Kheirkhabarov, oscd.community

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious File Execution From Internet Hosted WebDav Share
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects the execution of the "net use" command to mount a WebDAV server and then immediately execute some content in it. As seen being used in malicious LNK files
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: pH-T (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Cmd.EXE Missing Space Characters Execution Anomaly
process_creation\u001fwindows.description:
Detects Windows command lines that miss a space before or after the /c flag when running a command using the cmd.exe.
This could be a sign of obfuscation of a fat finger problem (typo by the developer).
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: NtdllPipe Like Activity Execution
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects command that type the content of ntdll.dll to a different file or a pipe in order to evade AV / EDR detection. As seen being used in the POC NtdllPipe
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Potential CommandLine Path Traversal Via Cmd.EXE
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects potential path traversal attempt via cmd.exe. Could indicate possible command/argument confusion/hijacking
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: xknow @xknow_infosec, Tim Shelton

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Potentially Suspicious Ping/Copy Command Combination
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects uncommon and potentially suspicious one-liner command containing both "ping" and "copy" at the same time, which is usually used by malware.
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: X__Junior (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious Ping/Del Command Combination
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects a method often used by ransomware. Which combines the "ping" to wait a couple of seconds and then "del" to delete the file in question. Its used to hide the file responsible for the initial infection for example
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Ilya Krestinichev

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Potentially Suspicious CMD Shell Output Redirect
process_creation\u001fwindows.description:
Detects inline Windows shell commands redirecting output via the ">" symbol to a suspicious location.
This technique is sometimes used by malicious actors in order to redirect the output of reconnaissance commands such as "hostname" and "dir" to files for future exfiltration.
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Directory Removal Via Rmdir
process_creation\u001fwindows.description:
Detects execution of the builtin "rmdir" command in order to delete directories.
Adversaries may delete files left behind by the actions of their intrusion activity.
Malware, tools, or other non-native files dropped or created on a system by an adversary may leave traces to indicate to what was done
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: frack113

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Copy From VolumeShadowCopy Via Cmd.EXE
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects the execution of the builtin "copy" command that targets a shadow copy (sometimes used to copy registry hives that are in use)
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Max Altgelt (Nextron Systems), Tobias Michalski (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Read Contents From Stdin Via Cmd.EXE
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detect the use of "<" to read and potentially execute a file via cmd.exe
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Persistence Via Sticky Key Backdoor
process_creation\u001fwindows.description:
By replacing the sticky keys executable with the local admins CMD executable, an attacker is able to access a privileged windows console session without authenticating to the system.
When the sticky keys are "activated" the privilleged shell is launched.
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Sreeman

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Sticky Key Like Backdoor Execution
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects the usage and installation of a backdoor that uses an option to register a malicious debugger for built-in tools that are accessible in the login screen
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), @twjackomo, Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Potential Download/Upload Activity Using Type Command
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects usage of the "type" command to download/upload data from WebDAV server
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Unusual Parent Process For Cmd.EXE
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects suspicious parent process for cmd.exe
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Tim Rauch, Elastic (idea)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: CMSTP Execution Process Creation
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects various indicators of Microsoft Connection Manager Profile Installer execution
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Nik Seetharaman

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: OpenEDR Spawning Command Shell
process_creation\u001fwindows.description:
Detects the OpenEDR ssh-shellhost.exe spawning a command shell (cmd.exe) or PowerShell with PTY (pseudo-terminal) capabilities.
This may indicate remote command execution through OpenEDR's remote management features, which could be legitimate administrative activity or potential abuse of the remote
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: @kostastsale

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Arbitrary File Download Via ConfigSecurityPolicy.EXE
process_creation\u001fwindows.description:
Detects the execution of "ConfigSecurityPolicy.EXE", a binary part of Windows Defender used to manage settings in Windows Defender.
Users can configure different pilot collections for each of the co-management workloads.
It can be abused by attackers in order to upload or download files.
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: frack113

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Powershell Executed From Headless ConHost Process
process_creation\u001fwindows.description:
Detects the use of powershell commands from headless ConHost window.
The "--headless" flag hides the windows from the user upon execution.
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Matt Anderson (Huntress)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious High IntegrityLevel Conhost Legacy Option
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: ForceV1 asks for information directly from the kernel space. Conhost connects to the console application. High IntegrityLevel means the process is running with elevated privileges, such as an Administrator context.
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: frack113

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Conhost.exe CommandLine Path Traversal
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: detects the usage of path traversal in conhost.exe indicating possible command/argument confusion/hijacking
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Uncommon Child Process Of Conhost.EXE
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects uncommon "conhost" child processes. This could be a sign of "conhost" usage as a LOLBIN or potential process injection activity.
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: omkar72

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Potentially Suspicious Child Processes Spawned by ConHost
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects suspicious child processes related to Windows Shell utilities spawned by `conhost.exe`, which could indicate malicious activity using trusted system components.
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Conhost Spawned By Uncommon Parent Process
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects when the Console Window Host (conhost.exe) process is spawned by an uncommon parent process, which could be indicative of potential code injection activity.
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Tim Rauch, Elastic (idea)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Control Panel Items
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects the malicious use of a control panel item
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Kyaw Min Thein, Furkan Caliskan (@caliskanfurkan_)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: CreateDump Process Dump
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects uses of the createdump.exe LOLOBIN utility to dump process memory
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: New DMSA Service Account Created in Specific OUs
process_creation\u001fwindows.description:
Detects the creation of a dMSASvc account using the New-ADServiceAccount cmdlet in certain OUs.
The fact that the Cmdlet is used to create a dMSASvc account in a specific OU is highly suspicious.
It is a pattern trying to exploit the BadSuccessor privilege escalation vulnerability in Windows Server
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Windows Credential Guard Registry Tampering Via CommandLine
process_creation\u001fwindows.description:
Detects attempts to add, modify, or delete Windows Credential Guard related registry keys or values via command line tools such as Reg.exe or PowerShell.
Credential Guard uses virtualization-based security to isolate secrets so that only privileged system software can access them.
Adversaries may di
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Dynamic .NET Compilation Via Csc.EXE
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects execution of "csc.exe" to compile .NET code. Attackers often leverage this to compile code on the fly and use it in other stages.
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), X__Junior (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Csc.EXE Execution Form Potentially Suspicious Parent
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects a potentially suspicious parent of "csc.exe", which could be a sign of payload delivery.
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), X__Junior (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious Csi.exe Usage
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Csi.exe is a signed binary from Microsoft that comes with Visual Studio and provides C# interactive capabilities. It can be used to run C# code from a file passed as a parameter in command line. Early version of this utility provided with Microsoft “Roslyn” Community Technology Preview was named 'rc
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Konstantin Grishchenko, oscd.community

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious Use of CSharp Interactive Console
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects the execution of CSharp interactive console by PowerShell
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Michael R. (@nahamike01)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Active Directory Structure Export Via Csvde.EXE
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects the execution of "csvde.exe" in order to export organizational Active Directory structure.
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Potential Cookies Session Hijacking
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects execution of "curl.exe" with the "-c" flag in order to save cookie data.
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Curl Web Request With Potential Custom User-Agent
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects execution of "curl.exe" with a potential custom "User-Agent". Attackers can leverage this to download or exfiltrate data via "curl" to a domain that only accept specific "User-Agent" strings
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: File Download From IP URL Via Curl.EXE
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects file downloads directly from IP address URL using curl.exe
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious File Download From IP Via Curl.EXE
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects potentially suspicious file downloads directly from IP addresses using curl.exe
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious File Download From File Sharing Domain Via Curl.EXE
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects potentially suspicious file download from file sharing domains using curl.exe
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Insecure Transfer Via Curl.EXE
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects execution of "curl.exe" with the "--insecure" flag.
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: X__Junior (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Insecure Proxy/DOH Transfer Via Curl.EXE
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects execution of "curl.exe" with the "insecure" flag over proxy or DOH.
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Local File Read Using Curl.EXE
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects execution of "curl.exe" with the "file://" protocol handler in order to read local files.
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious Curl.EXE Download
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects a suspicious curl process start on Windows and outputs the requested document to a local file
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious CustomShellHost Execution
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects the execution of CustomShellHost.exe where the child isn't located in 'C:\Windows\explorer.exe'. CustomShellHost is a known LOLBin that can be abused by attackers for defense evasion techniques.
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: ManageEngine Endpoint Central Dctask64.EXE Potential Abuse
process_creation\u001fwindows.description:
Detects the execution of "dctask64.exe", a signed binary by ZOHO Corporation part of ManageEngine Endpoint Central.
This binary can be abused for DLL injection, arbitrary command and process execution.
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Uncommon Child Process Of Defaultpack.EXE
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects uncommon child processes of "DefaultPack.EXE" binary as a proxy to launch other programs
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: frack113

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: PowerShell Defender Threat Severity Default Action Set to 'Allow' or 'NoAction'
process_creation\u001fwindows.description:
Detects the use of PowerShell to execute the 'Set-MpPreference' cmdlet to configure Windows Defender's threat severity default action to 'Allow' (value '6') or 'NoAction' (value '9').
This is a highly suspicious configuration change that effectively disables Defender's ability to automatically mitig
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Matt Anderson (Huntress)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Windows Defender Context Menu Removed
process_creation\u001fwindows.description:
Detects the use of reg.exe or PowerShell to delete the Windows Defender context menu handler registry keys.
This action removes the "Scan with Microsoft Defender" option from the right-click menu for files, directories, and drives.
Attackers may use this technique to hinder manual, on-demand scans a
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Matt Anderson (Huntress)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Remote File Download Via Desktopimgdownldr Utility
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects the desktopimgdownldr utility being used to download a remote file. An adversary may use desktopimgdownldr to download arbitrary files as an alternative to certutil.
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Tim Rauch, Elastic (idea)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious Desktopimgdownldr Command
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects a suspicious Microsoft desktopimgdownldr execution with parameters used to download files from the Internet
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Devcon Execution Disabling VMware VMCI Device
process_creation\u001fwindows.description:
Detects execution of devcon.exe with commands that disable the VMware Virtual Machine Communication Interface (VMCI) device.
This can be legitimate during VMware Tools troubleshooting or driver conflicts, but may also indicate malware attempting to hijack communication with the hardware via the VMCI
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Matt Anderson, Dray Agha, Anna Pham (Huntress)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Potential DLL Sideloading Via DeviceEnroller.EXE
process_creation\u001fwindows.description:
Detects the use of the PhoneDeepLink parameter to potentially sideload a DLL file that does not exist. This non-existent DLL file is named "ShellChromeAPI.dll".
Adversaries can drop their own renamed DLL and execute it via DeviceEnroller.exe using this parameter
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: @gott_cyber

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: DeviceCredentialDeployment Execution
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects the execution of DeviceCredentialDeployment to hide a process from view.
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Arbitrary MSI Download Via Devinit.EXE
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects a certain command line flag combination used by "devinit.exe", which can be abused as a LOLBIN to download arbitrary MSI packages on a Windows system
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Potentially Suspicious Child Process Of ClickOnce Application
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects potentially suspicious child processes of a ClickOnce deployment application
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: DirLister Execution
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detect the usage of "DirLister.exe" a utility for quickly listing folder or drive contents. It was seen used by BlackCat ransomware to create a list of accessible directories and files.
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: frack113

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: System Information Discovery via Registry Queries
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects attempts to query system information directly from the Windows Registry.
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: lazarg

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Potentially Suspicious Child Process Of DiskShadow.EXE
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects potentially suspicious child processes of "Diskshadow.exe". This could be an attempt to bypass parent/child relationship detection or application whitelisting rules.
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Diskshadow Script Mode - Uncommon Script Extension Execution
process_creation\u001fwindows.description:
Detects execution of "Diskshadow.exe" in script mode to execute an script with a potentially uncommon extension.
Initial baselining of the allowed extension list is required.
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Diskshadow Script Mode - Execution From Potential Suspicious Location
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects execution of "Diskshadow.exe" in script mode using the "/s" flag where the script is located in a potentially suspicious location.
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: PowerShell Web Access Feature Enabled Via DISM
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects the use of DISM to enable the PowerShell Web Access feature, which could be used for remote access and potential abuse
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Michael Haag

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Dism Remove Online Package
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Deployment Image Servicing and Management tool. DISM is used to enumerate, install, uninstall, configure, and update features and packages in Windows images
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: frack113

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Dllhost.EXE Execution Anomaly
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects a "dllhost" process spawning with no commandline arguments which is very rare to happen and could indicate process injection activity or malware mimicking similar system processes.
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: DLL Sideloading by VMware Xfer Utility
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects execution of VMware Xfer utility (VMwareXferlogs.exe) from the non-default directory which may be an attempt to sideload arbitrary DLL
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Potential Discovery Activity Via Dnscmd.EXE
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects an attempt to leverage dnscmd.exe to enumerate the DNS zones of a domain. DNS zones used to host the DNS records for a particular domain.
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: @gott_cyber

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: New DNS ServerLevelPluginDll Installed Via Dnscmd.EXE
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects the installation of a DNS plugin DLL via ServerLevelPluginDll parameter in registry, which can be used to execute code in context of the DNS server (restart required)
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: DNS Exfiltration and Tunneling Tools Execution
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Well-known DNS Exfiltration tools execution
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Daniil Yugoslavskiy, oscd.community

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Unusual Child Process of dns.exe
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects an unexpected process spawning from dns.exe which may indicate activity related to remote code execution or other forms of exploitation as seen in CVE-2020-1350 (SigRed)
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Tim Rauch, Elastic (idea)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Potential Application Whitelisting Bypass via Dnx.EXE
process_creation\u001fwindows.description:
Detects the execution of Dnx.EXE. The Dnx utility allows for the execution of C# code.
Attackers might abuse this in order to bypass application whitelisting.
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Beyu Denis, oscd.community

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Process Memory Dump Via Dotnet-Dump
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects the execution of "dotnet-dump" with the "collect" flag. The execution could indicate potential process dumping of critical processes such as LSASS.
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Arbitrary DLL or Csproj Code Execution Via Dotnet.EXE
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects execution of arbitrary DLLs or unsigned code via a ".csproj" files via Dotnet.EXE.
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Beyu Denis, oscd.community

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Binary Proxy Execution Via Dotnet-Trace.EXE
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects commandline arguments for executing a child process via dotnet-trace.exe
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Jimmy Bayne (@bohops)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Potential Recon Activity Using DriverQuery.EXE
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detect usage of the "driverquery" utility to perform reconnaissance on installed drivers
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: DriverQuery.EXE Execution
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detect usage of the "driverquery" utility. Which can be used to perform reconnaissance on installed drivers
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Potentially Over Permissive Permissions Granted Using Dsacls.EXE
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects usage of Dsacls to grant over permissive permissions
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Potential Password Spraying Attempt Using Dsacls.EXE
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects possible password spraying attempts using Dsacls
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Domain Trust Discovery Via Dsquery
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects execution of "dsquery.exe" for domain trust discovery
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: E.M. Anhaus, Tony Lambert, oscd.community, omkar72

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Suspicious Kernel Dump Using Dtrace
process_creation\u001fwindows.description: Detects suspicious way to dump the kernel on Windows systems using dtrace.exe, which is available on Windows systems since Windows 10 19H1
process_creation\u001fwindows.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

process_creation\u001fwindows.title: Potential Windows Defender AV Bypass Via Dump64.EXE Rename
process_creation\u001fwindows.description:
Detects when a user is potentially trying to bypass the Windows Defender AV by renaming a tool to dump64.exe and placing it in the Visual Studio folder.
Currently the rule is covering only usage of procdump but other utilities can be added in order to increase coverage.
